## Social Network Diffusion, Influence, and Source Inference

This community studies how information, products, tasks, and epidemics propagate through online and other networked systems. Core themes include influence maximization and marketing, adaptive seeding, product adoption and revenue, worker recruitment, cascade popularity, complex contagion, and diffusion under temporal, spatial, or changing network structure. A growing focus is on inverse problems: locating one or multiple diffusion sources, recovering hidden network topology, estimating edge-transmission probabilities, and identifying malicious origins from incomplete observations. Epidemic containment and spreading assisted by mobile or external agents extend these questions beyond social media.

Typical methods combine independent-cascade, linear-threshold, SI/epidemic, Bass, Hawkes, and continuous-time diffusion models with centrality, random walks, optimization, and stochastic simulation. Adaptive submodularity, greedy policies, mixed-integer programming, particle-swarm heuristics, Jordan-center/cover algorithms, dynamic programming, and approximation guarantees support intervention and resource allocation. Cascade trees, contrastive learning, text-aware models, and aggregate-observation inference connect graph structure with content and partial feedback.

Recent directions emphasize dynamic and adaptive networks, limited probing and partial observations, continuous-time processes, collective diffusion, and explicit uncertainty about propagation mechanisms. Applications increasingly optimize real outcomes—adoption, revenue, recruitment, and containment—rather than exposure alone, while incorporating incentives, pricing, online activities, and malicious-information response.

### Event, Scholarly, and Social-Data Intelligence

This community studies how to retrieve, structure, and interpret events, knowledge, and social behavior in large, evolving collections of text, images, links, and scholarly records. Key themes include social-media event detection and retrieval, geo-temporal image search, tourism and experience analytics, and multilingual event timelines derived from event-centric knowledge graphs.

A second focus is information discovery and scientific intelligence. Topic models connect ideas across domains through bisociative networks, while machine learning maps scholarly fields, detects emerging communities, and supports automated hypothesis generation. Candidate ranking and empirical analysis of abstracts, full text, corpus size, and document length address the validation and reliability of such systems.

Typical methods include interaction-graph random walks, temporal and geographic feature extraction, machine-learning query expansion, term association and distribution statistics (including KLD, Bo1, RM3), WordNet-based semantic expansion, topic modeling, knowledge-graph construction, and network analysis. Provenance-aware interactive visualization supports traceable exploration, while compact query sketches enable efficient what-if analytics.

Recent trends emphasize cross-lingual and multimodal retrieval, social and scholarly network structure, creative cross-domain discovery, provenance and explainability, and scalable systems for interactive analytics.

751b75ee1b662aa338a9d86103dda6c56d4e498e.text:
## Scientometrics, Citation Metrics, and Science Mapping

This community quantitatively studies scientific knowledge, influence, performance, and collaboration. Major themes include citation-based assessment of papers, authors, journals, institutions, countries, and research programs; field normalization and fractional attribution; interdisciplinarity, collaboration diversity, internationality, and technology emergence; and critiques of impact factors, h-indices, rankings, and evaluation regimes. It also examines whether citations reflect perceived impact, prestige, creativity, uncertainty, and the propagation of scientific ideas.

Typical methods combine Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar, Dimensions, Microsoft Academic, PubMed, patent databases, and bibliographic graphs. Citation, co-citation, bibliographic-coupling, co-authorship, author–paper, and citation-context networks are analyzed with centrality, community detection, similarity, entropy, cognitive-distance, and overlay mapping. PageRank-like algorithms distinguish popularity from prestige and support author, institution, and patent ranking. Other approaches include percentile indicators (I3 and variants), field-normalized scores, fractional counting, RPYS, half-life analysis, author disambiguation, expert surveys, text/subject-heading analysis, and deep-learning citation prediction.

Recent trends emphasize comparing scholarly data sources, open-access coverage, article-level and nonparametric evaluation, citation-context and epistemic analysis, network-based entity resolution, collaboration diversity, interactive science mapping, and forecasting influential papers and emerging technologies. Greater attention is paid to metric validity, database coverage, statistical concordance, and unintended assessment effects.

102ea2799a648772a7279917c37801bfe12f13da.text:
## Community Detection in Dynamic Networks

This community studies how to detect, evaluate, model, and exploit mesoscopic structure in complex networks. Themes include overlapping, attributed, weighted, multilayer, evolving, directed, and interdependent communities; local community search; node roles and centrality; and structure aligned with diffusion, influence, contagion, and other network dynamics. Applications span social and online networks, information propagation, interbank and cyber-physical systems, epidemics, bibliometrics, and knowledge networks.

Typical methods include modularity optimization with adaptive positive and negative edge weights, label propagation and semi-supervised constraints, spectral and diffusion-based techniques, personalized PageRank, random walks, core/truss decompositions, and multi-criteria or evolutionary optimization. Probabilistic approaches include stochastic blockmodels, degree-corrected and contextual blockmodels, dynamic latent-variable models, factor graphs, and message passing. Heat diffusion and signal distances provide tools for comparing graph-supported signals.

Evaluation remains central: work examines multi-criteria partition assessment, model selection, centrality consistency, dynamic link-prediction metrics, detectability, finite-size effects, and uncertainty-aware community tracking. Recent trends emphasize state-space and Markov models for evolving networks, incremental and distributed discovery, integration of topology with node covariates, adaptive damping and diffusion parameters, real-time event and dense-cluster detection, and community-informed influence maximization and resilience design.

ebb355fd5971a47243d7ed8881e1bfbfdf0a5f87.text:
### Semantic Search, Text Mining, and Mathematical Retrieval

This community focuses on scalable semantic analysis and retrieval. One major theme is text mining and classification, including probabilistic topic modeling, clustering, k-nearest neighbors, association rules, feature selection, dependency pruning, authorship analysis, active learning, and technology-assisted review. Recent work targets sparse short texts and automatic subject indexing, using learned representations and document-level quality estimation.

A second theme is fast similarity search. Methods include locality- and density-sensitive hashing, self-taught and deep supervised hashing, compact binary codes, semantic embeddings, and multigranularity topics and tags. These support large-scale document and nearest-neighbor retrieval, including previously unseen data. Time-series search introduces sketch-based indexing and pruning strategies to accelerate Dynamic Time Warping.

The community also develops mathematical information services. It addresses combined text-and-formula retrieval, presentation- and content-based search, identifier extraction and namespaces, faceted interfaces, formula repositories, and accessible MathML. Systems such as MIaS extend Lucene with mathematical preprocessing and formula-aware retrieval.

Typical methods include neural representation learning, convolutional networks, regression-based confidence estimation, topic modeling, hashing and Hamming-space search, DTW with branch-and-bound pruning, semantic enrichment, pattern matching, and canonicalization. Recent trends emphasize deep and unsupervised learning, compact representations, scalable similarity search, quality-aware indexing, and more semantic, interactive, and accessible mathematical retrieval.

793c0a794896ded98829395a809eadaefcf2b1e9.text:
## Network Diffusion, Influence, and Source Inference

This community studies how information, opinions, epidemics, failures, and tasks propagate through social, biological, infrastructure, and cyber-physical networks. Core problems include inverse diffusion—locating sources, estimating initiation times, reconstructing cascades, and inferring hidden network structure or influence probabilities from sparse, temporal, aggregate, or biased observations—and forward control through seeding, immunization, recruitment, advertising, and containment.

Influence maximization increasingly incorporates evolving networks, intrinsic node activation, community structure, competing products or opinions, multiphase campaigns, adaptive feedback, coupons, pricing, contests, and resource constraints. Opinion dynamics and strategic diffusion model competing camps, investment, referrals, and public sentiment; applications span marketing, mobile crowd sensing, conservation, policy, and citation networks.

Typical methods combine independent-cascade, threshold, epidemic, Bass, DeGroot/Friedkin, Markov, and continuous-time models with submodularity, approximation, game theory, mixed-integer optimization, centrality, random walks, message passing, sampling, and machine learning. Cascade inference uses temporally constrained Steiner trees, probabilistic cascade sampling, directed spanning trees, contrastive learning, and discriminative prediction.

Recent trends emphasize causal identification of influence under homophily and missing data, randomized experiments, fairness, robust and non-submodular objectives, partitioned sampling, online querying, evolving and adaptive networks, and realistic multiphase decision-making.

0a931fd2fba80807e5a9dd511e942209474efce6.text:
### Scholarly Communication, Impact, and Discovery

This community examines how scholarly work is disseminated, discovered, evaluated, and reused. Core themes include altmetrics and societal impact; relationships among citations, readership, downloads, tweets, social-media attention, and web visibility; open access through green and gold routes, institutional repositories, and mandates; and bibliometrics for authors, papers, journals, books, publishers, and conferences. It also studies academic profile platforms, scholarly search, expert discovery, recommendation, reviewer assignment, and research-group assessment.

Typical methods combine large bibliographic, usage, repository, and social-media datasets from Web of Science, Scopus, Mendeley, Twitter, Facebook, ResearchGate, Google Scholar, Dimensions, ROAR, and ROARMAP. Analyses use correlation, regression, PCA/factor analysis, ranking, network, distributional, and time-series methods. Machine learning, web crawling, scraping, API-based collection, sentiment analysis, and linguistic feature extraction support metric construction, visibility prediction, and platform evaluation. Case studies span physics, biomedical research, computer science, and scientometrics.

Recent work emphasizes heterogeneous, rapidly changing online signals and their uncertain relationship to peer-assessed quality, reputation, and societal impact. It highlights platform-specific engagement, title and author effects, API and URL-matching problems, gaming and “ghost” reputations, and biases in metric-based evaluation. Open-access research increasingly compares mandate strength, repository deposits, publication models, disciplinary patterns, and citation effects.

75b8c48262e391df4fb40453d0230a45adecd7d2.text:
## Network Diffusion, Influence, and Source Inference

This community studies how information, opinions, epidemics, products, and tasks propagate through social, biological, infrastructure, and cyber-physical networks. Core problems include forward diffusion and trend/adoption prediction; inverse diffusion, including source and initiation-time localization and cascade reconstruction from partial temporal observations; and influence maximization under evolving topology, competing campaigns, coupons, budgets, and recruitment constraints. Opinion formation, strategic diffusion, immunization, and robust network intervention are important application areas.

A growing emphasis is on measuring genuine influence rather than correlation, using causal models, randomized experiments, biased sampling, and adaptive querying. Work also ranks influential or changing nodes through PageRank variants, centrality, mixed-membership models, and composite or multimodal social networks, supporting recommendations, app adoption, marketing, and mobile crowd sensing.

Typical methods combine independent-cascade, threshold, epidemic, opinion, Bass, Markov, and continuous-time models with submodularity, approximation, game theory, mixed-integer optimization, robust and stochastic optimization, random walks, message passing, Steiner-tree reconstruction, sampling, heuristics, and machine learning—including contrastive learning over cascade trees.

Recent trends emphasize time-varying networks and external interests, intrinsic node activation, partial and biased observations, non-submodular and competitive cascades, causal identification, adaptive intervention, and resilient control.

65e7854603a09ebb64800528ac9c234a3f75ff07.text:
## Network Diffusion, Influence, and Source Inference

This community studies how information, opinions, epidemics, failures, and tasks propagate through social, biological, infrastructure, citation, and cyber-physical networks. Core problems include forward diffusion and influence maximization, source and cascade reconstruction, initiation-time estimation, hidden-structure recovery, immunization, and resilient containment under partial observations.

Influence-oriented work selects or recruits seeds to maximize adoption, coverage, revenue, worker participation, or diverse exposure. It increasingly addresses evolving networks, multiple phases, competitive opinions and products, coupons and pricing, strategic incentives, online activity, and resource or probing constraints. Related work learns influence from cascades, detects causal effects despite homophily and missing data, and applies influence centrality to domains such as patent citations.

Typical methods combine independent-cascade, linear-threshold, epidemic, Bass, DeGroot-Friedkin, Markov, and continuous-time models with submodularity, approximation algorithms, mixed-integer optimization, adaptive policies, game theory, randomized experiments, centrality heuristics, message passing, random walks, sampling, and machine learning. Recent methods include directed-spanning-tree and contrastive cascade models, robust densest-subgraph optimization, Steiner-tree cascade sampling, and learning-to-influence frameworks.

Recent trends emphasize adaptive and temporal diffusion, multiphase decision-making, strategic and competitive propagation, robust inference from sparse or noisy data, causal influence measurement, higher-order structure, and socially desirable objectives such as viewpoint diversity and resilient recruitment.

a501772c9416fbc7e0f7bbf086c7d3b8e318740a.text:
### Dynamic Social, Event, and Knowledge Intelligence

This community studies latent structure, events, opinions, and trends in large, evolving collections of text, links, images, spatial data, scholarly records, and social-media streams. Topic modeling remains central, spanning temporal and nonparametric models, hypertext and citation links, review aspects, personal timelines, and cross-domain networks for creative discovery.

A major focus is event detection, retrieval, and forecasting. Social platforms and geotagged media serve as sensors for sports, disasters, protests, tourism, and other physical-world events. Methods include burst and anomaly detection, event segmentation, query expansion using geographic and temporal tags, interaction-graph random walks, spatial clustering, sentiment and opinion modeling, and cross-source timeline construction. Multilingual event knowledge graphs support cross-lingual temporal summaries.

The community also analyzes scholarly ecosystems: machine learning maps emerging fields and collaboration networks, while knowledge-network systems generate and rank hypotheses and evaluate the effects of corpus size, abstracts, and full text. Provenance-aware interactive visualization and compact query provisioning support efficient exploratory analytics and what-if computation.

Recent trends emphasize scalable, continuous, and provenance-preserving analysis; integration of social, scholarly, geographic, and knowledge-graph evidence; multilingual and multimodal retrieval; and predictive decision support for civic activity, tourism, and public events.

437575920393a56e8cf293adf7d684782337eefb.text:
### Bibliometric Evaluation, Efficiency, and Equity in Higher Education

This community studies how research performance is measured and explained in national, institutional, departmental, and individual systems, with particular emphasis on Italy and comparative university evaluation. Themes include productivity, quality and impact, field-normalized indicators, rankings, VQR and other assessment exercises, research funding, technical and cost efficiency, and the validity and timing of citation-based measures. Equity remains central, encompassing gender-sensitive evaluation, recruitment and opportunistic behavior, seniority, and regional disparities. Research also examines international knowledge flows and the countries benefiting from national research, comparative advantage, and multidisciplinary collaboration as drivers of research diversification.

Typical methods include large-scale bibliometric analysis using Web of Science or Google Scholar, citation and h-index indicators, field normalization, sensitivity and ranking comparisons, regression and quantile analysis, DEA and other efficiency models, network and collaboration analysis, Gini and distributional measures, and conceptual critique of impact indicators. Department- and university-level benchmarking is common.

Recent trends emphasize gender-aware and cross-field evaluation, separating productivity from quality, uncertainty and citation-window sensitivity, clearer definitions of impact, scrutiny of perverse incentives in assessment systems, and policy-oriented mapping of international knowledge benefits and multidisciplinary research.

37d937a35ece4da51e2b66a46c628951e63960c8.text:
### Dynamic Topic, Event, and Knowledge Intelligence

This community studies how to extract structure, events, opinions, trends, and relationships from large, evolving collections of text, images, links, scholarly records, and social-media data. Topic modeling remains central, including temporal and nonparametric models, multi-domain bisociative networks, bibliographic community mapping, and knowledge-network methods for hypothesis generation.

A major focus is event retrieval and situational awareness across Twitter, photo platforms, YouTube, and news. Methods include burst and anomaly detection, event segmentation, social-interaction graphs and random walks, geotemporal tag analysis, query expansion, timeline generation, and cross-lingual event knowledge graphs. Opinion-dynamics models and social-network techniques address influence, friendship prediction, community formation, and engagement.

The community also emphasizes information access and analytical infrastructure: probabilistic and lexical query expansion, WordNet, provenance-aware interactive visualization, compact query provisioning, and scalable validation of automated hypothesis-ranking systems. Statistical dependence modeling, including vine copulas, supports analysis of large platform datasets.

Recent trends emphasize multilingual event-centric timelines, social and scholarly knowledge graphs, creative cross-domain discovery, large-scale platform analytics, and decision support for tourism and other applications. Evaluation increasingly examines corpus size, document granularity, candidate ranking, and the reproducibility of derived insights.

d61a028ddac28e3d5de6bb72fd5245723c716ba4.text:
### Social Networks, Misinformation, and Platform Integrity

This community studies how online platforms shape political discourse, collective beliefs, and information diffusion. Major themes include echo chambers, polarization, controversy, misinformation and rumor verification, extremist and conspiratorial communities, media bias, hate speech, harassment, and connective action. A parallel focus concerns platform integrity: social bots, spam, fake followers, astroturfing, malicious or fringe communities, coordinated influence campaigns, and manipulation of feeds, advertising, search, and popularity metrics. Applications increasingly include health communication and targeted public-health interventions.

Typical methods combine large-scale data collection from Twitter, Facebook, YouTube, Reddit, Gab, livestreaming, commenting, and crowdsourcing platforms with network analysis, surveys, content and sentiment analysis, temporal cascade analysis, and controlled experiments. Researchers use graph clustering, embeddings, communicability and diffusion measures, supervised and semi-supervised classification, stance and sympathy detection, neural language and image representations, anomaly detection, and dynamical contagion models. Hoaxy and repositories such as FakeNewsNet support reproducible study of information cascades.

Recent work emphasizes early detection of rumors, clickbait, polluters, and manipulated accounts; multimodal integration of content, social context, and dynamics; cross-platform political influence and ranking bias; interpretable stance-aware summaries; and evaluation of interventions including fact checking, bot-based health messaging, moderation, and defenses against coordinated manipulation.

5f7c8876870a9902e37dfdd00cda44461dc8642d.text:
**Graph-Based Entity Resolution and Social Structure**

This community focuses on integrating and interpreting complex relational data across devices, databases, and time. Major themes include cross-device user matching; record linkage for heterogeneous and historical records; genealogical and population reconstruction; temporal clustering; and the discovery of social roles in large-scale systems. It also studies recurring activity and propagation patterns in time-evolving graphs, anomalies in heterogeneous information networks, and data fusion for search and other information systems.

Typical methods combine extensive feature engineering, negative sampling, model selection, attribute- and graph-based record linkage, temporal graph clustering, community and role discovery, and multilayer representations of events across successive time steps. Tensor decomposition, clustering, user-directed queries, synthetic heterogeneous-network generation, and empirical comparison against manually constructed records support anomaly detection and validation.

Recent trends emphasize automated integration of fragmented records, computational reconstruction of long-term social and demographic structures, scalable mining of temporal propagation patterns, and role-based abstractions of social systems. The community also increasingly values transparent, open evaluation frameworks for data fusion and methods that handle heterogeneous entities, missing identifiers, noisy historical data, and evolving relationships.

ff45c01d4d2649e604edcaddf219af12e6696744.text:
## Community Detection and Network Structure

This community studies how to detect, evaluate, model, and exploit mesoscopic structure in complex networks. Key themes include overlapping and multiple-membership communities; multilayer, attributed, weighted, interaction, incomplete, and dynamic networks; local communities, cores and trusses; and the relationship between community structure, hierarchy, centrality, diffusion, and network dynamics. Applications span social, web, communication, biological, bibliometric, and recommendation networks.

Typical methods include modularity optimization with adaptive positive/negative edge weights, label propagation, clique and density-based approaches, spectral and random-walk methods, personalized PageRank, matrix factorization, stochastic block models, nonparametric Bayesian latent-feature models, and core/truss decomposition. Recent work also uses semi-supervised constraints, multiview attributes, probabilistic data fusion, and graph-based ascent or sampling algorithms. Theoretical analyses address detectability, spectral phase transitions, localization, finite-size effects, and PageRank damping.

Evaluation remains central: studies compare partition and node-level metrics, multi-criteria quality assessment, agreement indices, benchmarks, and threshold-free modeling of interaction counts. Current trends emphasize scalable and distributed processing, I/O-efficient decomposition, incremental discovery in evolving graphs, persistent dense subgraphs across snapshots, and principled integration of topology with covariates, topics, uncertainty, cognition, and partial observability. Other directions include centrality-aware analysis, synthetic-network realism, and community-informed recommendation and influence applications.

2fcb0e6597b68c394a27a5ff2e7670f566291dbd.text:
## Scientometrics, Research Evaluation, and Science Mapping

This community quantifies scientific influence, performance, knowledge accumulation, and collaboration across authors, papers, journals, institutions, and countries. Core themes include citation-based indicators, field normalization, percentile and distributional methods, university rankings, peer-review concordance, national evaluation, societal impact, and critiques of journal impact factors, h-indices, and assessment incentives. Fairness concerns include disciplinary differences, heavy-tailed citation distributions, international and institutional biases, database coverage, and credit allocation in multi-authored work.

Typical methods use Web of Science, Scopus, Dimensions, Microsoft Academic, PubMed, and regional databases, with citation, co-citation, bibliographic-coupling, co-authorship, and citation-context networks. PageRank-style prestige measures, centrality, community detection, RPYS, percentile indicators, I3 variants, field-normalized scores, econometric indices, and cognitive-distance maps are common. Author disambiguation, fractional or position-weighted counting, weighted h-indices, and statistical comparisons of rankings are also prominent. Machine learning, including deep neural networks, is used for citation prediction.

Recent trends emphasize cross-database validation, article-level and nonparametric evaluation, dynamic research-space and career-path modeling, preferential-attachment analysis, citation-context and epistemic-uncertainty analysis, and improved measurement of collaboration, internationality, and societal relevance. The community increasingly advocates transparent, empirically tested indicator systems and cautions against simplistic rankings and unintended behavioral effects.

09f5ec86e84455001c1fdad35222e3af5b025093.text:
### Robust, Multimodal, and Sequential Recommendation

This community centers on personalized recommendation under sparse, implicit, noisy, and heterogeneous feedback. Core themes include long- versus short-term and session-aware behavior; cold-start, cross-domain transfer, and long-tail items; diverse interests; multimodal and knowledge-enhanced content; social influence; and temporal, spatial, and multi-behavior modeling. Applications span news, music, education, images, products, and next-POI prediction.

Typical methods include matrix factorization, factorization machines, Bayesian and pairwise ranking, autoencoders, neural collaborative filtering, outer-product and nonlinear interaction networks, recurrent/attention models, and deep transfer learning. Graph methods increasingly model social diffusion, heterogeneous item relations, knowledge bases, trust, and user collaboration, while hyperbolic embeddings capture hierarchy. Reinforcement learning and bandit-style approaches address sequential recommendation, feedback, and exploration–exploitation. Multimodal systems combine text, audio, images, subtitles, and behavioral signals, with modality dropout and transfer learning for missing data and cold start.

Recent trends emphasize robust recommendation against shilling, camouflage, unreliable ratings, and adversarially corrupted multimedia; richer multi-action feedback; interpretable behavioral and cognitive user models; spatiotemporal sequence awareness; filter-bubble mitigation; and efficient deployment through binary embeddings, scalable graph models, online push services, and automated algorithm selection.

## Community Currently Empty

No papers currently remain in this community. Consequently, no active research themes, typical methods, or recent trends can be supported by its membership.

bcc7c0672fa1b8cc6441dbfa3e291e344e96a5b3.text:
## Social Media Analytics, Politics, Mobility, and Urban Life

This community studies how digital traces reveal collective preferences, social influence, migration, human movement, and urban experience. Political and media analysis uses Twitter, Facebook, news audiences, and heterogeneous online signals to infer voter preferences, political orientation, campaign and election trends, audience targeting, rumors, and public perceptions of technologies such as IoT. Related work examines migrant assimilation, diasporas, demographic roles, homophily, and online exposure to racism or homophobia.

A second theme concerns spatial and urban analytics. Geotagged posts, mobile-phone and app GPS data, check-ins, and location-based networks support studies of commuting, migration flows, toponym resolution, urban boundaries, neighborhood exposure, park-related affect, and qualitative experiences of cities. Entity-centered temporal analysis tracks changing sentiment, popularity, and associations in large archives.

Typical methods include machine-learning classifiers, hashtag and topic analysis, sentiment analysis, regression, gravity models, Kalman filtering, event studies, network/community analysis, diffusion simulation, contextual centrality, self-organizing maps, OCR and automated mobile sensing, and unsupervised gazetteer-based geolocation. RDF archives and scalable annotation enable reproducible analysis.

Recent directions emphasize heterogeneous, longitudinal, and partially observed data; validation against polls; fine-grained spatial and demographic inference; uncertainty and sampling bias; social-environmental measurement; and explainable modeling of diffusion, influence, and information reliability.

1a909594563dda6866ce8d0f209668f999f1393b.text:
## Community Detection and Network Structure

This community studies how to detect, evaluate, model, and exploit mesoscale structure in complex networks. Themes include overlapping, multilayer, attributed, weighted, signed, dynamic, distributed, partially observed, and two-mode communities; local search; cohesive cores; node importance; and structure aligned with diffusion, consensus, and other dynamics. Applications include social, communication, web, bibliometric, biological, and interaction networks, including real-time event discovery.

Typical methods include modularity optimization with adaptive positive/negative edge weights, label propagation and randomized speaker–listener methods, clique and density approaches, spectral and manifold techniques, personalized PageRank and random walks, core/truss decomposition, graph signal processing, centrality and entropy measures, and probabilistic models such as stochastic block models, contextual/attribute-augmented Bayesian models, and multiple-membership latent models. Semi-supervised constraints, data fusion, and graph-plus-covariate inference extend purely structural detection.

Evaluation remains central: research compares quality functions, multi-criteria and node-level metrics, benchmark and synthetic multilayer models, detectability limits, threshold effects, and algorithm selection. Recent trends emphasize scalable I/O-efficient and distributed processing, incremental discovery in rapidly evolving graphs, uncertainty-aware community tracking, incomplete-network inference, richer attributes and edge semantics, and diffusion-oriented simulation and prediction.

c0a040adb8cd4e4927940410077015bb0074f7ed.text:
## Online Networks: Diffusion, Influence, and Collective Risk

This community studies how online and affiliation networks form, evolve, and shape the spread of information, products, emotions, opinions, and behavior. Core themes include influence, centrality, brokers and network stars; cascade growth and diffusion protocols; popularity and virality prediction; recommendation and network effects; cross-community mobility; expertise routing; and collaboration, citation, and scientific-literature discovery. It also examines malicious URLs, hateful communities, media bias and toxicity, crisis communication, humanitarian response, and online well-being.

Typical methods combine community detection, threshold and contagion models, cascade measurement, agent-based simulation, Hawkes processes, embeddings, topic and sentiment analysis, crowdsourcing, and large-scale empirical studies. Deep attention models predict popularity and virality; multimodal language-vision systems, geolocation, and visual analytics support disaster monitoring. Graph optimization uses matroid-constrained maximization, polling, and intervention design, while MCMC and higher-order edge switching generate constrained network benchmarks.

Recent trends emphasize multimodal, multilingual, and geospatial signals; emotion and sympathy in cascades; activity across multiple communities; privacy-compliant prediction; and workload-aware emergency alert ranking. Research increasingly studies interventions such as platform bans, campaign targeting, incentives, malicious-link containment, and network resilience, alongside richer analyses of fan, forum, academic, and scientific communities.

8ed59e80eb74bcd9b7d4ae29b716d1a23de9e8fe.text:
**Information Retrieval: Neural, Semantic, Personalized, and Interactive Search**

This community advances information retrieval through neural relevance modeling, semantic representations, and scalable search infrastructure. Core methods include lexical–neural hybrids, recurrent/convolutional interaction models, kernel pooling, pretrained embeddings, unsupervised neural vector spaces, sequence-to-sequence query expansion, entity-salience modeling, and semantic matching for documents, passages, tables, and scientific content. Knowledge bases support entity linking, disambiguation, structured queries, semantic layers, and knowledge-aware conversational response ranking.

Scalable retrieval emphasizes supervised and deep discrete hashing, approximate nearest-neighbor search, compact signatures, clustering, and efficient candidate generation. Ranking research increasingly models users and context through session features, long- and short-term preferences, personalized e-commerce and sponsored search, collaborative filtering, slate optimization, and conversational recommendation. Applications include biomedical and clinical retrieval, archived-document exploration, question answering, table retrieval/generation, and health surveillance from web-search signals.

Typical methods combine learning-to-rank, distant or weak supervision, pairwise and differentiable online learning, relevance feedback, ensemble models, and benchmark-based evaluation. Recent trends emphasize end-to-end neural retrieval, improved initial recall beyond keywords, explainable and visual search interfaces, robustness to adversarial manipulation, reproducibility and distributed evaluation, and user-sensitive metrics that incorporate credibility, interaction, and personalization.

6b18171245ecd07f61cc7e340d88745de157981a.text:
### Social Media, Political Influence, and Information Integrity

This community studies how online platforms shape public opinion, collective behavior, and trust. Major themes include elections and political orientation, ideological communities, polarization, echo chambers, misinformation, rumors, conspiracy narratives, censorship, media bias, emotional contagion, and collective action. It also examines adversarial and automated activity, including social bots, spam, coordinated influence campaigns, fake engagement, and manipulation of visibility. Applications extend to crisis response, public health, online abuse, and cross-platform information diffusion.

Typical methods combine large-scale Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, Twitch, Weibo, Gab, and 4chan data with network, propagation, temporal, and content analysis. Researchers use sparse learning, topic models, regression, supervised and semi-supervised classification, stance and sentiment detection, convolutional neural networks, lexical and behavioral bot features, crowdsourced labels, experiments, and measurement frameworks. Studies also infer voter preferences, evaluate feed personalization, quantify censorship and bias, and model fact-checking and crowd-based interventions.

Recent work emphasizes cross-platform influence operations, multimodal and crisis-related content, content-inherent bot detection, emotional and attention dynamics, and scalable countermeasures. Researchers increasingly assess both harmful manipulation and constructive interventions, including automated health messaging, rumor verification, fact checking, and public-information systems.

ab842e951d8140ed2d7c66c58e90c73874d02f9b.text:
### Scholarly Communication, Impact, and Discovery

This community studies how scholarly work is disseminated, discovered, evaluated, and reused. Major themes include altmetrics and societal impact; relationships among citations, readership, downloads, tweets, Facebook activity, and web attention; open access, preprints, repositories, and scholarly platforms; and bibliometrics for journals, publishers, books, and conferences. Research also addresses academic profile services, expert and collaborator discovery, paper retrieval, recommendation, reviewer assignment, venue evaluation, and the quality and visibility of papers, including effects of author prominence and title language.

Typical methods combine large bibliographic, usage, and social-media datasets from Web of Science, Scopus, Dimensions, arXiv, Mendeley, Twitter, Facebook, Altmetric, and academic platforms with correlation, regression, PCA/factor analysis, ranking, network, latent-space, and distributional analyses. Machine learning, text mining, sentiment analysis, web scraping, APIs, and cloud-based analytics support reference matching, search, classification, and recommendation. Case studies span physics, astronomy, biomedical research, computer science, and humanities.

Recent work emphasizes multi-channel, computer-mediated communication and rapid signals alongside delayed citations. It tests open-access effects, evaluates altmetrics against peer judgments, and examines platform uptake and data quality. Studies increasingly highlight heterogeneous attention mechanisms, URL/API and coverage limitations, automated sharing, author and title biases, and the need for contextualized evaluation.

9c225cb48a3075e376e6533fd0152960b9ae69c2.text:
## Online Social Networks: Diffusion, Influence, and Online Communities

This community studies how online social networks form, evolve, and shape the diffusion of information, products, opinions, emotions, and behavior. Major themes include influence, centrality, brokers and weak ties; information cascades, virality, novelty, and popularity; recommendation and network externalities; and competing-product adoption. It also examines signed relations, structural balance, antagonistic or allied communities, online forums and fan groups, cross-community mobility, expertise routing, and scientific collaboration networks. Misinformation, malicious URLs, hateful communities, media bias, toxicity, privacy, and network robustness remain important risk-oriented concerns.

Typical methods combine temporal and weighted-network analysis, community and pivot detection, diffusion and contagion models, agent-based simulation, game theory, influence maximization, embeddings, text and sentiment analysis, and large-scale empirical studies. Deep attention models, temporal predictors, crowdsourced labels, and content-based recommendation support prediction; latent-agent models address unobserved participants, while polling and data-quality audits improve measurement.

Recent directions emphasize platform-scale, multimodal and cross-community data; recency, ageing, affect, semantics, and diffusion protocols beyond topology; and interpretable prediction of popularity, virality, expertise, and network stars. Research increasingly evaluates interventions such as targeted incentives, privacy-compliant modeling, community bans, harmful-content containment, and cost-aware attacks on network structure.

2cf18e48f3d2daadbbde6888e77ad40c6b4db105.text:
## Scalable Learning and Analysis of Complex Networks

This community develops methods for representing, comparing, modeling, and mining large, dynamic, uncertain, heterogeneous, signed, and multilayer networks. Themes include temporal link prediction and robust embeddings; community detection, antagonistic/allied structure, cores, cycles, structural roles, and network alignment; graph similarity and distance; knowledge-graph discovery; anomaly, fraud, trust, and hidden-population analysis; diffusion through direct and indirect co-location; and recommendation using network side information.

Typical methods combine dynamic latent-space and stochastic models, matrix completion and robust PCA, maximum-likelihood inference for uncertain graphs, modularity and nonlinear spectral methods, random walks, non-backtracking cycles, mutual information, and graphlet-based analysis. Representation learning includes node2vec/struc2vec, core-aware and temporal embeddings, meta-path/metagraph-guided heterogeneous embeddings, content fusion, feature propagation, and semi-supervised learning. Scalable streaming, distributed, and approximate algorithms support triangle counting, crawling, alignment, and graph comparison, with attention to convergence and quality guarantees.

Recent trends emphasize continuous-time and temporally stable representations, size-agnostic change-point detection, noisy-network reconstruction, signed/multiplex interactions, higher-order motifs and cycles, and semantics- and user-guided analysis of heterogeneous information networks. Applications increasingly integrate text, scholarly and patent knowledge graphs, IoT trust, social-media manipulation, and explainable structural similarity.

77abc64339d2ea5f35eb85dd4f094a357e2476ab.text:
## Social Media and Spatial Networks as Societal Sensors

This community studies how user-generated, social, and location-aware data reveal political communities, public opinion, demographics, migration, health behaviors, urban activity, and consumer or facility needs. Political research now emphasizes community structure, alliances and antagonisms, credibility, media targeting, legislative influence, and extreme-right ecosystems across platforms, rather than only electoral prediction. Urban and geographic work detects bursty regions, resolves place names, reconstructs mobility and diaspora flows, measures socio-spatial exposure and affect near parks, and supports spatial search, route planning, and trajectory-aware facility placement. Other applications include vaccination and health messaging, IoT perceptions, food recommendation, and financial guarantee-network risk.

Typical methods include topic modeling and sentiment analysis; sparse learning, regression, and probabilistic inference for demographic attributes; network analysis, link prediction, structural-balance modeling, community detection, and centrality; nonnegative and structured matrix factorization for multiview and dynamic graphs; self-organizing maps, density-based spatial mining, and visual analytics. Data span Twitter, Facebook, YouTube, mobile apps, check-ins, reviews, and streaming geotagged objects.

Recent trends emphasize cross-platform and multimodal integration, fine-grained spatiotemporal sensing, temporal dynamics and bursts, uncertainty-aware geolocation and attribute inference, privacy-preserving publication, dataset persistence and bias auditing, and translating online signals into health, migration, and regulatory insights.

84f51f34136ee1e875efe648a1efbcb233b7cdab.text:
### Bibliometric Evaluation, Equity, and Research Efficiency

This community studies how research performance is measured and explained across national, institutional, departmental, and individual levels, with strong emphasis on Italy and comparative university systems. Themes include productivity, quality and impact, field normalization, rankings, VQR and other assessment exercises, citation-based indicators, and the trade-off between publication volume and research quality. Equity concerns include gender gaps in performance and rankings, recruitment and opportunistic behavior, seniority, and regional inequalities.

Research also examines collaboration and diversification, including multidisciplinary teams, international knowledge flows, beneficiaries of national research, co-authorship, academic rank, and the effects of collaboration on research breadth. Greek university departments and PhD programs provide additional comparative cases.

Typical methods include large-scale Web of Science and Google Scholar bibliometrics; h-index, i10-index, MNCS, and related indicators; field normalization; regression and quantile analysis; DEA and other efficiency models; network and collaboration analysis; citation-window sensitivity tests; ranking and agreement comparisons; and distributional and inequality measures.

Recent trends emphasize clearer conceptualizations of “impact,” cross-field comparability, gender-sensitive evaluation, uncertainty and timing effects in rankings, efficient resource allocation, and identifying gaming or unintended consequences of performance-based assessment.

e361a41177f15c2a0f2018c6b85f231e54157a13.text:
### Dynamic and Temporal Graph Analysis

This community studies how evolving networks are modeled, queried, and exploited. A core theme is temporal-network analysis: stream graphs, link streams, time-varying graphs, and temporal quantities capture interaction timing, duration, and ordering, enabling analyses of journeys, connectivity, density, communities, and centrality. Algebraic semirings support foremost and latency-aware paths, while temporal graphlets characterize structure beyond static snapshots.

Another theme is scalable graph querying through indexes and labeling schemes for reachability, bounded or \(k\)-hop reachability, shortest paths, and temporal paths in dynamic or distributed settings. Methods include interval, hierarchical, distribution-based, hub, independent-set, and lightweight dynamically maintained labels.

The community also examines diffusion and influence via contagion, opinion spreading, dynamic monopolies, gossip, trust-aware recommendation, and information mobilization. New applications analyze fine-grained contact streams in hospitals, classify interactions by node groups, and use link-stream features for temporally aware movie recommendation. Hybrid recommenders additionally combine collaborative and content-based filtering with sentiment from microblogs. Dynamical studies connect SIS contagion and scale-free networks to emergent algorithmic information.

Recent trends emphasize real-world sensor traces, temporal semantics in recommender systems and centrality, sentiment and content integration, and scalable exact analytics for continuously evolving networks.

591eaee800f6dc88c793b5e81a1ece9851dbaea4.text:
**Multilayer Social Networks, Identity Resolution, and Information Diffusion**

This community studies social networks as multiplex systems, where friendship, communication, physical proximity, mobility, and cross-platform activity jointly shape social structure. Major themes include multilayer centrality, homophily and assortative mating, user identity resolution, record linkage, place-focused social ties, mobility routines, influence propagation, epidemic spreading, and community evolution.

Community dynamics are modeled with GED, SGCI, dynamic Louvain, Infomap, classifiers, and historical transition chains to detect and forecast group changes. Information diffusion is analyzed across online and physical layers, including interacting contagions, dormancy, broadcast strategies, and the strategic behavior of senders and receivers.

Typical methods combine graph clustering and centrality, feature engineering and negative sampling for cross-device matching, temporal graph clustering for historical linkage, computational genealogical reconstruction, trajectory simulation, game-theoretic and evolutionary models, threshold and branching-process diffusion models, and empirical analysis of social, location, news, browsing, and population-record data.

Recent work emphasizes integrated social–physical modeling, scalable entity resolution and population reconstruction, realistic human-mobility generation, place-based explanations of ties, strategic and co-diffusion phenomena, and improved evaluation and data fusion for heterogeneous records.

987e4986bc7398dee4a7b3d08716bb897ba5f24d.text:
**Information Retrieval: Neural, Entity-Aware, and Structured Search**

**Main themes.** This community advances relevance modeling, semantic matching, and scalable search across text, images, tables, knowledge bases, and spatio-textual data. Neural ranking addresses vocabulary mismatch through dense representations, query–document interaction models, topical segmentation, entity salience, and sequence-to-sequence query expansion. Entity-centric access includes query decomposition, entity linking and consolidation, golden-record construction, knowledge-base table answers, entity-focused spreadsheets, and semantic table retrieval. Data integration also targets schema discovery, syntactic pattern extraction, similarity joins, set containment, and data-lake organization.

**Typical methods.** Systems combine lexical retrieval with neural or semantic features, knowledge bases, embeddings, kernels, and probabilistic models. Scalable retrieval uses inverted indexes, GPU parallelism, locality-sensitive hashing, partitioning, minimum-hash methods, and adaptive near-neighbor search. Ranking is learned from clicks, list-level feedback, pairwise differentiable losses, personalization and session features; bandit methods support online ranker comparison. Evaluation increasingly models image-search interaction and user behavior, while explainable search uses local, model-agnostic interpretations.

**Recent trends.** Research is moving beyond keyword relevance toward entity-, table-, and structure-aware search; real-time query understanding; personalized advertising and e-commerce retrieval; end-to-end neural initial retrieval; multimodal and specialized search; and scalable, interpretable online learning.

1b8fe2742d80f9f36d214a4fe455ce3673a51a98.text:
### Scholarly Communication, Metrics, and Discovery

This community studies how research is disseminated, discovered, evaluated, and reused across journals, repositories, preprint servers, academic profile platforms, and social media. Major themes include altmetrics and societal attention; relationships among citations, readership, downloads, tweets, Facebook activity, blogs, and news coverage; open-access publishing; and the validity of metrics as indicators of scholarly quality. Other work develops scholarly search, expert-finding, recommendation, and researcher-visibility systems, including organizational and social-network analysis.

Typical methods combine large bibliographic, usage, and social-media datasets from Web of Science, Scopus, Dimensions, arXiv, Mendeley, Twitter, Facebook, and academic platforms. Analyses use correlation, regression, ranking, distributional analysis, principal-component and factor analysis, sentiment analysis, and latent-space or network models. Machine learning, web crawling, scraping, API integration, text search, and visualization support document retrieval, URL matching, classification, and recommendation.

Recent work emphasizes heterogeneous, rapidly changing signals and their relationship to peer-assessed quality. It examines author prominence, title characteristics, document types, and national or disciplinary differences in online attention; compares gold open access with subscription publishing; and builds richer discovery portals. Persistent concerns include API restrictions, identifier and URL disambiguation, incomplete coverage, automated sharing, confounding, and the danger of treating visibility as impact.

256a2264331133b5a8f98a987f40ce45063dd16a.text:
## Network Dynamics, Influence, and Navigability

This community studies how network structure shapes opinions, beliefs, influence, information access, navigation, and robustness. Opinion dynamics extend DeGroot and Friedkin–Johnsen models to signed, antagonistic, homophilous, bounded-confidence, Bayesian, noisy, biased, and community-structured interactions. Recent work emphasizes nonlinear state-dependent biases, heterogeneous belief systems, and multiple logically interdependent topics, analyzing consensus, disagreement, polarization, stability, and quasi-consensus. Stochastic models examine clustering and randomness-driven transitions, while recommender systems are modeled as feedback loops in which personalized content changes—and responds to—user opinions.

A second theme concerns important nodes, links, and paths. Research develops axiomatic and generalized centrality measures, navigability scores, traffic-based backbones, criticality and disconnection metrics, and methods for optimizing PageRank, coverage, discoverability, tagging, delays, and navigation. Random-walk similarities also support network reconstruction and privacy-risk analysis. Path-based and randomized optimal-transport frameworks produce graph distances for clustering and classification.

Typical methods combine graph theory, Markov chains, random walks, consensus and dynamical-systems analysis, Laplacian and logic-matrix methods, nonlinear stability, Fokker–Planck analysis, optimization, information theory, simulation, and scalable distributed computation.

Recent trends include biased and multi-topic social dynamics, stochastic and fluid-limit analysis, recommender–opinion coevolution, privacy-aware graph inference, entropic path distances, and interventions for influence, resilience, and navigability.

4f06bdd225bad419522bb8c43b8c9fdaedc4bdc0.text:
**Multilayer Social Networks, Identity, and Diffusion**

This community studies social networks as multiplex, heterogeneous, and socially embedded systems, where friendship, communication, professional, semantic, physical, mobility, and cross-platform ties interact. Themes include multilayer centrality and community evolution; online/offline identity, homophily, and assortative mating; cross-device user matching and historical record linkage; place-based social organization; recommender systems; influence, news, and information cascades; epidemic spreading; and organizational or population-scale network discovery.

A major focus is dynamic diffusion across overlapping social and physical networks, including competing or synergistic contagions, dormancy, strategic broadcasting, evolutionary games, and seed or pioneer selection. Community dynamics are modeled with GED, SGCI, dynamic Louvain, Infomap, and transition forecasting. Related work reconstructs genealogical and temporal population networks and generates realistic spatio-temporal mobility routines.

Typical methods combine graph similarity and centrality, tensor decomposition, clustering, spectral and multiplex analysis, record-linkage and feature-engineering pipelines, game-theoretic and branching-process models, independent-cascade and threshold simulations, and synthetic network generation. Evaluation uses social-media, browsing, location, news, email, census, and genealogical data.

Recent trends emphasize identity resolution across fragmented data, integrated social–physical modeling, mobility-aware epidemic control, co-diffusion, anomaly detection in heterogeneous networks, and strategic or content-aware diffusion involving trust, sentiment, topics, and media synergies.

8348306f9111dd1f67ecee760e3d45adcac55002.text:
### Online Influence, Integrity, and Platform Governance

This community studies how social platforms organize users, shape opinions, and enable manipulation. Core themes include ideological and fringe communities, polarization and information bubbles, misinformation, rumors, conspiracy narratives, political influence, censorship, clickbait, online abuse, demographic inference, and fairness. A parallel focus concerns adversarial and coordinated actors: social bots, fake followers, spam, content polluters, fraudulent reviews, loosely synchronized campaigns, and state-sponsored influence operations.

Typical methods combine large-scale Twitter, Facebook, Gab, YouTube, Twitch, financial-microblog, marketplace, and review-platform data with network analysis, diffusion modeling, temporal and behavioral features, and supervised, semi-supervised, neural, and domain-adaptive classification. Researchers use content, social-context, and dynamic signals; embeddings and sequence models; network motifs and clustering coefficients; stance, rumor, and credibility analysis; measurement studies, experiments, user studies, and fairness metrics. Systems include Hoaxy, real-time spam and abuse detectors, social bots for targeted health interventions, and crowdsourced fact-checking workflows.

Recent work emphasizes fringe-to-mainstream information flows, cross-platform political campaigns, early rumor detection, censorship measurement, personalized ranking and recommender fairness, multimodal and camouflaged bots, and intervention-oriented responses. Growing attention also targets privacy-sensitive demographic prediction and scalable detection under partial observability.

2eafb6f13b043b5451b99f0ab31ed62bd48646e3.text:
### Scalable Graph Querying and Analytics

This community studies systems and foundations for querying, indexing, integrating, and benchmarking graph data, especially RDF, SPARQL, knowledge graphs, federated Linked Data, and large dynamic or temporal graphs. Core themes include SPARQL algebra and OPTIONAL processing, federated query planning and source selection, heterogeneous-RDF indexing, characteristic sets, graph-pattern matching, reachability and shortest-path queries, label-constrained and regular-path queries, provenance graphs, and graph-oriented window analytics.

Typical methods combine formal query semantics, complexity analysis, algebraic rewriting, heuristic and adaptive plan optimization, cardinality estimation, structural and interval labeling, reachability oracles, partitioning, summaries, embeddings, approximate query processing, and incremental or dynamic index maintenance. Distributed implementations use cloud and NoSQL infrastructures, MapReduce, and scalable RDF stores; mechanized verification and certified view maintenance provide correctness guarantees. Evaluation increasingly relies on configurable synthetic-data generators and diverse big-data and stream-processing benchmarks.

Recent trends emphasize scalable distributed and federated execution, runtime adaptation under limited statistics, dynamic and temporal graph analysis, efficient path and reachability evaluation, explainable approximate answers and query recommendations, provenance-aware navigation, and graph-native analytics. The community is also expanding toward graph windows, social-network diffusion and recommendation, and unified benchmarking across batch, streaming, RDF, and property-graph systems.

a60bf3a0d02462005621359bfd607fb155b1fe7b.text:
## Adaptive Data Management for Reliable Science

This community studies database systems that remain performant, dependable, and usable as data, workloads, and hardware scale. Core themes include multicore and distributed OLTP, high-contention execution, RDMA-era cross-partition transactions, scheduling, distributed transactions, MVCC, serializability, recovery, and latency predictability. Scientific data management spans astronomical event streams, geospatial and multidimensional data, arrays, archives, metadata, provenance, reproducibility, and socio-technical data discovery and reuse.

The community increasingly treats databases as platforms for heterogeneous and multimodal data, including images, video, learned representations, visual search, and interactive exploration. It also examines notebooks, digital archives, knowledge maps, blockchain-backed storage, and auditable data sharing as infrastructure for open science.

Typical methods combine new execution, storage, indexing, and query-processing architectures with empirical benchmarking and qualitative studies. Examples include contention-aware scheduling and partitioning, adaptive recovery, predictive transaction models, fine-grained snapshotting, shared-I/O batching, spatial indexes, visual data management systems, learned aggregate approximations, and cloud pipelines for low-latency scientific analysis. Deep reinforcement learning is emerging for join ordering, query optimization, and automatic database administration.

Recent trends emphasize adaptive, learned, and autonomic systems; real-time analysis of streaming scientific data; multimodal data management; energy and resource efficiency; and reliable, reproducible, accessible infrastructure for large-scale science.

d7e66ee7047a2dce43816e5f0e2a5ea3991766ee.text:
### Social Networks, Influence, and Information Integrity

This community studies how social platforms organize users, shape opinions, and enable manipulation. Major themes include political communities and elections, polarization and echo chambers, misinformation, rumors, conspiracy narratives, extremism, online abuse, censorship, demographic inequality, and health or lifestyle behavior. It also examines adversarial actors and commercial manipulation: bots, socialbots, spam, clickbait, fake followers, coordinated accounts, fraudulent reviews, and financial-market promotion.

Typical methods combine large-scale Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, Gab, Twitch, marketplace, and review-platform data with network analysis, statistical modeling, and machine learning. Researchers use topic models, sparse learning, regression, graph and clustering methods, propagation and interaction features, stance and rumor classification, neural language models, lexical and behavioral bot detection, demographic and socioeconomic inference, and cross-platform campaign analysis. Measurement studies assess API bias, censorship, ranking visibility, credibility, and fact-checking or crowd-flagging interventions. Systems include social bots for targeted public-health messaging, spam and abuse detectors, entity-centric news exploration, and defenses against coordinated fraud.

Recent work emphasizes political microtargeting and foreign influence, fringe-to-mainstream information flows, personalized feeds, cross-platform coordination, temporal and loosely synchronized behavior, content-inherent detection, and scalable interventions. Researchers also increasingly study platform data bias, information overload, and the health and social consequences of digitally mediated consumption.

6d0858e816e339aadd6e25f8a2a9a5ccf01eb38b.text:
## Social Influence and Trust in Online Marketplaces

This community studies how social networks shape online commerce, recommendation, information sharing, and collective behavior. Core themes include combining marketplace activity with social-network and geographic data to recommend products and categories; understanding how friends, ratings, trust, and social ties affect consumer choice; and modeling information diffusion, including triadic closure and rumor dissemination in integrated commerce-and-messaging environments.

A growing focus is trust-aware collaborative filtering. Explicit trust ratings and implicit social connections are used to address data sparsity and the cold-start problem, with regular equivalence helping identify structurally similar users when direct rating overlap is limited. Typical methods therefore include large-scale marketplace and social-graph analysis, empirical user studies, recommendation experiments, and computational models of diffusion involving desires, trust structures, homogeneity, and convergence.

System-oriented work develops deployable services, including secure and privacy-conscious community classifieds and scalable REST-based social recommendation engines. Recent directions emphasize heterogeneous behavioral, social, geographic, and trust signals; robust recommendations for new or sparsely active users; comparisons of social-influence mechanisms; and translation of behavioral insights into scalable marketplace and online-community infrastructures.

9bd3b511bf7c602e6637f51df5ad103c255e9092.text:
## Recommender Systems: Context-Aware, Multimodal, and Adaptive Personalization

This community studies personalized ranking under sparse, implicit, noisy, heterogeneous, and evolving behavior. Core themes include collaborative filtering; sequential, session-based, news, music, education, and location recommendation; social and semantic networks; cross-domain and cold-start transfer; long-tail discovery; and modeling diverse interactions, substitutes, complements, trust, and user interests.

Typical methods range from matrix factorization, Bayesian ranking, factorization machines, nearest neighbors, Markov models, and hybrid content–collaborative approaches to neural recommenders, autoencoders, attention, recurrent and spatio-temporal networks, reinforcement learning, and graph convolution. Representations increasingly combine text, images, audio, video, knowledge bases, tags, geographic context, and multiple user–item actions. Hyperbolic embeddings, outer-product interaction maps, Wasserstein objectives, binary parameterization, and meta-learning support expressive or efficient modeling.

Recent trends emphasize short- and long-term behavioral integration, anonymous and session recommendation, exploration–exploitation, push delivery, and adaptation to demand and changing interests. Research addresses missing modalities, multimodal robustness, reliable ratings, adversarial and shilling attacks, implicit trust, filter bubbles, and interpretable diversity. It also investigates algorithm selection, personalized search, real-time scalability, and multi-signal graph-based recommendation.

0a66ac9233a527dd0e726924439c55114cf08f36.text:
## Recommender Systems and Semantic Information Services

This community studies personalized ranking and information access under sparse, implicit, noisy, biased, and evolving behavior. Core themes include collaborative and graph-based recommendation; sequential, session-based, news, mobile, venue, academic, and advertising recommendation; trust, reputation, spam robustness, privacy, and secure personalization; group formation and satisfaction; cold-start learning; and relevance–diversity trade-offs. It also connects recommendation with scholarly knowledge services, semantic publishing, information extraction, and content indexing.

Typical methods include collaborative and learning-to-rank models, heterogeneous graphs, random walks, trust inference, contextual bandits, Markov decision processes, deep reinforcement learning, counterfactual/unbiased learning from clicks, active learning, and hybrid content–collaborative models. Content methods use text, reviews, tags, metadata, keyphrases, concepts, citation links, and linked open data. Keyphrase extraction combines lexical, statistical, semantic, graph-based, and neural techniques, while large-scale mining and recommendation use Hadoop-style distributed processing and recommendation APIs.

Recent trends emphasize adaptive interactive recommendation, multi-behavior and context-aware modeling, push services, anonymous and cold-start users, reliable evaluation, and scalable deployment. Privacy-preserving computation, selective disclosure, fairness against feedback bias, and robustness to fraudulent reviews are increasingly central, alongside semantic scholarly discovery and quality assessment.

039c8c71b349f48d731c276b644b51a4fc14f2b6.text:
## Inferring Human Traits and Health Attitudes from Social Media

This community studies how publicly observable social-media data can reveal latent user attributes and population health attitudes. Major themes include gender, age, personality, political identity, religion, race, intelligence, and other trait prediction, demographic enrichment of Twitter datasets, and sentiment analysis concerning vaccination and HIV-treatment side effects.

Typical methods combine linguistic, behavioral, and network signals. Language models applied to Facebook status updates predict as many as 20 human traits, including personality, gender, political identification, religion, race, life satisfaction, IQ, self-disclosure, fair-mindedness, and belief in astrology. A single interpretable model achieves strong results on established tasks while extending prediction to less studied attributes. Twitter studies use usernames, followers, tweet content, LIWC features, social connections, celebrities followed, and knowledge-graph resources such as Wikipedia and Freebase. Age inference emphasizes language-independent signals from accounts users follow.

A related health-oriented direction mines social media for public-health surveillance: vaccination sentiment is compared spatially and temporally with CDC vaccination-rate estimates, while HIV research identifies medication-side-effect reports and analyzes sentiment.

Recent trends move from heuristic, platform-specific inference toward interpretable language models integrating linguistic, behavioral, and relational evidence, with applications spanning individual trait profiling and population-level health monitoring.

2f2a20d2965c3e56b675104fb21abb3450576540.text:
## Recommender Systems: Context, Robustness, and Representation

**Main themes.** This community studies personalized ranking from sparse, implicit, noisy, and evolving behavior across e-commerce, news, music, education, advertising, and location services. Key concerns include sequential and session-based recommendation, cold-start and cross-domain transfer, social and heterogeneous item relationships, multimodal content, knowledge-aware recommendation, exploration–exploitation, and fairness. Trust, shilling attacks, adversarial robustness, and behavioral bias are increasingly important.

**Typical methods.** Matrix factorization, Bayesian and pairwise ranking, factorization machines, collective modeling, and hybrid content–collaborative systems remain foundational. Neural methods include nonlinear latent-factor models, autoencoders, recurrent and attention architectures, deep transfer learning, and reinforcement learning for interactive recommendation. Graph convolutional and embedding methods model social influence, multiple behaviors, knowledge bases, and heterogeneous relations; hyperbolic representations capture hierarchy. Multimodal models combine text, images, audio, video, and handle missing modalities through modality dropout. Efficient systems use binary embeddings and feature compression.

**Recent trends.** Research emphasizes long- and short-term preference integration, spatiotemporal context, anonymous sessions, multi-action feedback, push recommendations, and real-time scalability. New directions include fairness-aware objectives, robust multimedia representations, reliable rating and trust inference, algorithm selection via metalearning, and principled exploration in sequential services.

aab49ce3a1169ecbc284a31d0152107b762302a4.text:
## Social Media as a Sensor of Society, Space, and Politics

This community studies how social, mobile, and location-aware data reveal political preferences, public opinion, human mobility, migration, urban activity, health-related exposure, and consumer behavior. Election research measures polarization, agenda setting, candidate support, virality, and opinion trends, increasingly validating online signals against polls and fusing heterogeneous sources. Studies also examine activism, connective action, user inclusion, news-audience targeting, public perceptions of technologies, and social influence.

Urban and geographic work infers commuting, diaspora and migration flows, toponyms, functional regions, and socially meaningful geographies. Social media measures environmental exposure and affect, including responses to parks, as well as attitudes such as racism and homophobia. Location-based services support analyses of colocation, neighborhoods, and place characteristics.

Typical methods include sentiment, topic and hashtag analysis; supervised and unsupervised user-role classification; network analysis, community detection, diffusion modeling, contextual centrality, and polarization analysis; regression, machine learning, CNNs, self-organizing maps, probabilistic models, Kalman filtering, and event studies. Data include Twitter, Facebook advertising, mobile-phone records, GPS-enabled apps, news, and reviews.

Recent trends emphasize multimodal and heterogeneous signal fusion, real-time nowcasting, validation and representativeness, inclusive and selective sensing, unsupervised geolocation, hyperlocal social-environmental inference, and modeling how offline events, physical context, and network structure jointly shape behavior.

d274d2109f7101472c3395252e2e6a0cea59900c.text:
### Mobile and Online Data for Societal Monitoring

This community studies how passively generated mobile and online traces provide timely, fine-grained measures of socioeconomic conditions, labor-market dynamics, and collective behavior. Core themes include detecting unemployment, estimating employment status, measuring regional and national economic activity, tracking mass layoffs and other employment shocks, and anticipating dangerous crowd formation and public-safety events.

Typical inputs include call-detail records; financial, social, communication, and mobility indicators; and location-based search or map-query data. Methods range from constructing employment and economic-activity indices to machine-learning models validated against household surveys. For labor shocks, researchers use structural-break detection to identify timing and scale, Bayesian classification to identify affected individuals, and aggregate estimation to measure unemployment changes. For crowd risks, spatiotemporal analysis of map queries is used to detect gathering signals and generate early warnings before mass events.

Recent work moves beyond static aggregate indicators toward multi-scale, dynamic monitoring: identifying affected individuals, linking behavioral changes to local or national outcomes, forecasting collective gatherings, and observing socioeconomic or safety consequences across days, weeks, months, and years.

e5c0c747de020443c1360de8934922bd9478454b.text:
### Scalable Network Analytics and Graph Mining

This community develops computational methods for analyzing large, complex, uncertain, heterogeneous, and evolving networks, including social, information, semantic, software, affiliation, and knowledge graphs. Major themes include community and core discovery, attribute- and theme-aware subgraphs, link prediction, graph distances, network comparison, diffusion, anomaly detection, and structural measures such as triangles, trusses, cores, and expansion.

Typical methods combine topology with text, attributes, interaction history, and noisy observations. They include random walks and graph sampling, stochastic and maximum-likelihood inference, matrix completion, clustering and clustering-agreement measures, spectral reductions, non-backtracking analysis, dense-subgraph optimization, and compact document signatures or knowledge-base-based query expansion. Efficient implementations use streaming and distributed processing, external-memory trees, distance labels, sketches, and indexing structures.

Recent work emphasizes scalable analysis of graph streams and massive scale-free networks; uncertainty and measurement error in network structure; multilayer, two-mode, intersection, and indirect co-location graphs; and attribute-aware community search. Applications increasingly support social activity and team formation, revenue-aware recommendation, privacy and deanonymization studies, event detection, trust in the social Internet of Things, software quality analysis, and retrieval over large document collections.

467603209a54671e1f35504a6ac5ca164bdf229e.text:
**Information Retrieval: Neural Matching, Entities, and Scalable Search**

This community focuses on improving retrieval through semantic relevance modeling, entity-aware understanding, and efficient search infrastructure. Neural ranking methods learn fine-grained query–document interactions using embeddings, convolutional or recurrent architectures, kernel pooling, topical segmentation, and end-to-end learning. Recent work targets vocabulary mismatch, entity salience, query decomposition, phrase dependence, semantic query expansion, and personalized ad retrieval.

A parallel theme is structured information access. Systems retrieve and complete Web tables, answer keyword table queries, populate entity-focused spreadsheets, and compose knowledge-base answers from graph patterns. Entity resolution and consolidation, schema and pattern discovery, wrapper repair, and extraction from changing Web structures extend retrieval toward data integration and data quality.

Typical methods include inverted indexes, GPU acceleration, locality-sensitive hashing, semantic and supervised deep hashing, partition- and sketch-based similarity joins, set-containment and matching joins, and adaptive high-dimensional nearest-neighbor search. Learning from interaction is prominent through behavioral models for image search, list-level feedback, differentiable unbiased online learning-to-rank, and bandit-based ranker evaluation.

Recent trends emphasize scalable hybrid lexical–neural retrieval, richer entity and table representations, real-time and heterogeneous search, explainable ranking, weak or implicit supervision, and user-centered online optimization.

90e0bfe0673eaaa81414607ebcaa1d7577a7b85a.text:
**Information Retrieval: Neural, Entity-Aware, and Interactive Search**
