This community advances information retrieval through semantic matching, relevance modeling, and scalable search infrastructure. Neural ranking uses recurrent, convolutional, interaction-based, kernel, and sequence-to-sequence architectures, often combining lexical signals with dense embeddings, knowledge bases, and entity salience. Research addresses vocabulary mismatch through semantic similarity, word-mover-style distances, query expansion, query decomposition, phrase dependence, and entity-aware representations.

Structured information access is a growing focus: systems retrieve, complete, navigate, and generate tables from Web collections, knowledge graphs, and data lakes. Entity-centric assistance supports table population, column discovery, and knowledge-base pattern composition. Efficient retrieval methods include supervised deep hashing, locality-sensitive hashing, approximate nearest-neighbor search, and compact vector or set representations.

Typical methods include end-to-end and weakly supervised learning, pairwise and list-level online learning to rank, Bayesian optimization, distant supervision, interaction modeling, and user-behavior analysis for clicks and image search. Evaluation increasingly uses interleaving, dueling-bandit ranker selection, differentiable unbiased feedback, and robustness testing against adversarial document changes. Explainable search uses local, model-agnostic interpretations.

Recent trends emphasize neural first-stage retrieval, personalized and conversational search, entity- and table-centric answers, interactive evaluation, explainability, and domain applications such as biomedical retrieval and web-based health surveillance.

e3004a65f96b17f23f9634773c0a4af871d165c4.text:
## Educational Data Mining for Student Success

This community applies educational data mining and learning analytics to improve higher-education quality, student outcomes, and institutional decision-making, particularly in India. Core themes include predicting dropout and student performance, identifying high- and low-performing learners, analyzing academic achievement, improving classroom teaching, and converting institutional data into actionable knowledge. Studies examine course enrollment, attendance, teaching language, examination irregularities, and abnormal result values as potential indicators of student success or risk.

Typical methods involve knowledge discovery from educational databases, experimental dataset construction, comparative analysis, classification, and predictive modeling. Decision trees are prominent supervised-learning methods, using divide-and-conquer rules to explore data and predict student performance. Bayes classification is also applied to shortlist students at risk of dropping out or underperforming, distinguish learning groups, and identify consistently strong performers. Data mining further supports analysis of relationships between teaching language and attendance.

Recent work emphasizes the underuse of knowledge-discovery processes in educational institutions and promotes KDD tools for evidence-based decisions. The community also reflects growing convergence between educational data mining and learning analytics through integrated frameworks and models that make learning processes more visible, enable early risk identification, and guide targeted performance improvement.

fe3f622a02e1a5f470d0f243071a011e9ee73398.text:
### Preserving, Modeling, and Discovering Evolving Digital Knowledge

This community studies durable, interpretable, and discoverable digital information across repositories, archives, scholarly data, and social media. Core themes include rich semantic and compound-object modeling, persistent identification, provenance, versioning, rights, data citation, nanopublications, and preservation of evolving Linked Open Data. Web and newspaper archives remain central, with attention to temporal search, event collections, entity histories, exploratory scholarly access, and structured representations of historical people, places, and organizations. Social tagging, entity linking, and social-commerce recommendation extend the focus toward user-generated knowledge and personalized discovery.

Typical methods combine standards-based architectures and empirical evaluation. Systems use RDF, SPARQL, PROV-O, PAV, Open Annotation, Memento, and repository frameworks; prototypes expose semantic layers, linked software and publications, and versioned scientific data. Large-scale crawl, archive, citation, and social-media datasets—including RDF tweet corpora—support longitudinal analysis. Retrieval and recommendation employ lexical and semantic matching, link analysis, diversification, collaborative filtering, neural embeddings, deep learning, and cognitive models of frequency, recency, forgetting, and context.

Recent trends emphasize social and live-web signals, human-centered exploratory search, atomic provenance-rich scholarly claims, data metrics and citation practices, and richer ontology-based models of mechanisms, activities, and state change. Persistent challenges include heterogeneous schemas, incomplete archives, cold-start and long-tail entities, inconsistent data citation, and maintaining meaning as resources evolve.

42c79110f6b72400f68c37148c3f78cc89a90ce0.text:
**Deep Multimodal Learning for Music Understanding, Retrieval, and Recommendation**

This community studies semantic relationships across music modalities, including lyrics, audio, listener responses, and multimedia representations. Key themes include hierarchical attention for lyric-based genre classification, cross-modal retrieval through deep sequential correlation and shared canonical spaces, and transparent content-based recommendation using interpretable lyric and acoustic features.

Methods increasingly use end-to-end neural architectures, self-attention, temporally structured representations, shared latent spaces, and joint feature/hash-code optimization. Deep cross-modal hashing supports efficient similarity search, while explicit linear semantic projections learn discriminative cross-media representations in Hilbert space. Self-attentive models trained on large lyric and acoustic collections expose salient genre-related content, linking representation learning with explanations for retrieved recommendations.

A recent trend is broadening music semantics beyond audio-derived tags. EEG listener signals can regularize audio models in two-view neural networks, emphasizing perceived meaning, while attention-based lyric and acoustic models support user-facing interpretability. Overall, the research moves from modality-specific or manually engineered features toward learned, semantically aligned representations that serve classification, retrieval, recommendation, and explanation.

faa916cfc592373475b2d20a61115ecfd4fe7b75.text:
### Dynamic, Heterogeneous, and Robust Network Analytics

This community develops computational methods for understanding large, complex, uncertain, and evolving networks, including social, information, semantic, scholarly, multiplex, signed, and hypergraph systems. Core themes include node and graph representation learning, community detection and comparison, link and tie-strength prediction, anomaly and deception detection, network alignment, centrality, motifs, triangles, and core-aware analysis.

Typical methods combine topology with attributes, text, and temporal signals. They include random walks, Markov and latent-space models, stochastic blockmodels, Bayesian inference, matrix completion, spectral and modularity methods, graphlets, non-backtracking distances, and neural or feature-propagation embeddings. Heterogeneous-network approaches use meta-paths, metagraphs, motifs, semantic transcription, and user guidance; content-aware models jointly learn structure and node text. Distributed streaming and sampling algorithms support triangle counting and large-scale inference.

Recent work emphasizes temporal robustness, smooth and continuous-time embeddings, dynamic latent positions, evolving text networks, and scalable prediction. It also broadens network modeling to uncertain, signed, multiplex, hypergraph, and indirectly co-located interactions, with attention to partial balance, trust, and negative links. Applications include scholarly knowledge discovery, patent analysis, multilingual information recommendation, social-media communities, online deception, account detection, and diffusion modeling.

ddb19d12d007681eaf937bb3068d4aa40b879889.text:
### Dynamic, Heterogeneous, and Robust Network Analytics

This community develops computational methods for understanding large, complex, and evolving networks, including social, information, citation, semantic, knowledge, multiplex, signed, uncertain, and hypergraph data. Core themes include node and graph representation learning, community detection, link prediction, similarity and alignment, diffusion, anomaly detection, centrality, and structural comparison.

Typical methods combine topology with attributes, text, and interaction semantics. They include random walks, non-backtracking and cycle-based methods, stochastic blockmodels, latent-space and latent-feature models, nonlinear modularity, robust PCA and matrix completion, mutual-information analysis, meta-path and metagraph-guided embeddings, feature propagation, and semi-supervised learning. Graph comparison uses spectral, topological, and graphlet-based distances; hypergraph extensions support multiway interactions.

Scalability remains central, with distributed streaming and sampling algorithms for triangle counting, approximate structural statistics, and efficient dynamic embedding. Recent work increasingly addresses temporal smoothness and offset-aware representations, continuous network evolution, noisy and probabilistic edges, signed and multilayer interactions, higher-order structure, and online updates. Heterogeneous-network models now integrate rich semantics, user guidance, and node content. Applications include scholarly knowledge discovery and citation diffusion, patent-growth analysis, cross-language knowledge recommendation, trust in social IoT, and detection of coordinated or multiple-account behavior.

79a54725ae108fffb4c5eb88f682592906a2ac55.text:
## Scalable Data Management and Intelligent Query Processing

This community studies efficient, scalable data-intensive systems, with emphasis on relational query optimization, cardinality and resource estimation, join ordering, worst-case-optimal and incremental query processing, and enumeration over structured or semi-structured data. It also addresses distributed and hybrid analytics, streaming graphs, data enrichment, and machine-learning workloads.

Typical methods combine formal complexity, communication, and space–time analyses with practical systems techniques: sampling and sketches, deep-learning cardinality and cost models, reinforcement learning, learned indexes, MILP and System-R-style optimization, factorized and worst-case-optimal joins, adaptive logging, parallel recovery, and memory-, I/O-, network-, and energy-aware execution. Declarative abstractions include SQL, functional query languages, Datalog-like processing, document spanners, and query operators for incomplete or untagged data.

A major theme is intelligent automation: learned query optimization, holistic cloud workload management, adaptive resource provisioning, progressive/pay-as-you-go enrichment, and interactive aggregate-answer exploration. Transactional systems remain important, particularly multicore and distributed OLTP, high-contention execution, MVCC conflict repair, snapshot isolation, replication, and RDMA-era partitioning. Recent trends include main-memory and hybrid DBMSs, cloud performance guarantees, reproducible numerical aggregation, evolving-stream model management, streaming subgraph search, and scalable information extraction.

b599e6c2cbdb0517e500dca64ca4ad4d37ab7139.text:
## Verifying Relational Data-Aware Processes and Artifact Systems

This community studies formal modeling and verification of systems where process behavior and relational data are equally central. Key themes include data-aware business workflows, artifact-centric processes, relational data-centric dynamic systems, database-process integration, and the completeness and quality of information produced by processes. Models represent database updates, artifact lifecycles, task hierarchies, concurrency, and interactions with external services that may introduce fresh data and infinite-state behavior.

Typical methods combine formal process models with database semantics. Foundations include **db-nets**, which extend colored Petri nets with relational databases, and approaches that add dynamics directly to existing relational databases rather than relying on ad-hoc data abstractions. Other work connects artifact-centric models to UML-based methodologies. Verification targets temporal and logical properties, including LTL-FO and first-order μ-calculus variants, as well as query completeness and data-quality conditions. Theoretical studies establish decidability and complexity results for hierarchical and GSM-inspired artifact systems.

A recent trend is toward integrated, practically usable modeling: unifying master data, relational databases, and business-process dynamics, while developing automated tools such as **SPINArt** and **VERIFAS** for verification.

0074af2fa4b7f29e87260ea837ede6cc502d0f41.text:
## Social Media Sensing for Crisis, Place, and Society

This community studies how user-generated, location-aware, and mobile data reveal social processes, geographic activity, and public experience. A major emerging theme is crisis informatics: detecting disaster-related posts, extracting locations, identifying social actions, tracking event evolution, summarizing situational information, ranking alerts under responder workload constraints, and forecasting civil unrest. Multimodal Twitter data, including imagery, support humanitarian mapping and damage assessment.

Urban and geographic research examines mobility and commuting, migrant and diaspora flows, geographic focus of documents, exposure to parks and social attitudes, and qualitative place characteristics. Social media also serves as a sensor of public perceptions of technologies, news-audience targeting, censorship, responsibility, cyberbullying, and social influence.

Typical methods include natural-language processing, toponym resolution, geolocation, topic and event modeling, sentiment and multimodal classification, distant and weak supervision, unsupervised learning, regression, clustering, network analysis, centrality, and scalable stream processing. Systems combine Twitter, Facebook, mobile-app and cell-phone data with news, blogs, satellite imagery, and other open indicators.

Recent trends emphasize real-time, actionable crisis intelligence; multimodal and cross-platform sensing; forecasting with interpretable precursors; workload-aware alert prioritization; fine-grained geographic inference despite sparse or noisy coordinates; and demographic, cultural, and spatially heterogeneous analysis. Attention also increasingly focuses on credibility, user types, bias, and representativeness.

a9b50f13ad9bffba87379e4d42843ac2dd1df14e.text:
### Graph Querying, Federation, and Graph Analytics

This community studies systems and foundations for querying, integrating, validating, and analyzing graph data, including RDF, SPARQL, knowledge graphs, XML, ontologies, and property graphs. Core themes include SPARQL algebra and OPTIONAL processing, federated and Web-source querying, query recommendation and contextualization, graph pattern matching, reachability, navigational queries, ontology exploration, and incremental view maintenance. Work also addresses heterogeneous RDF indexing, incomplete or inconsistent data, data marketplaces, and locality-aware multi-query processing.

Typical methods combine formal semantics, complexity analysis, Datalog and regular Datalog, chase-style reasoning, algebraic and heuristic query reordering, embeddings and edit-distance ranking, graph summaries, characteristic-set indexes, discrimination networks, and certified implementations using proof assistants. Empirical studies and benchmarks rely on realistic synthetic graph generators, including scalable social-graph and customizable property-graph generators, as well as large XML/schema corpora.

Recent trends emphasize adaptive federated optimization with limited remote statistics; approximate, explainable, and recommendation-oriented querying; certified and incremental graph computation; scalable generation and benchmarking of realistic graphs; support for label-constrained navigation and multi-query locality; and practical knowledge discovery over large biomedical ontologies and heterogeneous Web data.

9b8672f974c959d95b6d95dda673372907ceb418.text:
## Topic Modeling and Social-Media Event Intelligence

This community combines probabilistic and neural text modeling with large-scale analysis of social, spatial, temporal, and scientific data. Major themes include latent and evolving topic discovery in scholarly, bibliographic, review, hypertext, and social-media collections; modeling topic emergence, popularity, influence, and creator expertise; and extracting aspects, opinions, events, and multilingual timelines. Recent work applies literature-mining and knowledge-network methods to automated hypothesis generation, candidate ranking, creative cross-domain discovery, and systematic validation of scientific insights.

Social media is treated as a real-time sensor for sports, disasters, protests, disease, tourism, public anxiety, mood, misinformation, and environmental events. Related studies infer user interests, support recommendation and decision-making, predict population-level outcomes using user-level aggregation, and optimize location-aware routes and points-of-interest selections.

Typical methods include LDA and dynamic, hierarchical, nonparametric, relational, and joint extensions; coupled matrix–tensor factorization; knowledge graphs; neural and character-based embeddings; active learning; clustering (including density-based spatiotextual variants), fuzzy logic, submodular optimization, burst and anomaly detection, ranking, and extractive summarization. Systems emphasize scalable, streaming, geospatial, cross-lingual, and visual analytics.

Recent trends include validated AI-assisted discovery, multimodal and cross-source integration, real-time event intelligence, personalized recommendation, and operational support for science, public health, emergencies, and mobility.

7b8151a7ea8cf41a73bc35530060e991535328b1.text:
## Network Influence, Opinion Dynamics, and Structural Optimization

This community studies how network structure shapes information diffusion, opinions, influence, navigability, and robustness. Core themes include consensus, polarization, controversy, echo chambers, homophily, signed interactions, stubborn or biased agents, and evolving social power. It also examines competing-product diffusion, coexistence, adoption games, rating systems, influence resistance, and interventions that balance exposure or reduce manipulation. Recommendation systems are treated as feedback mechanisms linking personalized content, user opinions, market outcomes, and social ties; causal effects of recommendations are estimated from observational data.

Structural topics include centrality and navigability, link prediction, discoverability, communicability, PageRank, effective resistance, backbone extraction, and privacy risks from network-similarity leakage. Applications emphasize social media, political discourse, news, online markets, and communication networks.

Typical methods combine graph theory, nonlinear and continuous-time dynamical systems, control and stability analysis, Markov chains, random walks, spectral and resistance-based measures, optimal transport, game theory, equilibrium and complexity analysis, optimization, approximation algorithms, Bayesian semantics, and causal inference. Empirical work uses large Twitter, Facebook, news, and other online-network datasets, incorporating temporal, topical, ideological, and stance-aware signals.

Recent trends include multi-topic logically interdependent beliefs, stochastic and fluid opinion models, scalable graph computation, privacy-preserving influence mechanisms, stance summarization, and network interventions involving edge changes, exposure design, and recommender feedback loops.

6b4c4e2c79aec7fddcb5166c2df745f8580e8d65.text:
## Scalable, Temporal, and Applied Network Analysis

This community develops scalable methods for querying, modeling, and exploiting large, evolving networks. Core topics include indexed graph querying—reachability, bounded and regular reachability, shortest paths, single-source and \(k\)-hop queries—using labeling schemes, interval and hop-doubling indexes, landmark sketches, hubs, independent-set labels, distributed algorithms, and lightweight fully dynamic structures such as DAGGER.

A second focus is temporal-network analysis. Time-varying graphs and link streams represent contacts and interactions without losing event timing, supporting temporal paths, connectivity, density, communities, centrality, and generalized betweenness through algebraic and semiring methods. Temporal indexes enable efficient time-aware reachability and path queries. Recent empirical work analyzes fine-grained contact dynamics in hospital populations and develops group-aware link-stream analysis.

The community also studies diffusion, influence, and emergent information, including dynamic monopolies, opinion and contagion spreading, media and gossip, and algorithmic complexity arising in scale-free SIS-like populations. Applications increasingly connect dynamic graph structure to recommendation: temporal link-stream features improve movie-rating prediction, while hybrid recommenders combine collaborative and content-based filtering with sentiment from microblog data.

Recent trends favor native temporal representations over static aggregation, distributed and dynamic processing, theoretically justified indexing and pruning, and network-aware, sentiment-aware prediction.

adc02f3e3f4617cac3c7ab33b88d418b1da8625b.text:
### Graph Querying, Management, and Dynamic Graph Analytics

This community studies systems and foundations for querying, integrating, indexing, and analyzing graph-structured data, particularly RDF, SPARQL, knowledge graphs, federated Web data, and property graphs. Core themes include SPARQL optimization and federation, heterogeneous RDF indexing, graph-pattern and tree-pattern queries, regular and label-constrained path queries, reachability, shortest paths, and temporal or dynamic graph analysis. Work also addresses provenance and workflow graphs, graph view maintenance, knowledge-graph contextualization and recommendation, graph diffusion, and window analytics.

Typical methods combine formal semantics, complexity analysis, Datalog and chase-style reasoning, algebraic rewritings, query-plan optimization, characteristic sets, partitioning, summaries, labeling schemes, distance sketches, and incremental or dynamic indexes. Distributed implementations use MapReduce, HBase, cloud clusters, and federated endpoints; approximate and embedding-based techniques support scalable or incomplete-query answering. Mechanical certification, including Coq-verified evaluation and view maintenance, provides correctness guarantees. Empirical studies use large real-world graphs and synthetic generators such as Darwini and DataSynth.

Recent trends emphasize adaptive federated execution with limited statistics, scalable processing of massive and evolving graphs, temporal and provenance-aware reachability, explainable approximate answers, user-oriented query recommendation and contextualization, and convergence between RDF, relational, and property-graph analytics.

2cbbc112aee805ccc23c324d6a87e1f01ffd9ea6.text:
## Scientometrics, Scholarly Networks, and Fair Research Evaluation

This community measures, maps, and critiques science, technology, and scholarly communication. Core themes include citation-based indicators for papers, authors, journals, institutions, and countries; field and time normalization; interdisciplinarity; research assessment and rankings; and the validity, fairness, and unintended consequences of metrics such as impact factors and h-indexes. Network studies map fields, collaborations, knowledge flows, research fronts, and technological development through citation, co-citation, publication, patent, journal, and citation-context networks.

Typical methods combine Web of Science, Scopus, Microsoft Academic, Dimensions, PubMed, Chinese databases, Mendeley, Twitter, and patent data with graph analysis, community detection, PageRank-like centrality, clustering, entropy statistics, text and citation-context mining, RPYS/patent spectroscopy, visualization, and entity resolution. Fractional counting, percentile indicators, author-contribution measures, field normalization, and machine-learning models address skewed distributions, unequal credit, and citation prediction. NoSQL and interactive systems support large-scale exploration and recommendation evaluation.

Recent trends emphasize database concordance and coverage bias, multimodal and context-aware impact assessment, scholarly recommender systems, deep-learning citation prediction, author disambiguation, uncertainty-language mining, and gender or peer-review bias analysis. The community increasingly links bibliometric evaluation with research quality, historical reconstruction, innovation, and responsible assessment.

7832c850edbf32319f8cb396d0eb61e6c43e37d5.text:
### Preserving, Enriching, and Searching Evolving Digital Knowledge

This community studies durable, interpretable, and discoverable digital information across scientific, cultural, social-media, and web contexts. Core themes include repository and digital-object architectures, persistent identifiers, provenance, versioning, rights, data and software citation, RDF-based semantic layers, and preservation of evolving web and social-media archives. A growing focus is temporal exploration: finding, ranking, diversifying, and analyzing archived documents, entities, events, and historical search results.

Typical methods combine standards-based system design with empirical evaluation. Approaches use OAIS, Fedora, aDORe, MPEG-21, OAI-PMH, RDF, SPARQL, PROV-O, PAV, nanopublications, Memento, and linked-data models. Prototypes support semantic archive layers, scholarly exploratory search, joint software–publication discovery, and reproducible dataset extraction. Large-scale crawl, archive, news, citation, and social-media analyses measure persistence, retrievability, popularity, sentiment, citation, and change. Machine learning supports domain classification, entity linking, popularity prediction, and event-focused crawling; lexical, temporal, link, and diversity-based ranking support retrieval.

Recent trends emphasize publishing massive annotated social-media corpora as RDF, entity-centric temporal analysis, scholar-oriented archive search, data metrics and citation reproducibility, and integrating live-web and archived signals. Persistent challenges include heterogeneous schemas, incomplete archives, unstable search results, long-tail entities, and preserving context and meaning as resources evolve.

ae81a029abb728b9dfe262da0babc56384c3543a.text:
## Uncertainty, Data Quality, and Explainable Integration

This community extends database systems to noisy, incomplete, conflicting, and human-generated data. Core themes include probabilistic query answering and aggregation, unknown-data impact, data fusion and truth discovery, source dependence and copying, entity resolution, record linkage, and canonical entity consolidation. Work also studies causes, responsibility, causal effects, provenance, and explanations for query answers and non-answers.

Typical methods combine probabilistic and hybrid source models, possible-world reasoning, structural decompositions, knowledge compilation, provenance-aware query optimization, and approximate inference. Integration methods include blocking with locality-sensitive hashing, embeddings and deep learning, graph and collective matching, string-transformation learning, matching dependencies, and optimization under one-to-one constraints. Integrity-constraint discovery and enforcement covers functional and order dependencies, ontology dependencies, and target constraints in data exchange. Chase-based reasoning and acyclicity analysis support tractable ontology query answering.

A growing focus is human–machine data management: crowdsourced entity resolution, truth assessment, labeling, route selection, and RDF query completion, with worker-error models, confidence guarantees, adaptive task assignment, and latency-aware orchestration. Recent trends emphasize scalable, automated data cleaning and integration; multiple-truth and correlation-aware models; quality guarantees with minimal human cost; deep representation learning; and systems that combine machine computation, crowds, provenance, and interactive explanations for open-web and knowledge-graph data.

1cfe4949e9e12550fff0503bc583a1c02fd2d5da.text:
### Preserving, Modeling, and Exploring Evolving Digital Knowledge

This community studies durable, interpretable, and discoverable information across scientific, cultural, social-media, and web contexts. Core themes include digital repositories and direct/compound-object representations; semantic modeling of entities, activities, infrastructures, mechanisms, and state changes; persistent identification, provenance, versioning, rights, and reproducible data citation; and preservation and exploration of evolving web, news, and social archives. Increasing attention is given to linking publications with software and datasets, nanopublications, historical directories, and large RDF corpora such as TweetsKB.

Typical methods combine OAIS, Fedora, aDORe, MPEG-21, OAI-PMH, OpenURL, RDF/RDFS, SPARQL, PROV-O, PAV, nanopublication, and annotation models with ontology and object-oriented design. Prototypes and interactive interfaces support semantic archive layers, structured queries, exploratory and time-aware search, aspect-time diversification, scholar-oriented corpus creation, and human-assisted entity linking. Large-scale crawl, log, news, citation, and social-media analyses measure persistence, retrievability, popularity, sentiment, citation, and temporal change; supervised learning supports domain classification and popularity prediction.

Recent trends emphasize event-focused archiving, archive-collection curation, temporal entity analytics, social and live-web signals, dataset extraction traceability, software/data metrics, and richer provenance. Persistent challenges include heterogeneous schemas, incomplete archives, unstable search results, long-tail entities, inconsistent citation practices, and preserving meaning across versions.

a6bf114886084769153b1927d5b58e3c9d8bab00.text:
**Community Detection in Complex and Evolving Networks**

This community studies how to discover, interpret, and evaluate cohesive or dynamically related groups in large, heterogeneous networks. Themes include overlapping, multilayer/multiplex, weighted, signed, attributed, two-mode, hierarchical, core–periphery, and temporal communities, as well as communities inferred from graph signals and network dynamics. Applications span social media, bibliometrics, recommendation, cybersecurity, political voting, biological networks, and large-scale graph mining. Increasing attention is given to influential nodes, global bridges, and communities aligned with diffusion, consensus, or other dynamical processes.

Typical methods include modularity and likelihood optimization, label propagation, clique and subgraph discovery, spectral clustering, manifold learning, core/truss decomposition, personalized PageRank and diffusion, Markov Stability, vector partitioning, and graph-filter methods. Probabilistic approaches now include generative local models, latent heterogeneous multilayer models, variational Bayes, mean-field analysis, and detectability theory. Multi-objective and Pareto optimization, signed edge weighting, causal inference, and distributed incremental algorithms support richer settings.

A major strand addresses evaluation through multi-criteria quality assessment, comparative benchmarking, hierarchical reconstruction, sampling, uncertainty-aware data fusion, and alternatives to NMI. Recent trends favor scalable local and seed-based discovery, distributed detection on dynamic graphs, multiscale and dynamical interpretations, and joint integration of topology, attributes, interaction types, temporal information, and signal or behavioral data.

6daa2d8e627bfb3522559d5b237401469e0cdbf4.text:
## Scholarly Networks, Identity, and Information Discovery

This community studies scholarly communication and information retrieval through bibliographic, textual, and social data. Core themes include author-name disambiguation and entity resolution; coauthorship, citation, and collaboration structures; publication recommendation and expert search; citation and text reuse, plagiarism, and scientific writing; and researchers’ information-seeking behavior. It also examines digital libraries, preprint repositories, research-data archives, and the infrastructures that support sharing, reuse, preservation, and reproducibility.

Typical methods combine coauthorship and citation-network analysis, bibliometrics, metadata and full-text mining, keyword and semantic relationship modeling, rank aggregation, graph-based recommendation, and interactive visualization. Identity resolution uses labeled data, semi-supervised and deep learning, blocking and deduplication, feature analysis, and evaluation against multiple benchmarks. Retrieval research uses session logs, contextual browsing, search-stratagem analysis, user studies, relevance judgments, and task-oriented evaluation. Text reuse and extraction employ pairwise similarity, heuristic detection, OCR, rule-based and statistical parsing, while qualitative studies use interviews, ethnography, and document analysis.

Recent trends emphasize scalable, open, and reproducible scholarly workflows; Jupyter-based research and durable data infrastructures; visual maps for browsing collections; multilingual and domain-specific discovery; socio-technical data search; and machine-learning approaches to disambiguation, recommendation, and large-scale corpus analysis.

4d34655d7fcc3c89896eb1b3ad7ac4567922dcd3.text:
## Scalable Data Management, Query Processing, and Analytics

This community studies how to make data-intensive systems faster, more scalable, adaptive, and easier to use. Core themes include relational query optimization—join ordering, cardinality estimation, worst-case-optimal joins, incremental maintenance, inequalities, and RDF/SPARQL processing—alongside distributed query evaluation, cross-platform data movement, shared execution, and SQL-on-Hadoop analytics. Graph and spatial analytics include streaming subgraph search, interactive visualization and mining, and shared path-query processing.

Typical methods combine formal complexity, communication, and space–time analyses with practical systems techniques: MILP and reinforcement-learning optimization, deep learned cardinalities and indexes, worst-case-optimal and leapfrog-triejoin algorithms, adaptive and temporally biased sampling, sketches, histograms, typed linear algebra, materialized views, and I/O-, network-, and cost-aware execution. Declarative abstractions support machine learning, information extraction, incomplete data, progressive enrichment, and constant-delay enumeration.

Operational work addresses replicated and distributed databases, predictive transaction execution, contention-aware partitioning, bounded staleness, cloud cost control, and fast RDMA networks. Recent trends emphasize database–machine-learning integration—from SGD and model management to automated administration and validation—as well as reproducible aggregation, neural data cubes, interactive insight exploration, and scalable analytics over streaming, multimodal, and increasingly heterogeneous data platforms.

5920ac0b60658b74441f54e6fdf95b8647dfa3ef.text:
### Social Network Dynamics, Diffusion, and Risk

This community studies how online, organizational, and scientific networks form, evolve, and shape behavior. Themes include information and emotion cascades, misinformation and malicious-URL diffusion, influence and popularity, complex contagions, community structure, multiplex interaction, recommendation, knowledge markets, collective polling, collaboration diversity, and systemic risk. Applications span social media, online forums, disaster response, scientific collaboration, marketing, fashion, sports fandom, and emergency operations.

Typical methods combine graph-theoretic analysis—centrality, assortativity, modularity, rich-club structure, homophily, temporal paths, and cascade topology—with statistical, econometric, agent-based, and machine-learning models. Researchers use Hawkes processes for multiplex diffusion, neural and attention models for microscopic cascades and popularity, stochastic optimal control for engagement steering, threshold and game-theoretic models for contagion and network effects, and optimization for influence, polling, routing, and alert ranking. Other approaches include multimodal text-image analysis, temporal cascade reconstruction, content and propagation features, and large-scale empirical studies.

Recent work emphasizes diffusion on evolving, multiplex, and partially observed networks; heterogeneous users, latent agents, and complex diffusion protocols; and interventions constrained by attention, workload, cost, or governance. Multimodal crisis intelligence, emotion dynamics, concept drift, cross-community mobility, and diversity’s effects on scientific impact are growing priorities, alongside interpretable prediction and practical network control.

ab1f5dd068acfac5ef8687289c3f99c2d26bc130.text:
## Scalable Data Management, Querying, and Analytics

This community develops scalable, intelligent data systems for relational, graph, streaming, and semi-structured data. Core themes include query optimization and cardinality estimation, join ordering, worst-case-optimal and incremental algorithms, enumeration with low delay, RDF/SPARQL-style processing, and interactive graph mining and visualization. Increasing attention targets analytical and machine-learning workloads, including query-driven model training, data enrichment, validation slicing, and reproducible numerical aggregation.

Typical methods combine formal complexity, communication, and update-time analyses with practical systems techniques: sampling, sketches, histograms, factorized and incremental view maintenance, adaptive and learned indexes, deep learning and reinforcement learning for estimation and optimization, typed linear algebra, declarative extraction languages, and I/O-, network-, and hardware-aware execution. Systems span MapReduce, SQL-on-Hadoop, multicore and GPU platforms, RDMA clusters, and in-memory databases.

Operational research emphasizes scalable OLTP under contention, distributed transactions, concurrency control, replication, adaptive and parallel recovery, and synchronization design. Streaming and evolving data motivate time-biased sampling, continuous subgraph search, and distributed quantile estimation. Recent trends favor pay-as-you-go enrichment, interactive summarization and visualization, automatic database administration, learned components, and unified database–deep-learning architectures.

597e406302f44b2c4251389eb76f49dd2bf23706.text:
### Data-Centric Learning, Search, and Scalable Analytics

This community integrates three themes. First, it develops text mining, classification, and information retrieval using probabilistic models, topic modeling, clustering, k-nearest neighbors, association rules, feature selection, dependency pruning, hyperonymization, and active learning. Recent work improves high-recall review through sentence-level relevance feedback and estimates document-level quality for automatic subject indexing.

Second, it advances mathematical information services. Research covers text-and-formula retrieval, presentation- and content-based search, formula repositories, semantic conversion using textual context, accessible MathML, and math-aware question answering that links natural-language questions to computable Wikidata formulas. Systems such as MIaS combine full-text retrieval with formula preprocessing.

Third, it studies scalable data systems and their foundations, including D4M/Accumulo ingestion (now extended to Julia), provenance management for microservices, Graphulo- and GraphBLAS-style processing, external-memory analytics, associative arrays, tensors and polystores, relational semantics, and cross-platform execution.

Typical methods include deep learning for cardinality estimation and quality prediction, probabilistic learning, feedback control, matrix/tensor operations, graph transformations, algebraic modeling, caching, shared query execution, progressive evaluation over uncertain enrichment, benchmarking, and cost-aware optimization. Recent trends emphasize cloud-cost reduction, multi-query optimization, heterogeneous platform selection, uncertain data processing, semantic mathematical QA, and integrated, provenance-aware analytics.

0e3558d7e74df642619ed6b6e1b847b021ed9e45.text:
**Semantic Search, Knowledge Graphs, and Social Information Retrieval**

This community focuses on organizing, linking, and searching heterogeneous knowledge sources, especially RDF graphs, ontologies, Wiktionary, Wikipedia, and collaborative tagging systems. Major themes include semantic interoperability, multilingual ontology matching, thesaurus and classification construction, entity resolution, synonym and related-term search, and transforming semi-structured resources into machine-readable relational or graph formats.

A second theme is efficient graph and web search: RDF subgraph pattern matching, partition- and summary-graph query processing, learned query planning, semantic navigation, query expansion, and third-party reranking of opaque web databases. Social search and collective intelligence are also prominent, including expertise location, influential-node detection, collaborative product and tag analysis, and modeling attention, vocabulary growth, and user behavior in online communities.

Typical methods combine NLP, graph algorithms, ontology and schema modeling, statistical scaling analyses, clustering, link analysis (including HITS and PageRank-like measures), learned ranking, and empirical evaluation on large social or knowledge-graph datasets.

Recent trends emphasize learning-assisted graph query optimization, fairness-aware ranking and recommendation, multilingual and versioned semantic resources, explainable semantic exploration, and analysis of decentralized, socially produced knowledge.

07f522f0cd44a5fee6d6fc374fd8bf5898fa2b97.text:
## Network Dynamics, Opinions, and Structural Analysis

This community studies how network structure governs information flow, opinions, polarization, controversy, and robustness. Major themes include consensus and disagreement, bounded-confidence and Friedkin–Johnsen dynamics, homophily, signed interactions, stubbornness, heterogeneous biases, and logically interdependent multi-topic belief systems. It also examines echo chambers, partisan discourse, stance summarization, and diversity or balance of information exposure, alongside centrality, navigability, link inference, communicability, privacy risks, and graph distances.

Typical methods combine graph theory, dynamical-systems and control analysis, Markov chains, Laplacian and spectral techniques, random walks, matrix-based centralities, optimization, approximation algorithms, and stochastic or mean-field/Fokker–Planck analysis. Empirical work analyzes Twitter, Facebook, news, and other online communication data using temporal, topical, stance, sharing, and exposure patterns. Bag-of-paths and randomized optimal-transport methods provide alternative graph proximities.

Recent work emphasizes nonlinear and continuous-time opinion models, multi-topic logical coupling, stochastic clustering, and feedback between evolving opinions and personalized recommendation. Researchers increasingly scrutinize the discriminating power and failure modes of centrality measures, infer hidden network structure from similarity observations, and develop scalable navigability and proximity computations. Network interventions now focus on recommending edges or content to reduce polarization, broaden exposure, and improve deliberative diversity.

63ffd741b7fe2f1a1acee4db72aa9738a8a68021.text:
## Opinion Dynamics, Network Structure, and Information Exposure

This community studies how network structure shapes opinions, information flow, influence, navigability, and robustness. Major themes include consensus, polarization, controversy, homophily, signed or antagonistic ties, stubbornness, social biases, and heterogeneous belief systems. Recent work extends opinion dynamics to nonlinear bias-dependent interactions, continuous-time and multi-topic models with logically interdependent beliefs, stochastic effects and cluster formation, and feedback loops between opinions and personalized recommendations. Echo chambers, partisan media, stance, ideological networks, and diversity of information exposure are important applications.

A second focus is structural analysis: centrality axioms and discriminating power, walk regularity, link prediction, discoverability, communicability, PageRank, effective resistance, backbone extraction, latent-attribute network formation, and vulnerability or privacy risks from inferred similarities. Applications span social media, Wikipedia, the Web, transportation, communication, and interaction networks.

Typical methods combine graph theory, dynamical systems, control and stability analysis, Markov chains, Fokker–Planck equations, spectral and matrix methods, random walks, optimization, approximation algorithms, Bayesian modeling, and text or stance analysis. Path-based distances and randomized optimal transport support clustering and classification.

Recent trends emphasize scalable graph computation, interpretable centrality, network reconstruction, multi-topic and stochastic modeling, recommender-system intervention, and optimization of exposure to reduce polarization and increase viewpoint diversity.

2a6ca9be7ce3957e079df3d3f1369b732db796e7.text:
## Scholarly Impact, Discovery, and Digital Communication

This community studies how scholarly work is disseminated, discovered, discussed, and evaluated beyond traditional citation counts. Major themes include altmetrics and societal impact; relationships among citations, downloads, readership, social-media attention, and peer-assessed quality; scholarly identity and author-level metrics; open access, repositories, preprints, and gold-OA publishing; bibliometrics for books and research groups; and knowledge-graph-based literature discovery.

Typical methods combine large-scale Web of Science, Scopus, Dimensions, Google Scholar, arXiv, Mendeley, Twitter, Facebook, Altmetric, PlumX, book, and repository data. Researchers use correlation, regression, PCA/factor analysis, comparative and coverage studies, surveys, interviews, sentiment analysis, and validation against peer assessments. Computational approaches include web scraping to overcome API limits, URL/entity matching, text and network mining, topic and user modeling, automated crawling, natural-language querying, and visualization.

Recent work emphasizes the heterogeneity, incompleteness, and platform dependence of online indicators: tweets often signal dissemination or attention rather than impact, while misconduct, titles, author prominence, and document type can strongly affect visibility. Academic profile platforms and integrated databases are expanding author metrics. Open repositories and preprints remain central, alongside personalized search portals and knowledge-graph systems that combine textual and citation-network evidence.

b990f2d4a6f49e9fd0239654ea2e2212207cf6c4.text:
## Adaptive Data Warehousing, Big-Data Analytics, and Benchmarking

This community centers on performance engineering for data warehouses, complex data management, and evolving big-data systems. Major themes include XML warehousing—tree-pattern querying, XOLAP, summarizability, workload-aware fragmentation, and XML benchmarks—alongside automatic physical design through joint index/materialized-view selection, query clustering, frequent-itemset mining, cost models, and workload analysis. Cloud and distributed settings emphasize balancing latency, throughput, scalability, and monetary cost.

Benchmarking is a particularly strong strand. Work develops configurable simulation frameworks and benchmark suites for warehouses, XML, search engines, text analytics, and distributed stream-processing engines, measuring throughput, latency, windowed operations, and workload diversity. Methods include application-specific and synthetic data generation, feature-preserving dataset scaling, controllable 4V generation (volume, variety, velocity, veracity), workload modeling, and incremental benchmark design under workload churn.

The community also studies adaptive database organization, dynamic clustering, changing access patterns, and efficient top-*k* inference and keyword/document processing using separable relational models and weighted vocabularies. Applications span healthcare, archaeology, web data, Internet services, and multimodal information.

Recent trends move toward automated, reproducible, and domain-specific benchmarks; realistic synthetic data; streaming and distributed evaluation; big-data workload evolution; and efficient top-*k* analytics over large target and text spaces.

7caa525028bb556687e4efb5bef3019838e84752.text:
### Differential Privacy for Utility-Preserving Data Release

This community studies how to protect sensitive data while retaining analytical value. Its central focus is differential privacy for histograms, range and batch queries, high-dimensional predicate counts, marginal statistics, clustering, community detection, decision trees, frequent-itemset mining, search logs, spatial data, and data exploration. It also addresses provenance, unstructured records, mobility data, and microdata anonymization.

Typical methods add calibrated noise using hierarchical, wavelet, kd-tree, and multidimensional partitions; matrix mechanisms; workload-specific strategies; adaptive selection; convex optimization; and data- or workload-aware partitioning. New work targets high-dimensional workloads, hierarchical count-of-counts histograms, and efficient, modular range-sum mechanisms. Programming abstractions such as Ektelo compose reusable operators for private linear-query computations. Local differential privacy is extended to range queries, quantiles, and predictive analyses.

Recent trends emphasize practical deployment: computational efficiency, private parameter tuning, accuracy-aware exploration, near-optimal workload guarantees, and synthetic mobility datasets that mitigate demographic bias and protect organizational interests. The community also studies adversarial background knowledge, reconstruction, membership, attribute, and inference attacks, reinforcing the limitations of k-anonymity and motivating stronger privacy guarantees.

38e74853728328649d8809628c01160dedabfbd1.text:
## Data Integration, Uncertainty, and Human-Assisted Data Quality

This community studies reliable query processing over incomplete, noisy, conflicting, and heterogeneous data. Major themes include probabilistic data fusion and truth discovery, including source reliability, copying and dependence, multiple truths, unknown unknowns, and conflict resolution in Web, linked, and open data. Entity resolution and record linkage address noisy joins through deep representations, graph matching, collective matching, probabilistic blocking, address normalization, and unsupervised string transformation.

A complementary focus is human- and crowd-assisted data management: quality-controlled labeling, worker reliability and confidence intervals, human–machine entity resolution, interactive query execution, preference aggregation, route evaluation, and low-latency task assignment. Research also develops declarative data cleaning through matching dependencies, functional and order-dependency discovery, target constraints in data exchange, ontology dependencies, and tractable rule-based reasoning.

Provenance remains important for explanations, debugging, reproducibility, and provenance-aware query optimization, alongside causality, responsibility, repairs, and abductive diagnosis.

Typical methods combine probabilistic graphical and hybrid models, optimization and message passing, embeddings and locality-sensitive hashing, structural decomposition, crowdsourcing, logical chase procedures, and cost-based query planning.

Recent trends emphasize scalable Web-scale integration, automated and democratized entity resolution, dependence-aware truth finding, human-in-the-loop quality guarantees, and estimating completeness and the impact of unobserved data.

0b21713c7e050c30c0284081f2ebe5f6181c1bf8.text:
### Foundations and Systems for Complex Event Processing

This community studies real-time processing of heterogeneous event streams, particularly for RFID and Internet-of-Things applications. Its central goal is transforming high-volume sensor data into actionable complex events through filtering, correlation, pattern detection, inference, and query processing.

Typical methods include specialized CEP languages and stream-processing architectures such as SASE; integrated inference and query processing for recovering missing location and containment information; and distributed systems for scalable tracking and monitoring. Pattern detection commonly uses nondeterministic finite automata (NFAs), including lazy chain automata that reduce unnecessary processing of partial matches. CEP workloads are also treated as multi-join queries, motivating join-order and query-plan optimization techniques. Other concerns include load shedding for graceful degradation and consistency across event processing, data streams, and asynchronous messaging.

At a foundational level, the community seeks principled, extensible models that unify streaming technologies while distinguishing workloads by query features and consistency needs.

Recent trends move toward integrated, distributed stream infrastructures for IoT-scale data, real-time inference, and enterprise monitoring, with increasing emphasis on efficient automata execution, optimized event joins, scalability, robustness under resource constraints, and well-defined CEP semantics.

f3ad12efdd7949814f25ac87d5db236a18f6e2b7.text:
**Bibliometrics, Research Evaluation, and Scholarly Equity**

This community studies how research performance, impact, and efficiency are measured and governed, with particular emphasis on Italy and national research systems. Themes include individual and institutional productivity, excellence, quality–quantity trade-offs, gender, age and academic rank, regional and disciplinary disparities, research diversification, multidisciplinary collaboration, academic entrepreneurship and spin-offs, nepotism, opportunistic responses to assessment, and the network and international diffusion of knowledge. It also examines citation value, researcher rankings, h- and g-index benchmarking, referee selection, and the fairness and validity of evaluation exercises.

Typical methods combine Web of Science, DBLP, and other bibliographic datasets with field normalization, FSS/MNCS and network-based indicators, citation weighting, DEA efficiency analysis, productivity distributions, Pareto/Gini statistics, regression and quantile models, longitudinal and sensitivity analyses, decision-support systems, and complex-network visualization. Author-name disambiguation uses probabilistic similarity, supervised and unsupervised learning, multilayer perceptrons, clustering, topology, and analyses of class imbalance.

Recent trends emphasize uncertainty-, contribution-, and network-aware evaluation; knowledge-flow and beneficiary mapping across countries; improved author identity resolution and benchmark construction; gender-sensitive rankings; and scrutiny of how assessment rules shape institutional behavior. Work increasingly links collaboration structure, interdisciplinarity, internationalization, and network position to visibility, citations, and research diversification.

eaacbedd09b2f8121419ee989fc23362b692dcb8.text:
## Networked Scholarly Information and Retrieval

This community applies network science, bibliometrics, and information-retrieval methods to scholarly communication and broader knowledge systems. Core themes include author-name disambiguation, coauthorship and citation structure, network-based ranking, scholarly impact, information seeking, data discovery, and visualization. Research also examines social-media and political networks, urban infrastructures, and the durability, reuse, and governance of research data.

Typical methods include PageRank and Google-matrix variants, CheiRank, reduced Google matrices, centrality and spectral analysis, graph visualization, graph-based summarization, co-occurrence and citation analysis, and network-scale empirical studies. Author disambiguation increasingly uses supervised and semi-supervised learning, deep neural networks, ethnicity-sensitive features, blocking, and deduplication to scale to millions of records. Evaluation draws on labeled bibliographic datasets, retrieval logs, search sessions, user studies, interviews, ethnography, relevance judgments, and agreement measures.

A parallel strand improves discovery through knowledge maps, visual collection interfaces, contextual browsing, query expansion, thesauri, Linked Data, metadata enrichment, and socio-technical models of data search. Recent trends emphasize reproducible and open computational workflows such as Jupyter notebooks, sustainable data infrastructures, large-scale census and archive analysis, interactive and personalized retrieval evaluation, extractive and semantic text summarization, and scalable analysis of social, geospatial, and political networks.

562fe165584ca0e0af7b0de48d26efbf5d4554ac.text:
## Collaborative Knowledge and Social Search

This community studies how user-generated and curated resources—including Wikipedia, Wiktionary, folksonomies, social bookmarks, professional networks, microblogs, and web archives—support knowledge organization, discovery, and search. Themes include extracting structured data; constructing multilingual thesauri, ontologies, and knowledge graphs; analyzing collaborative links and categories; understanding tagging vocabulary and heterogeneity; and collaboratively building and exploring archival collections.

Search research addresses social and group information seeking, expertise location, personalized professional search, entity and related-term retrieval, and implicit-feedback evaluation. Emerging applications include breaking-news and event discovery, semantic navigation, talent search, product insight, and fine-grained forecasting of users’ future locations or points of interest from geospatial streams and behaviorally defined communities.

Typical methods combine large-scale crawling, archive and log analysis, graph modeling, centrality and influence measures, clustering, co-occurrence and similarity metrics, matrix factorization, entity linking, NLP, interactive visualization, and learning-to-rank. Recent work adds deep neural semantic ranking deployed at massive production scale, with modular architectures designed to preserve low latency.

Recent trends emphasize scalable multilingual processing, dense entity resources, personalization and expertise inference, unbiased click-based learning, collaborative archive curation, dynamic mobility modeling, and integrating social signals with structured semantic representations.

e94727cf41d6b052bd4c61ce846799cf41d8f3df.text:
### Social Networks, Misinformation, and Platform Integrity

This community studies how online platforms shape political discourse, collective beliefs, information diffusion, and collective action. Major themes include echo chambers, polarization, controversy, misinformation and rumor verification, extremist and conspiratorial communities, media bias, hate speech, harassment, and propaganda. Platform-integrity research addresses bots, autogenerated content, spam, fake profiles and followers, astroturfing, honeypots, malicious nodes, coordinated influence operations, and manipulation of feeds, advertising, search, and popularity metrics. Fairness, viewpoint diversity, demographic inequalities, and counterspeech are growing concerns, alongside applications in health communication.

Typical methods combine large-scale data from Twitter, Facebook, YouTube, Reddit, Gab, decentralized-web systems, livestreams, and crowdsourcing with network analysis, surveys, content and sentiment analysis, temporal cascade analysis, and controlled or simulated interventions. Researchers use graph clustering, embeddings, multimodal representations, stance and sympathy detection, supervised and semi-supervised classification, anomaly detection, spam and bot detection, causal influence estimation, opinion-dynamics and contagion models, mechanism design, and adversarial honeypots. Hoaxy and FakeNewsNet support reproducible cascade research.

Recent work emphasizes real-time autogenerated-tweet detection; state-sponsored and cross-platform influence campaigns; causal measurement of narrative influence; resilient decentralized information sharing; early detection and removal of malicious nodes; interpretable and fairness-aware ranking; diversity-promoting recommendations; and interventions including fact checking, crowdsourced flags, counterspeech, and bot-based messaging.

17874e6b4e053af23ed12714a20f780939bcee7e.text:
## Social Network Diffusion, Influence, and Community Dynamics

This community studies how information, products, opinions, emotions, and user activity propagate through online, mobile, and other networked systems. Core themes include influence maximization, adaptive and sequential seeding, coupons and adoption, misinformation prevention, complex contagion, cascade popularity and longevity, and diffusion across multiplex, mobile, spatial, and evolving networks. Increasing attention addresses the full network lifecycle: growth, interaction decay, community aliveness, resilience, user turnover, and failure. Related work infers user attributes, privacy exposure, interests, and socially relevant behavior from network and transaction data, supporting recommendation, marketing, safety, and content moderation.

Typical methods combine independent-cascade, linear-threshold, Bass, epidemic-copying, Hawkes, and agent-based models with graph statistics, centrality, k-core analysis, random walks, stochastic simulation, and temporal analysis. Greedy and approximate submodular optimization, reverse-reachability sampling, mixed-integer or enumeration methods, and link prediction support intervention and placement. Neural diffusion models, embeddings, marked multivariate Hawkes processes, and multimodal text/image signals enable microscopic cascade prediction, multiplex network inference, demographic prediction, and popularity modeling.

Recent directions emphasize heterogeneous platforms and relational data, continuous-time and microscopic diffusion, partial or hidden network structure, social feedback, privacy, misinformation response, and real-world outcomes such as adoption, revenue, recruitment, engagement, and community survival.

7a01059c0a3dc23f4ac514f1a7d192bd2cf4ae83.text:
## Scholarly Networks, Discovery, and Research Infrastructures

This community applies network science, bibliometrics, and information-retrieval methods to scholarly communication and knowledge organization. Core themes include author-name disambiguation, coauthorship and citation structure, researcher and publication impact, expert finding, recommendation, search behavior, and ranking beyond raw citation counts. It also studies classification systems, semantic/Linked Data, collection maps, metadata, and the infrastructures that support data sharing, reuse, reproducibility, and open science.

Typical methods include PageRank and related spectral algorithms, rank aggregation, centrality and graph analysis, co-occurrence and Markov models, graph visualization, machine learning and deep neural networks, semi-supervised learning, blocking and deduplication, and statistical evaluation. Disambiguation work emphasizes labeled-data triangulation, learned blocking, feature imbalance, and scalable processing. Retrieval studies use session logs, contextual browsing, query expansion, user studies, relevance judgments, and agreement measures; summarization combines lexical, semantic, graph, sentiment, and statistical features.

Recent trends include scalable and neural identity resolution, citation-aware publication recommendation, personalized and exploratory search, automatic summarization, visual and multimodal retrieval, large-scale urban and social-media network analysis, multilingual and semantic knowledge organization, and empirical attention to scientific data stewardship, archives, computational notebooks, and research-workforce measurement.

3b6392918f8885b587ef19073c36de2e34fc5c55.text:
**Efficient Search, Graph Querying, and Fair Ranking**

This community develops methods to make large-scale search, indexing, and analytical querying faster, more compact, and more expressive. Core topics include compressed bitmap, inverted, integer, and multidimensional indexes; B+-trees and Roaring bitmaps; and SIMD-friendly byte compression such as Stream VByte. Query-processing work spans set and bitmap operations, skyline and Pareto analysis, ranking and reranking, order-incomplete data, and efficient processing of RDF subgraph patterns.

A growing focus is graph and heterogeneous-data management: partition-based summary graphs, learned query planning, subgraph-isomorphism optimization, and entity-resolution blocking schemes, including skyline-based selection of blocking strategies. Search systems study third-party reranking over hidden databases, rank fusion using query variations, and adaptive candidate-generation and algorithm selection in multistage retrieval pipelines.

Typical methods combine theoretical analysis, learned or heuristic optimization, specialized indexes, query decomposition, blocking, and empirical benchmarking. Hardware-conscious implementation—SIMD, cache-aware layouts, compressed-data processing, multicore, GPU, and distributed execution—remains important.

Recent trends emphasize learned query optimization, scalable RDF and heterogeneous-data processing, dynamic efficiency–effectiveness trade-offs, stable and multi-criteria rankings, and responsible retrieval. Fairness is increasingly modeled through exposure, demographic-aware diversification, and constraints balancing relevance with equitable visibility.

bd7cab6dfaadc49195544a5ea6953b24060c42c2.text:
### Robust, Explainable, and Sequential Recommendation

This community studies personalized recommendation from sparse, implicit, explicit, noisy, heterogeneous, and multimodal feedback. Core themes include long- and short-term/session behavior, cold start and long-tail items, cross-domain and hybrid filtering, diverse interests, social influence, consumer–producer roles, and temporal, spatial, and multi-behavior modeling. Applications span music and playlists, news, education, healthcare matchmaking, food, photography, products, research, and next-item recommendation.

Typical methods range from matrix/tensor factorization, Bayesian and pairwise ranking, nonuniform missing-data weighting, factorization machines, and topic models to VAEs with user- and item-specific priors, autoencoders, memory networks, neural collaborative filtering, and DeepFM architectures for low- and high-order feature interactions. Systems fuse explicit and implicit signals, text, audio, images, aesthetic/style features, tags, and behavioral context. Graph and knowledge-graph propagation, hierarchical embeddings, and path-based reasoning support cold-start, semantic modeling, and explanations. Reinforcement learning addresses page-wise and online sequential decisions, while retrieval-style ranking, ranking fusion, and playlist continuation support scalable deployment.

Recent trends emphasize adversarial and contaminated-feedback robustness, explainable recommendations, adaptive session models for changing catalogs, long-tail discovery with limited metadata, multimodal hybridization, producer-aware personalization, offline sequence evaluation, and practical online ranking and exploration–exploitation.

baee8126bd963e159b6ccf5092763b391b97fe77.text:
**Scalable Search, Indexing, and Data Analytics**

This community develops efficient, expressive systems for searching and analyzing large, heterogeneous datasets. Core themes include compressed bitmap, inverted, integer, multidimensional, spatial, and RDF indexes; B+-trees, Roaring bitmaps, hierarchical triangular meshes, zone indexes, and partition-based summary graphs. Compression uses differential, Huffman, variable-byte, frame-of-reference, and SIMD-oriented schemes, often with data reordering to improve locality.

Query-processing research covers set and bitmap operations, skyline and aggregate queries, ranking and reranking, spatial matching, RDF subgraph patterns, entity resolution, graph query planning, and ad-hoc SQL generation. Systems target scientific databases, arrays, metadata and provenance, scholarly Linked Open Data, social/geospatial data, and petabyte-scale analytics. Query batching, data sharing, cache-conscious execution, and distributed Hadoop/dataflow processing improve throughput.

Typical methods combine algorithmic analysis, learned optimization, relational representations, indexing structures, semantic extraction and interlinking, empirical benchmarking, and hardware-aware implementation. SIMD, multicore, GPUs, in-memory execution, and server-side preprocessing recur.

Recent trends emphasize data-intensive scientific and scholarly applications, recommender systems as services, user modeling, counterfactual and fairness-aware ranking, stable and diversity-conscious recommendations, and learning-based query optimization.

775208ed6f3747bcbce36c40461609f1bc41c6b5.text:
## Scalable Entity Resolution, Data Quality, and Crowdsourcing

This community focuses on integrating noisy, heterogeneous data through entity resolution, similarity search, and data-quality improvement. Core topics include deduplication and record linkage without reliable identifiers, edit and set-containment joins, approximate nearest-neighbor retrieval, and knowledge-graph enrichment with context-dependent information. Data quality work addresses completeness, consistency, currency, and uncertainty across multiple sources.

Typical methods combine probabilistic and mixed-effects models, source and worker reliability estimation, transfer learning and deep representations, locality-sensitive hashing, randomized sketches, binary and angular hashing, blocking, partitioning, and approximate joins. Human computation supports preference aggregation, adversarial ranking, quality-controlled labeling, adaptive and synchronized task assignment, personalized task matching, and spatial or specialty-aware crowdsourcing.

Recent trends emphasize subquadratic and approximate algorithms for massive, high-dimensional, and long-string datasets; benchmarking and tuning approximate-neighbor systems; reducing feature engineering through reusable models and deep learning; and adapting ER across related domains with limited labels. Crowdsourcing increasingly incorporates worker heterogeneity, reliability, preferences, mobility, skills, and route constraints, while data curation combines automated learning with human oversight. Knowledge integration is also becoming more condition-aware, capturing when relationships hold for particular populations or circumstances.

99e8f0c8048decf1d78aa09b0dac7596cecdbcb5.text:
## Social Media, Politics, Geolocation, and Urban Mobility

This community studies how digital traces reveal political preferences, polarization, influence, misinformation, migration, mobility, and urban experience. Political research analyzes voting behavior, ideological communities, structural balance, media power, election outcomes, coordinated bot campaigns, and fake-news diffusion across Twitter, parliamentary, Wikipedia, and news data. Social influence and audience studies identify influential users and characterize information flow, homophily, division, and cross-group communication.

A major theme is inferring place and movement from sparse or indirect signals. Text, network structure, weather observations, check-ins, Flickr metadata, and mobile-phone records support user home-location estimation, geocoding without geotags, regional identity analysis, commuting and migration modeling, activity timelines, and urban cultural or venue-demand planning. Work also addresses ecological and environmental modeling through geospatial embeddings, as well as entity relatedness over time and corpus context.

Typical methods include deep multiview learning, CNN/RNN classifiers, topic and sentiment analysis, signed-graph clustering, structural-balance and correlation-clustering models, Ising models and graph cuts, Monte Carlo simulation, regression, gravity models, Kalman and stochastic trajectory inference, population-synthesis bias correction, validation surveys, and one-pass trajectory simplification.

Recent trends emphasize multimodal and longitudinal data, sparse-observation reconstruction, scalable geolocation, uncertainty and sampling-bias correction, explainable polarization and influence modeling, and data-driven urban and cultural planning.

98acea72f17fbd721cb3a3856b11c78570fc6a3b.text:
### Scholarly, Spatial, and Social-Data Intelligence

This community studies how to retrieve, structure, and interpret scholarly records, social behavior, events, and geo-temporal data in large, evolving collections. Major themes include semantic publishing and linked scholarly data, scientific-quality assessment, author-contribution and citation extraction, text reuse, hypothesis generation, and research-paper recommendation. It also addresses social-media user modeling, actionable population prediction, online navigation, and recommendation behavior, alongside spatial-textual search, optimal facility placement, bursty-region detection, and spatiotemporal term analysis.

Typical methods include hybrid rule- and machine-learning information extraction, OCR, citation and hyperlink parsing, knowledge-graph construction and interlinking, topic modeling, coupled matrix/tensor factorization, semantic query expansion with lexical resources, collaborative and content-based recommendation, active learning, density-based spatio-textual clustering, Bayesian trail analysis, random walks, and network analysis. Hadoop-based processing supports large scholarly corpora, while empirical evaluation examines ranking quality, user behavior, text reuse, and system reliability.

Recent trends emphasize Linked Open Data for scholarly services, recommender systems as deployable APIs, multilingual knowledge access, automated and actionable scientific discovery, scalable mining of document and social streams, fine-grained spatial-temporal burst detection, and improved explainability and validation of data-driven systems.

a17f435aedd6acd8e38ae83d9ab7631327f37f04.text:
**Scholarly Metrics, Search Coverage, and Open Access**

This community studies how scholarly information is measured, compared, and disseminated. A central theme is bibliometric evaluation, including citation counts, h-index and h5-index, cited half-life, highly cited documents, journal and institutional benchmarking, and the validity of indicators across disciplines. Particular attention is given to systematic comparisons of Google Scholar, Web of Science, and Scopus: Google Scholar generally provides broader citation and highly cited-document coverage, while database selection strongly affects evaluation outcomes.

A second theme is scholarly accessibility and publishing policy. Research measures open-access availability, distinguishes legal or sustainable access from less reliable versions, combines evidence from multiple sources, and examines mandates, self-archiving, open peer review, open data, and the economics of “pay-to-publish” models.

Methods are predominantly empirical and computational: large-scale database querying, DOI and web-data collection, cross-disciplinary and longitudinal comparisons, bibliometric correlation and statistical testing, source triangulation, and analysis of document and citation coverage.

Recent trends include more inclusive and diverse indicators, stronger scrutiny of database bias and metric validity, systematic monitoring of open-access compliance, and policy interest in reducing publishing costs while expanding lawful public access.

40a6178d70ced797f112b6d5b8f4f1dfc2061f36.text:
**Scholarly Evaluation, Open Access, and Information Retrieval**

This community studies how scholarly information is measured, ranked, accessed, and interpreted. Core themes include bibliometric evaluation—citation counts, h-index and h5-index, cited half-life, reference-list growth, citation contexts, and journal or institutional benchmarking—and systematic comparisons of Google Scholar, Web of Science, and Scopus. Studies examine database coverage, highly cited documents, document types, reliability, visibility, and metric manipulation or optimization under Goodhart’s law.

A growing focus is open science: measuring legal and sustainable open-access availability, combining evidence from diverse sources, evaluating national and institutional OA policies, and debating self-archiving versus publisher-led models. Work also investigates knowledge accumulation and the epistemic functions of citations.

Information-retrieval research addresses library catalogs, credibility signals, query expansion, representative query sampling, search-engine comparisons, and learning-based topic selection for lower-cost test-collection evaluation.

Methods are empirical and computational: large-scale database querying, longitudinal and comparative bibliometrics, citation-context analysis, statistical testing, web APIs, automated data collection with manual validation, and qualitative classification.

Recent trends include cross-database reproducibility, broader and more equitable scholarly metrics, open-access monitoring, rising reference density, scrutiny of metric validity and incentives, and increasingly large-scale analyses of publishing practices.

ab99387f218795725670f179ab6d115d9e1c19cc.text:
## Scalable Learning and Analysis of Complex Networks
