This community develops methods for representing, comparing, modeling, and mining large, dynamic, uncertain, heterogeneous, signed, multilayer, and higher-order networks. Themes include temporal link prediction, event-graph and motif analysis, evolving communities and change points, network alignment, structural roles and convex skeletons, graph similarity, anomaly and fraud detection, de-anonymization, trust and balance, knowledge-graph construction and entity normalization, and network-based recommendation and team composition. Applications span social, web, academic, financial, and recommender networks.

Typical methods combine latent-space and stochastic graph models, probabilistic graph grammars, matrix factorization, robust and spectral methods, random walks, non-backtracking operators, Ricci-flow metrics, PageRank variants, integer programming, minimum-description-length model selection, and graphlet, clique, butterfly, and motif analysis. Representation learning increasingly uses temporal, multilayer, multi-relational, multimodal, text-network, and supra-graph embeddings, including GCNs, autoencoders, neural inference, and structural feature propagation. Scalable approximate, streaming, and distributed algorithms address web-scale graphs, operator prediction, counting, and recommendation.

Recent trends emphasize lossless continuous-time representations, inter-event dynamics, higher-order connectivity, graph-domain classification, cross-network fusion, explainable fraud attribution, adversarial robustness, poisoning defense, imbalance-aware learning, and large academic knowledge-graph benchmarks.

291aae52ec4c668a859671d77a38e8c92010b54a.text:
**Dynamic Networks, Online Collaboration, and Knowledge Structures**

This community applies complex-network analysis to evolving social, scientific, software, web, and healthcare systems. Themes include community structure, mixing, centrality, preferential attachment, interdisciplinarity, data reliability, and network-based measures of design quality, influence, and knowledge impact. Recent work especially examines Wikipedia and other online collaborations: cooperation and disagreement, editor status, multilingual participation, collective memory, governance norms, and the sequential routines of distributed work. It also studies organizational elite interlocking, multidisciplinary knowledge fields, and entity-level citation networks.

Typical methods include crawling platforms and bibliographic sources; extracting edits, reverts, coauthorships, citations, board memberships, and entity relations; and representing interactions as multilayer or temporal graphs. Researchers compare degree distributions, assortativity, centrality, community structure, and longitudinal link dynamics. Methods include propagation-based detection, robust clustering, random walks, forest-fire sampling, graph simplification, hidden Markov and finite-state models, sequence analysis, null-model comparisons, and entity-based metrics. Cross-database validation exposes inconsistencies in bibliographic data.

Recent trends move beyond static datasets toward large-scale, multilingual, web-derived and autonomously collected data, with explicit treatment of sampling bias and database consistency. Analyses increasingly quantify dynamicity, conflict, norms, social status, collective action, and knowledge evolution through temporal, behavioral, and computational models.

baa005756561b91f40069354f49e93514fede6b9.text:
## Scientometrics, Evaluation, and Scholarly Networks

This community quantitatively studies scientific knowledge, influence, performance, collaboration, and evaluation. Major themes include citation-based assessment of papers, authors, journals, institutions, countries, and research programs; field normalization, fractional and contribution-weighted attribution; interdisciplinarity, collaboration diversity, gender and ethnic diversity; research funding, peer-review bias, and the validity and unintended effects of metrics. It also examines how citations reflect impact, prestige, recognition, and knowledge diffusion, including the historical roots of ideas and technologies.

Typical methods combine Web of Science, Scopus, Microsoft Academic, bibliographic and patent databases, funding acknowledgements, and large-scale scholarly graphs. Citation, co-citation, bibliographic-coupling, co-authorship, author–paper, reviewer, and citation-context networks are analyzed using centrality, community detection, similarity, entropy, cognitive distance, overlay mapping, and network sampling. Methods include weighted h-type indices, percentile indicators, field- and time-normalized scores, fractional counting, RPYS and patent citation spectroscopy, author disambiguation, text and subject-heading analysis, interactive visualization, NoSQL data systems, recommendation experiments, and AI-assisted classification.

Recent trends emphasize source concordance and coverage, diversity-aware collaboration analysis, article-level and nonparametric evaluation, funding and review-process data, interactive exploration, recommender-system validation, and mapping emerging technologies. Greater attention is paid to statistical robustness, metric manipulation, database limitations, and responsible assessment.

9fc8b4f1733cc41ac10553f69dd214b649d3daaf.text:
## No Active Papers

No papers currently remain in this community. Consequently, there are no supported research themes, typical methods, or recent trends to report.

b68baeb6fbb2cd865af4d6350eed3f07a9a49a29.text:
**Information Retrieval: Neural, Semantic, Personalized, and Interactive Search**

This community develops retrieval and ranking systems that bridge lexical matching, neural semantics, knowledge graphs, and user context. Core themes include deep query–document interaction, attention and convolutional matching, contextual and concept embeddings, entity linking, attribute and salience identification, dynamic entity relatedness, heterogeneous-network expert finding, entity-set and scientific search, taxonomy construction, and multilingual query expansion. Retrieval increasingly operates at adaptive document/passage granularity and supports non-factoid and complex-answer question answering, email, social-media, biomedical, academic, mobile, app, and e-commerce search.

Typical methods include learning-to-rank with pairwise, listwise, groupwise, multitask, and differentiable objectives; task-aware textual representations; pseudo-relevance feedback and iterative interaction; knowledge-aware neural ranking; clustering and query classification; Markov random fields; authority ranking; and cost-sensitive or propensity-corrected learning from clicks. Evaluation emphasizes reproducible, efficient tooling and benchmark collections.

Recent trends include cross-domain and adversarial training, adversarial sampling and robustness to recommendation attacks, interpretable/post-hoc ranking, unbiased click-based learning, temporal and personalized ranking, direct optimization of user-oriented metrics, result diversification via sequential decision processes, and unified conversational/mobile assistants with personal memory. Semantic search is expanding beyond keyword recall toward explainable, interactive, context-sensitive, and app-integrated retrieval.

848a01c356d4ef9fe020f872dab3ef39200289e7.text:
## Scalable, Reliable, and Real-Time Data-Intensive Systems

This community studies scalable database management across multicore processors, shared-nothing clusters, clouds, and distributed data centers. A major theme is high-throughput OLTP, including contention management, distributed transactions, MVCC, snapshot isolation, adaptive and command logging, parallel recovery, and repairing conflicts rather than aborting transactions. Recent work targets highly contended workloads through transaction scheduling that separates conflict-free transaction clusters from residual conflicts.

A second theme is scientific and spatial data management. Research develops multidimensional, zone-based, spherical, and hierarchical triangular-mesh indexes; relational backends for finite-element and array workloads; and batch processing for data-intensive queries. New emphasis is on cloud-based, low-latency analysis of continuously arriving scientific data, particularly real-time astronomical events, complementing long-term scientific data management.

Typical methods combine new concurrency-control protocols, distributed architectures, indexing schemes, workload-aware scheduling, analytical modeling, prototypes, and empirical evaluation on scientific and OLTP workloads. Studies also examine provenance, energy consumption, dynamic partitioning, and clusters of lightweight machines.

Recent directions emphasize autonomic resource adaptation, energy-efficient cluster design, scalable and highly available transactions, fine-grained snapshotting for mixed OLTP/OLAP, improved debugging and provenance, and cloud platforms for streaming scientific analytics.

95d714eefb4dc3725b10e32dd75d8f2853e271b1.text:
## Community Detection, Centrality, and Cohesive Subgraphs

This community studies mesoscopic structure and influential positions in complex networks, including overlapping, attributed, weighted, directed, multilayer, evolving, and heterogeneous graphs. Themes include global and local community detection, role and theme communities, core–periphery organization, bridges, centrality, cohesive subgraphs, and structure relevant to information transmission and social interaction. Applications span online and social networks, criminal and bibliometric networks, web graphs, knowledge bases, and group-activity planning.

Typical methods include modularity and generalized Louvain optimization, label propagation, local partitioning, k-core and k-truss decomposition, similarity and random-walk methods, Markov stability, relaxed minimum-spanning trees, and centrality measures based on paths, dependencies, diffusion, and transmission. Probabilistic approaches include stochastic blockmodels, nonparametric Bayesian multiple-membership models, graphons, and variational Bayes for shared and private multilayer communities. Multi-view networks are integrated through unified graph representations or Pareto/multi-criteria optimization.

Evaluation emphasizes partition quality, stability and continuity of centrality, detectability, cohesion versus separation, scalability, and comparisons with normalized mutual information. Recent trends include attribute-aware and query-centered community search, distributed and locally scalable discovery, explicit distinction between local and global influence, temporal filtering of noisy interactions, event and dense-cluster detection, and community-informed social coordination and influence analysis.

29411e33d4f8f6c8dc662c1f07cd66da3e226483.text:
## Social Influence and Trust in Online Communities

This community studies how social networks shape information exchange, consumer behavior, and collective dynamics. Key themes include the effects of friends, ratings, trust, and social ties on user decisions, as well as triadic closure in integrated commerce-and-messaging environments. Another focus is rumor dissemination, examining how desires, trust structures, social homogeneity, and convergence influence diffusion.

Typical methods combine large-scale social-graph and platform analysis with empirical user studies and experiments measuring responses to friend recommendations and aggregate ratings. Researchers also develop computational diffusion models to explain information spread and changing collective behavior. System-oriented work explores secure, private, and usable community-classifieds platforms, linking social interaction with practical online-community design.

Recent directions emphasize distinguishing forms of social influence, modeling the interaction between trust and homophily, and connecting behavioral findings to privacy-aware community systems. Together, the papers move from analyzing interpersonal effects on choices and information flow toward explaining and supporting trustworthy, secure online communities.

b2c065e2e12e79e631514e01aa13d4c2da625276.text:
### Graph Data Management and Semantic Web Querying

This community studies the modeling, validation, querying, and optimization of RDF, OWL, SPARQL, XML, and property-graph data. Core themes include SPARQL BGP and OPTIONAL semantics, OBDA and relational–RDF translation, entailment, conjunctive and navigational queries, label-constrained reachability, graph pattern matching, and query answering under TGDs. Property-graph type systems and RDF graph formalisms support convergence between semantic-web and graph-database models.

Typical methods combine formal semantics, decidability and complexity analysis, cost/cardinality estimation, graph summaries, sparse-matrix joins, partitioning, and approximate query processing. Practical systems use modular optimizers such as Apache Calcite, distributed and locality-aware graph processing, Gremlin–SPARQL translation, and relational-algebra reductions. Certified and incremental view maintenance—including Regular Datalog and discrimination networks—targets continuously changing graphs.

A growing applied focus is provenance: segmentation, summarization, version-aware analysis, and property-graph querying of data-science workflows. Other usability directions include embedding-based query recommendation, contextualized knowledge-graph facts, dynamic ontology exploration, validation and quality control, and explainable approximate answers. Recent trends emphasize federated and endpoint-free Web-of-Data access, scalable multi-query and data-in-motion analytics, heterogeneous-source integration, and schema evolution, with emerging applications in IoT and biomedical knowledge graphs.

812b357ed880e9a16b9935fd7b6c2786aa86ae38.text:
## Network Diffusion, Influence, and Source Inference

This community studies how information, opinions, misinformation, epidemics, products, and contamination propagate through social, biological, infrastructure, temporal, multiplex, and mobility networks. Core problems include forward diffusion and adoption prediction; source and patient-zero localization from partial snapshots; cascade reconstruction; influence maximization; epidemic containment; and robust intervention under budgets, competition, and evolving topology.

Typical methods combine independent-cascade, threshold, epidemic/SIR/SIS, Bass, Markov, trust-based, and continuous-time models with submodularity, approximation, game theory, mixed-integer and stochastic optimization, sampling, random walks, message passing, graph searching, and machine learning. Analytic and computational tools include higher-order moment closure, weighted-shortest-path and Monte Carlo simulation, rejection sampling, and scalable streaming algorithms.

Recent work emphasizes multiplex networks with heterogeneous diffusion models, adaptive and time-decaying interactions, metapopulation epidemics, heterogeneous susceptibility, competitive campaigns, sequential and multi-round seeding, coupon allocation, and resource-constrained prevention. Reverse prevention sampling and billion-scale influence algorithms improve practical intervention. Mobility and trajectory data support location- and trajectory-aware influence placement, while temporal observations enable more robust source inference and epidemic control.

d6f4e04e5036d61cbb8396c599a55239bb13b7e0.text:
### Semantic Retrieval, Structural Similarity, and Mathematical Information Access

This community develops scalable methods for semantic search, text mining, and mathematical information services. Text-mining research addresses classification, clustering, probabilistic topic modeling, feature selection, authorship analysis, and technology-assisted review. Recent work improves high-recall information retrieval through sentence-level relevance feedback and active-learning workflows that reduce reviewer effort while maintaining document-level accuracy.

A second theme is structural similarity and graph analysis. Methods include robust algorithms for ordered-tree edit distance and edit-distance-based inter-graph node metrics, supporting predictable comparison across diverse tree shapes and transfer of knowledge between graphs.

Mathematical retrieval focuses on combined text-and-formula search, presentation and content representations, identifier extraction, formula repositories, accessible MathML, and context-aware formula conversion. Math-aware question answering connects natural-language questions to Wikidata formulas and uses symbolic computation through systems such as SymPy.

Typical methods include active learning, simulation-based evaluation, edit-distance dynamic programming, local-neighborhood graph comparison, semantic enrichment, canonicalization, pattern matching, knowledge-base integration, and computer algebra. Recent trends emphasize efficient human-in-the-loop review, robust structural matching, context-sensitive mathematical representations, interoperability, and executable, multilingual mathematical question answering.

b7910a035e10307d37fda9f215bde522870d8c8c.text:
**Complex-Network Analysis of Software, Science, and Online Collaboration**

This community applies complex-network theory to large, evolving systems, including software, scientific, social, web, healthcare, and online knowledge networks. Themes include community structure, social status and influence, information and opinion propagation, node mixing, centrality, preferential attachment, interdisciplinarity, collective memory, and the reliability of network data. Software dependency networks support analysis of design quality, modularity, reusability, vulnerability, efficiency, and controllability. Scientific and healthcare networks reveal citation dynamics, researcher interdisciplinarity, collaboration, and links between physician coordination and patient outcomes. Wikipedia and similar systems are studied as arenas for social-movement documentation, knowledge reappraisal, and distributed work.

Typical methods include crawling web platforms, extracting revision, coauthorship, citation, and interaction data, and representing systems as temporal graphs. Researchers compare local and global graph statistics, degree distributions, assortativity, centrality, and community structure; forecast influential users and model propagation. They also develop group-detection and citation-dynamics algorithms, evaluate sampling and graph-simplification strategies, compare bibliographic databases, and apply sequence analysis to characterize organizational routines and coordination patterns.

Recent trends emphasize autonomously collected web data, temporal and multilevel evolution, sampling bias, database consistency, social-movement knowledge production, and sequential behavior in online collaboration, alongside network-based indicators of system quality and healthcare effectiveness.

677c2f45e8a5ae392bcf37754040842505fd2baf.text:
## High-Performance Search, Indexing, and Responsible Analytics

This community develops efficient, expressive retrieval and database-processing systems for large, heterogeneous data. Core themes include compressed bitmap, inverted, n-gram, and posting-list indexes; integer and byte-oriented compression; learned index structures; multidimensional and OLAP representations; and SIMD-accelerated encoding, decoding, and set operations. Reordering, differential coding, hashing, and succinct structures reduce memory use while preserving query speed.

Research also spans advanced retrieval and query processing: skyline, Pareto, representative and stable rankings; fuzzy summaries; incomplete-order and possible/certain query answers; graph-pattern search and learned graph query planning; workflow, biomedical, community-question-answering, and hidden-web search. Multi-stage retrieval, rank fusion, query variation, neural passage retrieval, and query-driven algorithm selection address effectiveness–latency trade-offs.

Typical methods combine complexity analysis, formal semantics, dynamic programming, ranking and learning-to-rank algorithms, machine-learned indexes, MapReduce and distributed in-memory processing, and GPU, multicore, SIMD, SSD, or NVM acceleration. Empirical evaluation on real systems and datasets is standard.

Recent trends emphasize adaptive and learned retrieval pipelines, hardware-conscious compression, scalable graph and language-data processing, and responsible ranking: fairness of exposure and attention, demographic satisfaction auditing, coverage assessment, and relevance–diversity trade-offs.

bb368a902dc2488b80fac598b61c35d3f81dbb66.text:
### Dynamic Text, Topic, and Knowledge Intelligence

This community studies how to organize, interpret, and derive actionable insight from large, evolving collections of scholarly, web, and social-media text. Core themes include temporal and emerging-topic discovery, semantic document indexing, bibliometric mapping, knowledge-graph construction, user-interest modeling, and population-level prediction.

Typical methods combine topic models, constrained coupled matrix/tensor factorization, semantic and hierarchical TF–IDF representations, WordNet-based query expansion, deep-learning classification, active learning, and user-level aggregation. Distributed near-duplicate and text-reuse detection—using MinHash, MapReduce, and scalable retrieval pipelines—supports identification of copied, conflicting, and reused information. Interactive semantic networks can compare keyword-, citation-, and full-text-based perspectives.

The community increasingly emphasizes practical and trustworthy information access: title-based annotation that approaches full-text performance, multilingual retrieval, efficient discovery of the final relevant documents in technology-assisted review, and automated hypothesis generation with expert- and validation-based evaluation. Social-media analysis now supports user profiling, publication recommendation, community-level nowcasting, and extraction of actionable knowledge from sensitive social issues.

Recent trends include time- and expertise-aware topic evolution, neural semantic indexing, open-science indicators, scalable text-quality analysis, and decision support that links mined patterns to concrete actions.

f5e38d14f2b4804a2244c01a7d3b6ec84d68714e.text:
## Network Representation, Prediction, and Dynamics

This community studies representing, comparing, and predicting structure in social, information, knowledge, communication, multilayer, and temporal networks. Core themes include link prediction, entity normalization and graph alignment, community and role discovery, anomaly and fraud detection, recommendation, and modeling evolving interactions. Applications span social influence and attitudes, online fraud and criminal activity, team formation, scientific and citation recommendation, ESG compliance, and web-scale personalization.

Typical methods combine random walks, spectral and structural similarity, centrality, motifs, triadic and higher-order patterns, blockmodels, change-point detection, and temporal event graphs with text, attributes, and heterogeneous evidence. Neural representation learning—including DeepWalk, matrix-factorization views of embeddings, dynamic and multilayer embeddings, GCNs, semantic encoders, and multimodal adversarial autoencoders—supports prediction, retrieval, and recommendation. Other approaches include continuous-time Bayesian models, fuzzy ensembles, discriminative paths, and geometric methods such as Ollivier–Ricci flow.

Recent directions emphasize continuous-time and event-level modeling without temporal aggregation, dynamic visualization that preserves the mental map, scalable graph operators and spectral prediction, joint multilayer learning, explainable alignment, and robust anomaly detection. The community increasingly targets real-time, web-scale systems and integrates network structure with language and behavioral evidence.

b14124abae6521d5a20e3b5a6c348078faf6a707.text:
## Network Diffusion, Influence, and Source Inference

This community studies how information, opinions, epidemics, misinformation, failures, and tasks propagate through social, biological, infrastructure, and cyber-physical networks. Core problems include source and patient-zero inference, cascade reconstruction, adoption and trend prediction, hidden-network estimation, influence maximization, epidemic containment, and contamination clearing from sparse, temporal, aggregate, or biased observations.

Influence and prevention increasingly address multiplex and composite networks, heterogeneous diffusion models, competing campaigns, trust and distrust, fixed or heterogeneous thresholds, coupons, pricing, sequential and multiround seeding, adaptive feedback, and budgeted resource allocation. Epidemic work emphasizes temporal, adaptive, metapopulation, and activity-driven networks.

Typical methods combine independent-cascade, threshold, epidemic, Bass, compartmental, DeGroot, Markov, and continuous-time models with submodularity and approximation, game theory, centrality, random walks, mixed-integer optimization, streaming algorithms, sampling, Monte Carlo, message passing, and machine learning. Cascade and source inference use probabilistic sampling, weighted shortest paths, spanning or Steiner structures, and discriminative prediction.

Recent trends emphasize scalable billion-edge influence algorithms, time-decaying interaction streams, realistic temporal contact data, robust epidemic thresholds, efficient stochastic simulation, reverse prevention sampling, and trajectory- or mobility-driven coverage and intervention. Applications increasingly span mobile sensing, app adoption, online advertising, public health, transportation, and misinformation mitigation.

61b1608c3108cf9c2a142bc936bf0628876f26e2.text:
### Preserving, Linking, and Enriching Evolving Digital Knowledge

This community studies durable, interpretable, and discoverable digital information across scientific, cultural, and Web contexts. Themes include repository and compound-object architectures, persistent identifiers, provenance, versioning, rights, research objects, and preservation of evolving Linked Open Data. Web archiving is central, including user-curated and institutional collections, private/public archive aggregation, event-focused and multilingual analytics, temporal search, semantic layers, ranking, missing content, and archival seed selection. Scholarly knowledge representation is expanding through formal scientific claims, nanopublications, provenance-centric linked data, and links between publications and scientific software.

Typical methods combine OAIS, Fedora, aDORe, Memento, MPEG-21, OAI-PMH, RDF, SPARQL, PROV-O, PAV, Open Annotation, arcp, and nanopublication models with prototypes, APIs, query languages, and analytics tools. Large-scale Common Crawl, web-archive, SERP, social, and longitudinal analyses measure persistence, retrievability, change, and collection quality. Machine learning supports binary domain classification of queries; link analysis, entity-aware semantic ranking, lexical and title comparison, timestamping, and researcher-strategy studies support retrieval and event detection.

Recent trends emphasize community-guided crawling, cross-archive and privacy-aware aggregation, semantic search over archives, formal and provenance-rich scholarly communication, software–publication discovery, and reproducible identifier tracking. Persistent challenges include heterogeneous schemas, temporal noise, incomplete archives, sensitive captures, multilinguality, and maintaining meaning as resources evolve.

d7dbae2456bf82c46e64de7732bcbf2e6ea658ff.text:
## Scientometrics, Research Evaluation, and Science Mapping

This community measures scientific influence, performance, knowledge accumulation, collaboration, and interdisciplinarity across authors, papers, journals, institutions, countries, and research topics. Themes include citation and percentile indicators, field normalization, rankings, peer-review validity and bias, funding acknowledgements, gender and geographic disparities, societal impact, scholarly communication, and critiques of impact factors, h-indices, and simplistic evaluation incentives. It also examines database coverage, missing affiliations, reference-link quality, credit allocation, and the relation between citations, readership, and research quality.

Typical methods use Web of Science, Scopus, Microsoft Academic, Dimensions, Mendeley, PubMed, patents, and web-search data. Citation, co-citation, bibliographic-coupling, co-authorship, researcher–topic, and citation-context networks support centrality, community detection, RPYS/patent citation spectroscopy, interdisciplinarity measures, cognitive-distance mapping, and knowledge discovery. Percentile and field/time-normalized indicators, econometric and statistical ranking comparisons, author disambiguation, fractional counting, visualization, NoSQL processing, and machine-learning recommendation or citation-prediction systems are common. Peer-review studies use large review datasets and network-informed reviewer matching.

Recent trends emphasize cross-database validation, sparse and nonparametric indicators, open citation expansion, article recommendation, funding and gender analytics, research-frontier and journal-change detection, and transparent real-world testing of evaluation and recommendation systems.

e26aeb952dfec2de986d5a7c8b0bdc953fa7a394.text:
### Scholarly Communication, Impact, and Discovery

This community studies how scholarly work is disseminated, discovered, evaluated, and reused. Core themes include bibliometrics and altmetrics; citation, readership, download, social-media, and web attention; journal, book, author, institution, and country-level impact; peer-assessment relationships; open access, repositories, mandates, preprints, and open-science practices; and academic search, profiles, recommendation, expert discovery, and research evaluation. It also examines web visibility and cross-sector networks linking universities, businesses, governments, and science parks.

Typical methods combine large bibliographic, repository, usage, web-crawling, and social-platform datasets. Researchers compare Google Scholar, Web of Science, Scopus, Microsoft Academic, ResearchGate, arXiv, and other discovery systems using coverage analyses, citation matching, rankings, correlation, regression, factor analysis, network analysis, benchmarking, and longitudinal studies. Machine learning, latent-space models, text and linguistic analysis, APIs, and automated querying support search, visualization, metric construction, and platform evaluation.

Recent work emphasizes Google Scholar’s broad but inconsistent coverage, academic-search evolution, citation aging, preprint–journal relationships, and institution-level benchmarking. It highlights platform-specific visibility, metadata and version-merging errors, metric manipulation, disciplinary and language bias, and weak links between online attention, citation impact, peer judgment, and societal value. OA studies increasingly measure legal availability, repository uptake, mandate effects, and publication-model differences.

aaddfd9bac5c4f3242ec6cefd7082840eef5020b.text:
## Scalable, Declarative Data Management and Analytics

This community develops scalable, efficient, and usable systems for data-intensive computation. Core themes include relational query optimization—join ordering, cardinality estimation, inequalities, incremental maintenance, worst-case-optimal joins, and functional aggregate queries—alongside graph, RDF, streaming, and time-series processing. Declarative paradigms such as SQL, Datalog, relational algebra, typed linear algebra, and document-spanner languages support analytics, reasoning, and information extraction.

Typical methods combine formal complexity, communication, and decomposition analyses with practical systems building. Techniques include MILP and semi-automated data-structure design, sparse tensors, factorized and incremental computation, adaptive indexing, LSM optimization, sampling and mergeable sketches, approximate query processing, data cubes, caching, and constant-delay enumeration. Systems target distributed, multicore, GPU, FPGA, array, browser, and cloud environments, with attention to reproducibility and interactive performance.

The community increasingly integrates databases with machine learning through in-database training, hardware acceleration, analytics-as-a-service, model management, data-market pricing, and dataset documentation. It also emphasizes interactive exploration, visualization recommendation, pay-as-you-go enrichment, and secure or split execution.

Recent trends favor unified declarative abstractions, automation of physical design and optimization, approximate or progressive answers, adaptive processing for evolving streams, and transparent, reproducible infrastructure for heterogeneous data.

43820e960a8070492c052357d984c875f02e6037.text:
### Dynamic Scholarly, Social, and Information Intelligence

This community studies latent structure, semantic relationships, user interests, and actionable knowledge in evolving collections of scholarly documents, social-media text, and linked information. Topic modeling remains important for discovering time-evolving and emerging themes, modeling creator expertise, and supporting publication recommendation.

A major focus is information retrieval and semantic document understanding. Query expansion uses distributional, association-based, probabilistic, and lexical-resource methods, including WordNet and FarsNet. Research also compares titles, abstracts, and full text for semantic annotation and subject indexing, increasingly applying deep learning to metadata-constrained settings. Technology-assisted review combines continuous active learning with entity- and question-based strategies to find high-value documents efficiently.

The community further develops scholarly knowledge and decision support: hypothesis-generation systems are evaluated and validated by experts, bibliometric and citation networks map research evolution, and mined patterns are transformed into actionable recommendations. Social-media analysis addresses user-interest inference, personalized publication recommendation, community-level prediction, and social-welfare discourse, with user-level aggregation improving population estimates.

Typical methods include topic and tensor/matrix factorization, semantic networks, neural representation learning, active learning, lexical ontologies, temporal decay, and interactive bibliometric analysis.

Recent trends emphasize scalable human-in-the-loop retrieval, semantic enrichment from limited metadata, validated automated discovery, user-aware social prediction, and actionable open-science analytics.

3e7e54a3f7aa76c4fa25b0271d68c658e3fced6a.text:
## Community Detection and Network Structure

This community studies the discovery, evaluation, modeling, and use of mesoscale structure in complex networks. Themes include overlapping, hierarchical, multilayer, heterogeneous, attributed, weighted, signed, dynamic, bipartite, partially observed, and two-mode communities; local partitions; cohesive cores and core–periphery organization; bridges and influential nodes; and structure relevant to consensus, diffusion, epidemics, and information spread. Applications span social, communication, web, bibliometric, biological, voting, and interaction networks, including temporal event discovery.

Typical methods include modularity and nonlinear spectral optimization, label propagation and seed-based local search, clique/density and subgraph mining, core/truss decomposition, random walks and personalized PageRank, manifold and graph-signal techniques, centrality and entropy measures, and stochastic block and other generative models. Variational Bayes supports shared/private multilayer inference; likelihood-based model selection, Pareto multiobjective optimization, bipartite co-clustering, graph-filter blind identification, and Markov-Stability geometric embeddings extend the toolkit. Semi-supervised constraints, attributes, temporal interaction filtering, and incomplete-network inference enrich structural analysis.

Recent trends emphasize scalable and distributed detection, metastability and dynamics-aware analysis, multiscale and hierarchical representations, uncertainty and noise robustness, centrality prediction from core structure, signed and multiplex modeling, and event discovery through dense temporal subgraphs.

ba8b4f7ae4bb845cc429c0624f93d6314695f511.text:
### Bibliometric Evaluation, Mobility, and Equity in Higher Education

This community studies how research performance, impact, and efficiency are measured across researchers, departments, universities, and national systems, especially in Italy and comparative higher-education contexts. Themes include productivity versus substantive impact, excellence, field diversification and specialization, citation validity, research funding and assessment exercises, institutional performance, academic entrepreneurship, and the effects of gender, age, rank, and researcher heterogeneity. International mobility—migrants, travelers, affiliations, and early-career movement—is examined as a mechanism for knowledge diffusion and access to networks. Equity, peer-review quality, referee selection, and the risks of metric-driven incentives remain central.

Typical methods include large-scale Web of Science bibliometrics, author disambiguation, citation curves and weighted citations, h- and g-index benchmarking, novel impact and “perfectionism” indicators, field-normalized measures, regression analysis, network and co-affiliation mapping, mobility classifications, distributional analysis, and decision-support systems. Qualitative taxonomies and peer judgment are treated as complements to metrics.

Recent trends emphasize bounded, researcher-centered impact measures over publication volume; integrating quantitative indicators with qualitative assessment; mapping mobility flows across countries, cities, and institutions; analyzing relatedness and intensity of individual diversification; and evaluating how top, low-performing, entrepreneurial, and mobile researchers shape organizational performance and policy.

4742cae338ea0b5d0da96e8dd4785f2025214d71.text:
## Data Integration, Entity Resolution, and Human-Assisted Data Quality

This community studies integrating, matching, and curating noisy, heterogeneous data from Web, open-data, enterprise, social, spatial, and knowledge-graph sources. Core themes include entity resolution and schema matching, deduplication, edit and set-similarity joins, semantic matching using taxonomies, truth discovery under correlated or conditional source reliability, and quality improvement for incomplete, inconsistent, conflicting, or stale data. It also addresses data-diff synthesis, constraint-based cleaning, Datalog reasoning, and trustworthy medical knowledge graphs.

Typical methods combine probabilistic, Bayesian, variational, and semi-supervised learning; deep representations, transfer and gradual learning; blocking, locality-sensitive and minimum hashing, prefix/pigeonhole filtering, graph matching, message passing, and similarity joins. Systems exploit distributed aggregation, CPU–GPU acceleration, and efficient verification. Human computation supports labeling, schema correspondence, risk-based ER verification, adaptive and quality-aware task assignment, worker modeling, and intelligent spreadsheets.

Recent trends emphasize deep-learning-driven, lower-feature-engineering curation; scalable and exact similarity search; semantic and condition-aware knowledge integration; and explicit analysis of how dirty data affects downstream learning. Crowdsourcing increasingly becomes personalized, budget- and route-aware, spatially constrained, specialty-aware, and optimized for accuracy, latency, uncertainty, and limited human effort.

8e547fa3b4222dd4614dda7833029f518aa7c848.text:
## Scientometrics, Citation Metrics, and Science Mapping

This community quantifies scientific knowledge, influence, performance, and evaluation across researchers, papers, journals, institutions, countries, and technologies. Core themes include citation-based indicators, field and time normalization, interdisciplinarity, collaboration, research histories, university rankings, peer-review validity, and critiques of impact factors, h-indices, percentile measures, and assessment regimes. Fairness concerns address disciplinary variation, skewed distributions, authorship credit, gender, international collaboration, and network-related bias.

Typical methods use Web of Science, Scopus, PubMed, Microsoft Academic, Dimensions, and patent databases. Analyses combine citation, co-citation, bibliographic-coupling, co-authorship, and citation-context networks with PageRank, community detection, centrality, entropy, similarity, cognitive-distance, RPYS/patent spectroscopy, visualization, and text or subject-heading analysis. Fractional counting, percentile indicators, I3 variants, PaperRank/AuthorRank, and graph-based author disambiguation are prominent. Statistical concordance studies compare databases and normalized scores.

Recent trends include multimodal network–text analytics, citation-context and uncertainty mining, deep-learning prediction of future citations, article-level and sparse-data altmetric normalization, and stronger integration of peer review with bibliometrics. Applications increasingly extend from scholarly literature to patents, technological innovation, and policy-oriented evaluation, while emphasizing metric validity and unintended behavioral effects.

9882fc87f6016bb4a5ce41a2bfcab5126f029586.text:
## Social Networks: Diffusion, Communities, and Influence

This community studies how social networks form, evolve, and shape information, opinion, behavior, popularity, and knowledge exchange. Major themes include centrality, rich clubs, brokers, weak ties, assortative mixing, hierarchical and indirect community structure, and the role of status, diversity, ethnicity, and homophily in social and scientific collaboration. It examines information cascades and complex contagion, topic and hashtag lifecycles, semantic continuity, cross-community interests, real-time event sensing, mobile content dissemination, and knowledge-market dynamics. Recommendation, social feedback, citation discovery, peer-review networks, and popularity prediction are recurring applications.

Typical methods combine temporal, multiplex, weighted, and multimodal network analysis; community detection and visualization; diffusion, epidemic, Hawkes-process, and agent-based models; stochastic optimal control, influence optimization, and adaptive polling; embeddings, matrix factorization, neural attention, text/image analysis, and content classification. Researchers use large-scale empirical datasets, randomized baselines, node categorization, interpretable economic models, and methods for inferring hidden diffusion links, demographics, status, and community membership.

Recent directions emphasize platform-scale and cross-domain data, transaction and relational signals, semantic and visual features, concept drift, microscopic cascade prediction, interpretable interventions to steer activity, governance of self-organizing communities, and richer measures of transmission, diversity, popularity, and citation impact.

785b5e808fb8a7ea90942ebeac125f9a6a689db6.text:
### Differential Privacy for Utility-Preserving Data Release

This community develops privacy-preserving publication and analysis of sensitive data while retaining statistical and operational utility. Core themes include differential privacy for histograms, range and batch queries, marginal statistics, clustering, community detection, decision trees, frequent-itemset mining, search logs, spatial data, and data exploration. New work extends this scope to hierarchical group-size and count-of-counts estimation across geographic levels, spatial-region analytics, mobility datasets, IoT data streams, and database query selectivity estimation.

Typical methods add calibrated noise using hierarchical, wavelet, kd-tree, multidimensional, or data-aware partitions. Query answering employs matrix mechanisms, workload-specific strategies, HDMM-style convex optimization, adaptive selection, basis sets, and modular histogram construction. Ektelo provides a compositional programming framework for implementing private linear-query algorithms. Other approaches use synthetic data generation, perturbation, mixture models, randomization, generalization, and approximation algorithms, including local differential privacy for range queries and quantiles.

Recent trends emphasize scalable, deployable utility: high-dimensional workloads, efficient computation, private parameter and selectivity tuning, bias-adjusted mobility release, stream mining, geographic consistency, and workload-independent or near-optimal guarantees. The community also studies adversarial background knowledge, reconstruction and inference attacks, and the limitations of k-anonymity, motivating stronger privacy models.

bd943c83fbeb6335dccedbc77d95cc83c041f855.text:
### Social Media, Political Influence, and Information Integrity

This community examines how online platforms shape public opinion, collective behavior, trust, and information flows. Core themes include political communities and controversy, polarization and antagonism, misinformation and propaganda, social bots and autogenerated content, spam and fraud, suspicious or deviant communities, privacy and contextual integrity, and collective attention. It also studies weak ties, emotional and behavioral influence, emergency information, crisis response, and constructive fact-checking.

Typical methods combine large-scale social-media and communication data with network, community, temporal, propagation, and linguistic analysis. Researchers use nonnegative matrix factorization, graph topology and communicability measures, anomaly and suspicious-link detection, supervised classification, demographic and latent-attribute inference, sentiment and stance analysis, surveys, experiments, ontology-based integration, and epidemic-style diffusion models. They evaluate credibility, visibility, feed fairness, source bias, coordinated manipulation, and users’ roles in spreading or correcting information.

Recent work emphasizes coordinated political influence and spear-phishing campaigns, real-time detection of autogenerated or anomalous activity, relations between allied and antagonistic communities, and fine-grained credibility and attention dynamics. Other trends include privacy-aware and decentralized social infrastructures, resilient network design, automated emergency-aid retrieval, guardian-based misinformation correction, and models that move beyond simple contagion to capture weak ties, context, and complex social influence.

6a808941e467229481a46c1eb8df9908d5217e35.text:
## Community Detection and Network Structure

This community studies mesoscopic structure in complex networks: detecting, evaluating, modeling, and exploiting communities, hierarchies, cores, trusses, bridges, and core–periphery organization. Key settings include overlapping, multilayer and multiplex, heterogeneous, attributed, weighted, signed, bipartite, temporal, spatial, simplicial, and partially observed networks. Applications span social, web, communication, biological, bibliometric, recommendation, political, security, and epidemic networks.

Typical methods include modularity and likelihood optimization, degree-corrected stochastic block models, variational Bayes, nonparametric latent-feature models, spectral and nonlinear eigenvector techniques, random walks and Markov Stability, label propagation, local generative models, clique/density and subgraph mining, dendrograms, matrix factorization, and core/truss decomposition. Recent work adds Pareto and multiview optimization, graph-signal and blind-filter approaches, neighborhood similarity, causal inference, and exact integer programming for signed-graph frustration and balance.

Evaluation emphasizes partition and node-level metrics, agreement indices, model selection, stability under noise, multiscale quality, and benchmarks. Current trends include distributed and scalable processing, efficient subgraph discovery, incremental analysis of evolving graphs, metastable network dynamics, persistent core structure, global-bridge and centrality-aware analysis, and principled integration of topology with attributes, language, interactions, latent agents, and uncertainty. Layer-specific signed and bipartite co-clustering, epidemic modeling, and community-informed influence and recommendation are growing application areas.

41d9372938e39f158c94a4fd313b49e37348c099.text:
**Bibliometric Networks, Scholarly Retrieval, and Information Mapping**

This community studies scholarly communication, information organization, and networked influence. Themes include ranking institutions, authors, papers, patents, and web resources; distinguishing popularity, prestige, and diffusion; analyzing citation, coauthorship, hiring, career, political, and geopolitical networks; detecting communities and temporal cores; and tracing novelty, workforce development, and epistemic inequality.

PageRank and Google-matrix methods remain prominent, including weighted, bipartite, reduced-matrix, spectral, and alternative normalization approaches. Work also examines the limitations and deceptiveness of matrix-based centrality. Other methods include stochastic block models, LSTM forecasting, temporal embeddings, graph-based centrality and core decomposition, large-scale network mining, PCA, geospatial graph analysis, and automated metadata collection, linking, and author-name disambiguation.

A parallel information-retrieval strand develops discipline-specific query expansion, KOS/SKOS and Linked Data integration, contextual browsing, knowledge maps, and bibliometric-enhanced ranking. User behavior is studied through search logs, mouse fixations, eye tracking, session traces, stratagem analysis, and interactive experiments, with growing attention to personalization, exploratory search, usefulness, and session-level evaluation.

Recent trends include scalable census and career analytics, predictive rather than retrospective impact and novelty measures, multilingual and geopolitical mining of Wikipedia, social-media diffusion and political communication, open petition datasets, improved evaluation test collections, and richer measures of influence across scholarly and online information ecosystems.

b998e8e4b7a93c076d7f75d2aa69f1d153058460.text:
### Data-Centric Learning, Search, and Scalable Analytics

This community integrates three themes. First, it develops text, Web, and document analytics, including topic modeling, clustering, classification, active-learning relevance feedback, information extraction, visual wrapper generation, and tree-edit or graph-based similarity. Recent work emphasizes efficient high-recall review, content-quality estimation, and formally characterized wrapping and node-selection languages.

Second, it advances mathematical and semantic information services. Research covers text-and-formula retrieval, presentation/content representations, formula conversion using textual context, mathematical question answering, computable knowledge-base formulas, semantic enrichment, and accessible digital mathematical libraries.

Third, it studies foundations and systems for heterogeneous, scalable data management. Topics include D4M/Accumulo ingestion, provenance, associative arrays, graph and tensor models, polystores, JSON and MongoDB semantics, SQL++, visual and relational query languages, guarded negation, conjunctive and monadic Datalog over trees, and query complexity on streaming or external-memory systems.

Typical methods include probabilistic and deep learning, simulation, feedback-driven review, formal semantics and finite-model theory, algebraic and matrix/tensor operations, graph transformations, tree automata, edit-distance metrics, caching and shared execution, cost-based optimization, benchmarking, and tight lower-bound analysis. Recent trends favor cross-platform query planning, cloud-cost reduction, reusable computation, provenance-aware distributed systems, richer semi-structured models, and mathematically informed, interactive search and QA.

08749821d0e7afe53e013bb16041acf4365b26bb.text:
**Graph-Based Entity Resolution and Multilayer Network Analysis**

This community studies the integration and interpretation of relational data across devices, databases, time, and heterogeneous network layers. Core themes include cross-device user matching; record linkage for historical and incomplete records; genealogical and population reconstruction; temporal clustering; social-role discovery; multilayer community structure; and ranking entities or scholarly artifacts in networked systems. It also examines how structural similarity and interlayer coupling shape communities and dynamic processes.

Typical methods combine attribute- and graph-based linkage, feature engineering, temporal and multilayer clustering, modularity optimization, community and role discovery, consensus clustering, layer-similarity measures, and random-walk ranking with alternative teleportation schemes. Citation-based eigenvector methods, computer vision, and machine learning are increasingly applied to scholarly networks and their visual artifacts.

Recent trends emphasize principled, parameter-robust analysis of multilayer networks; consensus communities that reduce algorithmic and configuration bias; ranking methods less sensitive to teleportation choices; and scalable mining of large scholarly corpora. The community increasingly values systematic taxonomies, experimental guidelines, and transparent evaluation, while addressing heterogeneous entities, missing identifiers, noisy historical data, evolving relationships, and the underuse of figures and other visual scientific information.

c3bd3c3604b5070c32fb136665cfdcdf3a42cdf6.text:
## Online Networks: Diffusion, Influence, and Collective Risk

This community studies how online, affiliation, scientific, and social-physical networks form and evolve, shaping information, products, emotions, opinions, behavior, and collective risk. Core themes include influence, centrality, rich-club and assortative structure, brokers, signed and multiplex ties, community formation, popularity and virality, complex contagion, topic lifecycles, recommendation, knowledge markets, and cross-community mobility. Scientific networks receive particular attention through collaboration diversity, ethnicity, peer-review interactions, citation impact, and paper discovery. Crisis research treats social media as a real-time sensor for events, resources, visual themes, and sentiment.

Typical methods combine community detection, clustering and mixing measures, threshold and contagion models, cascade analysis, agent-based simulation, stochastic control, Hawkes processes, embeddings, topic and sentiment analysis, and large-scale empirical studies. Neural models predict microscopic cascades, popularity, community-specific interests, and emerging trends; matrix factorization incorporates social ties into recommendation. Multimodal, geospatial, and ontology-based systems integrate text, images, sensors, and social data. Network optimization supports polling, intervention, incentives, and containment, while constrained rewiring generates benchmarks.

Recent trends emphasize complex and multiplex diffusion, coupling online with physical and opportunistic mobile networks, multilingual demographic inference, diversity and governance, concept drift, and social feedback across platforms. Applications increasingly target emergency response, marketing, scientific discovery, platform activity, and resilient information delivery.

3bb06bb9ec41fa6d025815f2d3a5ec0f73246c78.text:
## Data Integration, Uncertainty, and Assisted Data Quality

This community studies reliable management of incomplete, noisy, conflicting, heterogeneous, and evolving data. Core themes include probabilistic data fusion and truth discovery—incorporating source reliability, dependence, social context, multiple truths, privacy, and domain conditions—as well as entity and schema resolution using deep representations, graph and taxonomic matching, semantic similarity joins, probabilistic blocking, and human feedback.

Research develops declarative data cleaning and inconsistency management through functional and tuple-generating dependencies, repairs, chase-based reasoning, ontology rules, finite controllability, and complexity analysis. Data curation increasingly addresses Big Data warehouse and API/schema evolution, probabilistic unclean databases, data-diff synthesis, and the empirical impact of dirty data on analytics. Pattern discovery extends to utility-oriented, privacy-preserving, uncertain frequent-itemset, and closed-episode mining.

Provenance supports explanations, why/why-not answers, transaction debugging, auditing, and reproducibility, while knowledge compilation and model counting support probabilistic query evaluation. Typical methods combine probabilistic graphical and Bayesian models, optimization, variational inference, embeddings, neural and gradual learning, crowdsourcing, logical chase procedures, answer-set programming, circuit compilation, and cost-based algorithms.

Recent trends emphasize self-driving and human-in-the-loop curation, limited-label entity resolution, dependence-aware and socially informed trust discovery, integrity verification for outsourced analytics, scalable rule mining over knowledge graphs, and principled trade-offs among utility, privacy, uncertainty, and repair quality.

05a28f3d9d6a2b983e33b3f2a285da1cece0450d.text:
## Semantic Web Annotation and Scalable Data Management

This community combines semantic web infrastructure with scalable data management for big-data and IoT settings. A major focus is Schema.org for publishing machine-readable web content, especially tourism data and services. Research defines domain-specific vocabulary subsets, maps heterogeneous sources into annotations, builds regional knowledge graphs, and exposes annotated Web APIs with Schema.org actions so search engines, chatbots, and intelligent assistants can automatically consume services and complete tasks.

Typical methods include annotation platforms, RDF/graph-database storage, source-to-vocabulary mappings, public knowledge-graph publication, and automated quality assurance. Recent work addresses the scalability and selectivity of publishing dynamic data: context-dependent heuristics determine what, when, and how much information to release, improving performance while limiting server load, network latency, and unwanted disclosure. This extends the community’s emphasis from merely describing content to operationalizing and efficiently distributing it.

The second direction compares NoSQL, relational, and NewSQL systems for volume, variety, velocity, scalable online transaction processing, and IoT workloads. Graph-database simulations for wireless multimedia sensor-network surveillance illustrate application-oriented management of interconnected sensor data. Overall, the community trends toward end-to-end semantic ecosystems combining selective publication, actionable annotations, knowledge graphs, and scalable data infrastructure.

6e5df883b1f96808ffed0423ec0a3fed1082a516.text:
### Scalable Social-Network Analytics and Graph Mining

This community develops computational and theoretical methods for analyzing large, heterogeneous, evolving networks, especially online social, information, communication, infrastructure, affiliation, and bipartite graphs. Major themes include network growth and assembly, community and core discovery, link prediction, graph classification, navigability and distances, diffusion and competing cascades, influence and discoverability, robustness, network design, higher-order cohesion, and structural properties such as clustering, backbones, and butterflies.

Typical methods combine topology with attributes, activity, adoption behavior, and sampled observations. They include threshold and complex-contagion models, game-theoretic and agent-based analysis, random walks and sampling, centrality and link-ranking methods, machine-learning classifiers, stochastic inference and expectation-maximization, probabilistic graph grammars, hyperbolic and geometric random-graph models, spectral and clustering techniques, and path-functional approaches interpolating diffusion and shortest-path navigation. Scalable algorithms address large graph traversal, counting, mapping, and network optimization.

Recent work emphasizes comparative analysis of social-network assembly and institutional evolution; structural and behavioral drivers of homophily, sampling bias, and prediction; topic-specific information spread; coexistence and privacy in competitive diffusion; hyperbolic geometry and higher-order clustering; and applications to product adoption, risk prediction, web crawling, recommendations, collaboration, traffic activity, and network resilience.

416669628583a9c454c0ad25046b1cb1ff15bbde.text:
### Data-Centric Learning, Search, and Scalable Analytics

This community integrates three themes. First, it develops text, graph, and document analytics using probabilistic and deep classification, topic modeling, clustering, k-nearest neighbors, active learning, relevance feedback, and quality estimation under precision–recall constraints. Recent work evaluates sentence-level feedback for high-recall retrieval and studies tree-edit distance and inter-graph node similarity for robust structural comparison.

Second, it advances mathematical and semantic information services. Systems such as MIaS combine full-text retrieval with formula preprocessing, while new methods use textual context to improve formula representation and conversion. Work also includes identifier extraction, faceted mathematical search, accessible MathML, and math-aware question answering linked to Wikidata and symbolic computation.

Third, it builds scalable, heterogeneous data systems. Contributions include D4M.jl and Accumulo ingestion, provenance management for microservices, Graphulo/GraphBLAS-style processing, tensors for polystores, relational lattices, SQL++ semantics for semi-structured data, and Apache Calcite’s extensible query optimization across diverse stores.

Typical methods include matrix, tensor, and associative-array operations; algebraic modeling; graph edit metrics; deep regression; symbolic computation; benchmarking; and modular cost-based optimization. Recent trends emphasize open-source tooling, heterogeneous and semi-structured integration, provenance, context-aware mathematical retrieval, interactive high-recall review, and semantic graph analytics.

745efa4d89ac111e18788f7bc2be2092d4a16aab.text:
**Webometrics, Scholarly Evaluation, and Online Scholarly Communities**

This community studies how scholarly information, impact, and online interactions are measured, ranked, and interpreted. Core themes include bibliometric evaluation through citation counts, h-index and h5-index, cited half-life, highly cited documents, journal and institutional benchmarking, peer-assessment correlations, and comparisons among Google Scholar, Web of Science, Scopus, and Microsoft Academic. Google Scholar receives particular attention as a broad, dynamic but imperfect bibliometric and research-assessment source, including coverage, reliability, document types, profile maintenance, and metric manipulation.

Research increasingly examines open access and scholarly communication: legal and sustainable availability, self-archiving versus publisher pay-to-publish models, national OA indicators, and the use of heterogeneous data sources. Academic social networks such as ResearchGate are assessed for institutional visibility and the validity of platform scores. Other work maps disciplines and scholarly communities from citation profiles and studies delayed recognition (“sleeping beauties”) using patterns such as Benford’s law.

Typical methods are large-scale database and web querying, API and full-text/link analysis, longitudinal and cross-platform comparison, correlation and statistical testing, network visualization, profile-based classification, manual validation and deduplication, and crowdsourced relevance judgments. Recent trends emphasize open science, inclusive coverage, alternative platforms, multifaceted community mapping, and scrutiny of metric validity, comparability, manipulation, and changing citation dynamics.

b973775c643d911e9365fe6abf7db5779df8fdb0.text:
### Social Networks, Influence, and Information Integrity

This community studies how online platforms organize users, shape opinions, and enable manipulation. Core themes include political discourse and elections, polarization, misinformation and credibility, rumors, extremism and hate speech, demographic inequality, public-health communication, commercial spam, fraudulent profiles, and coordinated state-sponsored influence. It also examines community alliances and antagonisms, online collective attention, user relationships, and social-media-based prediction.

Typical methods combine large-scale Twitter, Facebook, Wikipedia, Meetup, review, and security-forum data with graph analysis, crawling and sampling, statistical modeling, and machine learning. Researchers use propagation and interaction features, sentiment and stance analysis, topic and community profiling, linguistic and behavioral bot detection, on-the-fly autogenerated-content classification, latent demographic inference, profile similarity, cross-forum extraction, and honeypots. Studies also evaluate credibility, fact-checking guardians, personalized-feed fairness, API and sampling bias, and targeted interventions such as public-health messaging.

Recent trends emphasize political microtargeting, foreign and extremist influence, fake-news propagation, adversarial communities, phishing and phone-number spam, and scalable detection of low-quality or coordinated accounts. Newer directions include decentralized-web search with privacy-preserving caching, interpretable news-feed design, prediction from aggregated social signals, cross-platform campaign analysis, and measuring how credibility and major events alter attention and hateful speech.

2d4690ef5ab42064ca9e9aba444995ca7bf01b55.text:
### Research Evaluation, Impact, Mobility, and Equity

This community examines how research performance, impact, excellence, and efficiency are defined and assessed across researchers, departments, institutions, and national systems, especially in Italy and comparative European settings. Themes include citation-based indicators, field normalization, rankings and assessment exercises, resource allocation, research quality, and the tension between productivity and meaningful impact. It also studies gender, age, rank, regional inequality, researcher mobility, international knowledge flows, collaboration, scientific diversification versus specialization, academic entrepreneurship and spin-offs, and the effects of high- and low-performing faculty on institutional outcomes.

Typical methods combine large-scale Web of Science and Google Scholar bibliometrics with h-, g-, i10-, MNCS-, citation-weighting, perfectionism, and impact-oriented indicators; citation-curve and citation-window analysis; regression, quantile, distributional, and inequality models; DEA and other efficiency approaches; co-affiliation, mobility, and collaboration networks; field-normalized comparisons; and ranking-agreement analysis. Peer-review taxonomies, expert-register analysis, and decision-support systems complement quantitative evaluation.

Recent trends emphasize researcher- and impact-centered alternatives to “publish or perish,” valuing citations by citing-item influence, benchmarking indicators robustly, integrating qualitative judgment with metrics, mapping global scientific mobility, and evaluating diversification, entrepreneurial activity, and assessment fairness.

839e715dd11fd15e3564aaf3b892f0bf5538849e.text:
## Adaptive, Reliable Data Management for Science and Society

This community develops database systems that remain performant, predictable, verifiable, and responsible as data, workloads, and hardware scale. Core themes include multicore and distributed OLTP, high-contention execution, actor-based in-memory databases, RDMA-era transactions, scheduling, MVCC, serializability, recovery, and latency control. Scientific applications span streaming astronomy, geospatial and multidimensional data, arrays, archives, metadata, provenance, video, and learned representations. The community also addresses stewardship of institutional and “grey” data, balancing open-access mandates with privacy, academic freedom, intellectual property, and accountability, as well as social-media data analysis.

Typical methods combine new execution, storage, indexing, and query-processing architectures with benchmarking and socio-technical studies. Examples include contention-aware scheduling, adaptive recovery, fine-grained snapshotting, imperative-program optimization, shared-I/O batching, spatial and bounded-approximate indexes, declarative video aggregation, and cloud pipelines for low-latency scientific analysis. Verifiable query processing extends trust to blockchain databases.

Recent work emphasizes autonomic optimization: deep reinforcement learning for join ordering and database administration, multi-armed-bandit adaptive query processing, feedback-driven plan selection, and online exploration of physical operators. Trends also include continuous full-lifecycle astronomical analytics, multimodal and video data management, resource-efficient indexing, predictable virtualization, and privacy-aware, auditable open-data infrastructure.

8373571720df0b7e673edfb522664a75c8c73e59.text:
## Data Quality, Trust, and Automated Data Integration

This community studies how to discover, integrate, clean, and assess noisy, incomplete, conflicting, and human-generated data. Core themes include entity resolution and schema matching, truth discovery and source credibility, database inconsistency and repair, uncertain and utility-oriented pattern mining, sequential episode discovery, and web/deep-web extraction. Work also addresses provenance, why/why-not explanations, data impact, and the effects of missing or conflicting values on analytics.

Typical methods combine probabilistic and condition-aware trust models, repair semantics, integrity-constraint analysis, complexity results, approximation, and optimization. Integration uses blocking, identifiers, semantic and taxonomy-based similarity joins, graph and collective matching, learned transformations, gradual or deep representation learning, and one-to-one matching constraints. Web systems employ wrapper induction, recursive tree matching, automatic or mutual supervision, and robust extraction from changing templates.

Human–machine data management remains important: crowdsourced matching, subjective knowledge acquisition, truth assessment, and risk-based verification use worker-error models, confidence estimates, adaptive assignment, and budget or latency constraints.

Recent trends emphasize self-driving data curation, scalable web catalog construction, privacy-preserving utility mining, correlation- and community-aware truth discovery, condition-specific knowledge-graph quality, and minimizing human effort while improving reliability and interpretability.

c821d1d2ad17e322120344364f7d0844a40c9546.text:
## Rich Semantic Models for Cultural and Historical Information

This community develops structured, model-oriented representations of complex cultural, scientific, and historical information. It moves beyond document-centric repositories and simple search toward interconnected descriptions of entities, relationships, activities, mechanisms, states, and scenarios.

Key themes include ontology and semantic-model design, object-oriented modeling, frame semantics, hierarchical representations, and computational support for historical research. The Semantic Modeling Framework represents mechanisms through *Transitionals* and hierarchies of *Aggregates* and *Mechanisms*, with possible implementation in the XFO programming environment. The Human Activity and Infrastructure Foundry models artifacts, their production, and differing aesthetic qualities. Related work develops repositories that represent content directly rather than merely storing documents.

Historical applications include digitized newspaper discovery, structured directories linking local entities to newspaper mentions, and quantitative prosopography. A machine-learning framework automatically constructs people gazetteers from biographies, surviving documents, and secondary sources, enabling collective analysis of ordinary people and their life histories across heterogeneous evidence.

Typical methods combine semantic and ontology engineering, hierarchical and object-oriented modeling, text mining, entity linking, machine learning, and formative user-interface design for exploratory interaction.

Recent trends emphasize automated construction of richly linked historical resources, integrating people, places, artifacts, documents, and contextual evidence to support discovery and prosopographical analysis beyond keyword search.

c5855d7a64b020d8f4432843006d57db4c3bccc3.text:
## Recommender Systems: Robust, Contextual, and Explainable Personalization

**Main themes.** This community studies personalized ranking from sparse, implicit, noisy, and evolving behavior in e-commerce, news, music, education, advertising, healthcare, and user-generated-content platforms. Core problems include sequential and session-based recommendation, cold start, long-tail discovery, playlist continuation, cross-domain and role-aware recommendation, social influence, multimodal content, knowledge-graph reasoning, exploration–exploitation, fairness, and causal impact. Trust, fraud, shilling, adversarial manipulation, and biased feedback remain important concerns.

**Typical methods.** Matrix factorization, Bayesian and pairwise ranking, factorization machines, hybrid content–collaborative models, tensor decomposition, and neighborhood methods remain foundational. Neural approaches increasingly include variational autoencoders, deep feature-interaction models such as DeepFM, attention and memory networks, adversarial training, and deep reinforcement learning or contextual bandits. Graph and embedding methods exploit heterogeneous knowledge bases and support explainable path-based reasoning. Multimodal models combine text, images, audio, and aesthetic features; semantic embeddings address sparse or short text. Causal inference, game-theoretic attack modeling, and robust optimization complement predictive modeling.

**Recent trends.** Work emphasizes multi-action feedback, explicit–implicit fusion, long-tail and cold-start performance, real-time page-wise decisions, fairness, explainability, causal evaluation, and reproducible benchmarking tools for sequential recommendation. Domain-specific systems increasingly target education, healthcare matching, advertising, and expert discovery.

fad92b297043cf48cd6492e7d13d10a4684f3f67.text:
## Scalable Data Integration, Similarity Search, and Trustworthy Curation

This community studies integration and quality improvement for noisy, heterogeneous, and uncertain data. Themes include entity resolution and schema matching, semantic and taxonomic similarity joins, deduplication, data diffs, uncertain frequent-itemset mining, knowledge-graph enrichment and reasoning, truth discovery, and source credibility. It also covers approximate retrieval over billion-scale vectors and visual features, biosequence alignment, and spatial crowdsourcing.

Typical methods combine probabilistic, Bayesian, variational, and reliability models; deep and gradual learning with limited labels; neural entity linking embedded in relational databases; Datalog-based reasoning; blocking, prefix and pigeonring filtering, locality-sensitive hashing, quantization and source coding, learned indexes, MapReduce, and CPU/GPU co-processing. Human-machine workflows use risk-based verification, worker accuracy estimation, crowdsourced schema decisions, and budget-aware spatial assignment. Integrity verification supports outsourced analytics over uncertain data.

Recent trends emphasize dynamic, durable, billion-scale retrieval; compressed-domain reranking and adaptive threshold search; semantic rather than purely lexical matching; scalable exact verification and network-aware aggregation; and automated data curation combining deep learning with human oversight. Increasing attention goes to how dirty data affects downstream models, trustworthy and condition-specific knowledge, social-context-aware truth discovery, fake-news resistance, and efficient cooperation between machines, experts, and mobile crowds.

5020adc6ee599c854c2ac9a4852f1072332879ac.text:
## Reliable Evaluation and Learning for Search and Recommendation

This community studies ranking and recommender systems when behavioral data and evaluation judgments are incomplete, biased, or costly. A central theme is **unbiased learning and evaluation** from implicit feedback: clicks and dwell times suffer from position and presentation bias, while relevance judgments require substantial human effort.

Key methods include counterfactual inference and inverse propensity weighting (IPW), which estimate exposure or click propensities and support unbiased training from logged interactions. Recent work extends these ideas beyond linear rankers and average-rank objectives to LambdaMART-style pairwise learning, deep models, and broad additive metrics such as DCG and Precision@k.

The community also develops probabilistic and active sampling strategies for constructing test collections, Monte Carlo estimators that remain valid with missing judgments, and preference-elicitation interfaces that gather dense judgments and richer user information. In applied settings, it examines sponsored-search ranking with deep reinforcement learning and the gap between offline and online recommender metrics in small e-commerce environments.

Overall, research is moving toward statistically principled counterfactual learning, flexible metric-aware optimization, reduced annotation costs, richer preference data, and adaptive ranking methods aligned with real user and business objectives.

7aadedf450d3d73aa15ab9f91a3e3fce1a4c93c7.text:
### Personalized Recommendation: Robust, Context-Aware, and Multi-Objective Systems

This community studies personalized recommendation for products, media, education, healthcare, expertise, research papers, and local events. Core themes include sparse explicit and implicit feedback, personalized and sequential ranking, cold-start and long-tail discovery, behavioral change, trust and reputation, and combining user, item, social, textual, and contextual signals. Increasing attention is given to privacy, fairness, robustness, and business objectives such as revenue.
