Typical methods range from slope-one predictors, nearest neighbors, matrix and tensor factorization, Bayesian and pairwise ranking, co-clustering, probabilistic graphical models, and signed or bipartite network analysis to autoencoders, variational generative models, factorization machines, deep feature-interaction models such as DeepFM, RNNs, and hierarchical latent-variable systems. Content-aware approaches use semantic text embeddings, reviews, tags, images, aesthetic/style features, and domain knowledge.

Recent trends include hybrid and cross-domain recommendation, active preference elicitation, negative-feedback-aware reinforcement learning, dynamic and online updating, non-uniform treatment of missing data, and interpretable interaction modeling. The community also increasingly addresses adversarial shilling and learned fake-user attacks, reputation-aware filtering, privacy risks, and recommendation effects on users and markets. Specialized applications emphasize educational progression, patient–doctor matching, expert discovery, playlist continuation, and revenue-aware ranking.

a33ceafd93944d42e59577025e9e6ffb4f9debf2.text:
### Online Influence, Integrity, and Platform Governance

This community studies how social platforms organize users, shape political opinion, and enable manipulation. Core themes include polarization, ideological and extremist communities, information bubbles, misinformation, rumors, conspiracy and propaganda narratives, political campaigns and elections, censorship, clickbait, hate and online abuse, demographic inference, activism, and fairness. It also examines adversarial and coordinated actors, including social bots, autogenerated content, trolls, fake followers, spam, fraudulent reviews, and state-sponsored influence operations.

Typical methods combine large-scale Twitter and other platform data with network, diffusion, signed-graph, and community analysis; temporal and behavioral features; sentiment, stance, credibility, and rumor analysis; sparse learning, regression, neural and computer-vision models; topic modeling; sampling-bias assessment; and measurement, experiments, and user studies. Systems include real-time bot and spam detection, fact-checking and guardian recommendation, interpretable and fairness-aware feeds, and intervention-oriented campaigns.

Recent work emphasizes election forecasting and voter-preference inference, cross-platform and state-linked influence campaigns, extremist propaganda, targeted spear-phishing, fringe-to-mainstream diffusion, and event-driven hate speech. Growing attention targets early and on-the-fly detection, partial observability, sampling reliability, demographic and group fairness in ranking and summarization, decentralized privacy-preserving Web infrastructure, and information-curator recommendation.

8a0da197a3d1a5a96e9d929f453c7a90a554c0ce.text:
## Social Media, Spatial Intelligence, and Crisis Response

This community studies how social, mobile, and location-aware data reveal social processes, geographic activity, public opinion, and crisis conditions. Core themes include crisis informatics: detecting emergencies and aid requests, extracting locations, identifying social actions, tracking events, supporting situational awareness, prioritizing alerts, and improving disaster preparedness and response. Urban research examines mobility, commuting, migration and churn, regional identities, place characteristics, facility placement, route planning, and spatial behavior. The community also investigates political polarization, junk news, influence campaigns, bots, media power structures, and online influence.

Typical methods include NLP, toponym resolution, geolocation, sentiment and multimodal classification, topic/event and burst modeling, weak supervision, deep CNN and multiview learning, embeddings, regression, clustering, network analysis, Ising models, minimum cuts, and scalable stream/spatial processing. Systems integrate Twitter, Reddit, Instagram, Flickr, Weibo, mobile and cell-phone traces, news, weather, satellite imagery, sensors, and surveys. Spatial databases support density-based spatiotextual clustering, trajectory simplification, optimal routes, facility location, and range-sum queries.

Recent trends emphasize geolocation without geotags, cross-platform and multimodal sensing, bias correction and external validation, real-time feedback for responders, bot/disinformation detection, and trajectory-aware, personalized geographic services.

ca7e409920cb18d79f0f8b43f5180e20231172d7.text:
## User Interaction and Online Learning in Search

This community studies how search systems learn from and model user behavior, with emphasis on online ranking, image search, and complex result-page presentation. It moves beyond isolated item-level clicks toward list-level feedback, preferences, intents, interaction sequences, and satisfaction signals.

A central theme is online learning to rank from implicit feedback. Methods include policy-gradient learning, online pairwise ranker comparison, and efficient gradient-space exploration. Null Space Gradient Descent restricts exploration to directions not recently discouraged by user interactions, while interleaving and dueling-bandit methods support scalable, safer comparison of rankers; Merge Double Thompson Sampling selects ranker pairs while limiting degradation to user experience.

Other work addresses complex ranking, where systems must jointly infer item relevance and the preferred display order across rich layouts. Evaluation models incorporate clicks, attention, and satisfaction, accounting for useful zero-click interactions and SERP features such as snippets, organized blocks, one-box answers, and side panels.

Behavioral studies examine sparse image-search clicks, two-dimensional layouts, image-search intent, and differences from general web search. The Click Sequence Model uses an encoder–decoder architecture to predict interaction order. Recent trends favor efficient exploration, richer feedback and satisfaction modeling, and joint optimization of ranking and presentation for large-scale online deployment.

9c682d7b62fb9d4042a4e060eacb94386a79a775.text:
**Deep Multimodal Learning for Music and Multimedia Retrieval**

This community studies semantic relationships across music modalities, including lyrics, audio, listener responses, and multimedia representations. Key themes include hierarchical attention for lyric-based genre classification, cross-modal retrieval through deep sequential correlation and shared canonical spaces, and transparent content-based recommendation using interpretable lyric and acoustic features.

Methods increasingly use end-to-end neural architectures, self-attention, temporally structured representations, shared latent spaces, and joint feature/hash-code optimization. Deep cross-modal hashing enables efficient large-scale similarity search across heterogeneous media such as audio, text, images, and video. Recent work emphasizes decorrelating hashing bits to reduce redundancy and improve the quality and efficiency of binary retrieval codes, alongside explicit semantic projections that learn discriminative cross-media representations in Hilbert space.

A recent trend is broadening music semantics beyond audio-derived tags. EEG listener signals can regularize audio models in two-view neural networks, emphasizing perceived meaning, while attention-based lyric and acoustic models support user-facing interpretability. Overall, research is moving from modality-specific or manually engineered features toward learned, decorrelated, semantically aligned representations for classification, retrieval, recommendation, and explanation.

d8b3946a6037ca2b604670e747fb804772f2f5d2.text:
## Recommender Systems: Context-Aware, Multimodal, and Adaptive Personalization

This community studies personalized ranking under sparse, implicit, noisy, heterogeneous, and evolving behavior. Core themes include collaborative, sequential, session-based, news, music, education, healthcare, location, and user-generated-content recommendation; social and semantic networks; cross-domain and cold-start transfer; long-tail discovery; and modeling diverse interactions, substitutes, complements, trust, and user roles.

Typical methods span matrix factorization, Bayesian ranking, factorization machines, tensor decomposition, neighborhood and memory-based models, Markov models, hybrid content–collaborative systems, and neural recommenders. Recent work uses variational autoencoders, attention and recurrent architectures, reinforcement learning, contextual bandits, adversarial training, and deep models for CTR prediction. Representations combine text, images, audio, video, tags, geographic and temporal context, knowledge graphs, and explicit and implicit feedback. Embeddings, semantic topic models, outer-product interactions, and knowledge-graph path propagation support expressive, explainable, and cold-start modeling.

Recent trends emphasize short- and long-term behavioral integration, anonymous and session recommendation, playlist continuation, page-wise ranking, exploration–exploitation, push delivery, and real-time adaptation. Research increasingly addresses long-tail exposure, selection and popularity bias, noisy or unreliable feedback, adversarial and shilling attacks, missing modalities, semantic context, interpretable explanations, diversity, and robust sequence evaluation.

d82e4c95e7a04cd1f8f6e9381e86d13c96c800aa.text:
### Network Ranking and Political-Social Graph Analysis

This community studies graphs and online data to rank entities, interpret influence, and analyze collective behavior. Ranking remains important through PageRank and reduced Google matrices applied to citation networks, universities, Wikipedia, geopolitical relations, and terrorist-group networks. Wikipedia is treated as a large knowledge graph for studying cross-country influence, cultural boundaries, and hidden relationships.

A major newer theme is computational political science. Twitter follower, like, retweet, rumor, and viral-content networks are used to measure campaign effectiveness, voter and topic preferences, information diffusion, demographic responses, polarization, migration between political camps, and ideological communities across elections and legislatures. Signed and multiplex voting networks support structural-balance analysis, community detection, party-fragmentation measurement, and temporal analysis of alliances and antagonism.

Typical methods include random walks and Google-matrix spectra, citation and institutional ranking, sparse learning, topic modeling, regression, convolutional neural networks, computer vision, matrix factorization, diffusion analysis, and temporal network modeling. Signed-graph optimization increasingly uses correlation clustering, frustration and line-balance indices, and exact binary or integer programming.

Recent trends emphasize political polarization and misinformation, fine-grained demographic and gender analysis, multilingual and cross-cultural inference, real-time social-media dynamics, and fairness-aware text summarization.

c418d0769b982f64e701bd37905a91aeba785fa7.text:
### Dynamic, Heterogeneous, and Robust Network Analytics

This community develops computational methods for large, complex, heterogeneous, and evolving networks, including social, information, citation, semantic, knowledge, multiplex, uncertain, bipartite, and hypergraph data. Core themes include node and graph representation learning, community detection, link prediction, similarity and alignment, diffusion, anomaly and fraud detection, centrality, structural comparison, and network sampling.

Typical methods combine topology with attributes, text, temporal events, and interaction semantics. They include random walks, temporal motifs and event graphs, latent-variable graph models and grammars, graph neural networks, matrix-factorization views of embeddings, meta-path-guided learning, feature propagation, semi-supervised learning, and multimodal neural models. Graph comparison and alignment use spectral, topological, graphlet, metric-flow, and edit-distance techniques; higher-order analysis includes cliques, butterflies, and multiway interactions.

Scalability remains central through distributed, streaming, sampling, indexing, sketching, and approximate algorithms for distances, motifs, structural statistics, and recommendation. Recent work emphasizes lossless temporal representations, dynamic link prediction and change analysis, multilayer and cross-domain fusion, sampling-bias correction, semantic entity normalization, and robust detection of coordinated fraud, deception, and adversarial or poisoned data. Applications span web-scale recommendation, citation and subject-label discovery, online-platform integrity, social behavior, ESG analysis, and scholarly knowledge graphs.

6d2559bec278fb298110442ba56649f397c076c1.text:
## Verifying Relational Data-Aware Processes and Artifact Systems

This community studies formal modeling and verification of systems where process behavior and relational data are equally central. Key themes include data-aware business workflows, artifact-centric processes, relational data-centric dynamic systems, database-process integration, and the completeness and quality of information produced by processes. Models represent database updates, artifact lifecycles, task hierarchies, concurrency, and interactions with external services that may introduce fresh data and infinite-state behavior.

Typical methods combine formal process models with database semantics. Foundations include **db-nets**, which extend colored Petri nets with relational databases, and approaches that add dynamics directly to existing relational databases rather than relying on ad-hoc data abstractions. Other work connects artifact-centric models to UML-based methodologies. Verification targets temporal and logical properties, including LTL-FO and first-order μ-calculus variants, as well as query completeness and data-quality conditions. Theoretical studies establish decidability and complexity results for hierarchical and GSM-inspired artifact systems.

A recent trend is toward integrated, practically usable modeling: unifying master data, relational databases, and business-process dynamics, while developing automated tools such as **SPINArt** and **VERIFAS** for verification.

9f8384b3ddbbf2db854cd927f2d66f8d16f73915.text:
## Social Media, Mobility, and Spatial Intelligence

This community studies how social, mobile, and location-aware data reveal public opinion, political communication, influence campaigns, human mobility, migration, urban activity, cultural interaction, environmental context, and consumer behavior. Political research increasingly examines polarization, junk news, disinformation, extremist networks, media power, and coordinated bot campaigns rather than only electoral preference prediction.

Urban and geographic work infers user and home locations, commuting and migration flows, activity timelines, socially meaningful regions, venue demand, cultural geographies, and spatial-textual clusters. It also supports place-aware search, route planning, and analysis of points of interest.

Typical methods include sentiment, topic, hashtag, and content analysis; network analysis, community detection, diffusion and influence modeling, polarization analysis, and bot detection; regression and machine learning; CNNs and multiview neural models for geolocation; Ising models and graph optimization; density-based spatial-textual clustering; probabilistic trajectory reconstruction; embeddings; and bias correction with external validation. Data span Twitter, Reddit, Instagram, Weibo, WeChat, Flickr, mobile-phone logs, GPS and check-ins, news, weather, and reviews.

Recent trends emphasize geolocation without geotags, multimodal and heterogeneous signal fusion, sparse-to-continuous location timelines, representative mobility estimation, real-time influence detection, scalable graph indexing, trajectory compression, and personalized keyword-aware route optimization.

1f8a4fc2212d74a16628c30d362c3eea8d53fa36.text:
### Semi-Metric Networks, Adaptive Knowledge, and Health Data Mining

This community studies how network structure and data-driven analysis support reasoning, recommendation, classification, and information management. A central theme is the relationship between weighted distance graphs and fuzzy or proximity graphs: different transitive closures can produce substantially different network properties, challenging conventional shortest-path assumptions. Semi-metric behavior—where indirect relationships are stronger than direct ones—is exploited for recommendation in user–item and document networks, including MovieLens and networks built from hyperlinks, citations, collaborations, and semantic tags.

Typical methods include graph-closure analysis, shortest-path computation, network-derived distance functions, item- and user-based recommendation, agent-based modeling, and lightweight statistical or linear text-mining models. Biologically inspired systems use T-cell cross-regulation for collective text classification, while TalkMine and @ApWeb adapt vocabularies and information resources through community interaction. Biomedical applications use uncertainty integration and word-proximity networks for abstract classification, protein-pair discovery, and interaction-sentence identification.

Recent work extends these methods to population-scale health-data analysis: city-wide electronic health-record and drug-dispensing data are examined longitudinally to detect drug–drug-interaction patterns, characterize risk factors, and reveal age- and gender-related disparities in medication administration. Overall, the community is broadening from foundational non-metric network analysis toward adaptive, distributed, socially aware, and public-health-oriented knowledge systems.

4fc446fa3165e7d0e9e7b784949f3027a3cd33fd.text:
## Social Media Geolocation, Influence, and Urban Mobility

This community studies how social, location-aware, and user-generated data reveal political polarization, disinformation and influence campaigns, regional identities, migration, urban mobility, cultural activity, and environmental or facility needs. Major applications include geolocating users and posts without explicit tags, reconstructing cross-border and migrant movement, predicting urban-migrant churn, validating mobility models, and supporting city cultural planning. Political work examines junk-news ecosystems, military-targeted propaganda, media power, bot coordination, and influential users across Twitter, Instagram, Facebook, Reddit, WeChat, Flickr, and check-in services.

Typical methods include CNNs and multiview neural networks combining text, profiles, networks, and metadata; heuristic labeling and probabilistic geolocation; weather matching and spatial embeddings; network analysis, influence scoring, link and interaction modeling, and Ising-model inference solved by minimum cut; spatial clustering, trajectory simplification, stochastic timeline reconstruction, population-synthesis bias correction, and out-of-sample validation. Data include sparse geotagged posts, check-ins, social graphs, news links, photos, and telecommunications traces.

Recent trends emphasize geolocation from weak or absent geotags, cross-platform and multimodal inference, scalable continuous location timelines, bias-aware mobility validation, trajectory compression for spatiotemporal queries, coordinated-campaign detection, and translating online signals into migration, urban-planning, and political-information insights.

d10010fe21bedba19a8ef1aa878438be01687bc3.text:
**Information Retrieval: Neural Ranking, Entities, and Scalable Search**

This community advances semantic, entity-aware, personalized, and interactive retrieval. Neural rankers model fine-grained query–document and question–answer matching with attention, CNNs, LSTMs, holographic composition, hyperbolic representations, listwise context, and groupwise scoring. Knowledge-graph semantics, entity salience and sets, concept hierarchies, temporal aspects, author-topic profiles, and complex question facets address richer information needs across scientific, social, email, mobile-app, and personal-memory search.

A parallel focus is structured information access: entity-oriented intents, passage and non-factoid answer retrieval, expert finding in heterogeneous bibliographic networks, table and knowledge-base search, and context-aware point-of-interest recommendation. Domain adaptation, multitask learning, adversarial regularization, auxiliary query clustering, and cost-sensitive training improve robustness under sparse, private, noisy, or long-tail supervision.

Typical infrastructure includes inverted indexes, compressed billion-scale vector search, GPU and cloud partitioning, MapReduce kNN joins, locality-sensitive and thresholded similarity search, spatial and moving-object indexes, and fast evaluation tooling. Learning from interaction remains central through propensity-corrected click learning, online gradient exploration, iterative relevance feedback, and reinforcement learning for sponsored ranking.

Recent trends emphasize hybrid lexical–neural and graph-enhanced retrieval, explainable ranking, direct metric optimization, adaptive display layouts, conversational and assistant search, temporal and contextual personalization, and scalable real-time search over heterogeneous data.

65b15b33f985fc65ad56975f03af9d84d04f45b5.text:
### Dynamic, Heterogeneous, and Robust Graph Analytics

This community develops computational methods for large, complex, uncertain, and evolving networks, including social, information, scholarly, semantic, multiplex, multilayer, bipartite, and hypergraph systems. Core themes include node and graph representation learning, community detection and change segmentation, link prediction, anomaly and fraud detection, network alignment, ranking, graph classification, and higher-order structure such as motifs, cliques, triangles, and butterflies.

Typical methods combine topology with attributes, text, temporal events, and cross-network evidence. They include random walks, Markov and latent-space models, stochastic blockmodels, Bayesian inference, matrix factorization, spectral and modularity techniques, graph grammars, Ricci-flow distances, and neural embeddings including GCNs, autoencoders, and feature propagation. Heterogeneous-network approaches use meta-paths, supra-graphs, motifs, multimodal evidence, and entity normalization; scalable streaming, sampling, and distributed methods support web-scale inference and subgraph counting.

Recent work emphasizes lossless temporal event graphs, inter-event times, temporal motifs, continuous-time embeddings, dynamic link prediction, and joint community/change-point detection. It also advances multilayer fusion, cross-domain recommendation, graph-operator modeling, higher-order clustering, robust anomaly detection, and adversarial attacks or de-anonymization. Applications include scholarly knowledge graphs, citation and collaboration discovery, web-scale recommendation, ESG intelligence, online fraud attribution, and social-media analytics.

5899ae91c98214bb26fee2b51c5626f397bda28a.text:
## Network Diffusion, Influence, and Source Inference

This community studies how information, opinions, epidemics, failures, rumors, tasks, and attacks propagate through social, biological, infrastructure, citation, and cyber-physical networks. Core problems include influence maximization and seed minimization, cascade and source reconstruction, latent-network inference, epidemic containment, rumor and misinformation blocking, election control, and resilient defense under partial or costly observations.

Influence-oriented work selects or recruits seeds to maximize adoption, coverage, revenue, participation, or diverse and equitable information access. Recent settings include adaptive and sequential seeding, multiple rounds and competing cascades, self-activation, coupons and pricing, multiplex and multilayer networks, multifeature diffusion, temporal activity streams, contact adaptation, and strategic attacker–defender interactions. Work also learns influence and hidden structure from cascades, reviews, and interaction data, while addressing homophily, missingness, and fairness across demographic groups.

Typical methods combine independent-cascade, linear-threshold, epidemic, compartmental, metapopulation, Bass, DeGroot-Friedkin, Markov, and continuous-time models with submodularity, approximation and bilevel optimization, adaptive policies, game theory, randomized experiments, centrality, message passing, random walks, sampling, simulation, and representation or machine learning.

Recent trends emphasize fairness and access, scalable billion-edge and streaming algorithms, robust sparse-data inference, higher-order and multiplex structure, adaptive epidemic networks, and socially desirable or strategically resilient objectives.

07669c38d3534557b8ce8b0eb3a0afa793e4b98e.text:
**Information Retrieval: Neural, Entity-Centric, and Interactive Search**

**Main themes.** This community develops relevance modeling and semantic matching for scholarly, web, social-media, email, mobile-app, question-answering, and conversational search. Key problems include entity salience, entity-set and expert finding, temporal entity aspects, complex and non-factoid answer retrieval, fact-check discovery, and personalized academic, location, and sponsored search. It also addresses query understanding, result presentation, and retrieval across heterogeneous domains.

**Typical methods.** Systems combine lexical and probabilistic language models with embeddings, concept hierarchies, knowledge graphs, neural interaction models, attention, CNNs/LSTMs, holographic composition, and hyperbolic representations. Ranking uses multi-task and listwise learning, query clustering, local ranking context, cross-domain adversarial regularization, and explicit optimization of retrieval metrics. Implicit feedback is corrected with propensity estimation and counterfactual learning; online rankers use gradient-space exploration and interleaving. Large-scale retrieval uses semantic hashing, binary signatures, sketching, K-tree clustering, and approximate similarity search. Evaluation relies on benchmark collections, accelerated tooling, and model-agnostic explanations.

**Recent trends.** Research is moving toward end-to-end neural retrieval and answer passage selection; entity- and intent-aware search; conversational and unified app access; temporal, contextual, and personalized ranking; robust transfer across domains; unbiased interactive learning; interpretable ranking; and compact, scalable representations for massive collections.

f559a76d8011b1282a4c092149273c4b18b2bafa.text:
### Graph Querying, Provenance, and Dynamic Graph Management

This community studies systems and foundations for querying, integrating, indexing, and analyzing graph-structured data, spanning RDF, SPARQL, knowledge graphs, property graphs, Gremlin, workflow graphs, and cloud data. Core themes include SPARQL optimization and translation to property-graph traversals, subgraph and conjunctive pattern matching, OPTIONAL and OBDA queries, cardinality estimation, federated or link-traversal querying, and query-aware graph partitioning. Provenance is increasingly central, covering lifecycle management, workflow reproducibility, cloud execution, differencing, privacy-preserving abstraction, segmentation, and graph summarization. Other work addresses property-graph type systems, formal RDF graph models, incremental view maintenance, distributed graph databases, and what-if analytics over evolving data.

Typical methods combine formal semantics, algebraic and relational rewritings, sparse-matrix joins, summary graphs, characteristic structures, partitioning, workload-aware repartitioning, incremental indexes, and graph generators for controlled evaluation. Implementations target relational backends, distributed clusters, cloud platforms, and graph DBMSs such as Neo4j.

Recent trends emphasize interoperability between RDF/SPARQL and property graphs/Gremlin, adaptive partitioning under changing workloads, scalable and explainable provenance summaries, cloud-aware reproducibility, schema governance for evolving graphs, and near-real-time analytics through incremental maintenance and data-in-motion systems.

c6a73ab3b1187cdc9b30d0ce824d6fea4928870d.text:
**Community Detection in Complex and Evolving Networks**

This community studies discovering, interpreting, and evaluating cohesive or dynamically related groups in large, heterogeneous networks. Themes include overlapping, multilayer/multiplex, weighted, signed, attributed, spatial, two-mode, hierarchical, core–periphery, temporal, hypergraph, and simplicial communities, alongside query-dependent community search. It also examines influential and vulnerable nodes, global bridges, low-degree-node inclusion and bias, structural consistency, and communities associated with diffusion, consensus, preferences, or other dynamics. Applications span social media, information and biological networks, recommendation, cybersecurity, voting, geo-social analysis, and large-scale graph mining.

Typical methods include modularity and likelihood optimization, belief propagation, stochastic block models, label propagation, hierarchical and density-based clustering, clique/truss/trapeze and core decomposition, spectral and graph-signal methods, personalized PageRank and diffusion, Markov Stability, vector partitioning, variational autoencoders, and convex optimization. Structure- and semantics-preserving multilayer models, higher-order representations, network completion, and learned resolution parameters support richer settings.

Evaluation emphasizes multi-criteria quality, community size, detectability, consistency across near-optimal solutions, uncertainty, benchmarking, sampling, and bias-aware analysis. Recent trends favor scalable local, seed-based, spatial, incremental, and distributed detection; adaptive multilayer coupling; interpretable cohesive subgraphs; integration of topology, attributes, interaction types, higher-order structure, temporal information, and behavioral signals; and robustness, privacy, and fairness in network data and algorithms.

09178d44295558cbb33f2ed848600e2c08c33c5b.text:
### Scalable Graph Querying, Provenance, and Stream Analytics

This community studies systems and foundations for querying, modeling, integrating, and analyzing RDF, SPARQL, property, provenance, temporal, and large dynamic graphs. Core themes include SPARQL algebra and OPTIONAL processing, RDF–property-graph interoperability, graph type systems and schemas, subgraph and contextual pattern matching, reachability and neighborhood queries, federated and distributed execution, provenance capture and summarization, and continuous queries over graph streams.

Typical methods combine formal semantics, complexity analysis, algebraic translation and rewriting, query decomposition, selectivity- and statistics-driven optimization, sparse-matrix joins, partitioning and query-aware routing, structural summaries, sketches, compression, clustering, and incremental index or result maintenance. Provenance methods use graph segmentation, differencing, abstraction policies, aggregation by provenance types, and cloud-aware capture to support comprehension, disclosure control, and workflow reproducibility. Human-in-the-loop exploration employs surprise, entropy, and contextual relationship models.

Recent trends emphasize high-throughput analysis of evolving and multi-relational streams, time-constrained subgraph detection, approximate querying from compact summaries, continuous neighborhood aggregates, and adaptive distributed execution. The community is also expanding toward schema-governed property graphs, SPARQL-to-Gremlin translation, investigative and cyber-security search, explainable exploration, and provenance-aware data science and scientific workflows.

81452355bc4fe2d2cea5b34ab1d0ebd0f1fefc2b.text:
**Information Retrieval: Neural, Entity-Centric, and Interactive Search**

This community advances semantic retrieval, relevance modeling, and scalable search infrastructure. Neural ranking combines lexical signals, dense embeddings, attention, recurrent/convolutional and interaction-based architectures, knowledge-graph semantics, and entity salience. Applications include passage and non-factoid question answering, personal-memory and email search, academic and expert finding, social-media retrieval, sponsored search, and unified mobile or conversational search.

Entity-centric research covers entity-oriented intents, salient and dynamically related entities, temporal aspect recommendation, entity-set scientific search, actionable services, and intent knowledge bases. Structured access includes tables, knowledge graphs, taxonomies, and data lakes. Personalization uses author-topic profiles, query/task modeling, and user context.

Typical methods include end-to-end, multitask, listwise, groupwise, and cost-sensitive learning to rank; query expansion, relevance feedback, local ranking context, and query decomposition; heterogeneous-network embeddings; hyperbolic and holographic representations; adversarial domain regularization; and reinforcement learning for online or sponsored ranking. Counterfactual propensity estimation and unbiased learning address click bias, while online exploration and interleaving optimize interaction.

Recent trends emphasize mobile, voice, and conversational interfaces; richer entity and intent understanding; adaptive, dynamic, and personalized retrieval; complex presentation layouts; robust cross-domain neural models; explainable post-hoc ranking; and standardized, efficient evaluation.

a0ff6b7e8a45c26ba3f63e69f2adfed489a9e6db.text:
**Multilayer Networks, Community Evolution, and Social Behavior**

This community studies multiplex, multilayer, temporal, and heterogeneous networks, where social, communication, semantic, professional, mobility, and cross-platform relations jointly shape structure and behavior. Core themes include multilayer centrality, layer similarity and entanglement, link prediction, homophily and social closeness, influence and information diffusion, epidemic containment, recommender and search-result fusion, and organizational or behavioral profiling.

A major focus is community structure and evolution. GED, SGCI, dynamic Louvain, Infomap, modularity maximization, and stochastic block models identify and track groups, while transition chains and comparative evaluations support forecasting. New work connects multilayer community detection with statistical network inference and develops supracentrality for directed temporal coupling and evolving node importance.

Typical methods include graph centrality and proximity indices, asymmetric local-clustering features, tensor decomposition and clustering for query-based anomaly detection, spectral and statistical models, association-rule mining with Apriori-style pruning, trajectory simulation, and empirical analysis of phone, social-media, news, email, mobility, and synthetic networks.

Recent trends emphasize principled measurement of interlayer similarity, integrated prediction across layers, temporal centrality trajectories, realistic human-mobility generation, anomaly and deception detection in heterogeneous networks, and extracting personality, social closeness, content-propagation, and behavioral signals from digital traces.

07965e12dcb69fa4bc5358fd5e60a745591e4285.text:
**Scalable Search, Indexing, and Social Data Analytics**

This community develops efficient methods for searching, querying, and analyzing large, heterogeneous, multidimensional, and user-generated datasets. Core themes include compressed inverted and integer indexes, high-dimensional and vector indexes, bitmap operations, hierarchical spatial structures, graph pattern retrieval, data cubes, and fuzzy or order-incomplete databases. Compression emphasizes differential, partitioned variable-byte, and other locality- and SIMD-aware representations.

Query-processing research covers top-k, cosine-threshold and approximate nearest-neighbor search, skyline and aggregate queries, multidimensional pruning, OLAP operations, fuzzy and possible/certain query answers, labeled-graph patterns, and representative or diversity-conscious ranking. Systems increasingly address social tagging, folksonomies, collaborative search, microblogging, expertise location, and community question answering.

Typical methods combine algorithmic complexity analysis, indexing and pruning structures, relational and graph representations, information extraction, similarity and tag-distribution modeling, clustering, empirical benchmarking, and hardware-aware parallel implementation. Flat combining, anytime algorithms, learned or adaptive ranking, and network analysis recur.

Recent trends emphasize social and collaborative information seeking; mining user-generated tags and attention networks; flexible, imprecise, and multidimensional analytics; scalable high-dimensional retrieval; and fairness, coverage, equity of attention, and diversity in rankings and recommendations.

2d37b326c8a92047c833c54671cd5ef7072a424f.text:
**Semantic Search, Knowledge Graphs, and Social Ranking**

This community studies how to organize, link, search, and rank heterogeneous, user-generated, and structured information. Major themes include multilingual entity linking and disambiguation; Wikipedia- and Freebase-derived knowledge resources; semantic navigation and query expansion; fuzzy, probabilistic, and partially ordered data; graph-pattern and top-\(k\) retrieval; expertise, talent, and group search; and collaborative information seeking.

A strong focus is ranking for people, documents, entities, and products. Topics include personalized and intent-aware search, category- and network-based entity ranking, credibility, representative results, expert recommendation, attention allocation, and fairness in rankings. The community also studies social activity, talent flows, topical expertise, and collaborative search behavior.

Typical methods combine NLP and large-scale annotation, entity resolution, graph centrality and link analysis, clustering, collaborative filtering, matrix factorization, learning-to-rank, threshold and any-\(k\) algorithms, vector indexing, set-function optimization, stochastic control, and user- or crowdsourced evaluation. Datasets include Wikipedia, professional and social networks, search logs, and large web collections.

Recent trends emphasize scalable multilingual knowledge extraction, personalized professional search, unbiased click-based learning, fairness and coverage auditing, cost-efficient IR evaluation, explainable and credibility-aware ranking, and flexible search over uncertain or imprecise data.

8bb435a72bcdcd91c1003a65458fd0c4b217f968.text:
### Graph Querying, Integration, Provenance, and Analytics

This community studies systems and foundations for querying, integrating, validating, summarizing, and analyzing graph data, including RDF, SPARQL, property graphs, knowledge graphs, provenance graphs, XML, ontologies, and IoT data. Core themes include SPARQL algebra and OPTIONAL processing, federated and link-traversal querying, RDF–property-graph interoperability, graph pattern matching, reachability and navigational queries, ontology-based access, query cardinality estimation, provenance abstraction, and incremental view maintenance. Work also addresses heterogeneous and evolving data, property-graph type systems, schema definition, incomplete or inconsistent content, and distributed graph analytics.

Typical methods combine formal semantics, complexity analysis, relational algebra and SQL reduction, Datalog-style reasoning, algebraic and heuristic query reordering, sparse-matrix joins, partition-based summary graphs, graph summarization and cardinality synopses, embeddings and ranking, and certified implementations. Systems use property-graph/Cypher and Gremlin traversals, SPARQL translators, scalable distributed engines, provenance policies, and graph/time-series processing.

Recent trends emphasize practical interoperability between RDF and property graphs; explainable provenance summarization and controlled disclosure; adaptive, approximate, and statistics-light query optimization; scalable distributed and IoT analytics; schema-aware property graphs; zero-knowledge Web link traversal; incremental graph views; and prescriptive “what-if” analytics over evolving data.

aa13ab81c56e7b8e2e09b3cfd9096f12847c4505.text:
### Social Networks, Misinformation, and Platform Integrity

This community studies how online platforms shape political discourse, collective beliefs, information diffusion, collective action, and public services. Core themes include polarization, echo chambers, controversy, opinion dynamics, misinformation and rumor verification, media bias, clickbait, hate speech, harassment, propaganda, extremist communities, and election influence. Platform-integrity work addresses bots, trolls, autogenerated content, spam, fake profiles, pathogenic users, astroturfing, coordinated state campaigns, ranking effects, and manipulation of feeds and popularity metrics. Fairness, viewpoint diversity, gender and demographic inequality, counterspeech, and risks to critical infrastructure are growing concerns. Applications increasingly include education, disaster response, hydroinformatics, and scientific-news quality.

Typical methods combine large-scale Twitter and other platform data with network analysis, cascade and temporal modeling, surveys, content, linguistic, sentiment, and stance analysis, and controlled or simulated interventions. Methods include graph clustering, embeddings, label propagation, weak and semi-supervised learning, transfer learning, multilingual and federated models, anomaly detection, causal inference, optimal stopping, source ranking, and opinion-dynamics models.

Recent trends emphasize real-time and early malicious-user or misinformation detection; ideology and influence tracing; cross-platform and state-sponsored campaigns; interpretable, fairness-aware, and diversity-promoting ranking; federated privacy-conscious detection; and interventions such as fact checking, crowdsourced flags, counterspeech, supportive bots, and resilient information sharing.

1d3e918ba897cef3af8503e5b8860d509a09e54f.text:
### Semantic, Temporal, and Collaborative Digital Archives

This community develops durable, interpretable, and discoverable representations of scholarly, historical, and web-based knowledge. Core themes include semantic layers over digital and newspaper archives, web-archive curation and aggregation, persistent and location-independent identification, provenance, annotation, compound objects, and linked knowledge graphs. Particular attention is given to historical people and organizations, multilingual events, cross-lingual timelines, entity histories, and formal representations of scientific claims.

Typical methods combine RDF, SPARQL, Open Annotation, Memento, provenance models, and repository or Research Object frameworks. Systems enrich archived documents with structured metadata and entity links, rank semantic-layer results, generate event timelines, and support collaborative collection building and exploration. Machine-learning methods construct gazetteers for quantitative prosopography and estimate entity relatedness using temporal and corpus-specific context. Formal claim languages, such as AIDA, aim to make scientific assertions machine-actionable for aggregation, consistency checking, fact checking, question answering, and semantic search.

Recent trends emphasize human-centered, evaluation-driven archive interfaces; multilingual and event-centric exploration; annotations as first-class web objects; privacy-aware integration of private, personal, and public archives; and richer, formally structured scholarly knowledge. Persistent challenges include heterogeneous schemas, incomplete and language-diverse archives, evolving resources, and balancing accessibility with sensitive archival content.

8c80627a26fca03ed85de93f629ea05e34d5fded.text:
**Efficient Search, Indexing, Ranking, and Responsible Data Systems**

This community develops scalable, compact, and expressive methods for search, indexing, querying, and data-driven selection. Core topics include compressed inverted and integer indexes, partitioned Variable-Byte encoding, n-gram indexing, learned index structures, and bitmap- or SIMD-friendly representations. High-dimensional retrieval covers cosine-threshold and approximate nearest-neighbor search using inverted indexes, hierarchical structures, binary codes, and multi-index hashing.

Query and ranking research spans labeled-graph top-*k* pattern retrieval, anytime algorithms, skyline and Pareto analysis, rank-regret representatives, expert recommendation, rank fusion, and order-incomplete data with possible and certain answers. It also addresses fuzzy relational data, flexible querying, and database formulations of voting and social-choice problems.

Typical methods combine theoretical complexity and optimality analyses with learned or heuristic indexes, query decomposition, compression, hashing, blocking, and empirical benchmarking. Hardware- and memory-conscious execution remains important.

Recent trends emphasize learned compression, approximate and time-bounded retrieval, scalable high-dimensional search, flexible querying over uncertain or imprecise data, and integrating social-choice semantics with databases. Responsible retrieval is expanding through exposure-aware fairness, demographic auditing, dataset-coverage assessment, and mechanisms balancing relevance, satisfaction, and equitable attention.

cf2ceef91b8fe522ff4f496e32133c0d6583f00e.text:
### Preserving, Modeling, and Exploring Evolving Digital Knowledge

This community studies durable, interpretable, and discoverable information across scientific, cultural, historical, news, social-media, and web contexts. Core themes include digital repositories and compound objects; semantic modeling of entities, events, claims, activities, infrastructures, and state changes; persistent identification, provenance, versioning, rights, reproducible citation, and traceable research objects; and collaborative curation and exploration of evolving web and news archives. It also develops formal representations of scientific claims and quantitative gazetteers for prosopography.

Typical methods combine OAIS, Fedora, OAI-PMH, RDF/RDFS, SPARQL, PROV-O, PAV, nanopublications, annotation models, AIDA, arcp URIs, and ontology/object-oriented design. Systems provide semantic archive layers, ranking and structured queries, entity-centric search and visualization, multilingual and time-aware analytics, and researcher-facing interfaces. Large-scale crawl, query-log, news, citation, and microblog analyses use entity linking, topic modeling, sentiment aggregation, supervised classification, regression, and co-occurrence networks.

Recent trends emphasize corpus- and time-specific relatedness, event and entity analytics, collaborative archive construction, private/public archive integration, richer claim and package provenance, and social/live-web signals. Challenges include heterogeneous schemas, incomplete archives, multilinguality, unstable search, long-tail entities, privacy, and preserving meaning across versions.

64b65550f9f95964e3ddba2e31c9fb1635096c62.text:
### Robust, Explainable, and Fair Sequential Recommendation

This community studies personalized recommendation from sparse, implicit, explicit, noisy, heterogeneous, and multimodal feedback. Core themes include long- and short-term/session behavior, evolving interests, cold start and long-tail discovery, cross-domain and hybrid filtering, diverse interests, social and producer influence, fairness, and temporal, spatial, and multi-behavior modeling. Applications span music, news, education, healthcare, food, products, playlists, POIs, advertising, and next-basket or next-item prediction.

Typical methods include matrix/tensor factorization, metric learning, Bayesian and pairwise ranking, factorization machines, topic and ontology models, VAEs, autoencoders, memory networks, neural collaborative filtering, DeepFM, recurrent and bidirectional Transformer models, and memory-augmented graph neural networks. Systems fuse ratings, clicks, purchases, reviews, text, images, audio, aesthetic/style features, and contextual or cascading behaviors. Knowledge graphs, semantic propagation, meta-learning, and shared cross-domain representations address sparse and cold-start settings. DPPs, maximal-clique optimization, re-ranking, and approximate relevance graphs support diverse set recommendation and scalable retrieval. Reinforcement learning targets online sequential and advertising decisions.

Recent trends emphasize popularity-bias mitigation, catalog coverage, provider and user fairness under continual updates, interpretable review- and style-based explanations, multimodal and context-aware representations, few-shot adaptation, robust session modeling, and evaluation of both user utility and business value.

a7e7941cda0dc9de39fdee8788a12f2454b29b9f.text:
## Scalable Data Management and Intelligent Query Processing

This community studies efficient, scalable data-intensive systems, emphasizing relational query optimization, cardinality and resource estimation, join ordering, worst-case-optimal and incremental processing, and analytics over structured, semi-structured, uncertain, and probabilistic data. It also addresses distributed and hybrid analytics, event streams, data integration, provenance, knowledge graphs, interactive exploration, and machine-learning workloads.

Typical methods combine formal complexity, tractability, communication, and space–time analyses with practical systems techniques: sampling and sketches, histograms, deep-learning and reinforcement-learning cost models, learned data structures, MILP and System-R-style optimization, factorized joins, adaptive execution, parallel aggregation, and memory-, I/O-, network-, and energy-aware processing. Probabilistic methods include lifted inference, knowledge compilation, decomposition and width-based representations, uncertainty-aware ranking, and relational representations of incomplete data. Declarative abstractions include SQL, Datalog and TGDs, functional query languages, provenance, event-processing languages, and operators for video and IoT analytics.

Recent trends include integrated learning over relational data, interactive query construction and benchmarking, what-if provisioning, explainable/provenance-aware analytics, adaptive complex-event processing, secure outsourced querying, evolving data warehouses, automated data-structure design, and declarative neural video analytics. Intelligent automation increasingly spans learned optimization, cloud workload management, adaptive resource provisioning, and approximate or progressive answers.

bd24a261ac49d6e7438f305d7a0e3281125490e4.text:
## Scalable Data Management, Query Processing, and Analytics

This community studies how to make data-intensive systems faster, scalable, adaptive, secure, explainable, and easier to use. Core themes include relational query optimization—join ordering, cardinality estimation, worst-case-optimal joins, incremental maintenance, inequalities, resilience, provisioning, and constant-delay enumeration—alongside distributed, cross-platform, multi-query, and interactive query processing. Emerging areas include LSM and array storage, streaming time-series and graph pattern matching, urban spatiotemporal analysis, visualization, provenance, and declarative video analytics.

Typical methods combine formal complexity, communication, and space–time analyses with MILP, reinforcement learning, learned models, adaptive sampling, sketches, histograms, hypertree decompositions, geometric data structures, caching, materialized views, typed linear algebra, and hardware acceleration. Systems increasingly support secure and verifiable queries over outsourced, encrypted, and blockchain data, as well as explanation, auditing, dataset documentation, and reproducible benchmarking.

Recent trends emphasize tighter database–machine-learning integration: learning directly over relational data, ML-as-a-service, human-in-the-loop experimentation, neural-network inspection, model-based data pricing, and FPGA-assisted analytics. Other trends include approximate query processing, browser/cloud split execution, automated data-structure design, cross-platform optimization, raw-array analytics, and resource-efficient processing of heterogeneous, multimodal, streaming data.

2a2150e6a56ef7681e764b50ec5d7914c7379d4f.text:
## Scalable, Intelligent, and Trustworthy Data Systems

This community develops scalable data management, querying, and analytics for relational, graph, streaming, semi-structured, array, probabilistic, and scientific data. Core themes include query optimization and cardinality estimation, join ordering, worst-case-optimal and functional aggregate queries, incremental and batched processing, interactive exploration, data provisioning, metadata and provenance, and machine learning over relational data. Emerging concerns include secure and verifiable querying over outsourced, encrypted, and blockchain databases, as well as data marketplaces and model-based pricing.

Typical methods combine formal complexity and decomposition analyses with sampling, sketches, histograms, factorized and incremental view maintenance, adaptive and learned indexes, LSM optimization, caching, sparse tensors, declarative extraction, probabilistic programming, and deep learning or reinforcement learning for optimization and analytics. Systems target in-memory, multicore, GPU, RDMA, cloud, workstation, and heterogeneous clusters, including actor-based OLTP and scientific data services.

Operational research emphasizes contention-aware transactions, concurrency control, replication, recovery, synchronization, resource adaptation, and energy-efficient infrastructure. Streaming and evolving data motivate continuous analysis, time-series pattern matching, quantile estimation, and real-time astronomy. Recent trends favor integrated database–ML platforms, neural video analytics, autonomic data-structure design, secure hardware, interactive benchmarks, hypergraph tooling, and energy- and hardware-aware execution.

f8ccfbd4e9f56bc4e41c02770c2dd9ca403f54af.text:
## Scalable Representation and Analysis of Complex Networks

This community develops methods for representing, comparing, generating, aligning, and mining large, dynamic, heterogeneous, multilayer, multimodal, signed, and higher-order networks. Themes include temporal link formation and state-sequence discovery, evolving communities and roles, graph similarity and alignment, graph coarsening, structural spectra and motifs, anomaly and fraud detection, adversarial robustness, knowledge-graph construction, multimodal social-media and urban-dynamics modeling, recommendation, bug localization, drug response, and community question answering.

Typical methods combine latent-space and stochastic dynamic graph models, probabilistic graph grammars, spectral and density-of-states analysis, matrix factorization, random walks, k-truss and core decomposition, graph distances, integer programming, and graphlet/motif analysis. Representation learning increasingly uses GCNs, attention, autoencoders, adversarial training, multimodal and multi-view embeddings, heterogeneous information networks, text-enhanced propagation, role- and polysemy-aware representations, and asymmetric embeddings for complementary relations. Scalable graph partitioning, coarsening, compression, streaming, and distributed algorithms address web-scale computation.

Recent trends emphasize continuous-time and timeslice-free modeling, cross-modal urban analytics, unsupervised and scalable network alignment, black-box attacks and poisoning defenses, explainable and imbalance-aware learning, robust graph compression, reproducible embedding benchmarks and evaluation toolkits, and graph-based applications in e-commerce, education, software engineering, biomedicine, and academic knowledge graphs.

92e64c118e3a4649cd440595623684c40300869a.text:
## Adaptive Data Warehousing, Big-Data Analytics, and Benchmarking

This community studies performance engineering for warehouses and complex, heterogeneous data systems. Core themes include XML warehousing—tree-pattern querying, XOLAP, summarizability, workload-aware fragmentation—and physical design through automatic index/materialized-view selection, query clustering, frequent-itemset mining, cost models, and workload analysis. Cloud and distributed settings balance latency, throughput, scalability, and monetary cost.

Benchmarking is expanding from configurable XML, object-oriented, and warehouse simulators (DWEB, XWeB, OCB, DOEF/DEF) to broad big-data and stream-processing evaluation. New work emphasizes application-specific, multi-4V data generation; feature-preserving synthetic scaling; diverse and evolving workloads; web-search benchmarks; and comparisons of Storm, Spark, and Flink using throughput and windowed-operation latency. Specialized text benchmarks target top-k keyword and document processing.

Methods also cover adaptive organization and workload analysis, scalable classification and document architectures, exact top-k inference for separable relational models, and temporal/probabilistic clustering of social-media content. Applications span healthcare, archaeology, web data, epidemics, and online communities, including models linking media activity to influenza transmission.

Recent trends favor automated, workload-aware adaptation; reproducible, domain-specific benchmark suites; scalable synthetic data; real-time stream and social-event analytics; and richer evaluation of changing, multimodal, and high-volume workloads.

e313a00dc74f240a664094d94e3d629646e45b0a.text:
## Opinion Dynamics, Influence, and Network Structure

This community studies how network structure shapes opinions, information flow, influence, navigability, and robustness. Major themes include consensus, polarization, controversy, homophily, signed or antagonistic ties, stubbornness, heterogeneous susceptibility, private versus expressed opinions, and feedback between opinions and recommendations. Applications include partisan media, ideological affinity, viewpoint discovery, echo chambers, filter bubbles, and diversity of information exposure.

A growing focus is competitive diffusion: threshold adoption of multiple products, coexistence, winner-take-all dynamics, strategic and bribery-resistant equilibria, privacy-preserving influence, and mitigating overexposure in viral marketing. Structural topics include influence-based centrality, information centrality optimization, link prediction and community detection under missing edges, latent similarity inference, and dynamic proximity search.

Typical methods combine graph theory, dynamical systems, control and stability analysis, stochastic processes, Markov chains, spectral and matrix methods, random walks with restart, optimization, approximation algorithms, Bayesian or statistical inference, and text, voting, or stance analysis. Methods increasingly address partial observations, incomplete and dynamic graphs, and large-scale computation.

Recent trends emphasize scalable and exact-or-approximate RWR, network reconstruction and robustness, strategic and privacy-aware diffusion, multi-product adoption, susceptibility-aware opinion models, and algorithmic interventions that increase viewpoint diversity while reducing polarization.

cbfd7db939dc34c14bc87f6b62132c00570cdc14.text:
## Network Influence, Opinions, and Structural Robustness

This community studies how network structure shapes information flow, influence, opinions, polarization, controversy, and resilience. Themes include consensus and disagreement, Friedkin–Johnsen and bounded-confidence dynamics, heterogeneous susceptibility and stubbornness, homophily, signed and private-versus-expressed opinions, multi-topic logical coupling, and stochastic clustering. It also examines political ideology inferred from voting and journalists’ networks, partisan media ecosystems, viewpoint discovery, echo chambers, filter bubbles, exposure diversity, and overexposure in viral marketing.

Typical methods combine graph theory, dynamical-systems and control analysis, Markov chains, Laplacian and spectral techniques, random walks, matrix centralities, influence-based and group centrality frameworks, optimization, approximation algorithms, and stochastic or mean-field analysis. Empirical studies use voting records, Twitter, Facebook, news, and communication data, analyzing temporal, topical, stance, sharing, and exposure patterns. Network inference employs vector-autoregressive estimation, similarity observations, missing-edge prediction, and community detection.

Recent work emphasizes randomized gossip opinion models, influence estimation from partial observations, nonlinear and continuous-time dynamics, and interventions that alter susceptibility or add edges to improve centrality. Increasing attention targets centrality’s discriminating power, stability under degree-preserving randomization and incomplete data, and robustness of community scores. Optimization increasingly seeks diverse information exposure, reduced polarization, controlled reach, and mitigation of reputational harm from overexposure.

d5a2c96160ae4fd74dea72c502f40bedfdb82c36.text:
**Information Retrieval: Neural, Semantic, Personalized, and Interactive Search**

This community develops retrieval and ranking systems that combine lexical matching, pretrained neural semantics, knowledge graphs, structured data, and user context. Core themes include deep query–document and cross-document interaction, BERT-based passage and document reranking, contextual and concept embeddings, entity and attribute identification, query expansion and suggestion, heterogeneous-network search, conversational question answering over knowledge graphs, and personalized e-commerce, email, mobile, social, academic, biomedical, and multimedia search. Scope increasingly includes dataset, table, open-government-data, and image retrieval, as well as non-factoid and complex-answer QA.

Typical methods include pointwise, pairwise, listwise, multitask, differentiable, adversarial, and reinforcement-learning objectives; multi-stage candidate generation and reranking; attention and hierarchical networks; pseudo-relevance feedback; graph embeddings; weak and positive-unlabeled supervision; domain adaptation; hashing for scalable approximate-nearest-neighbor search; and cost-sensitive or propensity-corrected learning from clicks. Evaluation emphasizes latency, efficiency, online experimentation, interaction quality, and reproducible benchmarks.

Recent trends include pretrained language models constrained by long documents and small datasets, lightweight personalization, semantic transfer across modalities, graph-aware neural ranking, explainability with feature attribution, unbiased and variance-reduced online learning, optimized multileaving, mutual-influence-aware ranking, and corpus-level agents for goal-oriented interactive search. Retrieval is becoming more contextual, conversational, structured-data-aware, and production-oriented.

0568cd41cc1e7e44ade0330d31fea6df58eb1f7e.text:
### Dynamic, Temporal, and Multilayer Graph Analysis

This community studies how evolving, multilayer networks are modeled, queried, and exploited. Core themes include stream graphs, link streams, time-varying networks, and temporal quantities that capture interaction timing, duration, ordering, and layer structure. These models support analysis of journeys, connectivity, density, communities, centrality, and shortest paths, including foremost, fastest, and latency-aware distances. Multilayer representations increasingly combine social, semantic, and interactional information, including narrative elements in movie scripts; layer centralities reveal the importance of layers in large human-interaction and flight datasets.

A second theme is scalable graph querying through reachability and shortest-path indexes and labeling schemes. Methods include interval, hierarchical, distribution-based, hub, independent-set, and lightweight dynamic labels. Recent work parallelizes Pruned Landmark Labeling with vertex-centric computation, SIMD multicore architectures, and batch execution while preserving exact results.

The community also examines diffusion and influence through contagion, opinion spreading, dynamic monopolies, gossip, trust-aware recommendation, and information mobilization. Applications use fine-grained contact streams, temporal recommender features, sentiment, and content.

Recent trends emphasize multilayer temporal semantics, efficient link-stream distance and latency algorithms, layer-aware centrality, parallel exact indexing, and richer integration of semantic information into dynamic network models.

d20a10eb0e98cae9d363c37776babd8faf030a66.text:
## Uncertainty, Data Quality, and Explainable Query Processing

This community studies database systems beyond complete, consistent, deterministic data. Major themes include probabilistic and uncertain databases, query answering, aggregation, joins, top-\(k\) ranking, possible-world semantics, incomplete information, and probabilistic models of dirty data. Work addresses correlations, functional dependencies, repairs, and statistical beliefs about intended data.

A second theme is data quality and integrity: inconsistency measurement, cardinality repairs, normalization, privacy-preserving utility mining, and schema evolution across heterogeneous Big Data sources. Explanations and provenance remain important, especially graph-based why/why-not provenance and efficient provenance-aware query optimization.

The community also investigates expressive reasoning over knowledge graphs and ontologies, including existential rules, TGDs, Datalog, contextual RDF, regular path queries, and integration of machine learning with logical reasoning. Tractability and undecidability frontiers are characterized through finite controllability, chase acyclicity, treewidth, automata, and query determinacy.

Typical methods include answer-set programs, repairs, knowledge compilation into d-DNNF/decision diagrams, lifted and weighted model counting, branch-and-bound with dissociation bounds, structural decompositions, fixed-parameter algorithms, and neural graph mining. Data mining now emphasizes utility-oriented and privacy-aware patterns, closed episodes with simultaneous events, noise-resistant episode screening, and Horn-rule discovery in massive graphs.

Recent trends emphasize scalable approximate inference, principled data integration under schema evolution, privacy–utility tradeoffs, and hybrid statistical–symbolic knowledge systems.

c2b90fc15c353633895e078ce8bc868954318312.text:
## Scholarly Networks, Ranking, and Discovery

This community studies scholarly communication, information retrieval, and knowledge organization through bibliographic, textual, behavioral, and social data. Core themes include author-name disambiguation and entity resolution; coauthorship, citation, and author–paper networks; scholarly ranking, impact, prestige, and popularity; publication recommendation and expert search; exploratory and multimodal retrieval; and semantic-web vocabularies and linked knowledge-organization systems. It also examines technology emergence in patent networks, researcher career trajectories, and university data stewardship, balancing open access with privacy, academic freedom, and intellectual property.

Typical methods combine bibliometrics, network construction and community detection, PageRank and weighted/random-walk algorithms, HITS-like iterative scoring, centrality, stochastic block models, and temporal prediction. Identity resolution uses probabilistic similarity, feature overlap, clustering, blocking, and benchmark evaluation. Retrieval studies use session logs, eye tracking, mouse-fixation signals, user studies, relevance judgments, and stratagem-level analysis; graph-based fusion integrates textual, visual, and metadata signals. Large-scale mining uses MapReduce and distributed frequent-itemset algorithms, while semantic integration uses SKOS and linked data.

Recent trends emphasize prestige-aware and future-influence ranking, dynamic prediction of emerging technologies and literature, novelty and trajectory modeling, scalable online retrieval, visual scientometric mapping, multimodal and semantic discovery, and responsible stewardship of open scholarly data.

d1c3ba49e3ddcce31a8497466565069353dd641d.text:
**Scholarly Metrics, Search, and Open Knowledge Systems**

This community studies how scholarly and web-based information is measured, organized, retrieved, and disseminated. Bibliometric work examines citation counts, h-index and h5-index, cited half-life, highly cited documents, journal and institutional benchmarking, citation contexts, reference growth, and discipline mapping. It compares Google Scholar, Web of Science, and Scopus while assessing coverage, bias, and metric validity.

A major expanding theme is open, collaboratively generated knowledge infrastructure, especially Wikipedia and Wiktionary. Research analyzes their semantic coverage, categories, classifications, multilingual annotations, editorial organization, and transformation into machine-readable databases, thesauri, ontologies, and linked-data resources. These resources support entity linking, ontology matching, synonym discovery, query expansion, and knowledge-oriented search.

Methods include large-scale crawling and database querying; DOI, web, social-media, and click-log analysis; graph centrality and influence modeling; longitudinal bibliometrics; citation-context analysis; statistical and correlation testing; source triangulation; semantic annotation; learning-to-rank; and meta-evaluation of search metrics using user preferences.

Recent trends include multilingual and cross-platform knowledge graphs, personalized and expertise-oriented search, bias-aware evaluation of rankings and click data, integration of scholarly, social, and collaborative signals, richer classification and linked-data standards, and more inclusive assessment of research impact and lawful open access.

f849be01f10b1818d078407964be9af3062bda2c.text:
## Scalable, Declarative Data Management and Analytics

This community develops scalable, efficient, and usable systems for data-intensive computation. Core themes include relational query optimization—join ordering, cardinality estimation, worst-case-optimal and similarity joins, incremental maintenance, functional aggregates, and resource-aware planning—alongside graph pattern matching, RDF and knowledge-base reasoning, streams, time series, JSON/document processing, and visual or multimedia analytics. Declarative paradigms include SQL, Datalog, relational algebra, JSONiq, document spanners, and typed or factorized representations.

Typical methods combine formal complexity and decomposition analyses with practical distributed systems. Techniques include compact indexes and tries, adaptive indexing and cracking, LSM/KV-storage optimization, sparse and factorized computation, sampling and mergeable sketches, probabilistic and imprecise query answers, approximate query processing, constant-delay enumeration, metadata cleaning and entity resolution, and incremental rule or query maintenance. Implementations target multicore, GPU, FPGA/reconfigurable hardware, Spark, cloud, and heterogeneous polystore environments.

A strong thread integrates databases with machine learning through SQL-based training, relational learning, textual embeddings, ingestion-time enrichment, and statistically aware inference optimization. Systems also support dataset discovery, interactive visual exploration, model and data documentation, and multi-stakeholder evaluation.

Recent trends emphasize hardware-accelerated joins and graph operations, automated physical design, hierarchical visual-content filtering, adaptive processing for evolving or uncertain data, stable cloud resource planning, and unified declarative workflows spanning analytics, machine learning, and heterogeneous data.

9699afcd85274fa3f9ddfb7cf07bf283908e58e2.text:
## Scholarly Literature Mining and Knowledge Discovery

This community focuses on making scholarly information discoverable, structured, and trustworthy. Major themes include metadata and document-structure extraction, semantic publishing, citation analysis, knowledge-graph construction, and automated search over scholarly collections. New work extends extraction to author-contribution statements, affiliations, bibliographies, tables, figures, and other article components.

A parallel theme is detecting text reuse and problematic scholarly practices. Studies examine copied citation sentences, reuse across scientific articles, plagiarism in arXiv, and large-scale duplicate or contradictory content in Wikipedia and other corpora.

Typical methods combine hybrid rule-based and statistical information extraction, natural-language processing, near-duplicate detection, MinHash and Jaccard similarity, citation and network analysis, and distributed MapReduce pipelines. Systems such as CL Scholar automate crawling, indexing, knowledge-graph mining, and natural-language querying, while OCR++ provides reusable open-source extraction infrastructure.

Evaluation remains important, particularly for extraction accuracy, reuse detection, and quality assessment. Research emphasizes reducing false positives, identifying writing and metadata patterns, and analyzing reuse at corpus scale.

Recent trends include automated processing of continuously arriving literature, richer scholarly knowledge graphs, large-scale distributed text-reuse analysis, open-source extraction frameworks, and broader integrity and provenance checks beyond conventional full-document plagiarism.

793e9545a4bd6c80c68ebb3ad1ce303aaebe5d3a.text:
## Scholarly Networks, Discovery, and Research Infrastructures

This community studies scholarly communication, knowledge organization, and research infrastructures through network science, bibliometrics, and information retrieval. Core themes include author-name disambiguation, coauthorship and citation structure, researcher and publication impact, expert finding, recommendation, exploratory search, user interests, and ranking beyond raw citation counts. It also addresses classification systems, SKOS and Linked Data, semantic vocabularies, metadata curation, novelty and scientific growth, and responsible stewardship of open and “grey” university data under privacy, academic-freedom, and intellectual-property constraints.

Typical methods include citation and collaboration graphs, centrality and network-based indicators, stochastic block models, PageRank-like ranking, temporal embeddings, LSTM prediction, probabilistic similarity, agglomerative clustering, learned blocking, multilayer perceptrons, and statistical evaluation. Retrieval studies use session logs, queries, mouse fixations, gaze and eye tracking, relevance judgments, user studies, and visualizations of search strategies. Disambiguation research increasingly exploits curated corrections, researcher identifiers, and large automatically constructed test collections.

Recent trends include predictive modeling of citation and technology-cluster growth, temporal measurement of scientific novelty, citation-aware retrieval and recommendation, personalized and exploratory digital-library search, neural and unsupervised identity resolution, and semantic-web migration of traditional knowledge-organization systems. Research is also emphasizing reproducible benchmarks, metadata quality, and privacy-conscious open-data governance.

6975098e0a7ed719702bebc806fc8ec98063bdae.text:
## Opinion Influence, Social Learning, and Online Engagement

This community studies how networked interaction shapes opinion formation, belief diffusion, influence, and collective sensing. Core themes include Friedkin–Johnsen opinion dynamics, social conformity, private versus expressed opinions, ideological affinity, asymmetric influence, weakly connected networks, and “mind-control” by influential agents. It also examines Bayesian social learning, information cascades, misinformation and data incest, ratings, and how network interaction affects estimation of hidden states.

A major application area is online-media behavior, especially YouTube engagement and popularity. Studies relate views, likes, comments, subscribers, click rates, watching time, titles, tags, thumbnails, and creator–user interactions, while modeling popularity evolution and multivariate dependence. Social sensing connects diffusion processes with event localization, advertising, disaster response, and financial sentiment.

Typical methods combine graph theory, stochastic and continuous-time dynamical systems, random gossip models, influence-matrix estimation, vector autoregression, Bayesian updating, signal processing, statistical inference, feature selection, simulation, and copula-based dependence analysis. Empirical work uses large-scale social-media and video datasets alongside political voting records.

Recent trends include learning influence from partial observations, characterizing influence on directed or weakly connected graphs, preventing redundant information reuse, integrating sensing with decision-making, and predicting engagement and popularity from coupled content and social features.

322303eb400cc5eb6ba00a065aedad1fbbd01995.text:
## Network Influence, Opinion, and Navigability

**Main research themes.** This community studies how network structure shapes opinions, beliefs, influence, information access, and robustness. Opinion-dynamics research extends DeGroot and Friedkin–Johnsen models to signed, antagonistic, homophilous, bounded-confidence, Bayesian, noisy, stubborn-agent, and community-structured interactions. Models increasingly represent weighted-median updating, backfire and biased assimilation, private versus expressed opinions, random actions, and multiple interdependent topics, analyzing consensus, polarization, fluctuations, stability, and quasi-consensus. Applications include recommender feedback, political-affinity inference from voting records, and monitoring changing information sources.

A second theme concerns influential nodes, links, and paths. Work develops axiomatic, influence-based, group, and information centralities; studies their stability under noisy or degree-preserving randomization; and optimizes centrality, coverage, discoverability, and resilience through edge additions or strategic placement of stubborn agents. Research also addresses adversarial attempts to conceal covert-network leaders, partial-observation influence estimation, and planted-core recovery in hypergraphs.
