Themes include citation indicators, field normalization, rankings, research assessment and funding, peer review, resource allocation, productivity versus meaningful impact, gender differences, collaboration, diversification versus specialization, academic entrepreneurship, and institutional inequality. It also examines editorial-board structures and the relationship between scholarly communication venues.

Typical methods combine Web of Science, Google Scholar, Crossref, OpenCitations, and large-scale co-authorship or editorial-board networks with h-, g-, i10-, MNCS-, citation-weighting, and impact-oriented indicators. Regression and predictive models, citation-window and citation-curve analysis, peer-review concordance, distributional and inequality models, DEA, field-normalized comparisons, and network analysis are common. Books and DOI-to-DOI citations extend coverage beyond journal articles.

Recent trends emphasize open citation infrastructures and citations as first-class data, early prediction of long-term impact, and rigorous testing of bibliometric proxies against peer-review outcomes and research exercises. Attention is growing to gaming and unintended incentives, including self-citation and strategic behavior under evaluation regimes, while collaboration, gender equity, editorial interlocking, and the limits of specialization and ranking prediction remain central.

03c63844adce1d9697b68748945468acef9389d0.text:
### Social Media, Political Influence, and Information Integrity

This community studies how online platforms shape public opinion, political behavior, collective attention, and information flows. Core themes include electoral preferences and campaign tactics, polarization and antagonism, misinformation, fake news, propaganda, trolls, bots, hate speech, spam, fraud, and coordinated or pathogenic users. It also examines popularity and meme dynamics, user-generated-content engagement, recommendation, and social media applications in emergencies and hydroinformatics.

Typical methods combine large-scale Twitter, YouTube, Facebook, news, and communication data with network, community, temporal, propagation, and linguistic analysis. Researchers use sparse learning, topic modeling, regression, convolutional and transfer-learning models, unsupervised stance clustering, weak and semi-supervised labeling, crowd signals, anomaly and loosely synchronized-behavior detection, dynamic game-theoretic community detection, ontology-based filtering, and epidemic-style prevention models. They infer preferences, demographics, stances, credibility, influence, and suspicious behavior while modeling conflict and popularity growth.

Recent work emphasizes election manipulation and disinformation campaigns, fine-grained analysis of likes, follows, retweets, and audience preferences, weakly supervised fake-news detection, and proactive misinformation mitigation. Other trends include early prediction of content popularity, biologically inspired diffusion models, cross-platform news influence analysis, automated spam and hate-speech detection, and unsupervised or multimodal methods for studying political and social behavior.

ec7ab74b117a9645018758dcd60c2f64fdd71dc4.text:
**Community Detection in Complex and Evolving Networks**

This community studies discovering, interpreting, and evaluating cohesive, dynamic, and role-based groups in large, heterogeneous networks. Themes include overlapping, multilayer, weighted, signed, attributed, spatial, temporal, two-mode, hierarchical, core–periphery, hypergraph, and higher-order communities, as well as query-dependent, influential, vulnerable, and bursting-community search. It also addresses node roles, bridges, diffusion and information cascades, public–private graphs, partially aligned networks, and privacy-preserving community deception.

Typical methods include stochastic and degree-corrected block models, geometric and latent-channel models, belief propagation and message passing, modularity and modularity-density optimization, spectral and graph-signal methods, label propagation, hierarchical and density-based clustering, clique/truss/core decomposition, personalized and heat-kernel PageRank, diffusion, motif analysis, and nonlinear or game-theoretic optimization. Joint models support shared structure across heterogeneous non-aligned graphs, while multilayer models capture spatial and time-dependent roles.

Evaluation emphasizes detectability, phase transitions, stability, uncertainty, vulnerability, bias, robustness, self-validation, synthetic parameter tuning, and multi-criteria quality measures. Recent trends favor scalable local, seed-based, distributed, deterministic, incremental, and adaptive methods; richer integration of topology, attributes, interaction types, geometry, temporal behavior, and higher-order structure; and adversarial attacks, defenses, privacy, and robustness in community discovery.

c67b884e4197f77c292ee9a39b768dc5466feca8.text:
**Multilayer Networks, Dynamic Centrality, and Social Record Analytics**

This community studies multiplex and temporal networks integrating communication, mobility, physical proximity, online activity, and other heterogeneous relations. Major themes include multilayer community structure, layer similarity and entanglement, homophily and social closeness, evolving node roles, identity and record linkage, genealogical reconstruction, behavioral inference, and network-based epidemiological monitoring.

Typical methods include modularity and stochastic block models, dynamic mixed-membership models, temporal clustering, supracentrality and PageRank variants with time-dependent or marginalized teleportation, block-matrix representations, and interlayer-similarity link prediction. Researchers also use association-rule and frequent-itemset mining, feature-based classification, negative sampling, probabilistic record fusion, hidden Markov models, and trajectory or proximity analysis. Data span social-media, mobile-phone, genealogy, Wikipedia, virtual-economy, and population records.

Recent trends emphasize scalable analysis of evolving multilayer systems; principled comparison and fusion of network layers; dynamic ranking under changing external interests; predicting missing cross-layer links; modeling individual behavioral roles and personality from smartphone traces; and reconstructing family or population histories from heterogeneous archives. Mobile sensing is increasingly used for sparse-observation proximity analysis and individual-level infection modeling, while network methods are expanding into virtual-goods lifecycles and data-driven social analytics.

9482aeabf3d803b7231f706fe9d4f0b2d9330ffd.text:
**Multilayer Networks, Centrality, and Social Diffusion**

This community studies multiplex, temporal, and heterogeneous networks in which social, communication, mobility, physical, and cross-platform ties interact. Core themes include multilayer community structure and layer similarity, evolving node roles, centrality trajectories, link prediction, identity and record linkage, social closeness, and network-based epidemic modeling.

Typical methods combine modularity optimization, stochastic block models, mixed-membership models, clustering and community-evolution analysis, tensor and spectral techniques, local-neighborhood similarity, and interlayer structural features. Centrality research extends PageRank through time-dependent teleportation, parameter marginalization, and supracentrality with directed coupling. Diffusion and infection are modeled using graph-coupled hidden Markov models and proximity observations from mobile phones. Association-rule mining and itemset methods broaden the community toward relational pattern discovery, while behavioral features from smartphone data support personality and social-tie inference.

Evaluation uses social-media, mobile-call and proximity, browsing, Wikipedia, transport, communication, and other real or synthetic multilayer datasets.

Recent trends emphasize scalable analysis of evolving networks, principled comparisons between modularity and probabilistic community models, interlayer-aware link prediction, dynamic importance driven by external interests, heterogeneous-network anomaly and pattern discovery, and fine-grained inference of social behavior and disease spread from sparse sensing.

06336f56997c0e14fcf6a8f1982c4a253e30ca0f.text:
### Social Network Dynamics, Diffusion, and Risk

This community studies how online, organizational, and scientific networks form, evolve, and shape behavior. Themes include information, emotion, attention, and misinformation cascades; meme popularity and engagement; influence, polarization, community structure, complex contagion, indirect transmission, multiplex interaction, and systemic risk. It also examines scientific collaboration, citation copying, researcher productivity, and diversity’s effects on connectivity and impact. Applications span social media, political communication, disaster response, marketing, mobile networks, and public-interest interventions.

Typical methods combine graph-theoretic analysis—centrality, assortativity, modularity, homophily, temporal paths, cascade topology, and multidimensional outlier detection—with large-scale empirical studies, statistical models, agent-based simulations, and machine learning. Increasing use is made of continuous-time and tie-oriented network models, Hawkes and epidemic/self-exciting processes, latent-variable and Poisson productivity models, graph neural networks, attention and sentiment analysis, and POMDP-based influence optimization.

Recent work emphasizes evolving, continuous-time, partially observed, and higher-order networks; tie decay, global drift, indirect interactions, and heterogeneous attention; and prediction of popularity, impact, demographics, and participation. Polarization, opinion complexity, annotation bias, multimodal crisis intelligence, emotion dynamics, and interventions constrained by uncertainty, cost, and governance are growing priorities.

a59ad91fbc10903b912110003c04343753d29fdd.text:
## Data Integration, Uncertainty, and Reliable Data Quality

This community studies reliable management of incomplete, noisy, conflicting, heterogeneous, and evolving data. Core themes include entity resolution and consolidation—from blocking and matching to canonical “golden records”—schema and ontology alignment, semantic annotation of tabular data, syntactic pattern discovery in columns, and similarity search over strings, sets, graphs, and high-dimensional vectors. Applications span open geospatial knowledge bases, outsourced analytics, fact checking, and causal algorithmic fairness.

Research develops declarative data cleaning and inconsistency management through dependencies, repairs, chase-based reasoning, graph rewriting, probabilistic databases, and database repair. It also addresses data and query testing through mutation-killing dataset generation, explanation of disagreements across datasets, provenance, lineage, and temporal-probabilistic joins. Model counting and complexity analysis characterize incomplete databases, conjunctive queries, resilience, Shapley values, and path queries.

Typical methods combine Bayesian and Markov-logic models, generative and neural representations, knowledge-base lookup, genetic programming, crowdsourcing, causal reasoning, logical rules, blocking/filtering, hashing, partitioning, GPU indexes, and cost-aware algorithms.

Recent trends emphasize automated and unsupervised end-to-end integration, heterogeneous-schema blocking, scalable approximate similarity search, explainable and fairness-aware repair, semantic understanding of unlabeled tables, and principled selection of data to clean or verify under uncertainty.

464969b47347f98878a44cf599d720502e1b9bf8.text:
**Graph-Based Retrieval, Entity Resolution, and Multilayer Network Analysis**

This community studies relational data integration, search, ranking, and interpretation across heterogeneous databases, documents, devices, time periods, and network layers. Core themes include record linkage and genealogy search; information retrieval and document-list fusion; query reformulation and pseudo-feedback; spam, deception, and fact-checking; temporal role and community evolution; multilayer structure, interlayer similarity, and link prediction; and dynamic ranking.

Typical methods combine attribute- and graph-based linkage, association-rule mining, language models, term-frequency normalization, cluster-based retrieval, graph propagation, probabilistic and sliding-window data fusion, tensor decomposition, anomaly detection, modularity optimization, stochastic block models, temporal clustering, mixed-membership role models, and multilayer centrality. PageRank-style methods use dynamic or evolving teleportation, parameter marginalization, and supracentrality formulations.

Recent trends emphasize scalable analysis of evolving and heterogeneous networks; robust ranking that adapts to changing external interest; retrieval systems that exploit corpus and document relationships; and multilayer prediction based on cross-layer similarity. The community also increasingly addresses noisy or deceptive user-generated content, incomplete historical records, and principled evaluation of data-fusion systems through open, reproducible benchmarks.

7adffaf47d16b85f2b3ca08a8e552e3ca0c56eb1.text:
## Scalable Entity Resolution and Trustworthy Data Curation

This community studies integration and quality improvement for noisy, heterogeneous, uncertain, and semi-structured data. Core themes include entity resolution and deduplication, schema and semantic matching, metadata cleaning, dependency discovery, statistical constraints, truth discovery, knowledge fusion, fact-checking, and data-quality effects on downstream machine learning. Applications span scholarly metadata, web and RDF data, social networks, and unstructured text.

Typical methods combine blocking and filtering schemes, token and string similarity, probabilistic and generative models, Markov logic networks, sparse-regression and graphical-model structure learning, neural representations, knowledge-base lookup, and distributed or massively parallel processing. They also use holistic clustering, query-driven sampling, transfer and active learning, interpretable risk analysis, and constraint-based error detection. Human-machine workflows support crowdsourced ranking, hierarchical truth inference, budget-aware verification, and implicit content curation.

Recent trends emphasize automated, schema-agnostic, and heterogeneous-data integration at scale; learned blocking with limited labels; semantic and contextual rather than purely lexical matching; distributed optimization that accounts for communication costs; and auditable cleaning measured by statistical distortion as well as error reduction. Increasing attention goes to selecting which data to clean, diagnosing errors through query histories, connecting cleaning to model performance, and combining automation with targeted human oversight.

1f92f16fb30b8ac1b5c20a87feb445adc8f55dea.text:
## Scholarly Impact, Discovery, and Digital Communication

This community studies how scholarly work is disseminated, discovered, discussed, curated, and evaluated beyond traditional citation counts. Themes include altmetrics and societal impact; relationships among citations, usage, readership, social-media attention, and peer assessment; disciplinary, geographic, and document-type variation; scholarly identity and author metrics; open access, repositories, preprints, theses, gray literature, books, and derivative publications; and knowledge-graph-based discovery, reviewer recommendation, and research mapping.

Typical methods combine Web of Science, Scopus, Dimensions, Google Scholar, Crossref/OpenCitations, arXiv, Mendeley, repositories, publisher platforms, Twitter, Facebook, news, policy, and Altmetric data. Researchers use correlation, regression, factor analysis, coverage and validity studies, surveys, interviews, network analysis, topic modeling, sentiment analysis, text similarity, and comparisons with peer or case-study assessments. Computational approaches include scraping and search-strategy design, entity matching, NLP, visual-feature analysis of figures, graph databases, personalized PageRank, classification, recommendation, and interactive portals. Crowdsourcing and decentralized curation are emerging approaches.

Recent work stresses that online indicators are heterogeneous, incomplete, private, discipline-dependent, and often measure attention or dissemination rather than impact. Studies increasingly analyze Facebook reactions and hidden activity, hashtag-topic networks, visual communication, books and gray literature, and open citation infrastructure. Personalized, multimodal discovery systems and transparent reviewer or content recommendation are expanding alongside preprint and early-view publishing.

0b57bc84c1fc6c796b3bded9604c50a9e7084e52.text:
## Social Media, Spatial Intelligence, and Crisis Response

This community studies how social, mobile, transactional, and location-aware data reveal social behavior, geographic activity, public opinion, health, consumption, and crisis conditions. Core themes include crisis informatics—detecting emergencies, extracting locations, filtering relevant reports, tracking events, and supporting response—as well as urban mobility, transportation resilience, traffic optimization, trajectories, migration, and spatial behavior. It also examines political and health sentiment, misinformation, demographic and socioeconomic attribute inference, online influence, and consumption patterns. Emerging applications include food, health, and recipe recommendation, personalized interventions, and knowledge-base content and structure recommendation.

Typical methods include NLP, multilingual and domain-adapted embeddings, toponym resolution, geolocation, sentiment and demographic classification, topic/event/burst modeling, weak supervision, active learning, deep and multimodal models, graph-based features, recommender systems, regression, clustering, network and dynamic-network models, and utility mining. Systems integrate Twitter, Instagram, Reddit, mobile and banking traces, news, weather, satellite imagery, sensors, surveys, and knowledge bases. Spatial and graph databases support trajectory and subtrajectory clustering, mobility simulation, route and facility optimization, and community discovery.

Recent trends emphasize standardized geolocation evaluation, geotagging-bias analysis, cross-lingual and cross-platform sensing, bias-aware annotation, real-time disaster filtering, personalized health services, and scalable analysis of dynamic mobility and socioeconomic networks.

814afadd83906dd545225542ab4fbb6fe55ec7ee.text:
## Data Quality, Integration, and Trustworthy Data Management

This community studies how to discover, integrate, clean, and assess noisy, incomplete, heterogeneous, and human-generated data. Core themes include entity resolution and consolidation, schema matching and semantic annotation, record linkage, data-quality repair, provenance, uncertainty, probabilistic query answering, and fact-checking. Applications increasingly involve scholarly metadata, web tables, geospatial knowledge, social-media streams, and crisis-response data.

Typical methods combine blocking and similarity joins, edit-distance indexing, locality-sensitive hashing, maximum-matching constraints, learned linkage rules, generative and neural representations, and distributed column or schema embeddings. Data cleaning uses integrity constraints, optimization, Markov logic, probabilistic models, and selective verification. Uncertainty is handled through possible-world representations, model counting, and principled top-k semantics. Human-in-the-loop systems model annotation error, adapt schedules, prioritize alerts, and control budget, workload, or latency.

Recent trends emphasize end-to-end and scalable entity resolution, automated and weakly supervised matching, multimodal crisis intelligence, ontology- and knowledge-graph-based integration, evolving data warehouses, and robust extraction from noisy sources. The community is also expanding toward causal database repair for algorithmic fairness, bias-aware annotation, privacy- and reliability-conscious data curation, and systems that minimize human effort while improving interpretability and trust.

ba21383d1f8a9470a3a2eeb53cd6ea6d904a05d0.text:
### Online Influence, Integrity, and Platform Governance

This community studies how platforms organize users, shape political opinion, and enable manipulation. Core themes include polarization, ideological and extremist communities, echo chambers, misinformation, rumors, conspiracy and propaganda, elections, censorship, clickbait, hate and abuse, demographic and group fairness, and news-source quality. It also examines coordinated actors such as bots, trolls, pathogenic accounts, fake followers, spam, and state-sponsored influence operations, alongside information diffusion during emergencies and environmental disasters.

Typical methods combine large-scale Twitter, news, and cross-platform data with network, diffusion, dynamic-community, signed-graph, and stance analysis; temporal and behavioral features; sentiment, credibility, factuality, and conflict modeling; topic modeling; NLP and computer vision; regression, neural, semi-supervised, unsupervised, and transfer-learning models; and causal inference. Intervention systems include crowd- and weak-supervision fact-checking, expert triage, optimal-stopping and influence-minimization algorithms, federated detection, source ranking, and supportive counter-speech bots.

Recent trends emphasize election forecasting and ideology tracing, cross-national and state-linked influence campaigns, early detection of harmful accounts and misinformation, polarized-crowd collaboration, targeted commenting, and automated assessment of news quality and bias. Growing attention targets real-time mitigation, limited labels, explainable and fairness-aware ranking and recommendation, popularity-induced bias, and privacy-preserving distributed learning.

d950cdc6efb85331e838e9334ed4ac32a8919e55.text:
### Social Networks, Misinformation, and Platform Integrity

This community studies how online platforms shape political discourse, collective beliefs, information diffusion, polarization, echo chambers, and collective action. Core topics include misinformation, rumors, propaganda, media bias, fake reviews, clickbait, hate speech, harassment, extremist and alt-right communities, election influence, bots, trolls, astroturfing, state-sponsored campaigns, and coordinated manipulation. It also examines privacy leakage, censorship and moderation, vandalism in collaborative knowledge bases, health misinformation, self-harm discourse, and credibility of news and public information. Fairness, demographic inequality, viewpoint diversity, and the representation and sampling of online debates remain important concerns.

Typical methods combine large-scale Twitter, Reddit, Facebook, Gab, Wikipedia, and cross-language platform data with network analysis, community detection, cascade and temporal modeling, graph labeling, embeddings, linguistic, sentiment, stance, topic, and identity analysis. Machine-learning approaches include weak, semi-supervised, multilingual, federated, adversarial, geometric-deep-learning, multi-task, and ordinal models, alongside anomaly detection, source ranking, credibility appraisal, controlled crowdsourced experiments, and opinion-dynamics or influence models.

Recent trends emphasize real-time and adversarial bot and misinformation detection; cross-platform, multilingual, ideological, and state-campaign analysis; message distortion and context-aware credibility; interpretable, privacy-conscious, fairness-aware moderation and summarization; and proactive interventions including fact checking, crowdsourced flags, counterspeech, supportive automation, and principled debate sampling.

d51228902bcd10c54aaf6b6a00af1186d5fcb19f.text:
### Social Networks, Influence, and Information Integrity

This community studies how online platforms organize users, shape opinion, and enable manipulation. Core themes include misinformation, fake news, rumors, credibility and fact-checking; political discourse, elections, polarization and controversy; hate speech, extremism, trolls and pathogenic accounts; fraudulent profiles, fake reviews, clickbait and coordinated campaigns; and information diffusion during emergencies and other anomalous events. It also examines evolving communities, low-connectivity users, interaction structure, collective attention, stance, ideology, and social-media-based prediction.

Typical methods combine large-scale Twitter, news, review, and platform datasets with graph analysis, dynamic and game-theoretic community detection, crawling, sampling, temporal-event mining, statistical modeling, and machine learning. Researchers use propagation, retweet, linguistic, sentiment, stance, topic, motif, and behavioral features; unsupervised clustering, label propagation, weak and semi-supervised learning, transfer learning, causal inference, and neural models. They also develop crowd-signal fact-checking, optimal-stopping and influence-minimization interventions, communicability-based graph modification, federated learning, and source-quality ranking.

Recent trends emphasize scalable and early misinformation detection, coordinated or loosely synchronized influence, state-sponsored election interference, adversarial camouflage, and cross-language or cross-community analysis. Newer directions include dynamic ideology tracking, diversity-aware recommendations, news factuality and bias assessment, emergency information analysis, and applications of social data to environmental and disaster response.

6eb09b0212476bca5f3acc7fb90bf8ef4b83e530.text:
## Social Networks, Mobility Analytics, and Digital Behavior

This community studies how online social, behavioral, spatial, and interaction data reveal influence, polarization, information diffusion, cultural practices, health discourse, mobility demand, and user behavior. Key applications include political communication, signed relationships, adoption and recommendation, ride-sharing and facility placement, burst detection, food and health conversations, and understanding navigation and collaboration on the Web.

Typical methods include signed-network analysis, structural-balance and frustration measures, community and core–periphery detection, influence and reciprocity modeling, graph partitioning, integer and quadratic programming, nonlinear spectral methods, and error-correcting formulations. Other approaches use matrix factorization, Bayesian hypothesis comparison, Markov chains, probabilistic diffusion and adoption models, mobile proximity sensing, synthetic trace generation, and network-based recommendation. Spatial and temporal analytics include density-based spatio-textual clustering, distributed subtrajectory clustering, trajectory-stream burst detection, road-network optimization, and scalable sequence or utility mining. Data include social graphs with positive and negative ties, retweet and interaction networks, mobile sensors, geo-tagged streams, check-ins, Web trails, reviews, and large-scale Instagram or Twitter discourse.

Recent trends emphasize signed and multilayer network structure, scalable streaming and subtrajectory analytics, multimodal spatial-text mining, explainable influence and diffusion analysis, bias-aware sensing, social recommendation, synthetic data, and translating digital traces into urban, political, health, and cultural insights.

8e0c5f18109e93ade227ff924b17f650b0525134.text:
## Recommender Systems: Adaptive, Multimodal, and Fair Personalization

This community studies personalized ranking and set recommendation under sparse, implicit, noisy, heterogeneous, and evolving behavior. Core themes include collaborative, sequential, session-based, music and playlist, fashion, marketplace, group-activity, social, location-aware, and user-generated-list recommendation; cross-domain and cold-start transfer; long-tail discovery; complementary and combinatorial recommendations; and modeling diverse interactions, substitutes, social ties, and user roles.

Typical methods include matrix, metric, tensor, Bayesian, and neural factorization; hybrid content–collaborative models; Markov and recurrent networks; transformers such as BERT4Rec; graph neural networks with memory; multi-task learning over cascading behaviors; reinforcement learning and contextual bandits; meta-learning; variational autoencoders; adversarial training; ontology and knowledge-graph models; and DPP or clique-based optimization for diverse or exact-size sets. Representations fuse text, images, audio, video, aesthetic features, tags, transaction context, geography, time, social networks, and click or purchase feedback.

Recent trends emphasize short- and long-term interest modeling, anonymous-session and next-basket prediction, playlist/list continuation, real-time retrieval, and approximate large-scale inference. Increasing attention targets popularity and provider fairness, smooth exposure updates, profit-aware objectives, explainability, style and diversity control, social/group coordination, robustness to noisy data, cold start, and interpretable multimodal representations.

bccac60a0d966de0e9de29dcda965b90b95874db.text:
### Robust, Explainable, and Fair Sequential Recommendation

This community studies personalized recommendation from sparse, implicit, explicit, noisy, heterogeneous, and multimodal feedback. Core themes include session and lifelong behavior, evolving interests and demands, cold start and long-tail discovery, cross-domain and shared-account recommendation, social and producer influence, market-basket and next-item prediction, diversity, fairness, and temporal, contextual, and multi-behavior modeling. Applications span commerce, music, news, advertising, jobs, and other online services.

Typical methods include matrix/tensor factorization, metric learning, Bayesian and pairwise ranking, factorization machines, topic and ontology models, autoencoders, heterogeneous neural networks, recurrent and Transformer sequence models, latent-state models, and graph neural networks for complex session transitions. Systems fuse clicks, purchases, ratings, reviews, text, images, audio, knowledge graphs, trust, and contextual signals. Shared representations, dual transfer, multi-task learning, semantic propagation, and distillation address sparsity, cold start, and efficient retrieval. DPPs, re-ranking, binary codes, and approximate relevance graphs support scalable and diverse recommendation.

Recent trends emphasize lifelong and robust session modeling, novelty and demand awareness, interpretable path- and tree-based explanations, causal/incremental-effect optimization, contextual bandits and multi-stage reinforcement learning for online decisions, temporal popularity-bias mitigation, fairness and calibration, real-time deployment, and more rigorous reproducibility and online evaluation.

cb83ac68c86c4602984ae09034f4ba1771287040.text:
## Recommender Systems: Adaptive, Diverse, and Explainable Personalization

**Main themes.** This community studies personalized ranking and recommendation under sparse, implicit, noisy, and evolving feedback across e-commerce, news, music, fashion, travel, education, advertising, and social platforms. Key problems include session and sequential recommendation, cold start, long-tail discovery and popularity bias, playlist and basket continuation, multimodal and style-aware recommendation, social and group activity planning, cross-domain matching, fairness for users and producers, explainability, and balancing user utility with business value.

**Typical methods.** Foundational approaches include matrix and metric factorization, Bayesian and pairwise ranking, factorization machines, hybrid content–collaborative models, and neighborhood methods. Neural methods include VAEs, deep feature-interaction models, multi-task learning over cascading behaviors, attention and memory networks, recurrent and Transformer encoders, and deep reinforcement learning or contextual bandits. Graph neural networks, translational embeddings, ontologies, and relevance-proximity graphs support sequential modeling, cold-start handling, retrieval, and interpretable recommendations. Multimodal models integrate text, images, audio, aesthetics, and transaction context. Diversity re-ranking, determinantal point processes, adversarial learning, and combinatorial optimization address exposure and set-level objectives.

**Recent trends.** Emphasis is shifting toward real-time session modeling, multi-action feedback, fair and smooth exposure, explainable style and content control, exact-card recommendation, scalable approximate retrieval, and profit- or price-aware marketplace decisions.

3388133d68646086e8ac355fdaecb089ef86cd00.text:
### Personalized Recommendation: Sequential, Diverse, and Multi-Objective Systems

This community studies personalized recommendation across products, media, fashion, travel, education, healthcare, expertise, research papers, and social activities. Core themes include sparse explicit and implicit feedback, cold-start and long-tail discovery, session and sequential behavior, group and social recommendation, multi-behavior learning, and combining user, item, textual, visual, semantic, and contextual signals. Increasing attention targets popularity bias, diversity, fairness, explainability, and marketplace objectives affecting both consumers and producers.

Typical methods span neighborhood models, matrix and tensor factorization, Bayesian and pairwise ranking, metric learning, ontologies, factorization machines, and probabilistic models, alongside neural collaborative filtering, autoencoders, multimodal networks, RNNs, transformers, memory-augmented and graph neural networks. Content-aware systems exploit reviews, tags, images, aesthetic features, MIDI, semantic embeddings, and scholarly metadata. Reinforcement learning supports online advertising and sequential decision-making.

Recent trends include session-based and next-basket recommendation, interest drift modeling, multi-task learning from cascading behaviors, hybrid playlist and complementary-item recommendation, and deep approaches to item cold start. Post-processing and combinatorial methods increasingly optimize long-tail exposure and set diversity, including determinantal point processes and clique-based exact-\(K\) selection. The community also explores smooth fairness updates in two-sided markets, explainable ranking, efficient approximate retrieval, and recommendation-as-a-service for digital libraries.

25ba175ba994ecc4d07ef3ccc60b79cff1a7ab3f.text:
## Social Media, Mobility, and Spatial Intelligence

This community studies how social, mobile, and location-aware data reveal public opinion, political communication, misinformation, collective action, human mobility, migration, urban activity, cultural boundaries, environmental context, consumer behavior, and lifestyles. Political work examines junk news, polarization, hashtag movements, platform differences, and coordinated influence. Urban and geographic research addresses geolocation, geotagging behavior, commuting, migration, venue preferences, transport resilience, traffic optimization, and spatial-temporal sentiment.

Typical methods include sentiment, topic, hashtag, and content analysis; network analysis, community detection, diffusion, influence, polarization, and bot analysis; regression and machine learning; graph-based user modeling and recommendation; CNNs and multimodal signal fusion for geolocation; multiplex-network simulation; trajectory reconstruction, ordering, compression, and subtrajectory clustering; density-based spatial-textual clustering; matrix factorization; and probabilistic or optimization-based mobility modeling. Data span Twitter, Reddit, Instagram, Facebook, Wikipedia, Weibo, Foursquare, mobile-phone logs, GPS, check-ins, news, weather, and reviews.

Recent trends emphasize standardized and bias-aware geolocation evaluation, sparse-to-continuous mobility recovery, distributed trajectory analytics, resilient and collectively optimized transportation, culturally aware venue and business recommendation, multilingual knowledge-gap and article-structure recommendation, and comparative analysis of social platforms, hashtags, and localized sentiment.

4b131f63ff6051c56a816542ccda8bb9b9dbd79a.text:
## Social Media, Politics, Geolocation, and Urban Dynamics

This community studies how digital traces reveal political preferences, collective identity, media influence, cultural assimilation, public health risks, and urban mobility. Political and social research examines ideological rhetoric, election discourse, hashtag-driven movements, gendered and demographic participation, sexual-violence reporting, news popularity, and mass-media effects across Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, Reddit, and newswire data. Graph-based user modeling supports recommendations, business partnerships, community detection, influence analysis, and social search.

A major theme is inferring place, movement, and population characteristics from sparse or indirect signals. Text, images, network structure, check-ins, and mobile or vehicle observations support high-resolution home geolocation, privacy-risk assessment, geosocial extraction, disease-risk mapping, sentiment localization, migration and assimilation studies, and city-scale traffic optimization.

Typical methods include deep learning and graph convolutional networks, multimodal image-text analysis, NLP, sentiment and time-series modeling, graph features and centrality estimation, supervised classification, topic analysis, MapReduce, distributed subtrajectory clustering and joining, sampling, regression, and spatiotemporal simulation.

Recent trends emphasize scalable distributed mobility analytics, multimodal and longitudinal social-media analysis, standardized geolocation evaluation, privacy and sampling-bias correction, sparse-observation reconstruction, real-time public-health applications, and data-driven urban planning and movement analysis.

5fa797aee44fd610bd8cfe7fb7c0c43468491f3b.text:
### Dynamic, Heterogeneous, and Robust Network Analytics

This community develops computational methods for large, complex, heterogeneous, multimodal, and evolving networks, including social, information, citation, semantic, knowledge, multiplex, bipartite, and hypergraph data. Core themes include node and graph representation learning, community and role discovery, link prediction, similarity and alignment, diffusion and temporal reconstruction, anomaly and fraud detection, and recommendation.

Typical methods combine topology with attributes, text, images, temporal events, and interaction semantics. They include random walks, temporal motifs and event graphs, latent-space and generative network models, probabilistic graph grammars, graph neural networks with attention, matrix-factorization embeddings, meta-path-guided learning, feature propagation, semi-supervised learning, and multimodal neural models. Graph comparison uses probabilistic graph-edit distance, spectral, topological, hyperbolic, metric-flow, and embedding-based techniques; higher-order analysis includes cliques, multilayer interactions, and role structure. Methods increasingly model node polysemy, asymmetric relations, and cross-graph alignment without anchors.

Scalability remains central through compression, sampling, distributed and approximate algorithms, efficient indexing, and streaming or continuous-time visualization. Recent trends emphasize dynamic generative modeling, urban and behavioral analytics, multimodal content-user fusion, heterogeneous information integration, adversarial robustness and black-box attacks, poisoning detection, and explainable biomedical and financial applications. Benchmarks and bias-aware evaluation are also growing priorities.

e5c989e1c1db59b48749653bfc4aeb149ffbbe7b.text:
### Dynamic, Heterogeneous, and Robust Graph Analytics

This community develops computational methods for large, complex, uncertain, and evolving networks, including social, information, scholarly, semantic, multiplex, multilayer, bipartite, and heterogeneous systems. Core themes include node and graph representation learning, community and role discovery, link prediction, graph similarity search, anomaly and fraud detection, network alignment, ranking, graph classification, and higher-order structure such as triangles and motifs.

Typical methods combine topology with attributes, text, temporal events, multimodal content, and cross-network evidence. They include random walks, latent-space and generative dynamic models, stochastic blockmodels, Bayesian inference, matrix factorization, spectral methods, graph grammars, graph distances, and neural embeddings such as GCNs, attention networks, autoencoders, and feature propagation. Approximate probabilistic methods address NP-hard graph-edit-distance search; compression, sampling, and distributed techniques support large-scale inference. Heterogeneous approaches exploit meta-paths, supra-graphs, multimodal relations, and entity normalization.

Recent work emphasizes continuous-time event modeling, temporal similarity, dynamic link prediction, changing community structure, multimodal and multi-view embeddings, node polysemy, explainable relational learning, and unsupervised cross-graph alignment. Robustness research increasingly studies black-box adversarial attacks and covert-network detection. Applications include urban dynamics, recommendation, social-media analysis, bug localization, drug-response prediction, and cryptocurrency anti-money-laundering.

0b7cb029de4d15a058838bd9ffb82f4564e6eb1c.text:
## Social Media Geolocation, Political Information, and Movement Reconstruction

This community studies how incomplete, noisy, and socially structured digital traces support geographic, behavioral, and political analysis. In Twitter geolocation, researchers combine tweet text and user-profile metadata with convolutional or hierarchical neural networks. Recent models predict locations coarse-to-fine—from country to city—using character-aware word embeddings to handle noisy text and feature fusion to integrate heterogeneous signals. Large-scale empirical work, including analysis of more than 40 billion tweets from 20 million users, examines geotagging behavior and challenges assumptions underlying geotagged-data studies.

A second theme is political communication, news diversity, and misinformation. Studies use news-source dictionaries, self-reported locations, and sharing patterns to measure junk-news consumption, polarization, and geographic concentration during US elections. The *Junk News Aggregator* supports transparent, systematic monitoring of Facebook content, while related work investigates misinformation and conspiracy networks targeting military personnel and veterans. Controlled experiments with benign, human-like social bots on Weibo examine how user preferences shape news-consumption diversity and polarization.

Another methodological contribution reconstructs event order from movement trails with insufficient temporal resolution.

Typical methods include neural text modeling, hierarchical classification, multimodal feature integration, large-scale behavioral measurement, controlled social-bot experiments, and temporal-spatial reconstruction. Recent trends emphasize coarse-to-fine geolocation, robust text representations, platform-scale measurement, and cross-platform information-diversity monitoring.

8ab4c8b6222a57c3d78d8936ba72b82ede7af5fc.text:
**Information Retrieval: Neural Ranking, Personalization, and Interactive Search**

**Main themes.** This community studies semantic matching and relevance modeling for web, scholarly, enterprise-email, e-commerce, dataset, table, multimedia, and question-answering search. Key problems include query understanding and expansion, passage and answer retrieval, entity- and graph-aware product search, personalized query completion and ranking, domain adaptation, high-recall technology-assisted review, and search-agent interaction.

**Typical methods.** Systems combine lexical retrieval and probabilistic language models with pretrained transformers (especially BERT), neural interaction and cross-document attention models, embeddings, knowledge graphs, and table representations. Ranking uses pointwise, pairwise, listwise, multi-stage, and globally optimized objectives, including purchase-aware and metric-learning formulations. Query expansion draws on pseudo-relevant text, term associations, ontologies, and user context. Active learning, relevance feedback, yes/no review questions, counterfactual correction, variance-reduced online learning, and optimized multileaving address implicit feedback and human interaction. Approximate near-neighbor search, graph-based imputation, and lightweight representations support scale. Evaluation emphasizes benchmark collections, online experimentation, efficiency, and model explanations.

**Recent trends.** Research is moving toward end-to-end pretrained retrieval and constrained-passage answering; graph-augmented and entity-aware ranking; personalized and domain-adaptive search; dataset and structured-data discovery; autonomous high-recall review; interactive search agents; unbiased online optimization; and interpretable neural retrieval.

22292ff95e35b5758d99b4dd599ec4cd42141b91.text:
## Scalable Representation and Analysis of Complex Networks

This community develops methods for representing, comparing, generating, aligning, and mining large, dynamic, heterogeneous, multiplex, multimodal, signed, and higher-order networks. Themes include temporal link formation and embedding trajectories, causal and higher-order path discovery, evolving communities and roles, graph similarity and alignment, typed motifs, hyperbolic geometry, graph coarsening, anomaly and fraud detection, knowledge-graph construction, recommendation, question routing, tagging systems, and network analysis in finance, education, software, and biomedicine.

Typical methods combine stochastic and latent-space dynamic graph models, graph convolution and recurrent networks, attention, variational and semi-supervised autoencoders, random walks, matrix factorization, graph distances, spectral analysis, motif and graphlet mining, k-truss and core decomposition, integer programming, and structural role identification. Embeddings increasingly fuse topology with text, attributes, tags, and multiple social contexts; ensemble, asymmetric, heterogeneous, and cross-network representations support collective link prediction and similarity learning.

Recent trends emphasize continuous-time and timeslice-free modeling, scalable streaming updates, interpretable clustering and churn prediction, automatic meta-path discovery, hyperbolic network mapping, causal temporal analysis, dynamic adversarial attacks, robust and multimodal embeddings, reproducible graph-statistics software, and practical deployment for fraud mitigation, real-time recommendation, Q&A, and blockchain transaction analytics.

09bcdfbcf9af3c7a4114bfe49efd093743138276.text:
**Information Retrieval: Neural Ranking, Interactive Search, and Structured Discovery**

This community advances semantic, entity-aware, personalized, and interactive retrieval across web, enterprise, e-commerce, scientific, clinical, multimedia, and dataset-search settings. Neural rankers—especially pretrained language models such as BERT—support multi-stage document and passage reranking, non-factoid question answering, entailment-based answer filtering, query suggestion, and user-intent modeling. Graph embeddings, knowledge resources, table representations, entity and product structures, and multimodal context address vocabulary mismatch, long-tail items, and heterogeneous search results.

Typical methods include pointwise, pairwise, and listwise learning-to-rank; attention and cross-document interaction models; query expansion and term refinement using pseudo-relevance, associations, ontologies, and query categories; domain adaptation, multitask and adversarial learning; and cost-sensitive or positive-unlabeled learning under sparse supervision. Continuous active learning, sentence-level feedback, answer interaction studies, counterfactual and online LTR, multileaving, and reinforcement-learning agents learn from reviewers and users while correcting interaction bias.

Recent trends emphasize production ranking pipelines balancing quality and latency, hybrid neural–graph retrieval, explainable neural ranking, direct business-metric optimization, personalized query auto-completion, contextual and aggregated search across result modules, interactive summarization and exploration, dataset and table discovery, and robust retrieval for long passages, private domains, and specialized scientific or clinical collections.

d94a715ea9ee253e6c6e6428a47cadab359989a1.text:
**Information Retrieval: Neural, Structured, and Interactive Search**

This community advances semantic retrieval, relevance modeling, and scalable search systems across web, enterprise, e-commerce, scientific, clinical, and multimedia settings. Neural ranking increasingly uses pretrained language models such as BERT in pointwise, pairwise, and multi-stage reranking, with cross-document interaction and passage-length handling for question answering. Entity- and graph-aware models incorporate product relations, dependencies, knowledge graphs, tables, and heterogeneous modules; retrieval also spans datasets, images, social tags, and high-dimensional vector spaces.

Typical methods include dense and lexical matching, query expansion and term refinement, pseudo-relevance feedback, graph embeddings, table/vector representations, hashing and locality-sensitive search, listwise or groupwise learning to rank, and context-aware personalization. Active and continuous learning support high-recall technology-assisted review, including sentence-level feedback and targeted yes/no questioning. Counterfactual propensity estimation, online learning, multileaving, and variance reduction address biased interaction data and efficient ranking evaluation. Interpretability methods such as DeepSHAP explain neural decisions.

Recent trends emphasize pretrained and domain-adapted neural retrieval, lightweight personalized context, dataset and structured-data search, aggregated result pages, conversational and dynamic task-oriented interaction, answer-centric interfaces, autonomous review, and production architectures balancing quality, latency, scalability, and user effort.

4e51dbfad6938ed6bde93a3c17611e1ef53d478a.text:
### Graph Data Integration, Querying, and Scalable Analytics

This community studies the foundations and systems for modeling, integrating, querying, and analyzing RDF, knowledge, property, relational, and large-scale graphs. Core themes include graph databases and query languages, RDF and property-graph interoperability, schema definition, validation and evolution, keyword and top-*k* graph search, regular-path and reachability queries, contextual and geospatial knowledge graphs, and distributed neighborhood or subgraph analytics.

Typical methods combine formal semantics, category theory, functorial data migration, algebraic data types, schema mappings, monads, chase-based reasoning, acyclicity and finite-controllability analysis, query rewriting using views, and complexity or undecidability proofs. Systems work uses landmark and hop-doubling distance indexes, pruning and compact distance sketches, vertex- and subgraph-centric distributed execution, query decomposition, heuristic graph assembly, semantic ranking, response-time bounds, and benchmark-driven evaluation.

Recent trends emphasize interoperable property-graph exchange formats, algebraic and schema-governed graph models, coexisting schema versions, and practical data integration across relational, streaming, microservice, and ontology-based sources. Research is also expanding toward scalable cloud graph analytics, cross-domain linked-data discovery, contextual RDF reasoning, geospatial RDF benchmarking, OLAP over graph data, and user-oriented search interfaces that provide approximate or progressively available answers.

5afa9fc641d30b32f41bf3322fb9954c0e880e6c.text:
**Information Retrieval: Neural, Structured, Conversational, and Personalized Search**

This community develops retrieval and ranking systems combining lexical matching, pretrained neural semantics, knowledge graphs, structured data, and user context. Core themes include query–document and cross-document interaction, permutation-invariant set and groupwise ranking, BERT-based passage/document reranking, fielded entity and attribute retrieval, entity linking with provenance, intent representation, query expansion, multilingual and cross-lingual transfer, conversational and spoken search, and personalized e-commerce, news, advertising, mobile, social, academic, biomedical, and multimedia search. It also addresses FAQ, table, public-health, fact-checking, and complex-answer retrieval.

Typical methods include pointwise, pairwise, listwise, groupwise, multitask, curriculum, differentiable, adversarial, and reinforcement-learning objectives; multi-stage candidate generation and reranking; attention and hierarchical networks; semantic hashing; graph and entity embeddings; axiomatic regularization; weak, positive-unlabeled, and pseudo-labeled supervision; click-log and counterfactual learning; domain adaptation; and scalable approximate-nearest-neighbor search. Evaluation increasingly combines benchmarks with online, contextual, content-focused, and user-behavior analysis.

Recent trends include multilingual zero-shot relevance transfer, learning with limited labels, history-aware conversational models, spoken interaction, rapid personalization, explainable neural ranking, set-level and axiomatic modeling, robust e-commerce quality prediction, and production-oriented open-source ranking infrastructure.

de989ac5a9d6a95722837ffd135251c25a3c8e2c.text:
### Graph Querying, Integration, Semantics, and Analytics

This community studies foundations and systems for querying, integrating, validating, evolving, and analyzing graph data, including RDF, SPARQL, property graphs, knowledge graphs, uncertain and geospatial graphs, provenance, XML, and linked Web data. Core themes include graph pattern matching and navigational queries, keyword-to-query-graph assembly, federated and client-side linked-data querying, RDF–property-graph interoperability, schema validation and coexisting schema evolution, reachability and reliability, semantic cross-domain discovery, graph OLAP, and explainable recommendations or social feeds.

Typical methods combine formal semantics, complexity analysis, relational algebra and SQL/Datalog reduction, heuristic query construction and reordering, semantic similarity and top-k search, sampling and indexing for probabilistic graphs, graph summarization, cardinality estimation, and distributed or online processing. Systems use SPARQL, GeoSPARQL, Cypher, Gremlin, integrated graph algebras, interoperable property-graph serialization, benchmarks, and machine-learning methods including embeddings, attention, capsules, and neural relation extraction.

Recent trends emphasize practical graph-database interoperability and standardization; schema-aware, evolving, and uncertain data management; bounded-latency and approximate search; geospatial and multidimensional graph analytics; semantic cross-domain knowledge discovery; explainable, context-aware applications; and combining symbolic graph querying with learned representations and information extraction.

0f5c95ca551b99e3c4e58449270749e584e207c2.text:
### Semantic Graph Databases and Algebraic Data Integration

**Main research themes:** This community studies querying, integrating, validating, and managing large, heterogeneous graphs and databases. Topics include RDF/SPARQL and linked-data interfaces, keyword and semantic graph search, property-graph models and exchange formats, schema validation and evolution, Schema.org annotation and publishing, and interoperable knowledge graphs. It also addresses categorical and algebraic foundations for database mappings, functorial data migration, uncertain graphs, OLAP, evolving news and social data, and scalable distance and subgraph analytics.

**Typical methods:** Formal semantics, category theory, monads, sketches, algebraic data types, schema mappings, query rewriting, heuristic graph assembly, semantic similarity, probabilistic sampling, landmark labeling and distance sketches, sparse or incremental indexing, and workload-aware distributed execution. Implementations target relational and graph DBMSs, cloud platforms, web APIs, and vertex- or neighborhood-centric frameworks.

**Recent trends:** Emphasis is shifting toward RDF–property-graph interoperability, machine-readable APIs, domain-specific semantic validation, and automated annotation pipelines. Schema governance increasingly supports coexisting versions and mappings across relational, streaming, microservice, and graph data. Scalable analytics combine response-time-bounded approximate search, cloud subgraph processing, OLAP, and provable distance indexes, while explainability, privacy-aware publication, and cross-domain knowledge discovery become prominent concerns.

6b1ee1fb9dbbbd2af0f8321664898dcf033bdfb7.text:
## Scalable Temporal and Multilayer Network Analysis

This community develops scalable methods for querying, modeling, and exploiting large, evolving networks. Core topics include indexed graph querying—reachability, bounded and regular reachability, shortest paths, single-source and \(k\)-hop queries—using labeling schemes, interval and hop-doubling indexes, landmark sketches, hubs, independent-set labels, distributed algorithms, and lightweight fully dynamic structures such as DAGGER. Pruned Landmark Labeling is also being parallelized through vertex-centric, SIMD-aware, and batch computation models.

A major focus is temporal and multilayer-network analysis. Link streams and time-varying graphs preserve event timing, supporting temporal paths, distances, latencies, fastest and shortest journeys, connectivity, density, communities, centrality, and generalized betweenness through algorithmic and algebraic methods. Multilayer stream graphs extend this perspective across interaction types or layers, with layer-oriented centralities validated on large human-interaction and flight datasets.

The community also studies diffusion, influence, emergent information, and recommendation, including dynamic monopolies, opinion and contagion spreading, media and gossip, and temporal or sentiment-aware prediction. New applications model narratives as multilayer character-and-semantic interaction networks for summarization and analysis.

Recent trends favor native temporal and multilayer representations, scalable parallel processing, theoretically grounded indexing and pruning, and network-aware analysis of complex interactions.

d3e344a62a91bab989b785e5b6218f1acc07ed2a.text:
**Fair Search, Data Management, and Approximate Retrieval**

This community studies how to represent, integrate, query, search, and rank heterogeneous structured, semi-structured, uncertain, and user-generated data. Major themes include fairness, diversity, and exposure in search and recommender rankings; semantic query relaxation; bibliographic and domain-specific access; relational learning and analytics robust to schema choices; incomplete, probabilistic, fuzzy, and imprecise data; skyline and top-\(k\) queries; and interactive spreadsheet- and browsing-oriented database interfaces.

Typical methods combine graph representations and rewriting, entity and schema-independent relational learning, semantic similarity, fuzzy logic, possible-worlds and probabilistic models, sensitivity and ordinal-rank analysis, functional-dependency reasoning, learning-to-rank, fairness-aware reranking, antidote data, and set-based optimization. Scalable retrieval uses locality-sensitive hashing, graph-based approximate nearest-neighbor indices, vector search, stream processing, and progressive query evaluation. Other techniques address time-series segmentation, encrypted multidimensional search, XML/object transformation, and distributed storage.

Recent trends emphasize responsible ranking and recommender systems, including protected-attribute auditing, diversity, polarization reduction, and representation-bias analysis; practical uncertainty management for scientific and incomplete data; interactive and accessible querying; representation-independent analytics; scalable approximate retrieval; and integration of spreadsheets, streams, XML, and heterogeneous databases.

89641cf13ae805e2b887e69d0fba35d457a88f9c.text:
### Graph Data Management and Semantic Web Querying

This community studies the modeling, validation, interoperability, querying, and evolution of RDF, OWL, SPARQL, XML, and property-graph data. Core themes include SPARQL pattern semantics and entailment, OBDA, conjunctive and navigational queries, regular-expression reachability, graph pattern matching, query answering under TGDs, and formal RDF–property-graph mappings. Property-graph schemas, exchange formats, bidirectional transformations, and co-existing schema versions address interoperability and controlled evolution.

Typical methods combine formal semantics, category-theoretic and complexity analysis, chase-termination results, cost estimation, graph summaries, indexing, partitioning, sparse joins, and heuristic or approximate query processing. Systems employ relational-algebra reductions, Datalog view-update programs, distributed MPP/BSP execution, GPU subgraph matching, client-side or preemptible SPARQL evaluation, and native graph engines. Benchmarks increasingly assess large-scale, geospatial, and social-network workloads.

Recent trends emphasize dynamic, rich, and uncertain graphs; reliability optimization; semantic top-*k* and keyword-driven query construction; graph OLAP; cross-domain knowledge discovery; and explainable user-facing analytics. Schema inference for XML and property graphs, federated and endpoint-free Web-of-Data access, multi-query and data-in-motion analytics, and database-service deployment continue to expand, alongside applications in IoT, biomedical, clinical, and news data.

a2c64d7ec0f8eb12efc75ee818fe9ed0fc8a3101.text:
**Scalable Search, Indexing, and Scientific-Social Data Analytics**

This community develops efficient methods for searching, querying, and analyzing large, heterogeneous, multidimensional, scientific, and user-generated datasets. Core themes include compressed inverted, integer, RDF, high-dimensional, and graph indexes; approximate nearest-neighbor search; bitmap and spatial structures; graph-pattern retrieval; data cubes; incomplete-data and skyline queries; and domain-specific query languages.

Query processing spans top-k, cosine-threshold, approximate, aggregate, multidimensional, fuzzy, possible/certain, streaming, and bibliographic queries. Systems increasingly support batch workloads, shared I/O, interactive and low-latency event analysis, large-result management, cloud and distributed execution, and scientific metadata, provenance, and lifecycle management. Astronomy and other data-intensive sciences provide major deployment settings.

Social-data research covers tagging, participatory media, hidden-population discovery, expertise and community analysis, attention networks, and demographic or geographic scaling. Fairness, representation bias, exposure, viewpoint diversity, and polarization are central concerns in ranking and recommendation.

Typical methods combine compressed and partitioned representations, pruning and graph traversal, similarity and tag modeling, clustering, relational/graph modeling, information extraction, empirical benchmarking, distributed scheduling, and hardware- or cloud-aware optimization.

Recent trends emphasize real-time scientific streams, petabyte/exascale archives, active online data services, accessible domain-specific analytics, and socially responsible search and recommendation through fairness-aware reranking, diversity optimization, and input-side “antidote” data.

0a4b51dc21d6e82b93da81c9b96d82f3000e30b4.text:
### Preserving, Structuring, and Searching Evolving Digital Knowledge

This community studies durable, interpretable, accessible, and discoverable digital information across scientific, cultural, social-media, and web contexts. Core themes include repository and digital-object architectures, persistent and location-independent identifiers, provenance, versioning, rights, fixity, accessibility, data and software citation, RDF-based semantic layers, and preservation of evolving, private, and public web archives. Increasing emphasis is placed on temporal, multilingual, event-centric, and entity-centric exploration, including collaborative curation, structured browsing, archive surrogates, and recommendations for missing pages.

Typical methods combine standards-based system design with user-centered and empirical evaluation. Approaches use OAIS, Fedora, aDORe, MPEG-21, OAI-PMH, RDF, SPARQL, PROV-O, PAV, nanopublications, Memento, arcp, linked-data models, and semantic archive layers. Prototypes aggregate heterogeneous archives while protecting sensitive captures, verify fixity across sources, and support research-object and scholarly knowledge-graph infrastructures. Formal or semi-formal models organize scientific claims, research designs, and structured reports for semantic search, validation, and reuse; automated and crowdsourced multimodal acquisition populate these graphs. Large-scale crawl and archive analyses, temporal evidence mining, entity relatedness, pseudo-relevance feedback, and lexical, link, temporal, semantic, and diversity-based ranking support retrieval.

Recent trends emphasize collaborative archive construction, structured and machine-actionable scholarly communication, cross-lingual event analytics, accessibility, and integrating live-web and archived signals.

ca36cab043b3677acccac9985ae06b1757d2e7cb.text:
### Scholarly Discovery, Evaluation, and Reproducibility

This community studies how scholarly and library materials are indexed, ranked, discovered, summarized, evaluated, and reused. Core themes include bibliometrics and citation-context analysis; search-engine and catalog effectiveness; ranking, relevance, credibility, fairness, and user behavior; citation-based summarization and topic discovery; open-access availability; software and computational-research credit; and reproducibility practices. It also examines citation growth, knowledge accumulation, co-citation similarity, and structural patterns in evolving networks.

Typical methods combine bibliographic, full-text, repository, search-result, and usage datasets with web-scale collection and manual or crowdsourced judgments. Researchers use citation matching, co-citation and citation-context networks, clustering, community detection, graph motifs, similarity analysis, regression, longitudinal comparisons, rankings, benchmarking, and information-retrieval measures such as reciprocal rank and precision. Learning-to-rank, query expansion, regular expressions, text mining, extractive summarization, APIs, and automated querying support retrieval and analysis.

Recent work emphasizes representative and low-cost test-collection design, deep-versus-shallow relevance judging, enriched search-result pages, featured snippets, commercial and language effects, and credibility-aware ranking. It highlights metadata and citation limitations, metric gaming and Goodhart effects, and challenges in measuring software impact. Open science increasingly focuses on institutional OA indicators, research software credit, executable environments, shared code and data, and consistent reproducibility terminology.

a833530622435aa9320cbf684da221c9a9ed68d7.text:
## Efficient Retrieval, Indexing, and Responsible Ranking

This community develops efficient retrieval and database-processing systems for large, heterogeneous, and streaming data. Core themes include compressed inverted, bitmap, trie, RDF, n-gram, and posting-list indexes; integer-sequence partitioning and compression; columnar execution; learned and geometric indexes; and multidimensional operators such as skyline, k-nearest-neighbor, and preference queries. Applications span semantic and bibliographic search, hidden-population discovery, clinical decision support, ride-sharing, and participatory media.

Research addresses expressive query processing under uncertainty, including incomplete-data streams, graph and semantic pattern matching, domain-specific query languages, and pruning and matching for spatial data. Retrieval pipelines combine query variation, ranking, re-ranking, diversity, and multi-objective optimization.

Typical methods include formal models and axioms, complexity analysis, dynamic programming, geometric pruning, compressed and succinct data structures, column-at-a-time execution, machine-learned or domain-specific query planning, and empirical evaluation on real datasets and systems. Hardware-conscious implementation using memory hierarchies, SIMD, multicore, GPU, SSD, or NVM remains important.

Recent trends strongly emphasize responsible search and recommendation: distributional fairness, exposure and attention allocation, demographic and semantic-bias auditing, fairness-aware re-ranking, viewpoint diversity, and social-good optimization through antidote data. Adaptive, scalable retrieval increasingly integrates these objectives with effectiveness, relevance, coverage, and latency constraints.

dac42379c9b39052db0e81a0d5f9204efc2d1f04.text:
## Graph Signal Processing, Network Inference, and Opinion Influence

This community studies how network structure governs signals, opinions, influence, diffusion, and collective behavior. Core themes include graph-based representations of social and spatiotemporal data, opinion dynamics with stubborn or influential agents, signed-network polarization and boomerang effects, event and infection propagation, community detection, and influence estimation in online networks. It also examines recommender systems, popularity-driven diffusion, latent agents, preference aggregation, and link importance for information propagation.

Typical methods include spectral graph theory, graph Fourier transforms and filters, diffusion and superposition distances, bandlimited-signal sampling and reconstruction, variation minimization, dictionary learning, and distributed ARMA filtering. Network structure is inferred from consensus dynamics, spectral templates, stationary or filtered signals, and low-rank excitations, using convex optimization, spectral clustering, causal inference, stochastic processes, and simulation. Methods increasingly address directed, signed, time-varying, irregular, and partially observed graphs.

Recent trends include scalable and inexact graph transforms; blind community detection and topology recovery without direct edge observations; localized-attribute, anomaly, and infection detection; graph learning from long- and short-term spatiotemporal correlations; efficient sampling and percolation-based reconstruction; and causal measurement of influence and propaganda. Opinion research is also moving beyond averaging models toward weighted-median dynamics, random actions, and time-varying stubbornness.

740c7508efc883c39a446416e86c847f4358f3b5.text:
## Scalable, Intelligent, and Trustworthy Data Systems

This community develops scalable data management, querying, and analytics for relational, graph, streaming, semi-structured, array, probabilistic, and scientific data. Core themes include query optimization and cardinality/resource estimation, join ordering and worst-case-optimal joins, incremental processing, interactive and approximate query processing, data integration, workload management, and machine learning over relational data. It also addresses transactional consistency, concurrency, cloud performance guarantees, privacy-preserving data release, and blockchain–database design.

Typical methods combine formal complexity and cost analyses with sampling, sketches, histograms, compact indexes, factorization, incremental maintenance, adaptive and learned indexes, deep likelihood and generative models, Monte Carlo estimation, probabilistic representations, and reinforcement or supervised learning. Systems exploit multicore, GPU, MapReduce, shared-nothing clusters, cloud elasticity, and heterogeneous database pipelines, including graph stores supporting both transactions and analytics.

Recent trends include learned optimizers and workload advisors, vector representations of SQL workloads, declarative end-to-end SQL/ML workflows, ML inference optimization, neural visual-content predicates, learned sequence indexes for genomics, and generative approximate query answering. Other directions include SLA-aware cloud autoscaling, cloud resource markets, heterogeneous data tunneling, synthetic data generation, hardware-conscious graph joins, hybrid relational platforms, and high-throughput transactional graph storage.

2f38f4a9eada49469802dc29ba7412b7fef2307b.text:
## Adaptive Data Management and Analytics

This community studies how to make data-intensive systems scalable, adaptive, efficient, and easier to use. Core themes include relational query optimization—join ordering, cardinality and resource estimation, worst-case-optimal and multiway joins, factorized query processing, incremental maintenance, and complexity bounds—alongside distributed, multi-database, cloud, stream, graph, document, and heterogeneous-data processing.

Typical methods combine formal complexity and communication analyses with learned optimizers, deep reinforcement learning, neural likelihood models, workload embeddings, adaptive and learned indexes, probabilistic summaries, uncertainty modeling, sampling, sketches, caching, materialized views, and compact data structures. Systems increasingly integrate databases with machine learning through declarative SQL workflows, in-database text learning, optimized inference, workload management, and domain-specific search such as genomics. Hardware acceleration using FPGAs, reconfigurable fabrics, and specialized graph-join architectures is also prominent.

Recent trends emphasize approximate and probabilistic query processing for interactive exploration, including generative models and incomplete-query guarantees; cost-aware execution over memory-resident and geographically distributed data; and scalable visual/video analytics that combine neural models with predicate and representation optimization. Other directions include privacy-preserving synthetic data, blockchain and Byzantine-fault-tolerant data systems, cross-platform workload analysis, heterogeneous data integration, and resource-efficient processing of multimodal, streaming, and graph workloads.

b04de2659f525f6c7c2293aad1ad0dc6025759cf.text:
**Bibliometric Networks, Scholarly Retrieval, and Information Mapping**

This community studies scholarly communication, information organization, and networked influence. Themes include ranking authors, institutions, papers, patents, venues, grants, and web resources; distinguishing popularity, prestige, diffusion, and historical influence; analyzing citation, coauthorship, contributorship, hiring, career, gender, political, and geopolitical networks; mapping communities, collaboration structures, inequality, and behavioral evolution; and tracing novelty, technological change, and research impact.

PageRank and Google-matrix methods remain prominent, including weighted, bipartite, reduced-matrix, personalized, spectral, and alternative-normalization approaches. Scalable sampling and dynamic updating support massive evolving graphs. Other methods include stochastic block models, regression, neural forecasting, sequence-to-sequence models, hidden Markov models, graph centrality and convexity, community detection, multilayer networks, large-scale network mining, and automated metadata integration and author disambiguation.

Information-retrieval work develops bibliometric-enhanced ranking, discipline-specific query expansion, KOS/SKOS and Linked Data integration, knowledge maps, integrated research-data libraries, title simplification, and session-topic segmentation. User behavior, personalization, query bias, and exploratory search are evaluated through logs and interactive studies.

Recent trends include longitudinal multilingual Wikipedia and geopolitical influence analysis; predictive citation, patent, venue, and grant analytics; scalable career and inequality studies; social-media and cultural-network mining; interpretable behavioral archetypes; and efficient personalized retrieval over dynamic graphs.

d07115254ca343a97b3de180296231472a7f83d1.text:
### Scalable Graph Mining and Network Analytics

This community develops computational and theoretical methods for analyzing large, heterogeneous, dynamic networks, including social, information, web, communication, software, citation, infrastructure, and bipartite graphs. Core themes include community and hierarchical-structure discovery, core and truss decomposition, centrality and influence, graph distances and convexity, network sampling, diffusion and indirect transmission, robustness, vertex-cover and network-design problems, graph generation, and structural comparison across domains.

Typical methods combine topology with attributes, activity, spatial information, and partially observed data. They include spectral and constrained clustering, random walks and sampling, entropy- and path-based centralities, statistical analysis of graph metrics, stochastic diffusion models, differential-equation dynamics, spatial and preferential-attachment models, probabilistic graph grammars, maximum matching and vertex-cover decompositions, and convex optimization using ADMM. Scalable implementations use nearly-linear algorithms, GPU parallelism, external-memory processing, and general-purpose graph-mining libraries.

Recent work emphasizes billion-scale web-graph characterization; dynamic and hierarchical communities; sampling bias and structure preservation; localized core estimation and critical-edge identification; higher-order cohesion and indirect interactions; privacy risks from attribute inference; software and citation networks; evolving news and interdisciplinary scholarship; and formal, interoperable graph representations. Geometry-aware generation, model calibration, and efficient analysis of streaming or out-of-core graphs are growing trends.

47c21e3ce871b08a585f9dda035e1414198583d7.text:
**Deep Multimodal Learning and Cross-Modal Retrieval**

**Main themes:** This community studies semantic relationships across music and multimedia modalities, including lyrics, audio, listener responses, images, text, video, and social-media events. It addresses cross-modal retrieval, lyric-based genre classification, interpretable recommendation, multimodal event search, and efficient similarity search across heterogeneous sources and views.
