Research on text mining and review supports probabilistic modeling, topic modeling, clustering, k-nearest neighbors, association rules, feature selection, dependency pruning, hyperonymization, active learning, and sentence-level relevance feedback. Recent work models retrieval stopping criteria with Poisson processes.

Mathematical information services combine text-and-formula retrieval, presentation- and content-based search, formula repositories, semantic conversion, accessible MathML, and question answering that links natural-language questions to computable formulas. New directions jointly model equations and surrounding text, automate semantics-preserving translation between LaTeX and computer algebra systems, and examine the challenges of machine learning for mathematics.

Scalable analytics builds on associative arrays, D4M/Accumulo, Graphulo- and GraphBLAS-style processing, provenance, external-memory analytics, tensors, polystores, and relational semantics. New work emphasizes high-rate streaming graph updates across Python, Julia, and MATLAB, AI data wrangling, scalable monitoring pipelines, serverless analytics over cold data, and automatic discovery and presentation of dataset views. Methods include matrix/tensor algebra, graph transformations, query-predicate optimization, semantic mappings, benchmarking, feedback control, caching, and cost- and execution-time modeling. Recent trends favor cloud elasticity, cross-platform execution, data discovery, integrated mathematical semantics, and provenance-aware analytics.

2abb10d63134b62e6853f581d94a9c88c6d7cc8b.text:
## Diffusion, Influence, and Network Inference

This community studies propagation of information, opinions, epidemics, misinformation, failures, and attacks across social, biological, infrastructure, and cyber-physical networks. Core problems include source and patient-zero inference, cascade reconstruction, network-structure and edge-weight learning, epidemic containment, influence maximization or minimization, competitive and complementary cascades, welfare-aware adoption, and strategic defense.

Recent work emphasizes multiplex, multilayer, evolving, spatial, and heterogeneous networks; noisy or incomplete cascades; mixtures of contagion graphs; negative influence, trust, synergy, self-activation, and competing campaigns; and diversity-aware, targeted, adaptive, and resource-constrained seeding. Applications include elections, advertising, coupons, misinformation prevention, MOOCs, privacy, and social welfare.

Typical methods combine independent-cascade, threshold, epidemic, Bass, compartmental, Markov, non-Markovian, DeGroot, and game-theoretic models with submodularity, approximation, bilevel and convex optimization, centrality, percolation, message passing, mixed-integer programming, Bayesian inference, graph learning, sampling, Monte Carlo, and stochastic simulation. Exact Markov analyses, lumping and approximate master equations support scalable epidemic computation.

Recent trends include full-feedback adaptivity, evolving-topology influence, scalable or sampling-free estimation, robust competitive interventions, influence-overlap reduction, seed and audience diversification, probabilistic uncertainty quantification, privacy under social contagion, and graph generation or characterization under structural and attribute constraints.

a68fe7d306039456290b199546762c2c7153a493.text:
### Web Navigation, Ontology, and Mobility Intelligence

This community studies how people explore, use, and reshape large semantic, scholarly, encyclopedic, and urban information spaces. Themes include biomedical ontology discovery and reuse, collaborative ontology engineering, Wikipedia knowledge organization and cross-lingual historical narratives, hyperlink structure and missing-link identification, search versus navigation, user motivations, and urban taxi mobility.

Typical methods combine access-log and clickstream analysis with page content and semantic metadata; Markov models of varying order, Bayesian hypothesis comparison (HypTrails/MixedTrails), PageRank variants, mixed-effects hurdle models, and user-feature modeling. Other approaches include graph-structured datasets, co-word networks with sparse temporal representations, nonnegative tensor factorization for spatiotemporal mobility, and computational timeline comparison across language editions. Studies use large-scale Wikipedia, BioPortal, ontology-project, and taxi traces, often examining navigation bias, semantic proximity, memory, roles, and heterogeneous behavior.

Recent trends emphasize data-driven improvement of hyperlink and ontology interfaces, navigation-aware ranking beyond random-surfer assumptions, explainable analysis of semantic-network exploration, automated discovery of missing or useful links, reproducible graph datasets, and Bayesian, temporally sensitive modeling of human trails across web and physical environments.

0f61473950a33151ee24cd18d703d462edac1ada.text:
**Bibliometrics, Evaluation, and Scholarly Equity**

This community studies how research performance, impact, efficiency, and fairness are measured and governed, especially across Italy and national research systems. Themes include individual and institutional productivity, excellence, quality–quantity trade-offs, gender and collaboration, academic rank and mobility, foreign versus domestic faculty, regional and disciplinary disparities, specialization versus research diversification, entrepreneurship, nepotism, self-citation, and opportunistic responses to assessment. It also examines peer review versus bibliometric evaluation, citation and readership impact, researcher rankings, h- and g-index benchmarking, knowledge diffusion, geographic proximity, internationalization, and global balances of knowledge flows.

Typical methods combine Web of Science, DBLP, ScienceDirect, Mendeley, and open citation data with field normalization, FSS/MNCS and network indicators, citation weighting, gravity and regression models, longitudinal and sensitivity analyses, productivity distributions, Pareto/Gini statistics, and efficiency analysis. Studies use early citations and journal impact factors to predict long-term impact, compare peer-review judgments with bibliometric forecasts, and construct country-level knowledge-flow accounts. Author-name disambiguation employs probabilistic, supervised, and unsupervised similarity methods, clustering, topology, and class-imbalance analysis.

Recent trends emphasize open, reproducible citation infrastructures such as OpenCitations; altmetrics and readership distributions; uncertainty-, contribution-, and network-aware evaluation; gender-sensitive and internationally comparable benchmarks; improved identity resolution; and scrutiny of how evaluation rules influence self-citation, collaboration, diversification, and institutional behavior.

96bfb363f37cdab74111732e4c76bcb57058206d.text:
## Community Detection and Network Structure

This community studies mesoscale structure, importance, and dynamics in complex networks. Themes include overlapping, hierarchical, multilayer, heterogeneous, attributed, weighted, signed, directed, bipartite, geometric, dynamic, uncertain, and partially observed communities; core–periphery and other block structures; dense subgraphs and trusses; node centrality, alignment, influence, diffusion, cascades, and network vulnerability. Applications span social, communication, web, recommendation, bibliometric, biological, software, transportation, IoT, and information networks.

Typical methods include modularity and nonlinear total-variation optimization, spectral and eigenvector methods, PageRank and supracentralities, belief propagation and EXIT analysis, stochastic block models, graphons, geometric block models, label propagation, local and seed-based search, random walks, motif and subgraph mining, bipartite co-clustering, core/truss peeling, curvature and Ricci flow, graph signals, manifold methods, and likelihood or variational inference. Generative recommendation, graph alignment, sampling, and incremental/streaming algorithms are also prominent.

Recent trends emphasize scalable analysis of massive, sparse, public–private, multiplex, and temporal networks; principled stability and uncertainty guarantees; evolving importance and change detection; nonlinear and geometric formulations; structure-aware recommendation and group formation; recovery from heterogeneous data; and applications to diffusion, cultural coexistence, influence, robustness, and transportation vulnerability.

6bd5d9050d6d7a91b4f4b8c1a0c7f22f9b1b1d25.text:
## Scientometrics, Citation Metrics, and Science Mapping

This community quantifies scientific influence, performance, knowledge flows, and evaluation across researchers, papers, journals, institutions, countries, and technologies. Core themes include citation indicators, field and time normalization, interdisciplinarity, collaboration and diversity, scientific mobility, research histories, university comparisons, authorship credit, and critiques of impact metrics and assessment regimes. Fairness concerns address disciplinary variation, skewed distributions, authorship allocation, demographic and geographic bias, homophily, and incentive effects of evaluation policies.

Typical methods use Web of Science, Scopus, Dimensions, PubMed, patent databases, conference proceedings, and sometimes alternative scholarly or public-web data. Analyses combine citation, co-citation, bibliographic-coupling, co-authorship, affiliation, and temporal networks with PageRank, community detection, centrality, entropy, similarity, fractional counting, RPYS/patent spectroscopy, visualization, and text or controlled-vocabulary analysis. I3, percentile indicators, beamplots, graph-based author disambiguation, name embeddings, and statistical concordance and validity tests are prominent.

Recent trends include dynamic and multilayer network analysis, improved field delineation, embedding-based mapping of interdisciplinary and translational science, causal designs separating journal effects from article quality, prediction of citation bursts and delayed recognition, and systematic measurement of collaboration, migration, and diversity. Applications increasingly connect scholarly impact with patents, innovation, and national evaluation policies while emphasizing indicator validity and unintended behavioral effects.

dd43b40d96b6359c119eac33395b0b088a3560d0.text:
## Declarative, Scalable Data and ML Systems

This community develops scalable, efficient, and usable systems for data-intensive computation and end-to-end data science. Core themes include relational query optimization—join ordering, cardinality estimation, worst-case-optimal and hybrid joins, incremental maintenance, containment, ranked/random-order enumeration, functional aggregates, and resource-aware planning—together with graph pattern matching, streaming and temporal graphs, multidimensional time series, JSON/documents, information extraction, and multimedia/video analytics. Declarative paradigms span SQL, Datalog, relational and linear algebra, LARA, MATLANG, DataFrames, document spanners, and annotated or factorized representations.

Typical methods combine formal complexity, information-theoretic, and decomposition analyses with distributed systems engineering. Techniques include compact indexes and tries, adaptive and overlay indexing, learned storage design, model-based and log compression, sparse/factorized computation, equality saturation, sampling and mergeable sketches, approximate answers, constant-delay enumeration, provenance and weighted annotations, and incremental query maintenance. Implementations target multicore, GPU, FPGA, Spark, cloud, polystore, and high-throughput streaming environments.

A strong thread integrates databases with ML through declarative data-science workflows, in-database inference, relational learning, semantic type detection, Bayesian precomputation, and SQL/linear-algebra optimization. Recent trends emphasize adaptive analytics for dynamic workloads, error-bounded telemetry and time-series summaries, declarative deep-video filtering and Top-K/event queries, scalable graph ingestion, hardware-aware storage, and unified optimization across relational, numerical, and ML computation.

38083748266e34a34756ab9dd2d9229a5044ed7a.text:
## Scientometrics and Scholarly Networks

This community quantitatively studies scientific impact, influence, reputation, collaboration, knowledge diffusion, and research evaluation. Themes include citation- and percentile-based assessment of papers, authors, journals, institutions, countries, books, and venues; field normalization, fractional attribution, interdisciplinarity, diversity, and disciplinary delineation; and the validity, coverage, bias, and unintended effects of metrics. Altmetrics—including readership, downloads, hyperlinks, and online attention—are examined as timely but heterogeneous impact traces. Scholarly communication and peer-review workflows are also analyzed through reviewer expertise, bidding, and paper–reviewer matching.

Typical methods combine Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar, DBLP, ADS, patents, funding, peer-assessment, web, and bibliographic-graph data. Analyses use citation, co-citation, bibliographic-coupling, co-authorship, author–paper bipartite, readership, hyperlink, and temporal networks, applying centrality, PageRank, community detection, similarity, entropy, network decomposition, and visualization. Methods include field- and time-normalized indicators, burst and diffusion models, text/context similarity, author-name disambiguation, OCR reference resolution, regression, machine learning, and integer programming.

Recent trends emphasize granular and context-sensitive co-citation, temporal network evolution, prestige versus popularity, predicting author and paper impact, validating indicators against peer judgment, comparing databases, assessing open-access and preprint effects, and improving reproducible author-oeuvre construction and reviewer assignment. Responsible assessment stresses source concordance, statistical robustness, and database limitations.

2d2bc6bbf782997576cd4bdb07e5ffe71fb90a1c.text:
## Social Networks: Diffusion, Attention, and Collective Intelligence

This community studies how social networks form, adapt, and shape information, opinion, creativity, collective intelligence, behavior, popularity, knowledge exchange, and socioeconomic activity. Themes include centrality and global bridges, assortative mixing, structural diversity, roles and embeddings, attention and influence, anonymity, expertise, organizational hierarchy, online discourse, misinformation, political communication, citation and software adoption, community Q&A, and content engagement. It also examines information cascades, epidemics, online popularity, academic productivity and impact, wellbeing-related sentiment, and consumption stratification.

Typical methods combine temporal, weighted, multiplex, relational-event, and location-aware network analysis; community detection; cycle-based clustering; centrality and role measures; and diffusion models including epidemic, Hawkes/self-exciting, delay-differential, stochastic, and adaptive-network models. Machine learning uses graph neural networks, embeddings, latent-variable and Poisson models, deep neural networks, text and affect analysis, and popularity or quality prediction. Researchers also use surveys, controlled experiments, causal analysis, anomaly detection, and scalable data-harvesting pipelines.

Recent directions emphasize adaptive ties and performance-based network evolution, platform-scale attention and cascade forecasting, real-time temporal analysis, root-source identification, network-aware recommendation and marketing, interpretable opinion modeling, scientific influence dispersion, and cross-domain analyses linking social structure to economic behavior.

2611779114ed3fcee9a27882506bec36a410cd6a.text:
## Community Detection and Network Dynamics

**Main themes.** This community studies mesoscopic organization in complex networks, including overlapping, hierarchical, multilayer/multiplex, attributed, weighted, signed, directed, bipartite, temporal, geometric, and higher-order communities. It also addresses core–periphery structure, rich-club organization, trusses, dense subgraphs, network alignment, centrality, vulnerability, diffusion, and change detection. Applications span social and information networks, recommendations, affiliation data, road systems, online video, research influence, and public–private graphs.

**Typical methods.** Approaches combine modularity, stochastic and geometric block models, belief propagation, label propagation, random walks, spectral methods, matrix factorization, co-clustering, entropy, graph-signal learning, and nonlinear total-variation optimization. PageRank, heat-kernel methods, tunable eigenvector centralities, Ricci curvature/flow, and network motifs support ranking, local clustering, alignment, and dynamic analysis. Higher-order structure is captured with k-trusses, bipartite peeling, motifs, and core–periphery block models.

**Recent trends.** Work increasingly addresses temporal and streaming updates, evolving teleportation and multiplex dynamics, local scalable discovery, active learning, and change detection. Emphasis remains on detectability, phase transitions, stability, significance, modularity bias, vulnerability, and improved information-theoretic evaluation. Community-aware recommendation, influence analysis, diffusion, semantic clustering, and structure-preserving analysis of heterogeneous networks continue to expand.

64256a4a2ab8fcb2df02536c5f31c62a7e2e1e8a.text:
**Webometrics, Scholarly Communication, and Digital Communities**

This community studies how scholarly information, impact, and online interaction are measured, ranked, and governed. Core themes include bibliometric indicators—citation counts, h-index variants, highly cited papers, citation dynamics, journal and institutional benchmarking—and comparisons of Google Scholar, Web of Science, Scopus, and other platforms. Google Scholar is examined as a broad but imperfect source, including coverage, profile quality, anomalies, and possible manipulation.

Research increasingly addresses open-access infrastructure and policy: university-level green, gold, and hybrid OA indicators, repository coverage, deposit delays, and compliance with funder or national mandates. ResearchGate and other digital institutions are studied through scoping reviews, platform evaluation, governance, participation, and institutional visibility. Scholarly communication is also mapped through diachronic analyses of disciplinary corpora such as the ACL Anthology.

Methods include large-scale database, repository, and web querying; API and full-text/link analysis; longitudinal and cross-platform comparison; citation, correlation, and statistical testing; network construction, modularity-based community detection, and visualization; classification, deduplication, and manual validation. Newer work analyzes search-engine snippets and result features, as well as geographic and ethnic influences on collaboration networks. Recent trends emphasize open and timely access, digital-institution design, community and discipline mapping, search visibility, and detection of unusual or unstable citation trajectories.

1a246f9feb2fee713b11b4924f64ba3572d565ba.text:
**Multilayer Diffusion and Social Network Identity**

This community studies multiplex and overlapping social, physical, and online networks, emphasizing how information, rumors, influence, and multiple contagions spread across interacting layers. It also addresses cross-platform user identity linkage, heterogeneous interaction prediction, network pattern discovery, and the emergence of information-sharing ties.

Typical methods include threshold, epidemic, co-contagion, rumor–truth, and dormancy models; game-theoretic and evolutionary formulations; constrained optimization for intervention; and empirical analysis of temporal interaction patterns. Identity linkage uses unsupervised factoid embeddings, profile/content/network features, and graph neural networks. Multiplex graph matching, graphlets, and structural motif analysis support template detection and relational characterization, while lightweight API crawling enables large-scale collection of Twitter relation graphs. Behavioral and interaction signals are also used to detect flaming and predict cross-type interactions.

Evaluation draws on Twitter and other online social networks, social–physical communication systems, economic trade multiplexes, synthetic multilayer graphs, and large observed interaction networks.

Recent trends emphasize coupled spreading processes, synergy and competition among contagions, strategic information dissemination and rumor containment, scalable cross-platform identity resolution, multiplex-aware graph matching, and fine-grained mining of heterogeneous social interactions.

508950450a30adbb09d47fe1a70dc1a7e789ac39.text:
## Dynamic Community Structure in Complex Networks

This community studies mesoscopic organization and cohesion in large, evolving networks. Core themes include overlapping communities, core–periphery structure, directed and multilayer organization, dense subgraphs, weak and strong ties, bridges, influence, information diffusion, and structural vulnerability. Applications emphasize online social and information networks, criminal networks, recommendation systems, web graphs, and behavioral or communication dynamics.

Typical methods include modularity optimization and generalized Louvain, stochastic blockmodels and graphons, geometric blockmodels, label propagation, spectral and random-walk techniques, consensus clustering, and nonlinear total-variation optimization. Cohesion is modeled with k-trusses, core numbers, density, and triangle-based decompositions. Centrality, pair-dependency, PageRank, and diffusion-based distances identify influential intermediaries and compare network signals. Graph signal processing, graph Fourier methods, and spatiotemporal graph learning support analysis of signals and evolving structure.

Evaluation emphasizes detectability, stability, scalability, resolution effects, algorithm selection, robustness, and the relationship between modularity and generative models. Recent trends include online visualization that preserves temporal continuity, evolving centrality under changing external interests, privacy-aware public–private graph mining, dynamic and multilayer inference, weak-tie effects on diffusion and cascades, active learning, and scalable analysis of massive networks.

35fe8e9353e53f358c9e9bdda7920f02ccda4123.text:
## Structured Discovery and Navigation of Web Data

This community studies how to make heterogeneous web, document, and data-lake information comparable, searchable, and navigable. A foundational theme is defining shared, potentially multidimensional ordered domains so values can be compared and retrieved precisely.

Research maps keyword queries to knowledge-graph patterns that aggregate entities or joins into tables, retrieves multi-column answers from web-table collections, and supports schemaless queries over tables embedded in reports, manuals, and guidelines. Web tables increasingly serve as open-domain question-answering resources, supporting factoid, list-intent, superlative, and non-factoid queries. Systems emphasize high precision and broad coverage when selecting answer-bearing tables and rows.

New work treats table construction itself as a query task: given a natural-language description, desired column names, and an example row, systems such as AutoTableComplete retrieve additional entity tuples from knowledge bases to automatically complete tables for information gathering and decision support.

Methods include RDF and SPARQL, database dependencies, transformations for non-relational layouts, neural semantic similarity between questions and tables, and learned ranking using textual and structural features. Data-lake navigation models organizations as graphs of attribute sets linked by subset relationships, with probabilistic user models and optimization objectives. Scalable search uses locality-sensitive hashing and Jaccard set containment.

Recent trends are toward schemaless semantic access, neural table retrieval and QA, automated table synthesis, and optimized interactive exploration.

64770974032ff3841482f4e090973a18f68caf62.text:
## Online Networks: Diffusion, Attention, and Collective Dynamics

This community studies how online, affiliation, scientific, mobile, and social-physical networks form and evolve, shaping information, opinions, behavior, creativity, health, markets, scientific impact, and collective risk. Core themes include influence, centrality and global bridges, assortativity, structural diversity, brokers, multiplex and signed ties, community formation, reputation and authority, attention, popularity and virality, information cascades, meme and topic lifecycles, collective intelligence, opinion complexity, engagement, scholarly productivity and influence, and cross-community mobility. It also examines political communication, inequality and homophily, mental health, crisis sensing, and the relationship between online and geographic contexts.

Typical methods combine community detection, cycle-aware and temporal network analysis, mixing measures, latent-variable and productivity models, threshold and contagion models, delayed differential equations, generalized epidemic and Hawkes processes, cascade and diffusion-path analysis, agent-based simulation, stochastic control, embeddings, topic, sentiment, and keyphrase analysis, interactive learning, and longitudinal studies. Neural and graph-neural models forecast popularity, engagement, question quality, geolocation, and content moderation; generative models identify root sources and latent opinions.

Recent trends emphasize adaptive networks and peer selection, continuous-time diffusion, network-aware popularity prediction, user attention and retweet motivations, disaster situational awareness, social feedback, scientific influence dispersion, and integrating online signals with physical, environmental, financial, and health data.

206af388f734b86c3c5a40e9dd0c96ca50daf02c.text:
## Social Media Intelligence, Geolocation, and Crisis Response

This community studies how social, mobile, transactional, and location-aware data reveal human behavior, public opinion, spatial activity, health risks, and crisis conditions. Core themes include crisis informatics: detecting events and sub-events, extracting keyphrases and actionable reports, filtering noisy or multimodal streams, tracking sexual violence, and supporting real-time responder situational awareness. It also examines geolocation and home-location inference, privacy risks, mobility and subtrajectory analysis, continuous-time interaction networks, collective identity and cultural assimilation, demographic and personality inference, misinformation assessment, and opinion representativeness. Emerging applications include disease-risk mapping, sports prediction, personalized food and recipe recommendation, and knowledge-based mobile-app services.

Typical methods include NLP, keyword and keyphrase extraction, supervised and interactive learning, multilingual and character-aware embeddings, hierarchical and deep neural geolocation, multimodal classification, sentiment and trait inference, topic and sub-event modeling, graph convolutional and dynamic-network models, relational event models, string similarity, MapReduce trajectory joins, recommender systems, and survey-based evaluation. Systems integrate Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, mobile traces, news, and health or environmental data.

Recent trends emphasize real-time disaster analytics, user-in-the-loop relevance modeling, cross-lingual and city-level geolocation, privacy-aware location inference, multimodal sensing, scalable continuous-time networks, and personalized health-oriented recommendations.

beb8efeef4d19e4cb1a5ffc2314a81be2d0ff9d7.text:
### Context-Aware POI Recommendation

This community focuses on personalized point-of-interest (POI) and venue recommendation in location-based social networks (LBSNs), aiming to model user preferences and mobility despite sparse check-in histories. Key challenges include geographical influence, temporal variation, contextual relevance, local popularity, and effective user representation.

Typical methods include collaborative ranking and logistic matrix factorization enhanced with geographical information, multiple location-based similarities, and temporal regularization reflecting changing popularity and user activity. Recent work jointly models geographical and temporal effects, emphasizing that the influence of physical proximity can itself vary across time rather than treating spatial and temporal factors independently. Other approaches use probabilistic mappings between user-generated tags and location-taste keywords, or scoring functions combining venue content, reviews, social information, and user context. Context-aware models explicitly predict location appropriateness under different circumstances.

A complementary line replaces dot-product factorization with metric factorization, representing users and items in Euclidean space. Neural representation learning further generates POI embeddings from sequential behavior while incorporating categorical information. Overall, the field is moving toward hybrid, jointly spatial-temporal, context-aware models with richer side information and learned representations.

2bf0c4575af82706fbf1d028e7f2092609ec18af.text:
### Mathematical Information Retrieval and Formula Semantics

This community focuses on making mathematical knowledge searchable, interpretable, and interoperable across scientific documents. Its central themes include semantic retrieval of equations, joint modeling of mathematical expressions and their surrounding natural-language context, and representation learning for formula symbols and structures.

Typical methods include neural embeddings such as symbol2vec, recurrent neural networks, correlated topic models, and multimodal topic models that connect equations with textual topics. The community also addresses symbolic and syntactic normalization, expression canonicalization, and semantic-preserving translation between document-preparation systems such as LaTeX and computer algebra systems including Maple and Mathematica.

A recurring challenge is the mismatch between mathematics’ precise formal semantics and the ambiguous, context-dependent ways mathematical knowledge is written in documents. This limits direct application of conventional machine-learning and information-retrieval methods and motivates representations that combine symbolic structure, presentation, and linguistic context.

Recent trends emphasize neural formula embeddings, large-scale equation–context corpora, topic-aware scientific retrieval, automated CAS/DPS conversion, and improved machine understanding of mathematical language. Together, these efforts aim to bridge textual, visual, and formal representations while supporting more accurate retrieval and computational reuse of mathematics.

5f80d3640693acbabd8b51fcbdef193cd6b118ef.text:
### Resource-Efficient Systems for Large-Scale Video Analytics

This community develops systems that make visual analytics practical under growing data volumes and constrained resources. A central theme is shifting computation and data management closer to cameras. **AutCam** and **iCam** support approximate analytics and counting/query services on battery-powered or autonomous IoT cameras, extending camera intelligence to off-grid and highly network-constrained environments. **Zero-streaming cameras** retain video locally and communicate with the cloud only when analytics is requested.

Another theme is accelerating exploratory and machine-learning workloads over large video collections. **BlazeIt** uses neural networks for fast exploratory queries while addressing inference cost and imperative analytics complexity. **VDMS** provides machine-oriented access to images, videos, and feature vectors through graph-based metadata search and specialized storage formats.

Typical methods include approximate and selective processing, learned models, metadata-driven retrieval, local inference, and hardware- and storage-aware optimization. **VStore** manages the full video path and applies backward derivation to select video-format configurations while balancing quality, quantity, and multiple resource types.

Recent trends emphasize frugal, autonomous, and privacy-preserving edge analytics; minimizing network transfer; supporting useful queries in off-grid settings; exploiting cold or sparsely queried video; and jointly optimizing accuracy, latency, energy, storage, and compute.

42c6ee15755f82bac18b08252f6377bdeabf2da8.text:
### Social Networks, Influence, and Information Integrity

This community studies how online platforms organize users, shape opinion, and enable manipulation. Core themes include misinformation, fake news, rumors, credibility, fact-checking, and research-information recommendation; political discourse, elections, polarization, ideology, and controversy; bots, trolls, state-sponsored influence, hate speech, gangs, abuse, and coordinated campaigns; privacy, data leakage, vandalism, and platform governance; and demographic, mental-health, and behavioral inference from social data. It also examines community identity and cohesion, debate sampling, collective attention, cross-language communication, and fairness in algorithmic summaries and moderation.

Typical methods combine large-scale Twitter, Reddit, Instagram, news, review, and geo-social datasets with graph and retweet analysis, crawling, sampling, temporal-event mining, PCA, statistical modeling, and machine learning. Researchers use linguistic, sentiment, stance, topic, embedding, image, metadata, and behavioral features; supervised, unsupervised, semi-supervised, graph-labeling, transfer, adversarial, and neural models. They develop conversational-network moderation, malicious-node removal, privacy access control, vandalism detection, and fairness-aware summarization.

Recent trends emphasize early and adversarial bot/misinformation detection, loosely coordinated influence and election manipulation, cross-language analysis, proactive responses to online abuse, and polarization measurement. New directions include privacy and data-quality governance, fairness-aware information curation, platform-content constraints, health and demographic prediction, and analysis of online responses to public controversies.

8d118ca50ebeb7001f6d874e39b92c855ac05af0.text:
**Multiplex Social Networks and Online Integrity**

This community studies heterogeneous and multiplex social and information networks, including cross-platform identities, user interactions, reviews, news discussions, and economic or social relations. Major themes include unsupervised identity linkage, multiplex structure and motifs, cross-layer interaction prediction, deceptive or abusive behavior, anomaly detection, and the spread and containment of rumors or other information.

Typical methods include factoid embeddings and graph neural networks for identity matching; multiplex graph matching and graphlet analysis; tensor decomposition with clustering for heterogeneous-network anomalies; generative models for deceptive reviews; network-based spam detection; feature-based interaction prediction; and multilayer spreading models with constrained optimization for rumor containment. Analyses use profile, content, network, and temporal interaction signals.

Recent trends emphasize reducing reliance on labeled data for cross-platform identity resolution, jointly exploiting multiple information channels, and evaluating individual linkage outcomes rather than only aggregate accuracy. Research is also moving toward integrated detection of spam, deception, flaming, and anomalous entities in online communities, while modeling interacting spreading processes and designing cost-aware interventions. Multiplex motifs, matched-filter graph search, and cross-type link prediction provide increasingly fine-grained views of structure and behavior.

eb0ee78f43e4c96b6f3f843fc547d52a3be278de.text:
### Social Media, Political Influence, and Information Integrity

This community studies how online platforms shape public opinion, political behavior, collective attention, and information integrity. Core themes include elections and computational propaganda, polarization, antagonism, misinformation, fake news, trolls, bots, malicious URLs, hate speech, spam, fraud, coordinated behavior, online abuse, and privacy risks. It also examines demographic and political-attribute inference, social influence, recommendation effects, content moderation, fair ranking and summarization, and real-time event or situational awareness.

Typical methods combine large-scale Twitter, Reddit, Facebook, YouTube, news, geospatial, and communication data with network, temporal, propagation, linguistic, and cross-language analysis. Researchers use PCA and stance clustering, topic modeling, embeddings, regression, convolutional and transfer-learning models, weak or semi-supervised labeling, interactive learning, anomaly and multidimensional outlier detection, adversarial training, conversational-network analysis, and epidemic or control-based diffusion models. They infer demographics, preferences, stances, credibility, influence, and suspicious behavior while evaluating privacy, bias, and fairness.

Recent work emphasizes fairness-aware ranking, recommendation, and summarization; antidote-data interventions against polarization; adversarially robust bot detection; proactive, context-sensitive moderation; privacy protection; and cross-platform or cross-language analysis of political campaigns. Other trends include identifying influential strangers, detecting geo-temporal events, measuring reactions to data scandals, and modeling malicious-URL propagation and user engagement.

8f09cfd96797b6b2f8ecb80c743f7a925b067921.text:
## Community Status

No papers currently remain to substantiate this community’s research themes, methods, or recent trends. Consequently, claims concerning unbiased learning-to-rank, counterfactual evaluation, propensity weighting, LambdaMART, and offline–online recommender evaluation have been removed.

4a29bbd1f7d6d1215a65af5c4027d93623ae51b8.text:
## Recommender Systems: Sequential, Adaptive, and Responsible Personalization

**Main themes.** This community studies personalized ranking under sparse, implicit, noisy, and evolving feedback across e-commerce, media, advertising, and other platforms. Core problems include anonymous session and lifelong sequential recommendation, cold start, cross-domain and shared-account personalization, long-tail discovery and popularity bias, multimodal and content-aware matching, explainability, fairness, and balancing user utility with business revenue and demand timing.

**Typical methods.** Approaches span matrix and metric factorization, Bayesian and pairwise ranking, factorization machines, hybrid content–collaborative models, and probabilistic latent-state models. Neural methods include VAEs, feature-interaction and multi-task models, attention, recurrent and Transformer encoders, graph neural networks, knowledge-graph embeddings, and deep reinforcement learning. Contextual and multi-armed bandits support online adaptation and causal or incremental-effect optimization. Multimodal models use text, images, audio, reviews, and transaction context. Binary hashing, distillation, approximate retrieval, diversity re-ranking, and temporal exposure correction improve efficiency and fairness; path-based and tree-guided models improve explanations.

**Recent trends.** Emphasis is shifting toward real-time session and multi-action modeling, novelty and demand awareness, whole-chain optimization, revenue-aware recommendation, cross-domain transfer, scalable lifelong personalization, unbiased offline evaluation, reproducibility, and time-sensitive control of popularity and exposure.

0ad141d0bcfbf3187a678ceee8a328d574b076cf.text:
### Online Influence, Integrity, and Platform Governance

**Main themes.** This community studies how platforms organize users, shape political opinion, and enable manipulation. Core topics include polarization, ideological and extremist communities, echo chambers, misinformation, rumors, conspiracy and propaganda, elections, censorship, hate and abuse, demographic inference, mental-health signals, privacy, and news-source quality. It examines bots, trolls, malicious accounts, spam, state-linked influence operations, cross-platform communities, and information diffusion during crises.

**Typical methods.** Research combines large-scale Twitter, Reddit, Instagram, news, and cross-language data with temporal and continuous-time network models, diffusion, dynamic and overlapping-community detection, graph labeling, signed-graph and stance analysis, and link prediction. Other methods include topic modeling, sentiment and credibility analysis, NLP, computer vision, multimodal features, semi-supervised and adversarial learning, transfer learning, causal and statistical analysis, and interpretable graph inference. Systems include automated moderation, abuse and bot detection, fact-checking, influence minimization, privacy-preserving access control, and principled sampling or API-query optimization.

**Recent trends.** Increasing attention targets election and state-linked manipulation, cross-national and cross-lingual analysis, targeted demographic propaganda, harmful-account early detection, contextual moderation, platform-content constraints, and data-source bias. Work also emphasizes continuous-time dynamics, fairness in summaries and classification, explainability, privacy, limited labels, adversarial adaptation, and proactive mitigation.

6e80f642dc4a0f79492e8ba83d10d5da05cc9dad.text:
**Cross-Platform Identity Linkage and Multilayer Diffusion**

This community studies relational integration and behavioral analysis across heterogeneous databases, documents, devices, time periods, and online social networks. Core themes include record and user-identity linkage; cross-platform profile, content, friendship, and activity alignment; privacy and deanonymization; information, rumor, innovation, and complex-contagion diffusion; multilayer structure and interlayer similarity; graph pattern discovery, anomaly detection, and network formation; and spam, flaming, and deceptive-content mitigation.

Typical methods combine attribute-, content-, and graph-based matching; unsupervised factoid embeddings; graph neural networks; multiplex graph matching and graphlets; temporal multilayer representations; threshold, epidemic, thermodynamic, and game-theoretic diffusion models; evolutionary and optimization-based analysis; topic mixtures and state prediction; clustering; and unsupervised temporal anomaly detection. Empirical work uses cross-platform datasets, behavioral distributions, and visual analytics to evaluate linkage and sharing patterns.

Recent trends emphasize scalable analysis of multiplex and evolving networks; identity resolution with scarce labels; privacy-aware study of cross-platform personas; platform-specific behavior and cross-posting; coupled contagions and social-physical diffusion; and robust detection or containment of rumors and anomalous activity. The community increasingly combines network topology with content, geography, media exposure, and temporal signals to explain and predict online behavior.

e4ff5066897eadaaad20d863ff151f082d166c1e.text:
### Research Software as Citable, Reproducible Scholarship

This community examines how research software, data, and computational workflows can become recognized, durable, transparent, and measurable components of scientific scholarship. Key themes include integrating software into citation graphs, improving reproducibility, establishing consistent terminology, and creating incentives and evidence of software impact.

Typical approaches are conceptual, infrastructural, and policy-oriented: proposing graph models for relationships among papers and software; designing publication venues such as the Journal of Open Source Software (JOSS) to provide quality review and academic credit; and advocating complete, executable research environments rather than isolated source archives. Literature surveys and decision trees classify competing meanings of reproducible research, while empirical studies assess citation-based software impact, including through the lme4 R package. Reviews also examine infrastructures for transparent scholarly communication and the requirements imposed by funders, journals, and conferences.

Recent trends treat software and associated data as first-class research objects. Open-science policies increasingly require data and software management plans and availability statements, although reproducible publication remains demanding: sharing scripts and files alone is insufficient. Efforts increasingly connect publication, credit, citation, and reproducibility through mechanisms such as transitive credit, while inconsistent practices, fragmented terminology, and unreliable impact measures remain unresolved.

4181e72926ac53e639395f8dd1fae4456aa8bd8f.text:
### Dynamic Heterogeneous Network Learning

This community develops methods for large, heterogeneous, multimodal, and evolving networks, including social, information, citation, semantic, knowledge, multiplex, bipartite, and tagged networks. Core tasks include node and graph representation learning, relationship and role profiling, community discovery, link prediction, graph similarity and alignment, temporal influence analysis, fraud and churn prediction, and recommendation.

Typical methods combine topology with attributes, text, tags, user activity, and interaction semantics. They include random walks, temporal motifs and causal paths, clustering coefficients and other higher-order structures, latent-space and hyperbolic models, graph convolutional and recurrent networks, attention, matrix-factorization embeddings, meta-path discovery, ensemble and multi-representation learning, semi-supervised variational models, and neural structure-content fusion. Typed graphlets, multiplex persistence, social exposure, and collective prediction across aligned networks are prominent. Graph comparison uses spectral, topological, metric, probabilistic, and embedding-based approaches.

Scalability is pursued through streaming and dynamic embeddings, approximate computation, graph statistics software, and scalable combinatorial optimization. Recent trends emphasize interpretable relationship semantics, dynamic link prediction, adversarial attacks on communities and temporal predictors, privacy-aware robustness, content-user recommendation, explainable churn and fraud mitigation, and evaluation on real operational platforms.

720de87b157f7c1744c515778215cf3ddd815c84.text:
## Probabilistic and Trustworthy Data Management

This community studies data management when information is uncertain, incomplete, inconsistent, correlated, or derived through complex rules. Core themes include probabilistic databases, uncertain joins and ranking, approximate and exact query answering, aggregates, provenance and lineage, inconsistent-data semantics, belief annotations, and ontology-mediated querying. It also investigates dependencies, query determinacy, finite controllability, and tractable reasoning over knowledge graphs and relational data.

Typical methods execute probabilistic inference inside relational engines using safe or bounded query plans, semirings and semimodules, possible-world models, knowledge compilation, BDDs, decomposition trees, and structural-width techniques. Provenance systems use query instrumentation, lineage graphs, rewriting, and heuristic or cost-based optimization. Rule-based reasoning relies on chase procedures, guarded or warded tuple-generating dependencies, acyclicity conditions, and graph rewriting. Uncertain similarity queries exploit indexing, sorting, probabilistic pruning, and ranking distributions.

Recent trends emphasize making probabilistic query processing practical at scale, supporting correlations, temporal data, negation, aggregates, and approximate answers. The community is strengthening theoretical guarantees on decidability, complexity, boundedness, and determinacy while connecting them to usable systems. Provenance-aware explanations, sensitivity analysis, interactive database exploration, SQL testing, performance debugging, and schema-agnostic progressive entity resolution broaden trustworthy, interpretable data management.

a47a0f16b06d412d6526e540902f2b6432a2637a.text:
**Information Retrieval: Neural, Structured, Interactive, and Bias-Aware Search**

This community develops retrieval and ranking systems that combine lexical matching, pretrained neural semantics, structured data, knowledge graphs, multimodal signals, and user or session context. Core themes include query–document and cross-document interaction, passage and document reranking, fielded entity and attribute retrieval, entity and table discovery, dataset and geoportal search, question answering, citation recommendation, conversational and reformulated search, and personalized e-commerce, email, news, multimedia, mobile, academic, biomedical, and expert search. It also addresses complex answers, scientific QA, and intelligent spreadsheet assistance.

Typical methods include pointwise, pairwise, listwise, groupwise, multitask, constrained, differentiable, and reinforcement-learning objectives; multi-stage retrieval and reranking; attention, recurrent, convolutional, sequence-to-sequence, and efficient Transformer architectures; semantic, hyperbolic, graph, and image embeddings; matrix factorization; query expansion and translation models; weak, pseudo-labeled, and selectively supervised learning; and scalable approximate retrieval. Counterfactual and inverse-propensity methods explicitly correct position, examination, and selection bias in click-based learning.

Recent trends include large-scale benchmarked neural ranking, generative relevance scoring, zero- and limited-label transfer, history-aware interaction, multimodal personalization, table and dataset reuse, efficient time-budgeted reranking, diversified academic retrieval, and rigorous offline/online and user-behavior evaluation.

b8cc8912a487d37293205b1cdd11a75255d1c34b.text:
## Recommender Systems: Sequential, Multimodal, and Responsible Personalization

This community studies personalized ranking and set recommendation from sparse, implicit, noisy, heterogeneous, and evolving behavior. Major settings include anonymous sessions, sequential and lifelong recommendation, next-item and next-basket prediction, music and playlist continuation, cross-domain and shared-account personalization, marketplace, travel, job, image, and user-generated-content recommendation. It also addresses cold start, long-tail discovery, novelty seeking, user demands, and two-sided provider–consumer objectives.

Typical methods include matrix, metric, tensor, Bayesian, and neural factorization; probabilistic latent-state models; recurrent networks and transformers; session graphs and graph neural networks; heterogeneous neural models; multi-task and dual-transfer learning; variational and adversarial methods; knowledge-graph embeddings; contextual bandits and reinforcement learning; causal and treatment-effect modeling; and binary or distilled representations for efficient retrieval. Systems fuse text, reviews, images, audio, acoustic and aesthetic features, transactions, geography, time, trust, and interaction feedback.

Recent trends emphasize real-time and large-scale inference, approximate or hashed retrieval, memory-based lifelong modeling, role-aware and cross-domain transfer, and production tooling and online experimentation. Growing attention targets revenue and demand optimization, provider and popularity fairness, temporal exposure correction, novelty and diversity, explainability, calibration, robustness to feedback and offline-evaluation bias, and causal measurement of recommendation impact.

062ef5d59667fa083f2fff99dfe9c91b8a42cead.text:
**Information Retrieval: Neural Ranking, Interactive Search, and Structured Discovery**

This community develops semantic, entity-aware, personalized, and interactive retrieval for web, enterprise, e-commerce, conversational, tabular, and multimodal settings. Neural rankers—especially BERT and multilingual encoders—support document and passage reranking, FAQ and conversational question answering, short-text similarity, query-intent representation, cross-lingual transfer, and relevance estimation. Entity fields, knowledge graphs, semantic hashing, tables, and approximate nearest-neighbor indexes address vocabulary mismatch, long-tail items, heterogeneous sources, and large-scale vector search.

Typical methods include pointwise, pairwise, listwise, groupwise, and permutation-invariant learning-to-rank; attention and cross-document interaction; query expansion and semantic field matching; weak supervision from unsupervised rankers and logs; multitask and adversarial learning; and axiomatic regularization. Graph-based indexing, graph merging, embeddings, and degree optimization support efficient retrieval. Evaluation and learning increasingly use clicks, purchases, multi-user activity trails, counterfactual feedback, and contextual mobile or spoken-search studies.

Recent trends emphasize production ranking libraries and multi-stage pipelines balancing quality and latency; explainable neural-ranking exploration; personalized autocomplete, news, recommendations, and conversational assistants; aggregation across heterogeneous result sources with reinforcement learning; direct business-metric and CTR optimization; robust query-performance prediction; and interactive discovery over tables, products, and other structured data.

5301517c27666bf6220cfe0ff7842b0841b37622.text:
## Graph, Sequence, and Social Behavior Analytics

This community studies graph-structured, sequential, spatial, and social-media data to discover behavioral patterns, relationships, influence, collective identity, mobility outcomes, and actionable knowledge. Applications include recommendation and content matching, team and investigative search, urban-migrant retention, sexual-violence report tracking, online movements, IoT analytics, mobility trajectories, and scholarly or information retrieval.

Typical methods include graph pattern matching, strong and contextual graph querying, temporal subgraph isomorphism, graph-based feature extraction, PageRank, MapReduce, and approximate big-data computation. Sequence analytics emphasizes frequent, closed, constrained, serial, parallel, and high-utility episodes or subsequences, including recency-, correlation-, uncertainty-, and individualized-threshold-aware mining. Other techniques include association-rule and tree-query mining, MDL-based pattern summarization, n-gram computation, supervised classification, and utility/privacy trade-offs.

Data include social and interaction graphs, relational and event databases, clickstreams, telecommunication logs, trajectories, IoT readings, scholarly networks, and Twitter or Instagram discourse.

Recent trends emphasize scalable distributed mining, utility- and trend-aware discovery beyond frequency, concise and interpretable pattern representations, privacy-preserving analytics, context- and relationship-aware graph search, temporal pattern matching, and automated analysis of sensitive social issues and collective action.

d6da90b97d6569020e4fa15bc20628f47101f675.text:
### Dynamic, Temporal, and Multilayer Graph Analysis

This community studies how evolving, weighted, directed, and multilayer networks are modeled, queried, and exploited. Core themes include stream graphs and link streams, temporal networks, and quantities capturing interaction timing, duration, ordering, weights, directions, and layer structure. Bipartite stream graphs support temporal recommendation from implicit user–item behavior, while social–financial networks enable analysis of how real-world friendships and cryptocurrency transactions co-evolve. These models support journeys, connectivity, density, communities, centrality, clustering, and shortest paths, including foremost, fastest, and latency-aware distances.

A second theme is scalable graph mining and querying. Methods include reachability and shortest-path indexes, labeling schemes, community detection over shared Git commits to identify related repositories, and parallel exact indexing using vertex-centric computation, SIMD multicore architectures, and batch execution.

The community also examines diffusion, influence, recommendation, and dynamic signals. Graph-variate signal analysis uses connectivity graphs to filter instantaneous multivariate interactions and detect changing activity, complementing contagion, opinion spreading, trust, sentiment, and information-mobilization models.

Recent trends emphasize richer stream semantics, temporal and implicit recommendation, joint social–economic analysis, graph-based signal processing, software-ecosystem mining, layer-aware centrality, and scalable exact computation.

c60e1662378958d3f511e0c8751037404c691f36.text:
## Social, Spatial, and Knowledge-Graph Intelligence

This community studies how social, mobile, and location-aware data reveal collective identity and action, public opinion, sexual-violence reporting, cultural assimilation, demographics, migration, human mobility, urban activity, and health or environmental risk. It also increasingly addresses open knowledge ecosystems, including Wikidata/DBpedia integration, vandalism, edit quality, data completeness, multilingual linking, and newcomer contribution.

Typical methods include supervised NLP, sentiment and topic analysis, hashtag and content classification, time-series analysis, and predictive behavioral modeling; network analysis of movements, scientific migration, and social interaction; regression and machine learning; deep neural methods for hierarchical geolocation, home-location prediction, image–knowledge-graph linking, and privacy-risk detection; trajectory reconstruction and distributed MapReduce subtrajectory joins; and gravity, radiation, statistical, rule-mining, and optimization-based mobility or completeness models. Data include Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, Wikipedia, Wikidata, DBpedia, ORCID, mobile and trajectory records, and demographic or health-related sources.

Recent trends emphasize scalable automated tracking of underreported harms, real-time content and knowledge-base moderation, completeness-aware collaborative knowledge graphs, multilingual semantic linking, high-resolution and privacy-conscious geolocation, demographic and culturally sensitive analysis, migration forecasting, and distributed mobility analytics. Social platforms are increasingly treated as infrastructure for collective identity, public-health intervention, and open knowledge stewardship.

470dd10e857f1804ad050ca2edf0f985020387c7.text:
### Preserving and Enriching Evolving Digital Knowledge

This community studies durable, interpretable, accessible, and discoverable digital information across Web, scholarly, cultural, and biomedical contexts. Themes include repository and compound-object architectures, persistent identifiers, provenance, versioning, rights, FAIR data management, research objects, structured interactive reports, and knowledge graphs for machine-actionable scholarly communication. Web archiving is central: cross-archive aggregation, temporal search, event-focused collections, seed generation, archive profiling, missing-page recommendations, accessibility, replay fidelity, and fixity verification. Scholarly communication increasingly includes entity resolution, semantic peer review, interlinked comments, and links among publications, data, software, and authoritative sources.

Typical methods combine OAIS, Fedora, Memento, MPEG-21, OAI-PMH, RDF, SPARQL, PROV-O, PAV, Open Annotation, nanopublications, and FAIR principles with APIs, portals, query languages, and reproducible datasets. Large-scale archive indexes and logs support memory-efficient profiling, caching, federated retrieval, and machine-learning prediction of holdings. Entity extraction and resolution, visual learning-to-rank, semantic recommendation, link analysis, and structured filter–extract–aggregate–visualize workflows support discovery and analysis.

Recent trends emphasize production-validated archive optimization, cookie-aware replay, community-guided crawling, micro-collection seeds, cross-archive datasets, semantic scholarly infrastructure, multimodal knowledge acquisition, and inclusive access. Persistent challenges include heterogeneous schemas, temporal noise, incomplete or biased captures, dynamic accessibility, privacy, and preserving meaning and integrity as resources evolve.

6078328efa4560f190f69c7e8f61c5959a11ddca.text:
### Personalized Recommendation: Sequential, Graph, and Multi-Objective Learning

This community studies personalized recommendation across commerce, media, music, fashion, travel, education, healthcare, jobs, and social activities. Core themes include sparse explicit and implicit feedback, cold start and long-tail discovery, anonymous sessions, lifelong and cross-domain behavior, shared accounts, multi-behavior learning, and the integration of user, item, textual, visual, knowledge-graph, temporal, and trust signals. Increasing attention targets diversity, popularity bias, fairness, explainability, novelty, user welfare, and business revenue.

Typical methods span neighborhood models, matrix, tensor, metric, and probabilistic factorization; Bayesian and pairwise ranking; hybrid and multimodal neural networks; autoencoders; RNNs and transformers; memory-augmented and graph neural networks; knowledge-graph embeddings; hashing and distillation for efficient retrieval; and latent-state models for dynamic interests. Reinforcement learning, contextual and multi-armed bandits, causal treatment-effect modeling, and multi-task transfer support online optimization and cross-domain recommendation.

Recent trends emphasize session and next-item prediction, demand and skip modeling, lifelong personalization, complex item transitions, whole-chain decision-making, and novelty seeking. Research increasingly optimizes revenue and long-term exposure alongside relevance, including temporally adaptive popularity mitigation. Explainable path-based and tree-guided models, fairness-aware ranking, causal and bias-corrected offline evaluation, productization at scale, and reproducibility are also prominent.

f2441db648ed11ba2ce6e34480bf08fdc3f1f3b9.text:
### Dynamic, Heterogeneous, and Robust Graph Analytics

This community develops computational methods for large, complex, uncertain, and evolving networks, including social, information, scholarly, semantic, multiplex, multilayer, bipartite, and heterogeneous systems. Core themes include node and graph representation learning, community and role discovery, relationship-semantic profiling, link prediction, graph similarity, anomaly and fraud detection, network alignment, ranking, recommendation, influence maximization, and typed motifs and higher-order structure.

Typical methods combine topology with attributes, text, tags, temporal events, multimodal content, and cross-network evidence. They include random walks, latent-space and hyperbolic geometric models, stochastic blockmodels, Bayesian and generative inference, matrix factorization, spectral methods, graph statistics, and neural architectures such as GCNs, attention networks, LSTMs, autoencoders, variational models, and feature propagation. Ensemble and multi-view embeddings capture multiple social contexts, while automatic meta-path discovery and co-embedding address heterogeneous networks. Sampling, compression, approximation, and software tooling support scalable analysis.

Recent work emphasizes continuous-time dynamics, causal and time-respecting paths, dynamic link prediction, multi-representation and ensemble embeddings, interpretable clustering and churn prediction, cross-network link prediction, and content–structure fusion. Robustness research increasingly studies multiscale and time-aware adversarial attacks. Applications include recommendation, question routing, influence analysis, fraud mitigation, organizational and social-media analysis, education, and cryptocurrency security.

bb79b82fb68dfe586124637712cc270dba65a124.text:
## Scholarly Metadata, Knowledge Organization, and Research Networks

This community studies scholarly communication and digital-library infrastructures through bibliometrics, information retrieval, semantic-web modeling, and network analysis. Core themes include author disambiguation, publication and coauthorship patterns, division of labor in research teams, citation-based technology forecasting, information-object identity and digital preservation, and the representation, evolution, and quality of knowledge-organization systems (KOSs). It also examines linked data for libraries, archives, and museums; RDF-based bibliographic repositories; classification systems, thesauri, and their relationship to natural-language concepts; and search behavior in digital libraries and the Web.

Typical methods include citation, coauthorship, author–task bipartite, and concept networks; centrality and temporal analysis; unsupervised similarity-based entity resolution; bibliographic mining; and comparisons of classifications and publishing venues. Semantic-web work uses RDF, OWL, SKOS, FRBR/FRAD, URI modeling, linked-data conversion, and computable vocabulary-quality checks. Retrieval studies analyze queries, sessions, task types, eye tracking, thesaurus- and classification-based topic segmentation, and user-reported difficulty. Knowledge discovery combines keyword co-occurrence, NLP, and predictive sequence models.

Recent trends emphasize machine-processable KOSs, linked cultural-heritage data, formal preservation criteria, automated metadata quality assessment, early identification of influential patents, and prediction of emerging relations in scientific literature.

ae1a9590576a256068af0ac72f3fab9a77df7813.text:
## Collaborative Knowledge, Social Search, and Network Intelligence

This community studies how user-generated and networked data—Wikipedia, Wiktionary, folksonomies, social media, web archives, and professional networks—support knowledge organization, discovery, search, and collective behavior. Themes include extracting structured and multilingual knowledge; building ontologies, thesauri, and knowledge graphs; analyzing tags, links, categories, and archives; collaborative collection curation; expertise and talent search; and modeling influence, diffusion, opinions, and mobility.

Typical methods combine large-scale crawling, archive and query-log analysis, graph and bipartite-network modeling, centrality and local-dimension measures, hierarchical-backbone extraction, clustering, co-occurrence and similarity analysis, statistical distribution modeling, matrix factorization, learning-to-rank, entity linking, NLP, agent-based simulation, and interactive visualization. Applications include entity and related-term search, personalized recommendations, breaking-news and location forecasting, influencer identification, semantic navigation, and collaborative web-archive exploration.

Recent trends emphasize production-scale neural ranking and low-latency deployment, adaptive statistical retrieval, bias-aware recommendation, fine-grained geospatial prediction, and richer modeling of social influence and opinion formation. Research increasingly integrates dynamic, multilingual, and heterogeneous network signals with structured semantic representations, while supporting collaborative curation and socially responsible personalization.

648cb01f2de6a59a80dc548d9b6867ede08be236.text:
### Semantic Graph Data Management and Integration

**Main research themes:** This community studies querying, integrating, validating, and managing heterogeneous relational, RDF, property-graph, XML, and cloud data. Core topics include SPARQL semantics and static analysis, RDF–property-graph interoperability, query translation and reverse engineering, programmable view updates, schema inference and coexisting schema versions, categorical data integration, and query-by-example. It also addresses public graph services, large-scale subgraph and regular-expression queries, graph database benchmarking, and semantic search, recommendation, and relation extraction.

**Typical methods:** Formal semantics, category theory, monads, sketches, CQL and Datalog, bidirectional transformations, schema mappings, query rewriting, entailment and containment analysis, abductive reasoning, semantic similarity, and example-driven inference. Systems use partitioning, preemption, sublinear indexes, GPU parallelism, MPP execution, BSP, distributed/cloud databases, and workload-oriented benchmarking. Neural methods include attention, LSTMs, graph/capsule networks, and hierarchical multi-label learning for text and entity graphs.

**Recent trends:** Research is expanding RDF/property-graph interoperability and rigorous SPARQL foundations while making updates, migrations, and schema evolution programmable and verifiable. Scalable graph processing increasingly combines cloud services, public-query preemption, GPU acceleration, native MPP engines, and standardized benchmarks. Semantic interfaces are becoming more accessible through query-by-example, intent discovery, contextual recommendation, and learned relation extraction, alongside continued attention to XML/schema learning and interoperable scientific data sharing.

e16a958ebe5e64202883be004aaec6bf2ba06735.text:
**Information Retrieval: Neural, Structured, and Interactive Search**

This community develops semantic retrieval, relevance modeling, and scalable search for web, enterprise, e-commerce, scientific, social, conversational, and structured data. Neural ranking increasingly combines pretrained language models (especially BERT), dense and lexical matching, cross-document interaction, permutation-invariant or groupwise scoring, multi-stage reranking, and passage- or field-aware representations. Research spans entities and knowledge graphs, tables, FAQs, short texts, multilingual transfer, user intent, and heterogeneous result aggregation.

Typical methods include learning-to-rank, query expansion, semantic similarity, axiomatic regularization, weak supervision and data programming, click/log-based supervision, graph embeddings and merged k-NN indexes, semantic hashing, locality-sensitive and high-dimensional vector search, and reinforcement learning for source selection. Personalization uses context, activity trails, neighborhood effects, and online adaptation. Evaluation increasingly addresses biased behavioral signals, query performance, metric validity, latency, and user effort, with exploratory tools supporting neural-ranker interpretation.

Recent trends emphasize domain- and multilingual-adapted neural retrieval, low-label training, permutation-aware ranking, graph-based approximate search, intent and history modeling, spoken and conversational search, personalized recommendations, dynamic news and e-commerce systems, answer-centric interfaces, web mining and classification, and production architectures balancing relevance, immediacy, scalability, and interaction quality.

18a590f3c16f57cb6438230f0b4e95f7d90e0671.text:
### Social Media Geolocation and Crisis Intelligence

This community studies how large-scale digital traces reveal location, movement, collective behavior, and rapidly evolving events. A central theme is geolocation from sparse or indirect signals, including tweet text, user profiles, interaction patterns, images, and multilingual content. Researchers also analyze mobility and migration networks, home locations, urban and population structure, scientific migration, and social-media user behavior.

Disaster and civil-unrest intelligence is increasingly prominent: systems detect events and sub-events, extract emergency aids and keyphrases, summarize situational and topical information, rank alerts under responder workload constraints, and support emergency mapping, flood awareness, disease-risk assessment, and forecasting. Multimodal social action and visual-theme analysis extend beyond text.

Typical methods include hierarchical and character-aware neural networks, convolutional and recurrent models, multimodal learning, embeddings and cross-lingual transfer, keyword and event-volume analysis, unsupervised clustering, graph-based ranking, network centrality, sentiment and behavioral classification, abstractive summarization, GIS interfaces, ontologies, and online forecasting. Active learning and models of annotation error address data quality and bias.

Recent trends favor real-time, high-resolution, multimodal and multilingual inference; explicit uncertainty, bias-aware annotation, and credibility assessment; integration with knowledge graphs; and operational decision support for emergencies, public health, and collective action.

9f54da675319efc5d80cf1510ef7f002aff8d116.text:
## Adaptive and Trustworthy Data Systems

This community builds data-management systems that remain fast, scalable, predictable, verifiable, and responsible across changing workloads, data, and hardware. Themes include multicore and distributed OLTP, strong and adaptive replication, transactional stream processing, concurrent stateful streaming, large-window stream joins, high-velocity multidimensional ingestion, and hardware-conscious execution. It also studies adaptive indexing and immutable, multi-version, tamper-evident structures; approximate analytics over relational, video, sensor, geospatial, and other data; and resilient, geo-scale blockchain databases.

Typical methods combine specialized execution and storage architectures with benchmarks, external-behavior testing, and feedback-driven modeling. They include MVCC and transactional state management, NUMA- and hardware-aware scheduling, partition-based and parallel stream joins, shared-I/O and merge scheduling, succinct and polynomial indexes, Merkle structures, query-driven layouts, and replication middleware. Machine learning supports cardinality, selectivity, runtime, resource, and error estimation—including monotonic deep models and models requiring neither database statistics nor execution plans—and enables learned cost models, approximate query processing, query composition, and adaptive optimization. Approximate video filters and learned sampling provide fast answers with quality guarantees.

Recent trends emphasize robust learned components, interactive and approximate analytics, hardware-efficient and concurrent streaming, adaptive execution under limited feedback, high-rate ingestion, and geo-scale, auditable Byzantine-resilient infrastructure.

85a2c79769daa6cfc3ef2cd38d4c75392293af7b.text:
### Graph Querying, Integration, Semantics, and Scalable Analytics

This community studies foundations and systems for querying, integrating, validating, evolving, and analyzing graph and structured data, including RDF, SPARQL, property graphs, knowledge bases, uncertain and geospatial graphs, XML, relational views, and cloud datastores. Core themes include graph-pattern, navigational, regular-expression, and subgraph-isomorphism queries; query-by-example and query-intent discovery; federated and preemptible Web querying; RDF–property-graph interoperability; ontology-mediated answering; programmable view updates; schema inference and coexisting schema evolution; reliability optimization; and graph-database benchmarking.

Typical methods combine formal semantics, category theory, complexity and undecidability analysis, relational algebra, SQL/Datalog reduction, abductive reasoning, semantic similarity, approximate homomorphism tests, indexing, partitioning, sampling, and approximation algorithms. Systems use SPARQL, GeoSPARQL, Cypher, Gremlin, GSQL, integrated graph algebras, and interoperable mappings, with GPU acceleration, massively parallel processing, and cloud or multi-tenant storage. Machine learning includes knowledge-graph embeddings, graph convolution, and neural relation extraction.

Recent trends emphasize RDF/PG standardization, programmable and bidirectional data evolution, schema learning for XML, ontology-aware semantics, billion-node and GPU query processing, bounded-latency Web services, cloud database deployment, and rigorous cross-system benchmarks, while combining symbolic querying with learned representations.

0e3fc8d989f20bb392c02d6b32fb00b7947bbfe2.text:
**Web Search, Semantic Data, and Social Network Analytics**

This community develops search, ranking, and knowledge-integration methods for large-scale, heterogeneous Web and user-generated data. Core themes include Wikipedia and Wiktionary mining, multilingual entity linking, ontology and thesaurus matching, semantic annotation, collaborative tagging, category and hyperlink graphs, query expansion, and graph-based retrieval. Search applications span news discovery, library catalogs, travel and experiential search, talent and expertise discovery, personalized professional search, and location forecasting from microblog streams.

Typical methods combine learning-to-rank, personalized and example-driven retrieval, graph centrality and traversal, HITS-style scoring, collaborative filtering and matrix factorization, information extraction, entity disambiguation, relational and RDF/SKOS modeling, SPARQL, clustering, and semantic visualization. Evaluation increasingly addresses topic selection, judging depth versus breadth, credibility, snippets, clickthrough bias, and user-oriented metrics.

Social-data research analyzes influence, homophily, reciprocity, communities, talent flows, and attention in Twitter and professional networks. Fairness and representational bias in recommendation and ranking remain important concerns.

Recent trends emphasize multilingual and high-throughput semantic infrastructure, knowledge graphs built from collaborative resources, interactive and experiential search, real-time social and geospatial analytics, personalized discovery, and bias-aware data collection and recommendation.

1c9c1fb06773aa7ba1e2255066ded5ad6faec3de.text:
## Computational Analysis of Fictional Character Networks

This community studies fictional narratives as social graphs, representing characters as nodes and interactions—such as conversation, friendship, or killing—as edges. It supports plot summarization, subplot and role detection, narrative classification, recommendation, and analysis of social dynamics in films and serialized television.

Typical methods include manual, co-occurrence-based, and machine-learning extraction of character networks, including speech- and multimedia-based speaker identification. Researchers compare extraction precision and its effects on network analysis, examining static structure, causality, centrality, temporal evolution, and changing relationships across episodes and seasons.
