Link prediction forecasts killer–victim pairs from prior interactions and metadata. Ecological-diversity measures based on Shannon entropy and Jensen–Shannon divergence estimate effective cast sizes and compare character composition for classification and recommendation.

Recent directions emphasize dynamic and temporally smoothed conversational networks, automated extraction at scale, and predictive modeling for plot reconstruction. Increasing attention is given to long-form serialized narratives and reusable annotated resources: the Serial Speakers dataset provides multimodal and speech annotations for 161 episodes of *Breaking Bad*, *Game of Thrones*, and *House of Cards*, enabling cross-episode speaker analysis and benchmarking for multimedia and speech-processing applications.

4e4422290c22fc7c6fea9f17edf0db9b124ec6d5.text:
## Graph Representation, Similarity, and Dynamic Network Analysis

This community studies how to represent, compare, align, and predict structure in social, information, knowledge, relational, heterogeneous, multiplex, and temporal networks. Core themes include entity resolution and data integration, link prediction, graph and node similarity, community and role discovery, anomaly and fraud detection, recommendation, user behavior and churn, privacy, and cross-network matching. Increasing attention goes to higher-order structure, reciprocal interactions, causal paths, and link persistence across layers.

Typical methods combine neighborhoods, motifs and higher-order cliques, clustering, centrality, random walks, spectral and geometric techniques, matrix completion, graph layouts, and probabilistic or latent-space models. Embeddings are central: dynamic, role-aware, multimodal, text- and attribute-enhanced, multi-context, ensemble, and cross-network representations support downstream prediction. GCNs, LSTMs, relational and hierarchical-attention GNNs, variational autoencoders, deep information fusion, automatic path discovery, and interpretable clustering are common.

Recent trends emphasize scalable, low-supervision entity resolution and schema matching; global-topology- and change-aware dynamic embeddings; end-to-end temporal link prediction; higher-order and time-aware modeling; adversarial attacks against community detection and dynamic prediction; privacy-aware and business-oriented fraud analytics; and robust, explainable similarity and recommendation. Multiplex research increasingly examines cross-layer persistence, while heterogeneous-network methods reduce reliance on manually specified meta-paths.

4def2a2924b5694338f5462b69b58828cd188dca.text:
## Network Science for Ranking, Knowledge, and Influence

This community studies directed, temporal, multilayer, and evolving networks to understand information flow, discoverability, centrality, social influence, and knowledge production. Google-matrix methods—including PageRank, personalized PageRank, Katz and Bonacich centrality, hubs and authorities, spectra, and communicability—are applied to Wikipedia, knowledge graphs, scientific migration, online communities, social movements, and narrative character networks. Research also examines centrality axioms, distinctiveness, strategic network formation, social status, learning, belief aggregation, and signed or balanced relations.

A major focus is improving network content and connectivity: recommending missing Wikipedia articles, sections, editors, and cross-language coverage; assessing RDF and knowledge-graph completeness; predicting missing facts; and designing edge additions, deletions, or rewiring to improve communicability or navigation. Other applications include narrative summarization and genre analysis, migration prediction, harmful-content immunization, and institutional or collective behavior.

Typical methods combine longitudinal and multilingual graph construction with random walks, Markov and learning models, spectral and matrix techniques, optimization, game theory, machine learning, rule mining, sequence analysis, null models, and visualization. Text mining and NLP increasingly extract signed, semantic, temporal, and multilayer relations.

Recent trends emphasize Wikipedia and collaborative knowledge-graph quality, newcomer participation, multilingual knowledge transfer, automated network extraction, explainable recommendations, dynamic social learning, and network design for resilience and information dissemination.

3ea68060b353f7ef5596d30f5d404f9c8cafabd8.text:
### Utility-Oriented Sequential and Correlated Pattern Mining

This community focuses on discovering informative patterns in complex, time-ordered, and multi-dimensional data beyond traditional frequency-based mining. Central tasks include high-utility sequential, episode, occupancy, and correlated-utility pattern mining, motivated by marketing, e-commerce, click-stream analysis, recommendation, route planning, IoT, medical analysis, and bioinformatics.

Typical methods develop utility-aware mining frameworks and efficient search algorithms, including UMEpi for high-utility episodes, projection-based mining (ProUM), fast utility mining for complex sequences, and occupancy-aware approaches that assess how substantially a pattern occupies or explains transactions. Newer methods also model correlations among items, recognizing that valuable combinations may include low-utility items associated with highly profitable products. Parallel processing and scalability remain important because utility mining is computationally and memory intensive. Privacy-preserving utility mining addresses the protection of sensitive information.

Recent trends move beyond uniform thresholds and isolated item utilities. Researchers propose individualized minimum-utility thresholds, recency- and trend-aware mining, multi-dimensional and multiple-sequence analysis, and uncertainty-aware models for heterogeneous IoT data. Occupancy and item-correlation modeling provide more realistic assessments of pattern quality, while surveys consolidate progress toward scalable, timely, privacy-conscious, and application-aware utility analytics.

95cb921d10c3945cb22f0be3b442a53f552ba47e.text:
**Efficient Retrieval, Indexing, and Fair Data Systems**

This community develops scalable methods for search, indexing, querying, and responsible ranking. Core topics include compressed inverted and integer indexes, trie-based RDF/SPARQL indexes, partitioned sequence representations, and memory-conscious columnar execution. High-dimensional retrieval emphasizes approximate nearest-neighbor search through locality-sensitive hashing, compact representations, and graph-based indexes, alongside efficient geometric pruning for applications such as ride sharing.

Querying research covers skyline and nearest-neighbor operators, including incomplete data streams and flexible combinations of objective and subjective attributes. It also develops domain-specific languages for accessible bibliographic search and systems for experiential information access.

Typical methods combine complexity and optimality analysis with compression, hashing, graph traversal, pruning, query-language design, column-at-a-time execution, and empirical benchmarking. Real-time constraints, scalability, and hardware-aware memory use remain central.

Recent trends strongly emphasize fairness-aware ranking and recommendation: measuring demographic and distributional bias, auditing representations and test collections, reranking for equitable exposure and viewpoint diversity, and using data interventions such as antidote data. The community is broadening toward socially responsible retrieval, hidden-population discovery, subjective search, incomplete streaming data, and higher-performance graph-based ANN systems.

64532cdd175e71cc76708a46dab68f281f8a4e99.text:
## Acknowledgements, Funding, and Evidence-Based Research Evaluation

This community examines scholarly acknowledgements as an underused source for understanding research funding, collaboration, credit, and evaluation. Studies of Web of Science funding-acknowledgement (FA) data track its rapid growth and updated collection practices across four journal citation indexes. They identify persistent coverage differences by time period, language, document type, database, and acknowledgement type, while finding improving FA collection in the humanities and social sciences. These limitations and interpretive biases require caution in bibliometric applications.

Humanities-focused research argues that acknowledgements reveal otherwise invisible contributions and interactions, complementing authorship and citation indicators. Combining authorship with acknowledged individuals also exposes disciplinary differences in credit attribution and can narrow apparent contrasts in collaborative team size.

Typical methods include large-scale bibliometric and database analyses, cross-index and cross-disciplinary comparisons, language and document-type analysis, and integration of authorship and acknowledgement networks. The community also includes data-driven evidential reasoning for multi-criteria R&D project selection, weighting expert evidence by reliability to produce belief-based rankings, demonstrated with a National Natural Science Foundation of China case study.

Recent trends broaden research assessment beyond authors and citations while emphasizing improved data coverage, transparency, bias awareness, and evidence integration for funding and project-selection decisions.

b4b3c798aefcd75c0d86865f11f7567cad78d399.text:
**Deep Cross-Modal Hashing and Multimodal Retrieval**

**Main themes:** This community studies semantic alignment and efficient retrieval across heterogeneous modalities, including music, lyrics, audio, images, text, video, and event data. It focuses on cross-modal search, multi-view similarity modeling, shared semantic spaces, unified binary representations, and interpretable links between content and user or listener responses.

**Typical methods:** Approaches include end-to-end deep networks, convolutional and graph convolutional text encoders, attention and temporal modeling, correlation alignment, latent-factor and matrix-factorization models, and shared or isomorphic hash-code learning. Supervised methods use fusion supervision, similarity preservation, cluster-unary objectives, and triplet-style ranking; discrete optimization reduces the accuracy loss of continuous relaxation. Generative coupling remains useful when paired labels are scarce.

**Recent trends:** Research increasingly targets large-scale, real-time retrieval through compact codes and specialized indexing rather than exhaustive Hamming search. Query-adaptive multi-view ranking, probability-based indexes, decorrelated or jointly quantized codes, and unified hash functions seek to preserve fine-grained similarity while reducing storage and computation. Newer models align nonlinear modality distributions and exploit graph structure in text, extending retrieval beyond isolated image–text pairs toward multimodal events and richer semantic relationships.

8f6b2a7895bab18fefadc7d5f76fc824d99a6716.text:
### Applied Graph Mining and Network Analytics

This community studies scalable analysis and modeling of heterogeneous social, information, semantic, citation, narrative, and organizational networks. Main themes include centrality and influence (including bipartite, group, signed, and entropy-based measures), core–periphery structure, roles and hierarchy, community discovery and graph summarization, network similarity and comparison, distance querying, link prediction, entity resolution, and indirect influence. It also examines diffusion, memes, sentiment, recommendations, and behavioral or relational prediction.

Typical methods combine topology with text, attributes, signs, spatial distance, and temporal interactions. They include random walks and path-based measures, structural-balance and signed-network models, machine learning, matrix factorization, semantic and multilayer representations, typed motifs, modularity with distance-aware null models, core and shell decompositions, maximum-matching ideas, and probabilistic models for degree-constrained graphs. Sampling, landmark sketches, hop-doubling labels, and randomized algorithms support efficient large-scale querying and similarity estimation.

Recent trends emphasize billion-scale distance and similarity search; interpretable centrality and rank measures; signed and heterogeneous graph mining; narrative character-network extraction and temporal analysis; meme and political diffusion; socially informed recommendation and sentiment analysis; organization and student-network analytics; and automatic graph construction from text and other unstructured content.

64d4c22a699272e1648e42310d7e1dda1e3a985a.text:
## Scalable Temporal, Multilayer, and Narrative Network Analysis

This community develops scalable methods for querying, modeling, and exploiting large, evolving, signed, and multilayer networks. Core topics include indexed graph querying—reachability, bounded and regular reachability, shortest paths, single-source and \(k\)-hop queries—using labeling schemes, interval and hop-doubling indexes, landmark sketches, hubs, independent-set labels, distributed algorithms, and lightweight fully dynamic structures such as DAGGER. Pruned Landmark Labeling is parallelized through vertex-centric, SIMD-aware, and batch computation models.

A major focus is temporal and multilayer stream graphs, including weighted, directed, and bipartite interactions. These representations support temporal paths, distances, connectivity, density, communities, centrality, recommendation, and analysis of changing user preferences. The community also studies signed networks, structural balance, social-financial ties, diffusion, influence, and contagion.

Narrative and fictional-character networks have become a prominent application area. Research addresses automated extraction from text through co-occurrence and machine-learning methods, dynamic conversational networks, genre and role analysis, plot summarization, character prominence, ecological cast-size measures, and prediction of narrative events such as character deaths. Movie, television, literary, cryptocurrency, and e-commerce data provide validation settings.

Recent trends favor native stream representations, temporal recommendation, signed and semantic interaction modeling, automated narrative analytics, and scalable parallel indexing and pruning.

23d59419329ad31dd04d4d56946eef0480e9d30a.text:
### Preserving and Making Evolving Knowledge Computable

This community studies durable, interpretable, and discoverable information across scientific, cultural, historical, news, social-media, and web contexts. Core themes include web-archive collection, profiling, recommendation, and maintenance; semantic modeling of entities, events, claims, activities, annotations, and research structures; persistent identification, provenance, versioning, rights, fixity, reproducible citation, and traceable research objects; and collaborative curation of scholarly and archival knowledge. Increasing attention is given to research software and data as first-class scholarly objects, their credit and impact, reproducibility terminology, semantic peer review, accessibility, and machine-actionable scholarly knowledge graphs.

Typical methods combine OAIS, Fedora, OAI-PMH, RDF/RDFS, SPARQL, PROV-O, PAV, nanopublications, Web Annotation, EventKG, DataCite, Zenodo DOIs, and arcp URIs. Systems provide semantic archive layers, Memento aggregators and maps, cache and holdings prediction, fixity verification, adaptive crawl and seed selection, entity-centric search, recommendations, timelines, structured browsing, and visualization. Analyses use citation and repository metadata, log and crawl data, entity linking, supervised and neural classification, ranking, graph inference, and multilingual temporal analytics.

Recent trends emphasize archive quality and bias control, cross-archive discovery, social signals for collection building, software/data citation and credit, automated scholarly knowledge acquisition, and richer provenance. Challenges include heterogeneous schemas, incomplete or unstable archives, multilinguality, accessibility, privacy, and preserving meaning across versions.

f20313c6c5a987d5aafbde123db4e6d5206a3af1.text:
**Information Retrieval: Neural Ranking, Semantic Search, and Interactive Discovery**

**Main themes.** This community studies relevance modeling and semantic matching across web, scholarly, enterprise, e-commerce, social-media, multimedia, entity, table, and question-answering search. Key problems include query and intent understanding, passage retrieval, cross-lingual transfer, event and entity discovery, conversational and spoken search, personalized ranking, structured-data exploration, and scalable similarity search.

**Typical methods.** Systems combine lexical and probabilistic retrieval with embeddings, pretrained and multilingual transformers, CNNs/RNNs, semantic hashing, knowledge graphs, RDF corpora, and fielded or table representations. Ranking models capture cross-document and groupwise interactions and use pointwise, pairwise, listwise, axiomatic, metric-learning, and weak-supervision objectives. Query expansion exploits salient context, entities, geography, usage signals, and conversation history. Approximate nearest-neighbor graphs, binary signatures, dimensionality reduction, and compact representations support large-scale retrieval. Evaluation increasingly includes benchmark collections, efficiency analysis, interactive exploration, and explanations of neural results.

**Recent trends.** Research is moving toward weakly supervised and end-to-end neural retrieval; cross-lingual and short-text semantic matching; graph- and entity-aware search; conversational, spoken, mobile, and personalized experiences; retrieval over tables and social/media collections; fast hashing and approximate graph search; permutation-invariant ranking; and more transparent tools for inspecting model behavior.

9a376f809160a31a119478b1cd4d3ec4f61ff0a5.text:
## Adaptive Data Management and Analytics

**Main themes.** This community develops scalable, adaptive, and usable systems for data-intensive workloads. Topics span relational query optimization—join ordering, cardinality and resource estimation, multiway joins, factorization, enumeration, containment, incremental maintenance, and complexity bounds—plus distributed, cloud, serverless, stream, graph, RDF, document, and heterogeneous-data management. It also connects databases with machine learning through declarative data-science languages, in-database inference, semantic type detection, and scalable DataFrame abstractions.

**Typical methods.** Research combines formal complexity, information-theoretic, and communication analyses with learned optimizers, reinforcement learning, workload-aware partitioning, adaptive indexes, neural index selection, probabilistic summaries, sketches, sampling, compression, caching, materialized views, and compact storage structures. Systems address LSM performance, push-based storage, correlated time-series modeling, and hardware-conscious execution. Video, visualization, and spatiotemporal retrieval use compositional queries, trajectory alignment, and neural predicates.

**Recent trends.** Emphasis is growing on approximate and probabilistic analytics with accuracy or error guarantees; adaptive execution under dynamic workloads; cost-aware processing across memory, geography, and serverless clouds; and resource-efficient edge analytics. Newer directions include declarative end-to-end ML, semantic-web optimization, high-velocity streaming graphs, authenticated indexes, blockchain emulation and cross-chain asset protocols, and globally managed decentralized data.

1db05c73ddb360a8619af87d1964518f492f424f.text:
## Scalable, Intelligent, and Trustworthy Data Systems

This community develops scalable data management, querying, and analytics for relational, graph, streaming, semi-structured, array, time-series, and scientific data. Core themes include query optimization and cardinality/resource estimation, join ordering and worst-case-optimal joins, ranked and random-order enumeration, incremental and interactive processing, view and workload management, data integration, semantic typing, and machine learning over relational data. It also addresses transactional consistency, isolation testing, cloud performance, privacy-aware edge analytics, and blockchain–database integration.

Typical methods combine formal complexity, information-theoretic, and cost analyses with sampling, sketches, histograms, compact and overlay indexes, factorization, model-based compression, incremental maintenance, adaptive and neural indexes, probabilistic estimation, reinforcement learning, and declarative algebraic optimization. Systems exploit NUMA multicore, GPUs, serverless clouds, shared-nothing clusters, and heterogeneous pipelines, including high-velocity graph ingestion and interactive visualization.

Recent trends include declarative end-to-end data-science platforms, DataFrame interfaces, in-database ML inference, adaptive aggregate estimation, RL-based view materialization, progressive neural index selection, learned key-value layouts, and model-based multidimensional time-series storage. Other directions include video and spatiotemporal event querying, RDF partitioning and view selection, top-k graph-pattern retrieval, autonomous-camera analytics, LSM performance stability, and blockchain emulation, cross-chain atomicity, asset management, and “chainifying” existing DBMSs.

159748af6b18c27e747a3acf37a9a5701f1eb3b7.text:
## Scholarly Discovery and Semantic Publishing

This community studies scholarly communication, information retrieval, recommendation, and knowledge organization using bibliographic, textual, behavioral, and linked-data sources. Core themes include citation and co-citation analysis, research-paper recommendation, scholarly impact and readership, interactive search behavior, bibliographic metadata, research-data citation, and discovery across publications, datasets, and repositories. It also addresses semantic publishing, information-object identity and preservation, and machine-processable knowledge organization systems.

Typical methods combine bibliometrics, citation and usage analysis, content-based and hybrid recommendation, collaborative filtering, meta-learning for per-instance algorithm selection, user and task modeling, and online or living-lab evaluation. Large-scale systems use citation graphs, abstracts, metadata, recommendation logs, distributed processing such as Hadoop, and recommender-as-a-service APIs. Scholarly extraction employs information extraction, entity linking, reference parsing, RDF/LOD, ontologies, SKOS, and quality-checking functions; behavioral studies use session variables, eye tracking, and choice-overload analysis. Evaluation increasingly includes altmetrics, click-through and usage measures, and reproducible benchmark datasets.

Recent trends emphasize deployable academic recommender services, algorithm selection tailored to users and contexts, large-scale recommendation datasets, semantic enrichment and interlinking of scholarly outputs, quality assessment of vocabularies and publications, research-data repositories and altmetrics, and richer, behavior-aware discovery interfaces.

0de7d08265e8f9eafc3453e3cc610165b18bca2a.text:
## Network Influence, Opinions, and Social Resilience

This community studies how network structure and platform mechanisms shape information diffusion, influence, opinions, polarization, controversy, and resilience. Themes include DeGroot, Friedkin–Johnsen, French–DeGroot, bounded-confidence, threshold, weighted-median, and nonlinear opinion dynamics; stubborn agents and leaders; correlated or multi-topic opinions; confirmation bias and repulsive interactions; homophily, signed ties, clustering balance, and competing information or products. It also examines influence campaigns, opinion maximization and control, recommendation systems, filter bubbles, news diversity, cyberbullying-detection fairness, auditing, and immunization against harmful content.

Typical methods combine graph theory, dynamical systems and control, Laplacian, spectral and centrality analysis, mean-field and stochastic analysis, optimization, game theory, Nash-equilibrium and complexity analysis, and combinatorial algorithms. Empirical and computational work uses social-media, news, voting, communication, and diffusion data, alongside controlled social-bot experiments. Network analysis includes topology inference, community and partition discovery, Katz-based proximity, temporal block-matrix formulations, and text-aware embeddings.

Recent work emphasizes strategic network formation and rewiring, signed-network balance, intrinsic versus socially induced activation, multi-topic polarization, competitive spread with confirmation bias, leader selection, and optimal investment. Growing attention targets fair influence and recommendation auditing, diverse exposure, controlled persuasion, scalable sampling, temporal networks, and robustness or immunization against manipulation and harmful cascades.

7ff0d449e1ceab6c04429a41ee81eb5231c7027e.text:
### Utility-Aware, Structured, and Concise Pattern Mining

This community extends pattern mining beyond frequency toward **utility, economic value, recency, correlation, and significance**. Major themes include high-utility itemsets and multidimensional sequences; individualized or item-specific utility thresholds; trend- and recency-aware mining; correlated utility patterns; and utility analytics over uncertain, multi-sequence, privacy-sensitive, and temporal data. Applications include retail, IoT, clickstreams, social content, targeted marketing, and NLP.

A parallel focus is expressive mining over structured data. Work discovers tree-query associations in graphs and association rules expressed as conjunctive queries over relational databases, including constants and existential variables. These approaches target large graph and relational datasets while providing formal support and optimality guarantees.

Controlling pattern explosion remains central. Research mines closed episodes, non-derivable itemsets, generic rule bases, compressed serial episodes, and statistically significant or non-free-rider patterns, while also summarizing pattern collections for interpretability through quality simplification, ordering, and compression. Subsequence constraints include length, gap, span, regular-expression, and hierarchy restrictions.

Typical methods include projection-based utility mining, correlation-aware measures, upper-bound pruning, query-guided search, closure and equivalence-class models, Minimum Description Length, statistical testing, and distributed processing. Recent trends combine richer semantics and structured queries with concise, interpretable summaries and scalable utility mining.

2939dce7349b05217063d9a3ff8ac681b2202e2b.text:
### Graph Data Integration and Scalable Query Processing

This community studies interoperable graph and data-management systems, spanning RDF and property graphs, relational and complex-value data, knowledge graphs, and high-velocity event streams. Core themes include graph query languages and semantics, schema and view management, RDF–property-graph mappings, query-by-example and user-oriented search, continuous subgraph and complex-event detection, graph-stream summarization, and distributed graph analytics.

Typical methods combine formal query semantics, Datalog and rewriting, dependency and complexity analysis, schema mappings, programmable view updates, provenance and data differencing, and benchmark-driven evaluation. Systems research emphasizes adaptive and workload-aware indexing, learned query planning, query-aware partitioning and smart routing, parallel joins and sorting, declarative ingestion, approximate sketches, and massively parallel graph databases. Human-in-the-loop techniques support semantic ranking, relationship discovery, explanations, and visual querying.

Recent trends emphasize practical interoperability across graph models and heterogeneous sources; streaming, dynamic, and time-constrained graph processing; lossy summaries for high-volume labeled streams; adaptive storage and indexing on multicore, GPU, and cloud platforms; and scalable MPP execution. The community is also moving toward declarative, self-adapting data systems, controllable benchmarking and ingestion pipelines, transparent social-feed and knowledge-graph explanations, and accessible interfaces that reduce the need for specialized query expertise.

dc244562b4575ff12e8795c42436b5ae335f88d3.text:
## Cognitive, Social, and Scalable Recommender Systems

This community studies recommender systems that incorporate human cognition, social influence, and contextual behavior rather than relying solely on historical interactions. A major theme is cognitively inspired tag and hashtag recommendation, modeling memory activation, frequency, recency, semantic context, forgetting, and lexical–semantic distinctions with ACT-R and Base-Level Learning. These approaches address sparse folksonomies, tag reuse, and user acceptance.

Social recommendation combines marketplace behavior with social-network, trust, location, and relationship data. Research examines weak and strong ties, regular equivalence, heterogeneous social influence, negative influence, and social commerce across products, jobs, resources, music, and other domains.

Typical methods include collaborative filtering, hybrid and content-based models, matrix factorization, graph and triadic analysis, semantic similarity, embeddings, deep learning, online user studies, and scalable search infrastructure. User pre-filtering with Apache Solr reduces candidate neighborhoods and accelerates collaborative filtering, while deep models address cold-start recommendation. Embeddings support real-time similar-job and homepage personalization.

Recent trends emphasize temporal and context-aware recommendation, multi-source data, scalable online services, diversity, novelty, fairness across music-consumption patterns, cold-start robustness, and user acceptance—not accuracy alone. Evaluation increasingly includes online click-through performance alongside conventional offline metrics.

26c1586b0fb98ced7c029ebe5952861d92aff84c.text:
## Collaborative Knowledge and Social Search

This community studies how user-generated content—Wikipedia, Wiktionary, folksonomies, social bookmarking, and professional networks—supports knowledge organization, discovery, and search. Themes include extracting structured data, building thesauri, ontologies, and multilingual knowledge graphs, analyzing categories and hyperlinks, and modeling tagging vocabulary, semantics, heterogeneity, and growth.

Search research covers collaborative and social information seeking, expertise location, personalized professional search, entity ranking, semantic navigation, synonym retrieval, talent search, and product insight from tagging data. Recent work also examines content-based Web communities, talent mobility and job-hopping networks, geospatial behavior, and opinion formation in social networks.

Typical methods combine large-scale crawling and log analysis with graph modeling, centrality and influence measures, clustering, topic classification, co-occurrence and similarity metrics, matrix factorization, statistical distribution modeling, learning-to-rank, neural semantic matching, entity linking, and agent-based simulation. Web links are analyzed jointly with lexical content and topic taxonomies, while SKOS and SPARQL support semantic interoperability.

Recent trends include production-scale deep ranking, scalable multilingual and language-agnostic processing, dynamic location and workforce analytics, psychologically informed social modeling, and increasingly sophisticated influence detection using local, fuzzy, and fractal network dimensions. Social search is expanding from individual retrieval toward propagation, group behavior, and network-level dynamics.

e336df403fa101999f19faf37310c317bfe578b4.text:
### Database Recovery and Heterogeneous Persistent Storage

This community studies database reliability, recovery, and storage management across modern hardware and failure models. A central theme is extending recovery beyond system, media, and transaction failures to include **single-page failures**, using page-recovery indexes and transactional maintenance.

Several works redesign recovery for speed and availability through commit coordination, logging, propagation control, fine-grained locking, partial rollback, snapshot isolation, and concurrent redo-only recovery. Instant restore enables read/write access during media repair and restores segments on demand, making recovery workload-guided rather than strictly sequential.

Another major focus is the convergence of memory and storage technologies. Systems span DRAM, persistent memory (PMem), flash, and disks, using persistent buffer pools and optimistic consistency to support CPU-level access while preserving recoverability. PMem-specific performance evaluation motivates optimized I/O primitives for log writing and block flushing. Heterogeneity-aware DBMS frameworks exploit semantic information about data and I/O, rather than relying solely on workload monitoring, to place data across diverse devices.

Overall, research trends toward finer-grained failure handling, reduced undo and downtime, persistent data structures, hardware-aware I/O, and adaptive storage hierarchies tailored to dynamic workloads.

0ad251ba318e60a618c43d6dd7f767635902f325.text:
## Scholarly Discovery and Recommendation

This community develops systems that make scholarly information discoverable, structured, trustworthy, and actionable. Major themes include metadata and document-structure extraction, semantic publishing, citation analysis and matching, knowledge-graph construction, automated search, trend visualization, and personalized scholarly recommendation. Graph-based platforms support expert finding, indirect-connection discovery, and exploratory querying, while extraction systems process authors, affiliations, bibliographies, tables, figures, reference strings, and citation segments.

Recommendation research combines content and network signals, including titles, abstracts, embeddings, keyphrases, co-citation, and citation graphs. Large-scale systems address incomplete citation data and cold-start problems; the Microsoft Academic recommender supports roughly 160 million papers and patents. The community also emphasizes reusable evaluation resources, exemplified by RARD II, with 89 million recommendation events over 24 million items, and Mr. DLib’s living lab, which delivers online experiments through APIs to digital libraries and reference-management platforms.

Typical methods include rule-based and statistical information extraction, NLP, blocking and binary classification for citation matching, near-duplicate detection, MinHash and Jaccard similarity, graph databases, machine learning, meta-learning, embeddings, and distributed processing.

Recent trends include production-scale hybrid recommenders, rich behavioral-log datasets, API-based living-lab evaluation, and improved citation matching through combined reference-string and text-segment features.

7bb09fc3e215f9f610c006bf5e985f10d672d710.text:
## Scalable Data Management and Intelligent Query Processing

This community studies efficient, adaptive data-intensive systems: relational optimization, cardinality and resource estimation, join ordering, enumeration, indexing, compression, view selection, and analytics over structured, semi-structured, RDF, graph, spatial, temporal, and uncertain data. It increasingly emphasizes flexible access through fuzzy and imprecise queries, keyword and entity summarization, semantic typing, hidden-database crawling, reranking, and exploratory search.

Typical methods combine complexity, tractability, communication, and space–time analysis with sampling, sketches, probabilistic summaries, approximate nearest-neighbor hashing, model-based compression, factorized and adaptive joins, skyline and top-k processing, random-access enumeration, MILP and System-R-style optimization, learned optimizers and indexes, deep reinforcement learning, and workload-aware partitioning or materialization. Declarative interfaces support end-to-end ML and DataFrame analytics, in-database inference, interactive visualization, and compositional video-event queries. Systems target distributed, GPU/SIMD, memory-, I/O-, network-, and hardware-aware execution, while formal methods address fuzzy semantics, probabilistic ranking, consistency, and reproducible numerical aggregation.

Recent trends include adaptive learned systems, scalable semantic and heterogeneous-data exploration, concise summaries, approximate and interactive analytics, spatiotemporal retrieval, dynamic RDF and graph workloads, ML-serving integration, transparent scaling, and blockchain layers for existing databases. Progress combines rigorous guarantees with probabilistic, user-centered, and hardware-specialized execution.

2311d56d6c39ca46147e3198c09183a2f27a903e.text:
### No Current Community Theme

No papers remain to support the previous focus on dynamic sentiment analysis of music, lyrics, gang-associated culture, or audience engagement. The community’s former methods—sentiment analysis, trajectory modeling, NLP, pattern discovery, and statistical testing—were likewise supported by departed papers.

No joined papers were provided, so there is insufficient evidence to identify the community’s current research themes, typical methods, or recent trends.

b52c2ea65dd2eaa84f93fa1ee7905f57360fb5a6.text:
## Scalable, Consistent, and Adaptive Data Systems

This community studies high-throughput data management across multicore servers, shared-nothing clusters, clouds, and distributed systems. Core themes include OLTP, contention management, distributed transactions, MVCC and isolation, adaptive and command logging, parallel recovery, conflict repair, and workload-aware partitioning. New work explores asymmetric replication, omittable writes, deterministic and queue-oriented execution, and machine-learning-guided scheduling to reduce coordination and conflicts in write-heavy workloads.

A growing theme is scalable stream processing on shared-memory multicore architectures. Systems use NUMA-aware operator placement, asynchronous transactional state management, and partitioned in-memory indexes for high-throughput stream joins.

The community also investigates consistency and verifiability: the complexity and practical detection of serializability violations, black-box testing of isolation-level implementations, and transparent concurrency-control layers decoupled from DBMS internals. High availability for key-value and transactional systems remains important, as does integrating blockchain layers with existing heterogeneous data-management systems rather than replacing them.

Typical methods combine concurrency-control protocols, formal complexity analysis, deterministic scheduling, replication and logging architectures, multicore-aware indexing, workload-driven optimization, prototypes, testing tools, and empirical benchmarking.

Recent trends emphasize reduced coordination, adaptive execution, highly available serializable transactions, transactional stream state, modular DBMS architecture, and blockchain-backed data systems.

254fe3efdab10b251f0db2b0e4e1dbe6b0abf32f.text:
### Ranking, Search, and Semantic Network Analytics

This community studies graph-based ranking, influence, expertise, information retrieval, and semantic organization across Web, Wikipedia, social-tagging, scholarly, and knowledge networks. Major applications include PageRank, HITS, FolkRank, entity and author–paper ranking, credibility and expertise discovery, collective attention, social search, library catalogs, and multilingual ontology and thesaurus construction.

Typical methods include random walks, personalized and seeded ranking, spectral and graph-based similarity, learning-to-rank, collaborative filtering, link prediction, clustering, and network visualization. Researchers also analyze tag co-occurrence, vocabulary growth, category and hyperlink structure, clickstreams, user behavior, and multimodal graphs. NLP techniques support query expansion, synonym discovery, semantic retrieval, topic selection for IR evaluation, and fusion of textual and visual evidence.

Recent trends emphasize longitudinal, multilingual Wikipedia and Wiktionary datasets; machine-readable semantic resources and knowledge graphs; scalable search over collaborative and social data; user-centered and social models of information seeking; credibility-aware ranking; and improved evaluation efficiency through intelligent topic selection. Emerging work also examines collective expertise, influential-node and group power detection, dynamic attention and geospatial behavior, and structural evolution in tagging and Web communities.

21c41e6fd8d61dd431c3471eafe01a042e2fdd45.text:
### Scholarly Text, Knowledge Graphs, and Recommendation Intelligence

This community studies how to organize, interpret, connect, summarize, and recommend content in large scholarly and historical text collections. Core themes include topic discovery and evolution, semantic document indexing, RDF knowledge-graph entity summarization, citation matching and interlinking, bibliometric and interdisciplinarity analysis, spatialized research mapping, historical-corpus classification, and research-paper recommendation.

Typical methods combine probabilistic and neural topic models, textual and semantic embeddings, TF–IDF and keyword extraction, supervised machine learning, OCR and domain knowledge, citation and co-word networks, sparse temporal visualization, graph analysis, and scalable MapReduce implementations. Entity summarization selects compact, size-constrained triple sets, increasingly using deep models that encode textual semantics and triple interdependence. Citation matching combines blocking with classifiers over reference strings and segments. Recommenders integrate content, co-citation, knowledge-graph, and interaction data to address scale, incomplete metadata, and cold starts.

Recent trends emphasize explainable and user-tunable opaque-model recommendations, large scholarly recommendation datasets, recommendation-as-a-service and online living-lab evaluation, benchmark-driven entity summarization, dynamic visualization of changing research trends, and combined semantic–citation analysis of scientific landscapes. Applications are broadening to historical travelogue discovery and other large digitized collections.

d0fa5ebce3433f94e865f8c47c2d206bcf32b311.text:
## Natural-Language and Online Access to Scientific Data

This community studies how non-experts and scientists access complex structured data through natural-language, keyword, and interactive online interfaces. Core themes include bridging user language with schemas, values, predicates, and join paths; supporting ad-hoc business questions over complex warehouses; and enabling knowledge-rich exploration of heterogeneous entity and scientific data graphs. Astronomy is a major application, spanning public archives such as SDSS SkyServer, online science portals, and large-scale time-domain surveys.

Typical methods include natural-language question-to-SQL translation, query-log and schema/value mapping, intent preservation, join-path inference, specialized keyword query units, ranked retrieval, and entity-graph preview tables. The community also develops distributed and cloud database architectures capable of continuous ingestion, streaming analysis, low-latency event detection, and combined real-time and historical queries. Online archives increasingly serve as active analytical systems that summarize data, detect anomalies, and cross-correlate multiple sources.

Recent trends include movement from manually engineered mappings toward neural and knowledge-rich NLIs, alongside more systematic comparison and evaluation of NLI systems. In parallel, research is shifting from offline database access toward scalable, cloud-based, real-time scientific data services and exploratory interfaces that make complex warehouses and archives usable to broader audiences.

c39f672e5de8a1beefab8b4c59ae3117df7fab5e.text:
### Semantic Archives, Event Knowledge, and Scholarly Web Infrastructure

This community develops durable, interpretable, and discoverable representations of scholarly, historical, and web-based knowledge. Core themes include web-archive aggregation and profiling, persistent identification, provenance, first-class Web annotations, structured scholarly communication, software-aware citation graphs, and event-centric knowledge graphs. It also supports cross-lingual timelines and completion of missing events and relations in knowledge bases.

Typical methods combine RDF, SPARQL, Open Annotation, Memento services, cache optimization, machine-learned holdings prediction, compact archive summaries, and provenance- or HTTP-aware crawling and replay. Other approaches include graph-based event inference, temporal reasoning, multilingual relevance modeling, seed discovery from micro-collections, and semantic interlinking of peer-review comments. Systems support archive discovery, responsive aggregation, faithful replay, timeline generation, knowledge-graph completion, and richer assessment of research contributions through software and transitive credit.

Recent trends emphasize scalable and adaptive web-archive infrastructure, cookie- and protocol-aware preservation, semantic annotations as reusable objects, multilingual event exploration, automated completion of event series, and more comprehensive scholarly graphs that represent software and review activity. Persistent challenges include incomplete and evolving archives and knowledge graphs, heterogeneous schemas, preservation fidelity, scalability, and trustworthy interpretation of machine-generated links and inferences.

9588665bed9951bfae1f8b2481fd02f820c3ee1f.text:
## Social Networks: Diffusion, Sensing, and Resilience

This community studies how social networks form, evolve, and shape information diffusion, attention, opinion, behavior, adoption, collective intelligence, and socioeconomic activity. Key themes include influence and centrality, community structure and deception, homophily and multilayer ties, initiative and latent agents, online discussion and information overload, cultural variation in question answering, trust and misinformation, emergency and disaster communication, disease and behavioral diffusion, mobility and ride-sharing, cybersecurity intelligence, and network resilience against failures or attacks. It also examines hashtag popularity, stories and rumors, sexual-harassment discourse, personality and wellbeing signals, and spatial patterns of human activity.

Typical methods combine temporal, weighted, multiplex, relational-event, proximity, mobility, and location-aware network analysis; community detection, motif and role analysis, sampling, and influence benchmarking; and epidemic, Hawkes, master-equation, stochastic, adaptive, and resilience models. Machine learning uses graph and content embeddings, latent-variable and Poisson models, neural prediction, semi-supervised bootstrapping, relation and entity extraction, anomaly detection, sentiment analysis, and event forecasting. Data come increasingly from smartphones, Bluetooth/GPS sensing, calls, social media, forums, and large-scale platform traces.

Recent directions emphasize crisis-time monitoring, sparse-observation inference, real-time cascade and discussion forecasting, interpretable influence and trust estimation, network-aware targeting and pricing, cross-platform cybersecurity extraction, and robust, privacy-conscious network measurement.

ba6e9927fdac548f13d4cdf93aedd3d5dfa274dc.text:
## Information Identity, Preservation, and Linked Cultural-Heritage Data

This community examines how libraries, archives, and museums define, preserve, model, and connect information objects and knowledge structures in digital environments. A central concern is identity: maintaining the ontological identity of objects despite changes in carriers, migrations, encodings, or representations, and clarifying what URIs denote when they identify bibliographic or subject concepts. Related work addresses significant properties in digital preservation and debates whether they can be formally specified.

A major expanding theme is the publication of knowledge organization systems (KOS)—thesauri, classifications, authority files, and code lists—as Semantic Web data. Studies explain the design and OWL formalization of SKOS/SKOS-XL, compare KOS expressiveness and machine processability, analyze relationships between KOS and natural-language concepts, and convert resources such as LCSH from MARCXML to SKOS/RDF. Work also treats vocabularies as reusable linked-data infrastructure, sometimes integrated with Dublin Core.

Typical methods include conceptual and ontological analysis, framework comparison, literature review, natural-language processing, implementation proposals, and computable vocabulary-quality checks.

Recent trends emphasize RDF, SKOS, Linked Data, URI-based identity, reusable and interoperable vocabularies, automated quality assessment, and more flexible metadata and catalog structures.

d6ab42c37af59f31cb7d30cb687f64661c4030a4.text:
## Diffusion, Influence, and Opinion Dynamics in Evolving Networks

This community studies how information, products, misinformation, and opinions spread through social and other networks, and how network structure and interventions shape collective outcomes. Core themes include influence maximization and prevention, competitive or complementary cascades, adaptive marketing and resource allocation, evolving networks, and diversity-aware seed and audience selection. A substantial strand models opinion and belief formation using DeGroot, Friedkin–Johnsen, bounded-confidence, Bayesian, and multi-topic dynamics, including biases, antagonistic interactions, signed links, polarization, consensus, and structural balance. Related work examines recommendation feedback, political behavior, temporal events, and topic-specific user susceptibility.

Typical methods combine independent-cascade and threshold models with game theory, dynamical systems, control, percolation, graph algorithms, stochastic optimization, and approximation analysis. Greedy and adaptive policies, reverse-reachability sampling, Markov and mean-field analysis, equilibrium and best-response dynamics, spectral embeddings, centrality and communicability measures, graph partitioning, and scalable network mining are common.

Recent trends emphasize feedback-driven and online intervention, temporal and growing topologies, competitive resource allocation, latent user behavior, and richer multi-feature or lattice-valued campaigns. Objectives increasingly include misinformation blocking, privacy, fairness, diversity, reliability, and social cohesion rather than reach alone, while signed and dynamic-network models challenge assumptions of static, purely positive influence graphs.

b6ce52124c23857f4d104132ebb784e9eb6073ca.text:
### Scholarly Communication, Metrics, and Discovery

This community examines how research is disseminated, discovered, evaluated, and reused across journals, repositories, preprints, scholarly search services, social media, and open scholarly infrastructure. Themes include citation and altmetric validity; open citations and Linked Open Data; open-access and preprint publishing; journal, author, institutional, and national benchmarking; citation gaming and self-citation; editorial-board influence; and scholarly recommendation, classification, and visibility. It also studies books, figures, gray literature, predatory journals, and societal attention as parts of scholarly communication.

Typical methods combine large bibliographic, citation, usage, web, and social-media datasets with APIs, crawling, scraping, identifier matching, repository mining, and semantic-web pipelines. Analyses use correlation, regression, normalization, longitudinal and distributional analysis, benchmarking, sentiment and reaction analysis, and citation, editorial, two-mode, and latent-space networks. Machine learning supports recommendation, classification, visual-signature analysis, and expert or content curation.

Recent work emphasizes OpenCitations/COCI and crowdsourced open-citation infrastructures; the relationship of usage, citations, altmetrics, and peer-assessed societal impact; hidden Facebook activity and unstable Twitter data; disciplinary, national, and linguistic visibility effects; editorial interlocking; and evaluation-induced citation behavior. Emerging systems use figures for domain discovery and token-curated, citation-aware recommendation. Persistent concerns include platform instability, incomplete coverage, disambiguation, commercial dependence, sparse data, confounding, and mistaking attention for quality or impact.

13e7e7b2d6245ffd319a7c025e3f1af09f183b1a.text:
### Acknowledgements, Funding, and Evidence-Based Research Evaluation

This community studies acknowledgements and related funding data as underused sources for understanding research support, credit, collaboration, leadership, and project evaluation. A major theme is systematic analysis of funding acknowledgements in Web of Science, whose coverage began in 2008, alongside efforts to make otherwise invisible contributions visible—especially in the humanities, where acknowledgements complement authorship and citation measures.

Typical methods are bibliometric and quantitative: large-scale analysis of scholarly records; classification of acknowledgement and contribution types; comparisons across citation indexes, languages, and disciplines; and network analysis of authors, acknowledgees, institutions, and funding relationships. Studies also examine leadership through corresponding-author affiliations and geographic, cognitive, institutional, social, and economic proximity.

A related emerging direction applies historical expert assessments and likelihood-based evidence acquisition to multi-criteria R&D project selection. Data-driven evidential reasoning combines evidence with different weights and reliabilities to rank projects, demonstrated in National Natural Science Foundation of China case studies.

Recent trends therefore broaden the scope from documenting credit and collaboration toward evidence-based funding and research-management decisions. Interpretation remains cautious because acknowledgement and funding data are incomplete, inconsistently indexed, and vulnerable to coverage, language, and classification bias.

32e916af2fe52dcbfe9c0a580f52a44c5a67bbb5.text:
**Multilayer Diffusion and Social Network Identity**

This community studies information, rumors, influence, and competing contagions across multiplex and online social networks. It also examines how users’ identities, roles, and interactions are represented and evolve on platforms such as Twitter, including cross-platform identity linkage, heterogeneous interaction prediction, and the emergence of information-sharing ties.

Typical methods include threshold, epidemic, co-contagion, rumor–truth, and dormancy models; game-theoretic and evolutionary formulations; constrained optimization for intervention; and empirical analysis of temporal interaction patterns. Identity and user analysis combines profile, content, network, and behavioral features with unsupervised embeddings, supervised machine learning, and graph neural networks. Multiplex graph matching, graphlets, and structural motif analysis support relational characterization, while large-scale platform data collection enables analysis of online networks.

Recent work examines when users update profile fields such as names, descriptions, and locations, relating changes to life events, seasonality, language, and cultural context. It also classifies heterogeneous user types—including humans, bots, spammers, businesses, and professionals—using profile and tweeting behavior, with manually labeled data and cross-validation.

Recent trends emphasize coupled spreading processes, strategic rumor containment, scalable identity resolution, temporal modeling of profile evolution, automated user-role classification, and fine-grained mining of heterogeneous social interactions.

a2482507f0e9350bc66ee753b136599e922673c2.text:
### Semantic and Social Information Intelligence

This community studies latent structure, semantic relationships, and actionable knowledge in evolving scholarly, textual, knowledge-graph, and social-media collections. Topic modeling supports discovery of research themes, domain evolution, document understanding, and interdisciplinary scientific landscapes, increasingly using correlated models, embeddings, and hierarchical or multidimensional representations.

A growing focus is concise, user-oriented knowledge-graph access. Entity summarization selects size-constrained, informative subsets of RDF triples, combining textual semantics and triple interdependence; benchmark construction enables systematic evaluation. Large-scale scholarly analysis connects keywords, citations, and full text to map semantic proximity, interdisciplinarity, and field evolution.

Social-media mining supports event detection and situational awareness. Informative Twitter keywords can identify protests and other events despite informal, noisy language. Research also applies machine learning and domain knowledge to classify historical travelogues in digitized corpora.

Typical methods include topic models, embedding-based neural ranking, supervised classification, text mining, citation and co-word networks, sparse representations, temporal analysis, entity summarization, and distributed MapReduce implementations.

Recent trends emphasize scalable semantic modeling, benchmarked knowledge-graph summarization, dynamic visualization of changing research trends, interdisciplinary science mapping, robust analysis of noisy social streams, and machine-assisted exploration of large historical and scholarly collections.

ff9b9dc2a639b6748221a4b53538fdb168ffc5de.text:
## Reliable Data Integration, Cleaning, and Uncertainty

This community studies reliable management of incomplete, noisy, conflicting, heterogeneous, and evolving data. Core themes include schema-agnostic entity resolution and consolidation, relational embeddings, canonical records, ontology alignment, semantic extraction from unlabeled tables and the Web, wrapper induction and repair, and similarity search over strings, sets, graphs, and dense vectors. It also examines data markets, query pricing, provenance, lineage, data completeness, and user-oriented query-result exploration.

Research develops declarative and automated data cleaning through dependencies, approximate order constraints, repairs, chase-based reasoning, graph rewriting, view-based architectures, and learned repair rules. Uncertainty is addressed using probabilistic databases, certain-answer approximations, knowledge compilation, temporal-probabilistic joins, and contribution measures such as Shapley values. Query answering under constraints and ontologies includes complexity analysis, consistent answers, deletion propagation, and chase termination.

Typical methods combine Bayesian and Markov-logic models, neural and local embeddings, CNN-based approximate edit distance, blocking and hashing, inverted indexes, GPU or bit-level search, SAT solving, genetic programming, crowdsourcing, hybrid human–machine screening, weak supervision, and cost-aware optimization.

Recent trends emphasize end-to-end automated cleaning pipelines, schema-agnostic progressive ER, few-shot and unsupervised error detection, scalable semantic/vector search, robust web extraction, explainable repairs, principled uncertainty handling, and data marketplaces that align sharing incentives with integration quality.

7f663fc338354bb2f4b91f52896866c339996a15.text:
### Semantic Retrieval, Mathematical Language, and Scalable Data Analytics

This community develops data-centric methods for searching, comparing, integrating, and managing heterogeneous information. Semantic retrieval uses named entities, WordNet and ontological relations, latent concepts, and supervised models for query expansion, opinion analysis, and spam detection.

A major thread addresses mathematical information retrieval and representation. Systems combine full-text and formula search with contextual embeddings, symbol2vec-style representations, joint topic–equation models, identifier extraction, faceted search, accessible MathML, Wikidata links, and symbolic computation. Work also explores semantic-preserving translation between LaTeX and computer algebra systems, while examining the challenges of applying machine learning to ambiguous mathematical language.

Scalable data engineering emphasizes associative arrays, D4M databases, Accumulo, Graphulo/GraphBLAS-style operations, tensors, polystores, relational lattices, SQL++, Calcite, column-store execution, and robust SQL progress estimation. Data discovery increasingly includes automatic view search across databases, lakes, and cloud storage. Applications integrate agricultural IoT, sensors, satellites, weather, equipment, and other inconsistent sources.

Typical methods include semantic and ontological expansion, neural embeddings, topic modeling, graph and hypergraph similarity, matrix/tensor algebra, statistical estimation, symbolic computation, benchmarking, and modular data integration. Recent trends favor billion-scale streaming updates, AI-oriented data wrangling, knowledge-enhanced mathematical retrieval, automated dataset discovery, and multimodal agricultural analytics.

6c3db719a094d83d5d4f9b5edd496d4e0d6188fc.text:
### Semantic Graph, Scientific Data, and Query Integration

**Main research themes:** This community studies management, integration, querying, and exploration of heterogeneous relational, RDF, property-graph, XML, and scientific data. Topics include RDF–property-graph interoperability, compact knowledge-graph storage, SPARQL and graph-query optimization, semantic-association search and query relaxation, schema/ontology generation, spatial and multidimensional RDF analytics, metadata and provenance, and entity resolution. A growing focus is making complex databases accessible through natural language, keywords, query logs, previews, programming-by-example, and machine-learning tools.

**Typical methods:** Formal semantics, schema mappings, ontology learning, query rewriting and containment, graph traversal and topological similarity, embeddings and graph convolutional networks, intent and join-path inference, and example-driven specification. Systems employ adaptive and compressed indexes, topology-aware storage, batching and data sharing, MPP and distributed/cloud execution, GPU or parallel processing, workload benchmarking, and server-assisted interfaces such as Triple Pattern Fragments. Scientific platforms combine streaming, low-latency event processing with historical analysis and large-scale metadata management.

**Recent trends:** Research increasingly bridges database technology with data-intensive science, especially astronomy and biomedicine. RDF ecosystems are becoming more interoperable, compact, spatially expressive, and usable by ML pipelines. Querying is shifting toward hybrid natural-language, visual, keyword, and example-based interfaces, while systems emphasize scalable public access, real-time scientific discovery, contextual knowledge graphs, and principled evaluation of usability and performance.

9b6103a5a8f1101de028f2f5ddb94920bc81ebff.text:
## Adaptive Data Systems, Versioning, and Distributed Analytics

This community studies performance engineering and adaptive management for heterogeneous data systems, spanning XML and tree-pattern queries, multimodel databases, semantic similarity joins, data integration, declarative array processing, and workload-aware optimization. A major theme is managing evolving data: collaborative dataset and relational-database versioning, provenance, workflow lifecycle management, immutable and shared storage, historical graph queries, graph deltas, and query languages for evolving graphs.

Distributed-system research increasingly addresses blockchain databases and decentralized applications, including cross-chain atomicity, global asset management, verifiable queries, genomic-access auditing, lightweight emulation, and scalable Byzantine-fault-tolerant consensus. Work also examines autonomic resource-aware databases, dynamic partitioning, elastic clusters, and the relationship between query performance, hardware architecture, and energy efficiency.

Typical methods include adaptive query processing and indexing, delta-based reconstruction, version-aware storage layouts, deterministic data-exchange and update propagation, declarative interfaces over HPC arrays, semantic and taxonomy-aware matching, and consensus or cryptographic mechanisms for trustworthy distributed data.

Recent trends favor unified multimodel backends; reproducible, provenance-rich collaborative analytics; temporal and historical graph management; energy-proportional infrastructure; blockchain-based verifiability and interoperability; and metadata, datasheets, recommendation, and example-driven tools that improve dataset discovery, integration, and responsible reuse.

61aa41d35b5c588743b5f54e66fc0f7ae681d242.text:
## Scalable Entity Resolution and Data Curation

This community studies integration and quality improvement for noisy, heterogeneous, uncertain, and semi-structured data. Core themes include schema-agnostic and progressive entity resolution, deduplication, relational and ontology alignment, semantic matching, metadata cleaning, dependency and rule discovery, truth discovery, knowledge-base population, and data-quality effects on accurate, fair, and robust machine learning. Applications span scholarly and Wikipedia metadata, knowledge graphs, social and geo-social data, search systems, and data-sharing markets.

Typical methods combine blocking, filtering, approximate string and Hamming-distance search, probabilistic models, graphical methods, random forests, neural and local relational embeddings, Siamese transformers, and vector search over full-text engines. They also use holistic clustering, relational match propagation, learned repair rules, order dependencies, automated pipeline optimization, distributed processing, and query- or budget-aware sampling. Human-machine workflows support crowdsourced screening, expert identification, active verification, truth aggregation, and knowledge-base curation through voice interfaces.

Recent trends emphasize schema-free and time-aware progressive ER, contextual and embedding-based matching beyond lexical similarity, production-ready semantic search, and data markets that improve discoverability and integration incentives. Increasing attention goes to automated rule and pipeline generation, communication- and cost-efficient scaling, hybrid human–machine decisions, and cleaning data specifically to improve downstream accuracy, fairness, and robustness.

85ab3f1d46f5e7f78dab7ed72110c457807b5f25.text:
### Scalable Data Algebra, Schemas, and Distributed Analytics

This community studies scalable management, integration, and analysis of heterogeneous structured, semi-structured, array, matrix, graph, and streaming data. A core theme is interoperable data modeling and computation through associative arrays, LARA, relational and tensor abstractions, polystore architectures, and distributed key-value, NoSQL, NewSQL, and DBaaS systems.

Recent work substantially expands toward data semantics and schema management. It covers learning and validating XML schemas, unordered and interleaved regular expressions, RDF shape expressions, Schema.org annotation, semantic APIs, and knowledge-graph construction. Related efforts address discovering useful views across data lakes, schema-driven stream processing, XML projection and XPath rewriting, logical graph-pattern queries, and provenance-aware reachability and regular-path queries.

Typical methods include algebraic system design, schema inference and static complexity analysis, query rewriting and optimization, semantic annotation and validation, database connectors, distributed storage, server-side sparse computation, external-memory algorithms, workflow labeling, prototyping, and empirical benchmarking.

Recent trends emphasize high-throughput D4M associative-array updates and multilingual implementations; scalable Accumulo/D4M platforms; automated semantic publication and domain-specific knowledge graphs; schema-guided processing of web and streaming data; and practical integration of heterogeneous cloud and big-data systems.

47e01afdfff95db259d3125619aea5ca5b7f6214.text:
**Scalable Search, Indexing, and Data Analytics**

This community develops high-performance data-management and retrieval methods for large, multidimensional, spatial, graph, and social datasets. Core themes include compressed inverted and bitmap indexes, multidimensional OLAP, spatial proximity and cross-matching, frequent subgraph mining, geotagged social-network analysis, and expert discovery in collaborative networks.

Typical methods combine relational and distributed database architectures, B-trees, zone and spatial indexes, relational algebra, bitmap operations, set intersection, hashing, tensor and matrix factorization, hierarchical topic modeling, and domain embeddings. Compression is central: variable-byte, Huffman, difference, gap, run-length, and frame-of-reference coding are optimized for inverted lists, integer keys, multidimensional data, and bitmap indexes. Data ordering and attribute reorganization are used to improve compression and query speed.

Recent work emphasizes hardware-conscious acceleration through SIMD vectorization, GPU and multicore execution, cache-aware algorithms, and compressed-data processing. Distributed in-memory dataflow systems support scalable graph mining, while relational backends increasingly serve scientific, spatial, and social-data workloads. Systems research also targets high-throughput OLTP, lower index-storage and maintenance costs, efficient n-gram retrieval, and portable database implementations. Expert recommendation remains an application area, increasingly using factorization and embedding-based representations across collaborative networks.

616b9c29d58ef261b5da90ef2b82c4d62de2f912.text:
### Database Recovery and Heterogeneous Persistent Storage

This community studies database reliability, recovery, and storage management across modern hardware and failure models. A central theme is extending recovery beyond system, media, and transaction failures to include **single-page failures**, using page-recovery indexes and transactional maintenance.

Several works redesign recovery for speed and availability through commit coordination, logging, propagation control, fine-grained locking, partial rollback, snapshot isolation, and concurrent redo-only recovery. Instant restore enables read/write access during media repair and restores segments on demand, making recovery workload-guided rather than strictly sequential.

Another major focus is the convergence of memory and storage technologies. Systems span DRAM, persistent memory (PMem), flash, and disks, using persistent buffer pools and optimistic consistency to support CPU-level access while preserving recoverability. PMem-specific evaluation motivates optimized I/O primitives for log writing and block flushing. Heterogeneity-aware DBMS frameworks exploit semantic information about data and I/O to place data across diverse devices.

Recent work extends these ideas to **native, scalable data structures on real byte-addressable PMem**. Dash presents a holistic persistent hash-table design targeting high scalability, high load factors, low latency, and instant recovery, addressing limitations of emulation-based and piecemeal approaches.

Overall, research trends toward finer-grained failure handling, reduced downtime, persistent data structures, hardware-aware I/O, and adaptive storage hierarchies.

c84eced7ccb18cfab3b749fc79e61d3b616b5312.text:
## Scholarly Networks, Discovery, and Research-Data Infrastructures

This community studies scholarly communication, knowledge discovery, and research-data ecosystems through bibliometrics, information retrieval, and network science. Themes include author disambiguation and bibliographic curation; coauthorship, co-contributorship, citation, patent, institutional, and social-learning networks; collaboration, division of labor, geographic and ethnic structure, scientific careers, venue practices, and technological emergence; and dataset citation, reference extraction, provenance, reproducibility, and data impact. It also examines Wikipedia’s longitudinal multilingual link networks and scholarly infrastructures such as OpenAIRE, DataCite, and ResearchGate.

Typical methods include PageRank, Personalized PageRank, CheiRank, 2DRank, network flow, centrality, modularity and stochastic block models, spectral and multilayer analysis, temporal prediction, regression, rank aggregation, and graph visualization. Machine learning includes unsupervised author disambiguation, similarity and clustering, LSTM knowledge forecasting, and thesaurus- or classification-based search-session segmentation. Evaluation uses DBLP, Web of Science, patent and citation corpora, DataCite and data-citation indexes, full-text datasets, Wikipedia revisions and clickstreams, search logs, eye tracking, mouse behavior, surveys, and user studies.

Recent trends emphasize multilingual longitudinal analysis, early detection of important technologies and emerging knowledge, bibliometrically enhanced and task-aware scholarly retrieval, explicit dataset linking and traceable extraction, open-data metrics, and models of belief diffusion and information quality in social networks.

2beba29dc5d8c4bef5e440fad7c765f084229f55.text:
## Graph-Based Recommendation and Information Dynamics

This community studies recommender systems and information flows over user–item, social, and other evolving networks. Key themes include popularity- and social-tie-driven recommendation, market influence, link prediction, information filtering, and the effects of recommendation on diversity, polarization, and misinformation. Applications span news, food and recipe choice, fashion, fitness, and online marketplaces, with increasing attention to health, taste, and other domain-specific preferences.

Typical methods include random walks and diffusion, graph-based ranking and feature extraction, community-aware and local-structure link prediction, collaborative filtering, social influence modeling, and scalable or incrementally updated network algorithms. Researchers also use controlled experiments, offline multi-metric evaluation, observational causal inference, and analyses of social-media behavior. Robustness methods address malicious nodes, unreliable links, spam, and coordinated disinformation.

Recent trends move beyond accuracy toward causal measurement of recommendation effects, cold-start and new-user performance, diversity and filter-bubble mitigation, and personalization using content or domain knowledge. Studies increasingly examine polarization, junk-news exposure, social bots, and the trade-offs between influence and reliability. Healthier and more explainable recommendations, as well as community structure and network reconstruction for improving prediction, are also gaining prominence.

315fd5f593dace85aa7b9471d15009eee34fc51d.text:
### Social Media Mining of Substance Use and Markets

**Main research themes:**  
The community studies substance use and online markets through social media, including e-cigarette brands and flavors and illicit drug-use patterns. It emphasizes how regulatory environments shape vaping product availability and popularity across countries, while also addressing public-health and law-enforcement needs that are difficult to serve through conventional surveys.

**Typical methods:**  
Researchers collect large-scale data from Reddit, Twitter, Instagram, and related online communities. Methods include extensive data cleaning, text mining, and analysis of multimedia content—combining images with captions or other text—to identify fine-grained patterns, brands, flavors, behaviors, and market activity. Cross-national comparisons are used to relate online trends to differences in laws and regulations.

**Recent trends:**  
The field is moving toward worldwide, platform-spanning analyses of emerging substance markets and toward automated mining of user-generated multimedia data. These approaches aim to complement or overcome survey limitations, especially underreporting and difficulties obtaining representative samples for sensitive topics such as illicit drug use.

e134bd2ac624e441750b0e2bd94f2cacb53b1b67.text:
### Structuring, Preserving, and Exploring Evolving Digital Knowledge

This community studies durable, interpretable, accessible, and discoverable digital information across scientific, cultural, social-media, and web contexts. Themes include repository and digital-object architectures, persistent identifiers, provenance, versioning, rights, fixity, accessibility, FAIR research-data management, semantic annotation, and preservation of evolving web archives. Increasing emphasis is placed on temporal, multilingual, event-centric, and entity-centric exploration, collaborative curation, structured peer review, and machine-actionable scholarly communication.

Typical methods combine standards-based system design with empirical, bibliometric, and user-centered evaluation. Approaches use OAIS, Fedora, OAI-PMH, RDF, SPARQL, PROV-O, PAV, Memento, linked-data models, Web Annotation, and FAIR-oriented repository platforms. Prototypes support biomedical data management, interlinked semantic reviews, repository profiling, and third-party annotations. Large-scale archive indexes, cache systems, machine learning, and compact MementoMaps improve archive discovery and response time; cookie-aware crawling and replay preserve faithful composite pages. Social-media micro-collections and search results generate archive seeds. Event knowledge graphs support cross-lingual timelines and completion through relation prediction and missing-event inference, while supervised tree-based and neural models classify research-data metadata by discipline.

Recent trends emphasize adaptive web-archive infrastructure, event-series completion, multilingual temporal analytics, FAIR and secure research-data portals, and annotation- and AI-supported scholarly workflows.

29364a7b376a4a6d79b985c9038a59011dccccea.text:
### Privacy-Preserving Data Integration and Secure Analytics

This community develops methods for analyzing, linking, and querying sensitive data while balancing privacy, utility, fairness, scalability, and functionality. Differential privacy remains central, covering histograms, synthetic and social-media data, summation and range queries, trajectories, continuous release, location recommendation, and protection against temporal or behavioral inference.
