Location privacy extends from points and trajectories to visits, routines, and mobility patterns.

A growing theme is privacy-aware data integration and entity resolution across heterogeneous databases. Record linkage, address and name disambiguation, and large-scale deduplication use probabilistic signatures, locality-sensitive hashing, blocking, reinforcement learning, and parallel processing. Blocking schemes are optimized through skyline and multi-criteria selection methods.

Secure outsourced and federated query processing exploits differences between sensitive and nonsensitive attributes. Query binning, partitioned security, encrypted databases, spatial order-preserving encryption, secure multiparty computation, trusted hardware, oblivious processing, and private SQL reduce leakage while improving efficiency. Social-network and social-media publishing additionally address linkage and relationship-inference attacks.

Typical methods include calibrated, local, and correlation-aware noise; workload optimization; probabilistic matching; encryption; controlled padding; secure computation; and trusted execution environments.

Recent trends emphasize scalable entity resolution, hybrid cleartext/encrypted processing, practical privacy-utility tradeoffs, efficient spatial and trajectory queries, stronger resistance to linkage and behavioral inference, and fairness-aware private analytics.

2804dafab6600d9785ad7cbd46cf4fdf3ae894f4.text:
## Mobile Data, Mobility, Accessibility, and Public Health

This community studies how geospatial and anonymized mobile-phone data reveal human mobility, social interaction, accessibility, and population-level risks. Core themes include integrating spatial-temporal movement with communication networks to detect large social events through anomalous activity and mobility changes, and applying mobility data to epidemiology, including Chagas disease prevalence and risk zones in Argentina and Mexico. Urban research estimates population distributions and travel patterns for transportation and city planning.

Typical methods include geolocalized call-record analysis, mobility and social-network indicators, temporal and spatial aggregation, high-resolution mapping, and combining inferred links to endemic areas with environmental and socioeconomic vulnerability measures. New work adds accessibility analysis: computing distances and travel times from geographic origins to nearby opportunities such as schools, hospitals, parks, banks, firms, and retail, across alternative transport modes.

Recent trends move from descriptive mobility analysis toward operational decision support, including health campaigns, resource allocation, urban planning, event detection, and measuring access to services. A broader application landscape also includes epidemiologic mapping, traffic prediction, delay-tolerant networking, and modeling the predictability of human movement.

0695af52dcc488e4fdd6f16937d379df5ee2ac2c.text:
## Natural-Language and Example-Based Database Querying

This community studies how non-experts and domain users access structured relational data without mastering SQL or database schemas. Core themes include translating user language and examples into executable queries, resolving ambiguity, inferring query intent, and supporting expressive queries over complex schemas.

Typical methods include natural-language interfaces, programming-by-example, query-by-example (QBE), semantic similarity, abductive reasoning, schema and value matching, and dual-specification systems that combine natural-language descriptions with examples or other constraints. Research also addresses reverse engineering: converting input-output examples into explanatory conjunctive queries and studying the computational complexity of definability and QBE.

Recent trends emphasize moving beyond structural matching of examples toward context- and knowledge-aware intent discovery. Hybrid systems seek to combine the accessibility of natural language with the precision of examples and formal query specifications, enabling users to express queries too complex for simple NLIs or conventional QBE. At the same time, theoretical work isolates sources of computational hardness and develops relaxations and approximation techniques—such as existential pebble-game-based tests—to make reverse-engineering problems more tractable while preserving meaningful guarantees.

b0f425a93a98f64436eef32bc305db5f50d519ca.text:
## Community Structure, Roles, and Influence in Networks

This community studies mesoscale organization, roles, importance, and dynamics in complex networks. Themes include overlapping, hierarchical, multilayer, heterogeneous, attributed, weighted, signed, directed, bipartite, geometric, temporal, uncertain, and partially observed communities; polarization and structural balance; hidden layers; role and ranking hierarchies; cyclic structure; graph comparison; and influence, diffusion, navigation, vulnerability, and community deception. Applications span social and communication networks, online learning, scientific literature, trade, migration, climate, biological, software, and transportation networks.

Typical methods include modularity, stochastic block models and graphons, spectral, nonbacktracking, eigenvector, PageRank, diffusion, and effective-resistance methods; belief propagation, Bayesian and variational inference; label propagation, local and seed-based search; flow-based role similarity and Markov stability; graph signals and blind inference; motif and semantic-network analysis; bipartite and multilayer co-clustering; causal inference; random walks and Markov-chain graph generation; and likelihood, optimization, QUBO/annealing, and information-theoretic formulations.

Recent trends emphasize scalable randomized/sketched spectral algorithms, principled benchmarks and theoretical guarantees, uncertainty propagation when edges are unobserved, directed-role and hierarchy resolution, signed-network polarization detection, graph symmetrization and comparison, influence-aware diffusion prediction, and multiscale evolutionary attacks that hide communities at global, community, or node scales.

97887c9b1461e5cc337cc9a9f50bd1992bc3eb4a.text:
### Adaptive Networks and Knowledge Mining

This community studies how network structure and relational evidence support reasoning, retrieval, recommendation, and classification. Foundational work examines weighted distance graphs, fuzzy and proximity closures, and semi-metric behavior, including cases where indirect relationships are stronger than direct ones. These ideas apply across user–item, document, citation, hyperlink, collaboration, and other relational networks.

Typical methods include graph-closure and shortest-path analysis, network-derived distances, community-structure modeling, recommendation, statistical text mining, and supervised or multilabel classification. The community emphasizes representations that preserve relational structure and expose latent similarities, dependencies, and expertise.

Recent trends focus on scalable and adaptive analytics for heterogeneous networks, integrating textual and graph-based evidence while improving retrieval, ranking, and prediction. Applications increasingly connect network structure with knowledge discovery and decision support across dynamic information environments.

38760f246d137d3c697b92f02d08cc3996a2529f.text:
### Network Reasoning, Social Media, and Public-Health Intelligence

This community studies how network structure and large-scale heterogeneous data support reasoning, recommendation, classification, information management, sentiment analysis, and biomedical or public-health surveillance. It examines weighted distance, fuzzy, proximity, and semi-metric graphs, where indirect relationships may be stronger than direct ones, for recommendation and knowledge discovery across user–item, document, citation, hyperlink, collaboration, and semantic networks.

Typical methods include graph-closure and shortest-path analysis, network-derived distance functions, agent-based classification, distributed vocabulary adaptation, lightweight linear models, uncertainty-aware integration, multilabel classification, cross-platform user/content mapping, text mining, and multimodal analysis combining social-media text, images, metadata, and geolocation.

Recent work expands online intelligence beyond conventional recommendation and pharmacovigilance. Twitter is used for fine-grained measurement of geopolitical attitudes, while Pinterest–Twitter linkage enables topic-aware, visually diversified board recommendation. Reddit, Twitter, and Instagram support worldwide analysis of e-cigarette brands, flavors, markets, and regulatory differences. Geo-tagged images and automatic visual annotations complement text for monitoring obesity, smoking, drinking, and other lifestyle risks. Multimodal Instagram mining detects illicit drug dealing, abuse, and behavioral patterns, addressing limitations and reporting bias in surveys. Overall, the community is moving toward cross-platform, multimodal, geographically sensitive, and population-scale systems for adaptive knowledge management and public-health intelligence.

ffd64803b0ae7cea126811756d14527b3797adb6.text:
### Semantic Search and Structured Scientific Data

This community develops methods for searching, integrating, and analyzing heterogeneous text, XML, mathematical, and agricultural data. Core themes include semantic retrieval using named entities, aliases, classes, identifiers, WordNet concepts, ontologies, latent relations, and keyword weighting; XML collection exploration, indexing, path summaries, keyword search, and distributed storage; mathematical information retrieval and representation; plagiarism detection using mathematical content and citations; and decision support from integrated agricultural big data.

Typical methods combine generalized vector-space models, ontology-based query expansion, spreading activation, supervised term weighting, NLP, classification, and empirical retrieval evaluation. XML systems use declarative path descriptions, structural consistency constraints, path partitioning, materialized views, adaptive fragment redistribution, and distributed hash-table/P2P architectures. Mathematical search applies symbol embeddings, neural representations, topic models linking equations with text, corpus-scale notation analysis, and semantic-preserving mappings between computer-algebra and document-preparation systems. Agricultural applications emphasize normalization, homogenization, integration, warehousing, and quality management across IoT, sensors, satellites, equipment, and human sources.

Recent trends extend semantic search beyond ordinary prose to XML structure and mathematical notation, exploit neural and latent representations alongside explicit ontologies, improve detection of concealed plagiarism and deceptive content, and build scalable distributed repositories and analytics pipelines for scientific and sensor-rich domains.

32f2dea5afc5dfea6791217d4c0f529386eb34e6.text:
### Cross-Modal Hashing and Quantization

This community studies efficient cross-modal similarity search, especially between images and text, under large-scale storage and computation constraints. Its central goal is to learn compact shared representations that preserve semantic relationships across heterogeneous modalities.

Typical methods include discrete latent-factor and supervised matrix-factorization models, deep joint learning of modality features and binary codes, and correlation-based quantization. Recent work emphasizes **asymmetric correlation quantization hashing**, which addresses the information loss caused by forcing real-valued multimodal data directly into compact binary codes. By using asymmetric representations or similarity computation, these methods aim to retain richer semantic information while preserving the storage and computational advantages of hashing.

Beyond code learning, the papers address retrieval infrastructure: probability-based indexing avoids exhaustive search and improves on inaccurate direct Hamming-distance computation. Neural representation learning also moves beyond conventional word-level text features, using graph convolutional networks to model textual structure for cross-modal retrieval.

Overall, the field is trending from shallow factorization and binary relaxation toward discrete, jointly optimized, and quantization-based semantic representations. Current priorities include reducing information loss, improving cross-modal similarity estimation, and enabling accurate, storage-efficient, real-time retrieval at scale.

ff979f8f76e30ccdc2a405e84237095d643d313a.text:
## Social Diffusion and Evolving Online Networks

This community studies how information, opinions, emotions, behaviors, memes, malicious content, and social activity spread through online, temporal, multiplex, and location-based networks. Core themes include cascade dynamics, influence, weak and strong ties, homophily, reciprocity, tie diversity, community structure, network assembly, popularity and attention, engagement, privacy and contextual integrity, recommender-system manipulation, and collective behavior during emergencies. It also examines how network structure and diffusion co-evolve, including indirect co-location links and topic-specific user susceptibility.

Typical methods combine stochastic, threshold, Bass, rumor, agent-based, and continuous-time models with temporal/adaptive network analysis, graph statistics, centrality, community detection, signed and attributed graphs, higher-order representations, and power-law or burst analysis. Machine learning, NLP, multimodal analysis, and recommendation models support event recognition, influence and popularity prediction, risk and behavior profiling, privacy analysis, and detection of anomalous or malicious activity. Optimal control and experimentation are used to steer engagement and information exposure.

Recent directions emphasize platform and population-level network assembly, cross-context and weak-tie diffusion, real-time event sensing, emergency communication, emotional interaction with bots, endogenous/exogenous bursts, topic-dependent propagation, comparative network analysis, and the societal risks of manipulation, deviant communities, and privacy leakage.

aa6082f76a5fe71dcc87fb70049db2866fe0d1db.text:
### Dynamic Heterogeneous, Higher-Order Network Learning

This community studies large, heterogeneous, multimodal, and evolving networks, including social, information, citation, semantic, knowledge, multiplex, bipartite, and hypergraphs. Core tasks include node and graph representation learning, link and weight prediction, network alignment, diffusion and influence inference, community discovery, fraud detection, recommendation, graph comparison, and analysis of nonlinear dynamics.

Typical methods integrate topology with attributes, text, tags, activity, and interaction semantics. They include random walks and proximity measures, diffusion and heat-based distances, temporal and hypergraph motifs, graphlets, trusses and trapezes, spectral and nonbacktracking analysis, latent-space and generative models, matrix-factorization embeddings, graph convolutional, attentive, recurrent, and variational networks, meta-path aggregation, semi-supervised learning, reinforcement learning for network discovery, and structure-content fusion. Higher-order relationships and interpretable cohesion metrics support classification, sparsification, and prediction.

Scalability is pursued through streaming and dynamic embeddings, approximate SimRank and other similarity computation, block-approximated probabilistic models, sampling, and billion-scale recommendation systems. Recent trends emphasize dynamic link prediction, coexisting diffusion reconstruction, knowledge-graph construction and benchmarking, hypergraph modeling, explainable network structures, online entity disambiguation, robust influence estimation under incomplete networks, and real-time analytics on operational platforms.

487a9e114c40d8fa45645f638ec66e5cafe9cdf3.text:
### Research Software, Data, and Reproducible Scholarship

This community treats software and data as core scholarly outputs and advances the reproducibility, transparency, visibility, and credit of computational research. Key themes include reforming citation infrastructure—such as citation graphs that represent software and enable transitive credit—while assessing the limitations of software citations and name mentions, including evidence from the **lme4** R package. It also examines data-sharing practices, motivations, withholding, and the reputation economy surrounding openness.

Typical methods include conceptual and graph-model development, infrastructure reviews, empirical surveys, citation analysis, and classification of reproducibility terminology. Studies track thousands of citations to Zenodo data and software DOIs, evaluating version and concept DOIs for impact measurement. Institutional and publication solutions include the Journal of Open Source Software, ReScience’s executable research environments, and emerging journal and conference policies requiring data and software availability.

Recent trends show funders requesting data/software management plans, venues scrutinizing reproducibility, and reviewers sometimes rejecting inaccessible or non-reproducible work. The community increasingly emphasizes that reproducible publication requires more than releasing scripts and files: it depends on integrated, documented, executable infrastructures, standardized citations, explicit credit, and clearer expectations across the research lifecycle.

26758f78782e28e4f830a77f763f07ad3a2357df.text:
## Dynamic and Multimodal Network Structure

This community studies mesoscopic organization and cohesion in large, evolving, directed, multilayer, and bipartite networks. Core themes include overlapping and hierarchical communities, core–periphery structure, dense subgraphs and generalized cores, node roles, bridges, influence, communicability, link persistence, and causal diffusion. Applications span social, web, traffic, financial, political-violence, affiliation, recommendation, and narrative-character networks.

Typical methods include dynamic stochastic blockmodels, latent-space generative models, Bayesian community detection from time series, modularity and Markov-stability approaches, role-based similarity, spectral embeddings, random walks, consensus clustering, and isospectral reductions. Cohesion is assessed with k-cores, generalized two-mode cores, density, triangles, degeneracy, hyperbolicity, and convexity. Centrality, PageRank, betweenness approximations, communicability, and influence games identify important nodes and links. Spectral and geometric methods support scalable link prediction, network reconstruction, and backbone discovery.

Evaluation emphasizes detectability, uncertainty, stability, scalability, missing-data effects, robustness, and model-based comparison. Recent trends include lossless event-based temporal representations, continuous-time visualization, causal-path analysis, evolving communities and roles, multilayer persistence, fast large-scale prediction, community-deception attacks, directed-flow analysis, and automated analysis of narrative and behavioral networks.

3e9f9923a0c7cf14af4f3f313e3410bae79d4f79.text:
### Social Networks, Misinformation, and Influence

This community studies how social platforms shape opinion, spread information, and enable manipulation. Core themes include rumors, fake news, disinformation, credibility, fact-checking, health misinformation, spam, and malicious accounts; political advertising, elections, polarization, controversy, propaganda, and state-sponsored influence; coordinated campaigns, bots, pathogenic users, and deceptive content-display attacks; and privacy, data sovereignty, decentralized platforms, and auditing of platform content. It also examines overlapping beliefs, signed-network balance, cross-language controversy, public perceptions, and information diffusion across platforms.

Typical methods combine large-scale Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, Reddit, YouTube, Gab, and news datasets with diffusion, retweet, coordination, and heterogeneous-network analysis. Researchers use linguistic, stance, sentiment, topic, embedding, author, metadata, and behavioral features, alongside graph kernels, matrix factorization, spectral and dynamical-systems models, epidemic models, network comparison, and statistical causal adjustment. Machine-learning approaches include supervised, semi-supervised, unsupervised, attention-based, recurrent, graph-neural, adversarial, and ensemble models; applications include rumor-source inference, fact-checking recommendation, spam detection, and privacy-preserving recommendation.

Recent trends emphasize early message-level rumor detection, topology-only and multilayer misinformation classification, generalizable and explainable detection, coordinated-influence discovery, cross-platform infodemics, privacy-preserving architectures, and independent political-ad monitoring.

d0b051606ea4b6ba440f03a94003adcf7ed62ef8.text:
## Uncertain, Inconsistent, and Explainable Query Processing

**Main themes.** This community studies probabilistic, incomplete, and inconsistent data, including model counting, reliability, certain answers, joins, aggregation, negation, temporal and multiset semantics, and open- versus closed-world query answering. It investigates ontology-mediated querying, guarded and sticky tuple-generating dependencies (TGDs), conjunctive and path queries, query rewriting, chase behavior, and the tractability and hardness of these tasks. Data quality includes repairs, integrity constraints, inconsistency measurement, view-based cleaning, and learned error detection. Explainability covers provenance, lineage, why/why-not summaries, Shapley values, query-result exploration, counterexamples, and query grading.

**Typical methods.** Techniques include possible-worlds reasoning, inclusion–exclusion, knowledge compilation and deterministic decomposable circuits, model counting, SAT solving, repairs, constraint reasoning, graph rewriting, automata, structural and parameterized complexity, chase analysis, query containment and rewriting, sampling, data augmentation, and causal interventions for aggregate queries.

**Recent trends.** Work emphasizes scalable approximate certain answers and provenance, efficient temporal-probabilistic set operations, continuous-distribution probabilistic Datalog, principled open-world ontology querying, and sharper characterizations of chase termination and reliability. Practical directions include few-shot data-error detection, automated partial SQL grading, interactive result exploration, view-based cleaning, progress indicators for repairs, and efficient methods for deletion propagation and fairness-aware data interventions.

ea11f00b1a22d451c9f574b72cf193b18b9e5b39.text:
### Social Media, Networks, and Information Integrity

This community studies how online platforms shape public opinion, political behavior, collective action, attention, and information integrity. Core themes include polarization, controversy, overlapping beliefs, misinformation and rumor diffusion, bots, vandalism, coordinated or criminal behavior, demographic and socioeconomic inference, online abuse, information overload, and event awareness. It also examines viewpoint diversity, group dynamics, cultural differences, user intentions, and the effects of platform communication on society.

Typical methods combine Twitter, Facebook, Reddit, Wikipedia, Twitch, mobile-communication, transaction, and communication-network data with graph, temporal, propagation, linguistic, geospatial, and cross-platform analysis. Researchers use matrix factorization, topic and stance modeling, embeddings, supervised and semi-supervised classification, random walks, graph labeling, network motifs, graph kernels, regression, anomaly detection, master-equation and diffusion models, and scalable event-mining pipelines. Network sampling, sampling-bias correction, link prediction, and consensus clustering support inference from incomplete graphs.

Recent work emphasizes continuous-time network modeling, topology-based misinformation and rumor detection, motif-based controversy analysis, stance-aware summaries, diversity-oriented exposure, robust demographic prediction from multifaceted behavioral data, and geo-temporal detection of protests and collective action. Other trends include mobile sensing for socioeconomic measurement, group-level financial-crime detection, and evaluating sampling reliability and information overload in online communities.

845e84edc8157f89383af8f3e27a21cf13dc770e.text:
## Network Science for Knowledge, Influence, and Prediction

This community studies directed, temporal, multilayer, and evolving networks to analyze discoverability, centrality, information flow, social influence, and knowledge production. Applications span Wikipedia and Wikidata, linked-data integration, multilingual knowledge graphs, scientific citation practices, online communities, elections, mass media, and narrative media.

Google-matrix and walk-based methods—including PageRank, personalized PageRank, CheiRank, Katz/Bonacich centrality, communicability, navigability, and spectral embeddings—support ranking, link prediction, triadic-closure analysis, and network design. Research also addresses missing facts and links, graph completeness, knowledge-graph alignment, and improving connectivity and navigation.

A prominent concern is the quality and reliability of collaborative knowledge: vandalism detection, edit-quality prediction, online learning, ensemble classification, and automated moderation for Wikipedia and Wikidata. NLP extracts semantic, temporal, and contextual relations for word-sense disambiguation, media-influence analysis, and content characterization.

Typical methods combine longitudinal and multilingual graph construction with random walks, Markov and Kalman models, spectral and matrix techniques, optimization, machine learning, sequence analysis, null models, and diffusion simulation.

Recent trends emphasize scalable link prediction, clickstream-informed multilingual ranking, Wikidata ecosystem integration, real-time quality control, explainable knowledge-graph enrichment, digital-trace prediction of elections and public opinion, and principled centrality measures based on navigability and communication.

6a256563c4161506df59bdad3c2a8880021190dd.text:
## Scholarly Discovery, Recommendation, and Hypothesis Generation

This community develops systems that make scholarly information discoverable, structured, trustworthy, explainable, and actionable. Major themes include metadata and document-structure extraction, semantic publishing, citation analysis and matching, knowledge-graph construction, automated search, trend visualization, personalized recommendation, and automated hypothesis generation. Graph-based platforms support expert finding, indirect-connection discovery, and exploratory querying, while extraction systems process authors, affiliations, bibliographies, tables, figures, reference strings, and citation contexts.

Recommendation research combines content and network signals, including titles, abstracts, embeddings, keyphrases, co-citation, citation graphs, topic models, and behavioral data. Citation recommenders increasingly use candidate generation followed by neural re-ranking, including domain-adapted BERT models and hybrid retrieval systems. Large-scale hypothesis-generation systems mine multimodal, multirelational biomedical networks to surface implicit connections and rank research candidates.

Typical methods include rule-based and statistical information extraction, NLP, blocking and binary classification, near-duplicate detection, MinHash and Jaccard similarity, graph databases, knowledge networks, machine learning, meta-learning, embeddings, pretrained language models, and distributed processing.

Recent trends include rigorous numerical validation of hypothesis generation, analysis of corpus size and abstracts versus full text, explainable tuning of opaque recommenders, production-scale hybrid recommendation, and API-based living-lab evaluation. Bibliometric analyses also track changing collaboration patterns, including the decline of single-author computer-science publications.

c75d5be7de16ce598f1d22af97b73fc9cf16be76.text:
**Community Status: No Active Papers**

**Main research themes:** No research themes are currently supported because all previously associated papers have left the community.

**Typical methods:** None can be identified from the remaining membership.

**Recent trends:** No current trends or methodological developments are represented.

75bcf642ebcf4b16365fc6eba1d122be25a8855f.text:
## Keyphrase Extraction, Summarization, and News Analytics

This community develops methods for extracting and exploiting document concepts—keywords, keyphrases, topics, central sentences, and important passages—for indexing, retrieval, categorization, summarization, title generation, and news aggregation. It also studies conceptual representations that enable coherent, searchable views of heterogeneous and rapidly changing news.

Typical methods combine statistical, lexical, supervised, neural, and graph-based approaches. Features include position, frequency, inverse document frequency, semantic roles, and node properties from complex networks and graph-of-text representations. PageRank-style ranking supports keyphrase relevance, while supervised models learn from graph features and sequence models generate absent or revised keyphrases. Topic-aware graphs, dependency-tree compression, embeddings, and personalized ranking support summarization, title generation, and recommendation.

Applications span scholarly and biomedical information extraction, scientific title recommendation, large-scale news categorization, aggregation, and actionable information filtering from disaster Twitter. Recent work introduces KPTimes, a large news dataset with editor-curated keyphrases, and neural keyphrase generation for news. Disaster-response research targets automatic identification of useful hashtags, including recurrent neural models.

Recent trends emphasize reproducible, cross-domain evaluation; comparisons showing that simple baselines can remain competitive; scalable real-time processing; semantic and complex-network features; and generation-oriented extraction. The community increasingly addresses annotation quality, practical usefulness, and relevance–diversity trade-offs.

b290657f26928e8bf0ebf88ee7431f08ed5053bc.text:
### Graph Data Management, Integrity, and Analytics

**Main research themes:** This community studies management, integration, querying, and exploration of heterogeneous relational, RDF, and property-graph data. It emphasizes graph-processing practice, RDF–property-graph interoperability, compact storage, query optimization, semantic search, entity resolution, and accessible interfaces. Newer concerns include preserving data integrity during transformations, detecting invariant violations, and assessing trust in data-driven systems.

**Typical methods:** Approaches include formal semantics, schema mappings, query rewriting and containment, structural indexing for conjunctive path queries, graph traversal, embeddings, and graph neural methods. Systems use adaptive and compressed indexes, topology-aware storage, batching, parallel and distributed execution, and workload-driven benchmarking. Evaluation increasingly relies on realistic graph generators, synthetic agent-based network simulations, and standardized workloads such as the LDBC Social Network Benchmark. Large-scale ETL pipelines and visual interfaces support centralized log collection, monitoring, and exploratory analytics.

**Recent trends:** Research is becoming more empirical and systems-oriented, informed by surveys of how graph platforms are used in practice. The field is developing generators that balance structural realism, narrative fidelity, and statistical diversity, alongside benchmarks for interactive and analytical workloads. Query engines are adopting language-aware structural indexes, while data-management research increasingly treats transformation provenance, integrity invariants, and trustworthy downstream analytics as first-class requirements.

ea746d44af046ad931f66e2f80644e8f2b26d537.text:
## Probabilistic Data Integration and Trustworthy Curation

This community studies data management under uncertainty, incompleteness, inconsistency, noisy similarity, and complex probabilistic rules. Core themes include probabilistic databases, possible-world representations, uncertain joins and top-k ranking, approximate similarity search, inconsistency evaluation and repair, probabilistic programming, entity resolution, schema and semantic integration, and data curation. It also examines data marketplaces, query pricing, and the economic value of data access.

Typical methods include world-set decompositions, probabilistic inference, ranking-distribution semantics, semirings, stochastic kernels, and declarative Datalog extensions supporting continuous distributions. Data integration and entity resolution use blocking, locality-sensitive hashing, probabilistic signatures, edit-distance embeddings, distributed representations, deep neural models, relational match propagation, and crowd or human-in-the-loop labeling. Curation increasingly combines learned schema representations, semantic column annotation, automated cleaning, and parallel processing.

Recent trends emphasize scalable, low-human-effort entity resolution and self-driving data curation for heterogeneous, large-scale sources. Deep learning and embeddings are being integrated with relational structure, knowledge-base signals, and approximate indexing. Data marketplaces are emerging as a major application area, with research on arbitrage-free and revenue-maximizing query pricing and cost-effective acquisition for analytical joins. Theoretical work continues on expressive representations of uncertain data and principled semantics for probabilistic rule systems.

daa4b40f9056b608dffd1526342ba1d556553fe8.text:
### Ontology-Enriched Retrieval and Data-Driven Decision Support

This community studies semantic extensions of keyword-based information retrieval, emphasizing the complementary roles of keywords and named entities. It represents latent ontological features—aliases, classes, identifiers, and sometimes WordNet synonyms, hypernyms, hyponyms, and senses—to capture meaning absent from surface text, including implied concepts and related entities.

Typical methods extend the Vector Space Model with ontology-derived entity features and use query-oriented spreading activation for semantic query expansion. Later approaches improve precision by restricting activation to explicitly related entities and those connected to the original query, reducing irrelevant expansion. Experiments generally report gains over keyword-only systems such as Lucene.

The community also addresses integrated data management and decision support for precision agriculture. This work treats agricultural information as big data, combining heterogeneous sources including field, soil, fertilizer, pest, weather, drone, and satellite data. Data warehousing and agricultural data mining support analysis across high volume, variety, velocity, and veracity.

Recent trends therefore extend ontology-guided semantic representation and controlled expansion toward large-scale, heterogeneous data integration and domain-specific analytics, linking richer semantic search with practical decision-support applications.

3d35ff78d4d822c5e2dd77a21f6112e3771e8731.text:
## Scalable, Intelligent, and Trustworthy Data Systems

This community develops scalable data management, querying, and analytics for relational, graph, streaming, semi-structured, array, time-series, video, and scientific data. Core themes include query optimization, cardinality and similarity estimation, worst-case-optimal and projected joins, ranked enumeration, incremental processing, stream analytics, view and workload management, data integration, semantic typing, provenance, and machine learning over relational data. It also addresses polystore interoperability, open-world sampling, transactional consistency, Byzantine resilience, immutable storage, privacy-aware edge analytics, and blockchain transactions.

Typical methods combine formal complexity, algebraic and information-theoretic analysis with sampling, sketches, probabilistic models, Bayesian debiasing, histograms, compact and learned indexes, factorization, compression, incremental maintenance, reinforcement learning, and declarative optimization. Systems exploit associative-array algebras, GraphBLAS, NUMA multicore, GPUs, SSDs, serverless clouds, and distributed heterogeneous engines.

Recent trends include billion-scale graph and provenance ingestion using D4M/Accumulo, external-memory graph processing, unified relational/array/key-value/graph algebras, polystore query planning, approximate video and autonomous-camera queries, streaming similarity search and joins, and polynomial range-aggregate indexes. Formal work continues on relational lattices, document spanners, tree and complex-value queries, while storage research emphasizes LSM performance, immutable Merkle indexes, open-world estimation, and geo-scale cross-blockchain commit protocols.

109f7c8be39d3b161f4ba7d20ef786c6e1abd41b.text:
## Web, Knowledge, and Social Network Analytics

This community analyzes large hyperlink, knowledge, social-media, and interaction networks to study information flow, cultural and geopolitical relationships, collective behavior, influence, navigation, and decision-making. Key applications include multilingual Wikipedia and Wikidata analysis, university and scholarly ranking, political-attitude and voting prediction, event and breaking-news detection, ontology exploration, missing-link recommendation, vandalism detection, multimedia retrieval, and web navigation.

Typical methods include PageRank, CheiRank, two-dimensional ranking, reduced Google matrices, spectral and eigenvector analysis, centrality and robustness measures, graph-based random walks, link prediction, network vulnerability and power metrics, and longitudinal or multilanguage network comparison. Behavioral analysis uses temporal edit and social-media activity, power-law and self-similarity testing, Bayesian hypothesis comparison of web trails, Markov models, and time-aware learning-to-rank. Machine-learning classifiers support political prediction, word-sense disambiguation, recommendation, and anomaly detection, while graph-based multimodal fusion combines visual and textual evidence.

Data include Wikipedia and Wikidata revisions and links, multilingual encyclopedic networks, Twitter and geo-tagged streams, web-navigation trails, ontology-portal logs, multimedia collections, and survey-linked social-media activity.

Recent trends emphasize cross-cultural and geopolitical knowledge mining, dynamic event detection, interpretable network influence measures, collaborative-platform quality control, multilingual knowledge-gap completion, and behavior-aware retrieval and recommendation.

ff78db7af0b602f4a515d91e0d13722bd49f8563.text:
**Utility-Aware Pattern and Content Mining**

This community studies how to discover useful, nonredundant patterns in ordered event, transaction, and multidimensional data, using utility, profit, risk, cost, importance, or relevance rather than frequency alone. Key topics include high-utility sequential patterns, episodes, occupancy-aware patterns, and correlated utility patterns that account for item relationships and avoid misleading combinations of individually valuable items. Extensions address individualized thresholds, recent or trending utility, uncertainty, privacy, and complex or heterogeneous sequences.

Episode mining covers serial, parallel, strict, general, and simultaneous-event episodes. Researchers seek compact, actionable outputs through closed episodes, non-derivable itemsets, generic bases, minimum-description-length compression, and statistical or partition-based filtering of redundant and free-rider patterns. Constraint-based mining incorporates length, gap, span, regular-expression, hierarchy, and other subsequence constraints.

Typical methods include utility upper bounds, projected databases, sequence/episode growth, closure and equivalence classes, concise representations, correlation measures, encoding schemes, significance tests, and parallel or MapReduce algorithms. Distributed matching methods such as GreedyMR and StackMR optimize content relevance while balancing consumer load and supplier exposure.

Recent trends emphasize occupancy, correlation, relevance regulation, recency, uncertainty, privacy, scalability, and actionable output quality.

4c9112c3ae95a76d57f23ff4744223c17e3408c4.text:
## Collaborative Search and Social Data Analytics

This community studies how people collaboratively seek, interpret, and organize information, and how social data can improve search, knowledge work, and decision-making. Major themes include collaborative information seeking and retrieval: modeling collaboration by intent, depth, concurrency, and location; understanding group properties and user needs; and designing systems that combine profiles, shared context, and social interactions throughout the search process.

A second theme is extracting value from participatory data. Collaborative tags support product design, recommendation, and semantic interpretation, while tag-cloud interfaces enable shared exploration of ad hoc multidimensional data. Collaborative data analysis examines whether Web-scale visualization and structured-data platforms can support collective scientific and business reasoning.

Typical methods include conceptual taxonomies and qualitative field studies, critical-incident surveys, collaborative-IR system design, information-behavior analysis, mining of tagging data, user-profile aggregation, and empirical evaluation. Data-management work contributes multidimensional query operators such as diamond dicing for pruning data cubes, alongside OLAP operations including slicing, roll-ups, clustering, and drill-downs.

Recent trends emphasize group-aware and socially embedded search, shared and embedded analytics, rapid exploration of user-contributed data, and moving beyond solitary search toward coordinated, collaborative information work.

28a48bbc7b8db48cd9044a1d2f543f3607a5b2d6.text:
### Personalized Recommendation: Sequential, Graph, and Responsible Optimization

This community studies personalized recommendation across commerce, media, music, fashion, travel, healthcare, jobs, social activities, and specialized domains. Core themes include sparse implicit feedback, cold start, long-tail and complementary-item discovery, sequential and session behavior, long-term interests, social influence, heterogeneous user–item information, and contextual geographic or temporal signals. Increasing attention targets diversity, popularity bias, fairness, explainability, privacy, robustness, and business revenue.

Typical methods span neighborhood models, matrix and Bayesian factorization, overlapping co-clustering, pairwise ranking, hybrid and multimodal neural networks, GANs, autoencoders, RNNs and transformers, graph convolutional and attention networks, knowledge-graph and domain embeddings, and latent-state models. Meta-learning enables user-level model selection and ensembles; reinforcement learning supports joint recommendation–advertising and conversational decision-making; causal exposure modeling, privileged-feature distillation, and efficient random-walk retrieval address deployment constraints.

Recent trends emphasize next-item and long-term sequential prediction, future-context training, adaptive social diffusion, complementary-product modeling, interpretable aspect- and path-based explanations, and conversational preference elicitation. Research increasingly studies industrial web-scale serving, algorithm selection, and end-to-end revenue optimization. Offline evaluation is being reexamined for bias, novelty blindness, and unreliable satisfaction estimates, while poisoning and attribute-inference attacks motivate more secure, privacy-aware recommender systems.

e93c974109e7fbc9daa586f5c75879169849ad09.text:
## Concept-Centered Retrieval and Keyphrase Generation

This community studies extracting and exploiting document concepts—keyphrases, keywords, hashtags, tags, central sentences, and topics—for indexing, retrieval, recommendation, news categorization, summarization, and title generation. It spans scientific, news, and disaster-related social-media content, supporting information filtering, discovery, browsing, and emergency response.

Typical methods combine supervised neural classification and sequence generation with lexical features such as position, frequency, and inverse document frequency. Graph and complex-network approaches represent semantic, contextual, multipartite, or graph-of-text structure, using node properties, connectivity, topical reinforcement, PageRank-like ranking, and learned or preference-aware scoring. Semantic roles and document structure enrich relevance estimation, while category labels guide extraction. Other methods denoise text, rank information-rich sentences, cluster topics, and compress dependency trees into titles.

Recent work emphasizes actionable hashtag identification in disaster Twitter streams, editor-curated large-scale news keyphrase datasets, and supervised graph-based extraction. It also highlights the need for standardized, cross-domain evaluation, revealing that simple baselines can challenge state-of-the-art systems. Trends include parameterless or unsupervised semantic graphs, neural and graph-feature models, automatic keyphrase and title generation, scalable low-latency processing, and embedding-based evaluation of summaries.

0f32d9ca42114450d922fa0b20c1ea689b8a8faf.text:
### Social Media Geolocation, Event Intelligence, and Forecasting

This community studies how large-scale digital traces reveal location, movement, attention, sentiment, influence, and rapidly evolving events. Core topics include geolocating users and tweets from sparse textual, profile, interaction, and geographic signals; modeling urban and social structure; analyzing user behavior and influence; and tracking trends across online media.

A major focus is operational intelligence. Systems detect events and sub-events, identify relevant messages, summarize live situations, rank news and alerts, and support disaster response, emergency mapping, disease surveillance, environmental-risk prediction, and public-health assessment. Other applications include sports-outcome prediction, misinformation and rumor analysis, social welfare monitoring, and credibility-sensitive information triage.

Typical methods include dynamic and nonparametric topic models, scalable and parallel topic discovery, embeddings and cross-lingual transfer, character-aware neural networks, interactive and active learning, sentiment and behavioral classification, matrix/tensor factorization, network influence and contagion models, graph-based ranking, user-profile similarity, abstractive summarization, GIS visual analytics, and online forecasting. Differential-equation models and probabilistic network simulations complement data-driven approaches.

Recent trends emphasize real-time, high-resolution, multilingual inference; modeling evolving topics, influences, and user expertise; explicit uncertainty and annotation-noise handling; misinformation and source credibility assessment; privacy-aware network analysis; and decision support for emergencies, public health, and collective behavior.

c3b0af9b6f4fa4d73b189870d7ce834a78dc270a.text:
**Information Retrieval: Neural Ranking, Fairness, and Interactive Search**

**Main themes.** This community studies relevance modeling and semantic matching for web, scholarly, enterprise, e-commerce, multimedia, social-media, and question-answering search. Key problems include query and intent understanding, passage retrieval, cross-lingual matching, event detection, conversational and spoken search, personalized ranking, mobile discovery, and scalable retrieval. Increasing attention addresses fairness, bias, diversity, exposure, and satisfaction across demographic groups, as well as legal document review and trustworthy summarization.

**Typical methods.** Systems combine lexical retrieval with embeddings, pretrained and multilingual transformers, CNNs/RNNs, sequence-to-sequence generation, multimodal image-text representations, and probabilistic fusion of social and physical sensors. Ranking uses pointwise, pairwise, listwise, metric-learning, constrained-optimization, multi-objective, and weak-supervision objectives. Methods include query reformulation, session contextualization, active learning, click-bias correction, fairness-aware re-ranking, exposure allocation, antidote data, and interpretable or faithful generation. Efficiency remains important through compact contextualization and time-budgeted neural re-ranking.

**Recent trends.** Research is moving toward selective weak supervision, end-to-end neural and multimodal retrieval, adaptive real-time event detection, personalized query completion, abstractive and fact-aware snippets, explainable legal classification, and systematic auditing of ranking outcomes for fairness, selection bias, and disparate user satisfaction.

ef326674f8301775da0ab0183649f7ecda06c350.text:
## Scalable Graph Structure, Sampling, and Network Comparison

This community studies how to characterize, compare, generate, and sample social, information, semantic, heterogeneous, signed, and attributed networks. Core themes include graph and node similarity, link prediction, community and role discovery, centrality and influence, clustering, structural classification, network growth, and estimation of degree, clique, triangle, and motif statistics. Cross-platform identity and privacy remain relevant, alongside applications to social behavior and information diffusion.

Typical methods combine neighborhoods, clustering, centrality, random walks, Markov chains, spectral techniques, latent-variable and probabilistic graph models, graph grammars, and structural or attribute-based representations. Typed graphlets and signed-network measures capture heterogeneous and negative relationships. Sampling methods include vertex, edge, egocentric, wedge, traversal, random-walk-with-jump, and hybrid-affiliation sampling. Distributed, MapReduce, external-memory, and sublinear algorithms support massive graphs, while random forests and supervised models classify networks and predict links or attributes.

Recent trends emphasize provable, privacy-compatible estimation from partial graph access; scalable counting of triangles and larger subgraphs; improved synthetic graph generators that preserve clustering, attributes, and multifractal structure; robustness evaluation for generators; local-information algorithms; and models connecting social attributes, topology, and network evolution. Research also increasingly examines structural thresholds, core–periphery organization, graph domains, and quality guarantees for sampling and comparison.

4ee21911d53201223840eb9100023d94fdbbe4aa.text:
## Scholarly Discovery, Search, and Knowledge Organization

This community studies information retrieval, scholarly and library discovery, ranking, recommendation, and knowledge organization across publications, datasets, repositories, Wikipedia, social networks, and professional platforms. Core themes include citation and dataset-reference analysis, research-data attribution, bibliographic metadata, query expansion, entity and expertise search, credibility, personalized ranking, and user behavior in search.

Typical methods combine bibliometrics and network analysis with learning-to-rank, collaborative filtering, content and graph-based retrieval, query expansion, clickthrough experimentation, crowdsourced relevance judgments, and representative-query evaluation. Systems exploit Wikipedia links and categories, citation and social graphs, text and metadata, behavioral logs, and large distributed or relational databases. Information extraction and entity linking identify dataset mentions and connect scholarly artifacts. Scalable infrastructure includes batch query processing, multidimensional and spatial indexing, array databases, and geospatial data warehouses.

Recent trends emphasize user- and context-aware search, unbiased preference collection and position-bias analysis, low-cost yet reliable IR evaluation, credibility-aware ranking, semantic navigation through Wikipedia and linked graphs, large-scale expertise and talent search, and data-driven analysis of professional and social networks. They also highlight reproducible dataset discovery and improved attribution through explicit links between papers and research data.

bade640390365d6acd81325bb8e68deb091a76b7.text:
### Interoperable Graph Querying and Knowledge-Data Management

This community studies interoperable graph and data-management systems spanning RDF, property graphs, knowledge graphs, relational and NoSQL stores, contextual data, and cloud database services. Core themes include RDF–property-graph mappings, graph query semantics and determinacy, schema and view management, ontology-mediated query answering, graph pattern matching, relationship and relevance search, entity resolution, temporal interaction analysis, and trajectory and route data management.

Typical methods combine Datalog and existential rules, chase procedures, finite controllability, acyclicity analysis, rewriting, dependency and complexity theory, and formal undecidability results. Systems research develops topology-aware storage, graph and distance indexes, adaptive physical layouts, query and retrieval optimization, graph sketches and compression, polyglot persistence, and structured datastores. User-oriented methods include natural-language-to-query translation, query relaxation, semantic ranking, generative relevance models, previews, and visual or investigative graph search.

Recent trends emphasize practical interoperability across graph models and heterogeneous sources; contextual and temporal knowledge graphs; scalable indexing and storage for massive graphs; dynamic pattern, flow, and motif analysis; compressed trajectory representations; and cloud-hosted, multi-tenant data services. The community is also pursuing accessible query interfaces, explainable relationship discovery, and theoretically grounded guarantees for reasoning and query answering.

9b9dd1dce7426ffa47f4849bd45d9778b49a6262.text:
## Scalable, Adaptive Data and Graph Systems

This community studies high-throughput data management for relational, graph, streaming, spatial, scientific, and AI workloads. Key themes include scalable ingest and updates, graph analytics, join processing, indexing, storage design, provenance, complex-event detection, approximate analytics, and integration across heterogeneous engines. It also addresses declarative reasoning and query evaluation under ontologies and tuple-generating dependencies.

Typical methods combine complexity and tractability analysis with adaptive indexing, workload- and hardware-aware data structures, sort-merge and factorized joins, associative-array and matrix formulations, logging and external-memory techniques, sketches and approximate indexes, clustering, and polynomial models for range aggregates. Systems exploit distributed clusters, SSDs, large-memory multicore servers, GPUs, and constrained edge devices. Stream processing uses adaptive automata, lazy evaluation, approximate filters, and consistency-aware event models; polystore architectures select among relational, array, and key-value engines. Formal work studies relational algebra, ontology-mediated queries, rule-based reasoning, containment, and space-efficient recursion.

Recent trends emphasize extreme-rate graph and provenance ingestion, streaming network updates, GraphBLAS-style database processing, autonomous camera analytics, interactive video queries, AI data wrangling, and exploratory visual insight recommendation. Other directions include evolutionary and declarative storage, benchmark/data-generation infrastructure, semantic knowledge-graph reasoning, approximate spatial and aggregate processing, and immutable or tamper-evident indexes.

e3438df6c2c9810815d980eca391b78fa5df8e56.text:
## Influence, Signed Relations, and Community Structure in Complex Networks

This community studies how influence, opinions, products, and information propagate through social and other complex networks, and how network structure, relationship valence, and interventions shape collective outcomes. Core themes include influence maximization for viral marketing, positive and negative ties, polarization and cooperation, relationship and edge-type prediction, community and group detection, and network-based analysis of software systems and social institutions. Applications span advertising, recommendation, software quality and vulnerability, political or cultural divisions, and collaborative knowledge production.

Typical methods combine cascade-based influence models with scalable greedy and residual optimization, machine learning, quadratic-correlation predictors, propagation algorithms, graph partitioning, community detection, centrality and network-science measures, and empirical analysis of large interaction datasets. Sparse-label classification, local community information, surveys, and context-aware collective entity resolution support inference in noisy or heterogeneous networks.

Recent trends emphasize signed and polarized networks, evidential or opinion-aware influence selection, and empirical study of how ideological diversity affects collective performance. Researchers increasingly seek scalable algorithms that balance influence-estimation accuracy, memory, and computation, while exploiting local structure and sparse observations. Network analysis is also expanding beyond social media toward modular, mixing, and dependency structures in complex software systems and other organizational or societal networks.

55524f467a53b54ff6810568dfe8238a48b03d58.text:
### Semantic Schemas and Knowledge-Graph Integration

This community studies semantic integration and structured access across heterogeneous web, document, and graph data. Core themes include XML schema learning and validation, unordered and interleaved regular expressions, RDF shape expressions, Schema.org annotation, semantic APIs, and knowledge-graph construction. It also addresses discovering useful views across data lakes, schema-guided stream processing, XML projection and XPath rewriting, logical graph-pattern queries, and regular-path evaluation.

Typical methods include schema inference, static complexity analysis, constraint validation, semantic annotation, query rewriting and optimization, view discovery, graph-pattern matching, and empirical prototyping and benchmarking.

Recent trends emphasize automated semantic publication, domain-specific knowledge graphs, richer schema languages and validation techniques, schema-guided processing of web and streaming data, and scalable discovery and querying over heterogeneous graph and document collections.

e52204c54b65a66af11315ff8de4def996598fab.text:
## Influence and Diffusion in Dynamic Networks

This community studies how information, opinions, products, diseases, behaviors, and collective activity propagate through social, temporal, spatial, and multiplex networks. Core themes include cascade and complex-contagion dynamics, competing products, adoption versus influence, homophily and fragmentation, weak and strong ties, polarization, community structure, diffusion–network coevolution, and recruitment or participation through social propagation. It also addresses interventions, marketing, and network design under resource, fairness, revenue, and coverage constraints.

Typical methods combine threshold, independent-cascade, epidemic, rumor, Bass, agent-based, and continuous-time Markov models with adaptive or tie-decay temporal-network analysis. Graph statistics, centrality and group centrality, community partitioning, signed and attributed graphs, random walks, percolation, hyperbolic and geometric random-graph models, and stochastic optimization are prominent. Machine learning and optimization infer hidden diffusion dynamics from aggregate observations and support influence, adoption, pricing, seed-selection, and trajectory-coverage decisions. Methods include adaptive submodularity, approximation algorithms, mixed-integer programming, optimal control, and fairness-aware analysis.

Recent directions emphasize adaptive and online influence maximization with feedback, continuous-time and dynamic seeding, external spreading agents, competitive and multi-product diffusion, social-network-assisted crowd recruitment, revenue-aware interventions, fairness and polarization mitigation, geometric network models, and principled design of networks and marketing-strategy mixes.

595a8709accf65ceb81b5279e00cc4633bdd5e50.text:
## Scientometrics, Evaluation, and Scholarly Networks

This community studies scientific impact, influence, collaboration, knowledge diffusion, research evaluation, and inequalities in academic careers and institutions. Themes include citation- and percentile-based assessment; field normalization, fractional and contribution-aware attribution, interdisciplinarity, productivity distributions, and indicator validity; collaboration and knowledge-flow networks; and disparities associated with gender, geography, seniority, academic rank, nepotism, and institutional or regional context. Editorial-board interlocking and journal communities are also examined.

Typical methods use bibliographic databases, citation and affiliation records, institutional outputs, and scholarly-platform data. Analyses construct citation, co-citation, bibliographic-coupling, co-authorship, author–paper, editorial-board, and geographic knowledge-flow networks, applying centrality indices, PageRank, community detection, similarity, network decomposition, and visualization. Statistical approaches include field- and time-normalized indicators, stochastic and multivariate models, quantile and gravity regression, Granger causality, distributional and inequality measures, funnel plots, and uncertainty analysis. Semantic networks, neural prediction, and path-based network reduction support trend discovery.

Recent trends emphasize fairer and more uncertainty-aware evaluation, contribution-sensitive counting, career persistence and mobility, gender and regional inequality, institutional ranking distortions, geographic diffusion, interdisciplinary impact, and predicting emerging research through semantic and network models.

397d1fb2326fa39f69f030847d237220282b096a.text:
## Dynamic, Signed, and Multimodal Networks

This community studies mesoscopic structure and inference in large, evolving, directed, weighted, signed, and bipartite networks. Themes include overlapping and hierarchical communities, core–periphery organization, dense subgraphs, node roles, bridges, polarization and balance, link strength and persistence, anomaly and fraud detection, network sampling, diffusion, and graph-based risk or preference prediction. Applications span online social, financial, affiliation, recommendation, educational, biological, and scientific networks.

Typical methods include stochastic blockmodels, latent-variable graph grammars, modularity and spectral approaches, random walks and absorbing Markov chains, local-information algorithms, consensus clustering, and graph signal processing. Cohesion is assessed with k-cores, triangles, clustering coefficients, degeneracy, superbubbles, and weighted or signed similarity measures. Diffusion distances, centrality, graph Fourier transforms, machine learning, ensemble anomaly detection, and co-clustering support prediction, reconstruction, classification, and recommendation.

Evaluation emphasizes detectability, uncertainty, sampling bias, missing data, stability, robustness, scalability, and computational guarantees. Recent trends include temporal and spatiotemporal graph learning, weighted link and graph similarity prediction, privacy and fraud de-anonymization, signed-community and polarization analysis, quality-guaranteed sampling, scalable triangle counting and graph generation, structural network classification, and spectral equivalence for efficient graph analysis.

d5bbc11c6570d7ee0ef1faba9d45ead0372ba9ad.text:
### Mathematical and Semantic Information Retrieval

This community develops methods for making mathematical and scientific knowledge searchable, interpretable, and reusable. Core themes include semantic retrieval of equations, mathematical notation analysis, formula–text and citation integration, and representation learning for symbols, expressions, and document context. It also increasingly connects scientific retrieval with ontology-based search, structured data, and heterogeneous information networks.

Typical methods combine neural and symbolic representations, recurrent or embedding-based models, topic models, generalized vector-space retrieval, ontology-aware query expansion, spreading activation, and semantic query reformulation. Formula normalization, canonicalization, and semantic-preserving conversion between LaTeX and computer algebra systems remain important. Graph-based methods—random walks, SimRank, meta-path inference, and link-based ranking—support similarity search across papers, entities, and citation or knowledge graphs.

A recurring challenge is aligning mathematics’ precise formal structure with ambiguous notation, natural-language context, citations, and latent semantic relations. This motivates representations spanning presentation, syntax, meaning, and graph structure.

Recent trends include large-scale studies of mathematical notation, equation- and citation-aware plagiarism detection, ontology-enhanced retrieval, structured scientific search, scalable similarity computation on dynamic graphs, and integration of textual, XML, relational, and graph data. Together, these efforts advance contextual mathematical understanding and more effective discovery and computational reuse of scientific knowledge.

e6e801710e28f1b633ed5e60dced1a633ff9cd46.text:
### Social Media, Influence, and Information Integrity

This community studies how social platforms shape political opinion and behavior, collective attention, social influence, information diffusion, popularity, and public perception. Key themes include misinformation, rumors, fake news, coordinated disinformation, malicious URLs, illicit activity, sentiment and mood, racial and cultural network structure, weak and strong ties, memes, recommendation, privacy, and real-time awareness of social and physical events.

Typical methods combine Twitter, Facebook, YouTube, Wikipedia, Weibo, Instagram, wearable-sensor, and other online interaction data with retweet, diffusion, temporal, geographic, linguistic, sentiment, and multimodal analysis. Researchers use deep neural networks with attention and author or propagation context, supervised machine learning, propensity-score matching, matrix factorization, time-series clustering and regression, graph dynamics and diffusion models, anomaly and outlier detection, network vulnerability and entropy measures, and scalable stream-mining pipelines. Text-image fusion, event summarization, social voting, and privacy-aware or decentralized architectures broaden the methodological toolkit.

Recent work emphasizes early message-level rumor and fake-news detection, coordinated-campaign discovery, multimodal event and illicit-activity monitoring, popularity and trend forecasting, and retweet-graph models of collective attention. Other trends include theory-informed election prediction from sparse digital traces, sentiment and mood measurement, wearable sensing of interpersonal influence, weak-tie diffusion, privacy-preserving social networking, and socially informed ranking and recommendation.

bb0a5acd276ed0511a92fcefff364fb564c3ff1c.text:
**Community Status: Multilayer Social Network Analysis**

**Main research themes:** This community studies online and offline social networks as multiplex, multilayer, weighted, signed, and dynamic systems. Key topics include link prediction and network evolution; homophily, weak ties, and community structure; cross-platform identity linkage and persona differentiation; information, disease, and behavior diffusion; human mobility and place-based sociality; and threats from spam, impersonation, flaming, deception, deanonymization, and active re-identification.

**Typical methods:** Researchers combine graph-theoretic similarity and clustering measures with supervised, generative, entropy- and mutual-information-based prediction models. They analyze cross-layer dependencies, link persistence, temporal rates, and structural or homophily features. Other approaches include thermodynamic/Kalman diffusion models, trajectory simulation, multilayer community and anonymity models, and network-based detection of malicious behavior. Data commonly come from social-media platforms, reviews, calls, Bluetooth/GPS proximity, smartphones, and cross-platform profile datasets.

**Recent trends:** Emphasis is shifting toward coevolving multilayer networks, temporal and cross-platform inference, privacy under increasingly realistic active attacks, and high-resolution sensing of social interaction, mobility, health, and personality. Synthetic trajectory generation, interpretable identity-linkage evaluation, and modeling positive and negative interactions are also emerging themes.

0f0a589692ddf64d652073b0e85479d2df56d135.text:
### Diffusion, Influence, and Evolving Social Networks

This community studies how epidemics, information, opinions, and social ties spread and evolve across complex, temporal, heterogeneous, and adaptive networks. Epidemic work includes SIS and SI processes, awareness and intervention dynamics, and non-Markovian transmission and recovery, using stability and threshold analysis, exact or approximate stochastic models, and optimization.

A growing focus is influence and campaigning: direct recruitment, word-of-mouth incentives, and external opinion control are allocated across degree classes and finite time horizons to maximize dissemination or shape heterogeneous populations. Voter-like models capture conformists, rebels, and stubborn individuals, while cost-aware incentive placement addresses strategic diffusion.

Another major theme is social-network formation and evolution. Microfoundational models represent boundedly rational, heterogeneous agents who meet stochastically, learn under incomplete information, and form links through bilateral consent. Strategic formation, coordination, homophily, structural diversity, social capital, bridging, redundancy, and stable network dynamics are analyzed using game-theoretic and dynamical methods.

Topology is also used to infer latent social structure, including tie strength, hierarchical and romantic relationships, and research-community trajectories, through common-neighbor analysis, strong triadic closure, link ranking, and temporal data mining. Source localization, partial observation, adaptive querying, and robust intervention remain important, with recent trends toward strategic, data-driven, and uncertainty-aware network control.

8dfbae7e374bb5470200ba2d3e9264a5ab13637b.text:
## Semantic Data Integration, Rule Reasoning, and Data Curation

This community studies integration and curation of heterogeneous, noisy, and incomplete data, with growing emphasis on knowledge graphs, ontologies, web data, and provenance. Core themes include entity and semantic-link resolution, approximate similarity and joins, declarative data quality, constraint-based cleaning, ontology-mediated querying, query rewriting and determinacy, rule-based reasoning, information extraction, and provenance management.

Typical methods combine SQL-expressed similarity predicates, blocking and approximate string matching, knowledge-graph embeddings, text and path-based scoring, link analysis, and distributed MapReduce or cloud indexing. Rule-based approaches use tuple-generating dependencies, existential rules, Datalog, guarded and warded fragments, chase procedures, acyclicity conditions, finite-controllability analysis, and complexity-theoretic reductions. Query answering also employs ontology rewriting, containment and determinacy analysis, path queries, and semantic optimization. Curation methods include probabilistic, on-demand repairs of denial constraints, dependency discovery, provenance summarization, temporal provenance models, and semi-supervised tree-based web-wrapper repair.

Recent trends emphasize scalable semantic integration across linked and web data, explainable knowledge-graph fact checking, low-supervision extraction, and benchmark-driven evaluation. Research increasingly combines learned representations with symbolic rules and relational structure, while distributed processing supports large-scale similarity, spatial, and nearest-neighbor operations. Theoretical work continues to delineate decidable and tractable fragments, alongside fundamental undecidability results for chase termination and query determinacy.

6ed79ea6f32a7b14515e814ba003ac7f8e5b29bb.text:
## Web, Search, and Social Network Analytics

This community studies hyperlink, knowledge, social-media, and interaction networks to understand information flow, topical communities, cultural and linguistic differences, online extremism, collective behavior, and user information seeking. Applications include multilingual Wikipedia trends and editing, Twitter-list curation and community discovery, cross-platform influence, search ranking and credibility, snippets and result-page design, library discovery, query expansion, route recommendation, citation bias, and multimodal social-relationship inference.

Typical methods include graph centrality and random walks, community detection and list aggregation, temporal interaction features such as social vector clocks, link and hyperedge prediction, hypergraph convolution, and network representation learning. Text analysis uses topic modeling, semi-supervised extraction, co-occurrence and temporal-prevalence analysis, and NMF. Information-retrieval studies apply learning-to-rank, query sampling and expansion, crowdsourced relevance judgments, user-task experiments, and meta-evaluation metrics. Multimodal inference combines profile, textual, visual, and longitudinal behavioral signals; trajectory work uses one-pass spatial-temporal compression.

Data include multilingual Wikipedia activity, Twitter lists and streams, cross-platform links, search results and queries, library catalogs, online communities, citation networks, POI maps, and user trajectories.

Recent trends emphasize multilingual and cross-platform knowledge mining, higher-order interaction modeling, real-time search and trend analysis, trustworthy and user-centered retrieval, privacy-aware multimodal inference, and rigorous evaluation of ranking systems.

e72b7c0ffffcc5305a5f08edb2d0b97f8bba6dc1.text:
### Graph-Aware Personalized Recommendation and Network Prediction

This community studies personalized recommendation and behavioral prediction over social, commercial, semantic, and heterogeneous information networks. Core themes include collaborative and content-based filtering, cold-start users and items, evolving interests, social influence, semantic relationships, paper and product similarity, team or partner selection, churn, fraud, and link formation. Recommendations increasingly incorporate temporal, geographic, multimodal, and relational context.

Typical methods include neighborhood and slope-one predictors, matrix and Bayesian factorization, hybrid content–collaborative models, ontology- and knowledge-graph representations, distributed semantic embeddings, and neural user/item encoders. Graph convolutional, attention, recurrent, and multilayer models support heterogeneous-network reasoning, dynamic link prediction, graph clustering, and answer selection. Meta-paths, structural-role representations, random walks, and multi-relational constraints capture topology, while interpretable clustering and explanation-based model tuning improve usability.

Recent trends emphasize dynamic and continuous-time graph representation, forecasting future relationships, modeling recent structural changes and temporal decay, and distinguishing community proximity from structural identity. Work also increasingly evaluates embeddings on downstream business and security tasks, including fraud detection and covert-network analysis. Robustness and security are growing concerns, with research on shilling and adversarial attacks against recommender systems and dynamic link predictors. Semantic social networks and citation-context embeddings broaden recommendation beyond interaction co-occurrence.

3372960a2667ae976abbaae2ede8a48e5de8e9ff.text:
### Privacy-Aware Social Information Retrieval and Event Intelligence

This community studies how large-scale online text and social traces support information discovery, summarization, indexing, recommendation, and situational awareness. Core topics include extracting keyphrases, keywords, concepts, and titles from scientific, medical, broadcast, and news documents; organizing news for rapid access; identifying actionable hashtags in disaster communications; and analyzing social tagging, mobility, relationships, and information diversity.

Typical methods include supervised and neural keyword/keyphrase extraction, graph-based ranking (PageRank, multipartite and complex-text graphs), semantic relatedness and role features, text denoising, topic and concept representations, dependency-tree compression, hierarchical and extractive multi-document summarization, abstractive generation, and relevance–diversity optimization. Social applications use folksonomy graphs, recommendation and ranking models, controlled social-bot experiments, location-based traces, and predictive regression over content and engagement features.

Recent trends emphasize large-scale, domain- and editor-annotated evaluation; real-time news monitoring and popularity forecasting; semantic and graph-enhanced terminology extraction; actionable disaster information filtering; and privacy-preserving retrieval and summarization using secure binary embeddings. The community also increasingly addresses robust comparison with simple baselines, multilingual or cross-domain transfer, information diversity, and efficient interfaces for scholarly and public information access.

a2a11df98e6c29ae04cb98bc25e08cc0a2b46afa.text:
**Information Retrieval: Neural Ranking and Structured Data Discovery**

**Main themes.** This community studies relevance modeling and semantic matching across web, scholarly, enterprise, e-commerce, multimedia, conversational, and question-answering search.
