Growing emphasis concerns dataset and data-lake search, web-table retrieval and classification, table-based QA, entity and relationship discovery, table completion, expert and venue recommendation, citation diversification, and knowledge-base enrichment. Query and session understanding, scalable ad hoc and passage retrieval, and structured information access remain central.

**Typical methods.** Systems combine lexical matching with sparse and dense embeddings, pretrained multilingual transformers, sequence-to-sequence models, CNNs/RNNs, probabilistic models, and graph or knowledge-base representations. Methods include pointwise, pairwise, listwise, metric-learning, and weak-supervision objectives; semantic table vectors; schema-label generation; query reformulation; entity linking; graph-based organization; and generative completion. Ranking also uses diversification and sequential decision processes. Click data is corrected through randomized interventions or propensity estimation, while compact neural re-ranking supports efficiency.

**Recent trends.** Research is moving toward large-scale human-labeled ranking benchmarks, pretrained generative rankers, hybrid sparse–dense retrieval, table- and dataset-centric search, automatic organization of data lakes, web-table QA and completion, and retrieval systems that expose structured knowledge from heterogeneous sources. Unbiased learning from interaction logs and context-aware personalized recommendation remain active concerns.

90d8c8a847372a00dfc38491681fefd4a5e31478.text:
## Scholarly Discovery, Semantic Publishing, and Recommendation

This community studies scholarly information retrieval, digital-library discovery, research-paper recommendation, citation analysis, and knowledge organization. Core themes include bibliographic metadata and citation matching, semantic publishing and Linked Open Data, scholarly knowledge graphs, author-contribution extraction, research-data and publication interlinking, expertise discovery, and user-aware ranking.

Typical methods combine bibliometrics and citation-network analysis with information extraction, entity linking, reference parsing, NLP, content and graph-based retrieval, learning-to-rank, collaborative filtering, document embeddings, keyphrase modeling, and meta-learning for per-instance algorithm selection. Systems exploit article text, metadata, citation graphs, recommendation logs, and knowledge-graph queries, often using Neo4j, Hadoop/MapReduce, and automated crawling pipelines. Evaluation increasingly uses large-scale online experiments, randomized or shuffled rankings, living labs, representative datasets, and time-sensitive metrics.

Recent trends emphasize semantic enrichment of scholarly literature, automated extraction and interlinking for quality assessment, accessible recommender-as-a-service infrastructure, and reproducible datasets such as large related-article recommendation logs. Work also addresses choice overload, position bias, algorithm robustness across scenarios, and comparisons among rules, machine learning, embeddings, and keyphrases. Scholarly portals increasingly support natural-language search, visualization, trend analysis, and graph-based exploration of research communities.

bc73757821835c06f24cce7314732bf2b4faaeab.text:
## Scalable Semantic, Graph, and Data Systems

This community studies scalable management and analysis of relational, RDF, knowledge, property, temporal, and distributed graphs. Core themes include high-throughput ingest and updates, graph traversal and reachability, join and path-query processing, federated and heterogeneous queries, indexing, storage layout, provenance, versioning, and semantic interoperability. It also addresses incomplete, fuzzy, probabilistic, and preference-aware information, as well as declarative reasoning under ontologies and dependencies.

Typical methods combine complexity and tractability analysis with adaptive, topology-aware storage; hop-labeling, partition and summary indexes; sort-merge, matrix-based, and projected joins; incremental and runtime query optimization; sketches, locality-sensitive hashing, and probabilistic ranking; and Datalog-based semantics and update validation. Systems target distributed clusters, GPUs, large-memory servers, and lightweight blockchain emulators, while supporting RDF, SPARQL, Gremlin, property graphs, and OLAP data cubes.

Recent trends emphasize SPARQL federation and extensions, RDF–property-graph interoperability, semantic-web analytics, large-scale knowledge-graph storage, temporal and regular-path queries, provenance visualization and reproducibility, collaborative dataset version control, and cross-chain atomic transactions. The community also increasingly studies graph-system taxonomies, programmable graph schemas, blockchain/database tradeoffs, and practical benchmarking of large federations and heterogeneous engines.

90eae0f2ab8e5a096117bb0265a9548500c24c94.text:
### Fair, Diverse, and Scalable Recommendation

This community studies recommender systems, search, and information access over social, commercial, and web data. Core themes include collaborative filtering, hybrid recommendation, network- and marketplace-aware ranking, long-tail discovery, popularity bias, and fairness for users, providers, artists, and other stakeholders. Applications include music, e-commerce, talent search, social media, and hidden-web databases.

Typical methods include matrix and Poisson factorization, trust- and social-aware models, fairness-aware learning objectives, group and individual fairness metrics, and post-processing re-ranking. These include diversity/MMR methods, provider-exposure balancing, temporal compensation for popularity bias, and synthetic “antidote” data. Systems also combine social, geographic, behavioral, demographic, price, and profit signals. Query-reranking-as-a-service and semantic approaches support customized ranking over databases, while streaming similarity joins, locality-sensitive hashing, and time-sensitive indexing address continuous social-data streams.

Recent work increasingly treats recommendation as a socio-technical optimization problem rather than pure preference prediction. Trends include auditing bias and offline-evaluation error, improving catalog coverage and exposure equity, optimizing business value alongside user utility, supporting incremental and dynamic fairness, and building scalable tools and services for real-time, open-ended data. Related studies model information diffusion, rumors, and social-commerce trust.

918aa647a806b7780916d0dee58ad86c23955a4a.text:
## Social Network Structure, Influence, and Collective Behavior

This community studies how network structure, content, and temporal interaction shape influence, visibility, diffusion, controversy, and collective behavior. Major themes include centrality and discoverability—especially PageRank, Bonacich, influence-based, coverage, and peripheral distinctiveness measures—as well as strategic rewiring, link placement, network design, robustness, and delay minimization. Community structure is examined through overlapping communities, community roles, social capitalists, information segregation, and missing-edge effects.

A parallel focus is analyzing content-rich interaction networks: controversy and opposing political stances, rumor propagation, abuse moderation, topic-specific information spread, and social-media visibility. Narrative networks model characters, roles, interactions, and evolving plots in books, films, and television, often using multilayer or temporal representations. Signed relations and opinion influence remain relevant through learned edge signs, address-term formality, social dominance, and DeGroot–Friedkin-inspired interventions.

Typical methods include graph centrality and ranking, spectral and motif-based analysis, community detection, game theory, combinatorial and convex optimization, link prediction, label propagation, graph kernels, machine learning, NLP, and temporal/multilayer network construction.

Recent trends emphasize content-aware and dynamic analysis: inferring network structure and sentiment from text, detecting controversy and misinformation from interaction patterns, modeling topic-specific users, and designing networks or interventions to optimize influence, exposure, and resilience.

8570a5bc618581889fe1d3c59b222a55f6754151.text:
### Wikipedia-Centered Search, Entity Intelligence, and Social Network Analytics

This community now focuses on large-scale search and knowledge discovery over Wikipedia, multilingual Web content, and online professional and social networks. Core themes include entity extraction, disambiguation, linking, multilingual entity ranking, category- and graph-based retrieval, semantic coverage analysis, and Wikipedia as a news, knowledge, and meta-search platform. A related strand studies personalized talent and expertise search, federated search across professional-network verticals, career and talent-flow analytics, and expert recommendation.

Typical methods combine knowledge-base and hyperlink graphs, entity and category features, centrality and PageRank-style scoring, vector-space retrieval, collaborative filtering, matrix factorization, homophily features, learning-to-rank, query-by-example, and neural semantic ranking. Large-scale multilingual annotation and lightweight, high-throughput entity-linking pipelines support processing user-generated text and billions of tokens. XML retrieval remains represented through hybrid full-text and structural database search.

Network research emphasizes influence and information diffusion, including fast spreader detection, local and fuzzy information dimensions, and hierarchical backbone extraction from bipartite graphs.

Recent trends favor multilingual, graph-aware and socially personalized retrieval; production deployment of deep ranking models; cross-platform expertise discovery; and mining user activity, edits, profiles, and network structure for real-time news, talent, and knowledge intelligence.

0ce2eb812deda17e577101ec555f4892e9b0d701.text:
## No Current Community Evidence

No papers remain to support a substantive description of this community. The previously reported themes—adaptive and multimodel data systems, data versioning and provenance, historical graphs, distributed analytics, energy-aware databases, and blockchain infrastructure—were supported by papers that have since left. No joined papers provide replacement themes, methods, or recent trends.

ec64f397d058c86fccddb6b6e4ab6975f73bfee0.text:
### Privacy-Preserving Analytics and Preference-Aware Querying

This community develops methods for analyzing, querying, and disseminating sensitive or preference-driven data while balancing privacy, utility, fairness, scalability, and functionality. Differential privacy remains central, covering histograms, synthetic and social-media data, summation and range queries, trajectories, continuous release, location recommendation, and protection against temporal or behavioral inference. Location privacy extends from points and trajectories to visits, routines, and mobility patterns.

A major theme is preference-aware database querying. Research models individual and group preferences over numerical and categorical attributes using strict partial or weak orders, Pareto composition, prioritized preferences, and preference revision. Skyline and \(k\)-nearest-neighbor queries are generalized through Eclipse queries, dynamic nominal-attribute preferences, and continuous dissemination to users. Preference queries also address elicitation, semantic optimization, integrity constraints, and incremental evaluation.

Secure outsourced and federated query processing uses encrypted databases, spatial order-preserving encryption, secure multiparty computation, trusted hardware, oblivious processing, query binning, and partitioned security to reduce leakage. Social-network and social-media publishing address linkage and relationship-inference attacks.

Typical methods include calibrated, local, and correlation-aware noise; workload optimization; order-theoretic reasoning; skyline and Pareto algorithms; controlled padding; secure computation; and trusted execution environments. Recent trends emphasize workload-adaptive local differential privacy, scalable continuous preference evaluation, semantic query optimization, and practical privacy-utility tradeoffs.

726a97c30e0c4f6eea983a047e5ee7a5b5f1d299.text:
### Formal Data Integrity in Enterprise Transformations

This community focuses on preserving data integrity as enterprise data is migrated, integrated, and transformed across systems. It challenges informal, ad hoc data-lake practices that defer cleaning and validation until after data has been collected, emphasizing guarantees built into transformation processes.

Typical methods use formal specifications of data transformations, integrity constraints, automated validation, and correctness guarantees that transformations preserve required properties. The emphasis is on preventing corruption and inconsistency rather than relying on costly ex-post-facto cleaning by data scientists.

Recent trends favor proactive, formally grounded data management for enterprise integration. Data quality is treated as a property to maintain throughout transformation pipelines, supporting more trustworthy analytics and AI systems while reducing the operational burden of downstream data preparation.

d97db8bb42ca84275e384f6f17719b75bf95fc1d.text:
## Explainable Relationship-Centric Graph Search

This community studies how to discover, contextualize, and explain relationships among entities, facts, users, and events in large heterogeneous graphs and information streams. Core themes include knowledge-graph relationship discovery, semantic association search, query relaxation when direct connections are absent, contextualization of graph facts, and tracing the evolution and hidden connections of news stories. It also examines how user actions, social connections, and interests shape personalized feeds, with emphasis on transparency, filter bubbles, and privacy.

Typical methods combine graph search and compact connected-subgraph discovery with indirect-path and relaxed-query algorithms, entity-pair correlation analysis, weakly supervised learning, and relevance-based selection of neighboring facts. News analysis uses large-scale text mining, temporal event linking, and relationship discovery beyond conventional similarity search. Feed explanation frameworks connect behavioral signals, social graphs, and recommendation outputs to produce interpretable rationales.

Recent trends emphasize explainable and exploratory graph-based search, enriching isolated facts with useful context, recovering relationships across distant or incomplete data, and reconstructing story evolution over time. Research increasingly targets user-facing transparency in knowledge-intensive search and recommendation while addressing noisy supervision, graph scale, and privacy concerns.

3815ceed55c95809f3a5835f107fc1a4a7dea2c8.text:

### Foundations, Benchmarking, and Adaptive Complex Event Processing

This community studies real-time processing of heterogeneous event streams, especially RFID, IoT, and distributed sensor data. Its goal is to transform high-volume inputs into actionable complex events through filtering, correlation, temporal pattern detection, inference, joins, and query processing.

Typical methods include specialized CEP languages and stream-processing architectures such as SASE; nondeterministic finite automata (NFAs), including lazy chain automata that limit unnecessary partial-match processing; integrated inference for recovering missing location and containment information; and distributed architectures for scalable tracking and monitoring. CEP workloads are modeled as multi-join queries, motivating join-order and query-plan optimization, while load shedding and consistency mechanisms support constrained environments. Distributed sensor acquisition additionally addresses scalable event joins and guaranteed time coherence across independently synchronized devices.

The community also develops evaluation infrastructure: benchmarks and generators for application-specific big-data workloads, controllable volume, variety, velocity, and veracity, and tools for tuning features in synthetic datasets. Stream-processing engines such as Storm, Spark, and Flink are compared using throughput, latency, and windowed-operation workloads.

Recent trends emphasize adaptive automata and query execution, scalable and time-consistent IoT joins, reproducible benchmarking, synthetic data generation, distributed stream analytics, real-time inference, and robust performance evaluation under changing workloads.
